items.ma-16:
Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim narrated to us, he said: Zuhayr – meaning Ibn Muʿāwiyah – narrated to us, he said: Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid narrated to us, he said: Qays narrated to us, he said: Abū Bakr ﵁ stood, and praised Allah ﷿ and extolled Him, and said: O people, you recite this verse: {O you who believe, upon you are your own selves; he who has gone astray will not harm you when you are guided} to the end of the verse [al-Māʾidah: 105], and you place it in a place other than its own. And I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Indeed, when the people see the munkar and do not change it, Allah is about to encompass them all with His punishment.”
He said: And I heard Abū Bakr say: O people, beware of lying, for lying keeps apart from īmān.
items.ma-161: Al-Walīd ibn Muslim narrated to us, al-Awzāʿī narrated to us, that Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr narrated to him from ʿIkrimah, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: I heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while he was at al-ʿAqīq, say: “There came to me tonight one who came from my Rabb and said: Pray in this blessed valley, and say: ʿUmrah in a Ḥajj.” Al-Walīd said: meaning: Dhū al-Ḥulayfah.
items.ma-484: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from al-Musayyab, from Mūsā ibn Ṭalḥah, from Ḥumrān, he said: ʿUthmān used to bathe every day once since he accepted Islam. So I set out water for ablution for him one day for the prayer, and when he had performed ablution, he said: Indeed I wanted to narrate to you a ḥadīth that I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then he said: It occurred to me not to narrate it to you. Then al-Ḥakam ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ said: O Commander of the Believers, if it is good, we will take it, or if it is evil, we will guard against it. He said: So he said: Then I will narrate it to you: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed this ablution, then said: “Whoever performs this ablution, and perfects the ablution, then stands to the prayer and completes its rukūʿ and its sujūd, it has expiated for him what is between it and the other prayer, so long as he does not incur a maqtalah” – meaning: a major sin.
items.ma-512: Muḥammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, Sulaymān ibn ʿAtīq informed me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bābayh, from some of the sons of Yaʿlā ibn Umayyah, he said: Yaʿlā said: I performed ṭawāf with ʿUthmān, and we touched the Corner. Yaʿlā said: I was on the side nearer the House. When we reached the western corner which adjoins the black [one], I pulled [him] by his hand so that he would touch it. He said: What is the matter with you? I said: Will you not touch it? He said: Did you not perform ṭawāf with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? I said: Yes indeed. He said: Did you see him touching these two western corners? I said: No. He said: Is there not for you in him a good example? I said: Yes indeed. He said: Then pass on, away from yourself.
items.ma-806: Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, the son of the brother of Ibn Shihāb narrated to us, from his paternal uncle, Abū ʿUbayd informed me, the mawlā of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Azhar, that he heard ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “It is not permissible for a Muslim man that anything of the meat of his nusuk be in his house in the morning after three [days].”
items.ma-1050: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us. And ʿAbd al-Razzāq: Isrāʾīl informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū Ḥayyah al-Wādiʿī – ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: from Abū Ḥayyah – he said: I saw ʿAlī urinate in al-Raḥabah, and he called for water and performed ablution. He washed his two palms three times, and rinsed his mouth and sniffed water into his nose three times, and washed his face three times, and washed his forearms three times each, and wiped his head, and washed his feet three times each. Then he stood and drank from the remainder of his ablution water. Then he said: Indeed I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do like that which you saw me do, and I wanted to show it to you.
items.ma-1117: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Laylā, from al-Minhāl ibn ʿAmr, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, he said: My father used to converse by night with ʿAlī, and ʿAlī used to wear summer garments in the winter, and winter garments in the summer. So it was said to me: If only you would ask him about this. So I asked him, and he said: “Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for me, while I had sore eyes, on the day of Khaybar, and I said: O Messenger of Allah, indeed I have sore eyes. So he spat in my eye and said: ‘O Allah, remove from him the heat and the cold.’ And I did not find heat or cold after that.” He said: And he said: “I will surely send a man Yuḥibbuhu Allāh wa-Rasūluh, and who loves Allah and His Messenger, not one who flees.” He said: So the people stretched up for it. He said: So he sent ʿAlī.
items.ma-1429: Wakīʿ and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, both said: Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from his grandfather – Ibn Numayr said: from al-Zubayr – he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “For one of you to take his ropes, then come to the mountain, and bring a bundle of firewood on his back, and sell it, and be independent of need by its price, is better for him than to ask the people, whether they give him or refuse him.”
items.ma-1746: Yazīd narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah informed us, he said: I saw Ibn Abī Rāfiʿ wearing a ring on his right hand, so I asked him about that, and he mentioned that he saw ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar wearing a ring on his right hand, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to wear a ring on his right hand.
items.ma-2060: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Jahḍam, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to complete the ablution fully.
items.ma-2066: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Muslim al-Baṭīn, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that the Prophet ﷺ, when he recited: {Glorify the name of your Rabb, al-Aʿlā}, would say: “Glory be to my Rabb, al-Aʿlā.”
items.ma-2377:
Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq: Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAṭāʾ ibn ʿAbbās ibn ʿAlqamah, the brother of Banī ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy, narrated to us, he said: I entered upon Ibn ʿAbbās in the house of Maymūnah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, on the day after Friday. He said: And Maymūnah had bequeathed it to him. When he prayed the Friday [prayer], [a spread] was laid out for him in it, then he would turn to it, and sit in it for the people. He said: A man asked him, and I was listening, about ablution from what fire has touched of food. He said: Ibn ʿAbbās raised his hand to his eyes – his sight had been taken – and said: With the sight of these two eyes of mine, I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform ablution for the Ẓuhr prayer in one of his rooms, then Bilāl called to the prayer, and he rose, going out. When he stood at the door of the room, a gift of bread and meat met him, which one of his Companions had sent to him. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned with those who were with him, and it was placed for them in the room. He said: So he ate, and they ate with him. He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose with those who were with him to the prayer, and neither he nor any one of those who were with him touched water. He said: Then he prayed with them.
And Ibn ʿAbbās only grasped of the affair of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ its last [part].
items.ma-2695: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Abū Yaḥyā al-Aʿraj, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Two men brought a dispute to the Prophet ﷺ, and the oath fell upon one of them, so he swore by Allah, other than Whom there is no deity, that he had nothing with him. He said: Then Jibrīl descended upon the Prophet ﷺ and said: Indeed he is lying; indeed he has his right with him. So he commanded him to give him his right, and the kaffārah of his oath is his knowledge that there is no deity except Allah, or his testimony.
items.ma-2722: Isḥāq – he is Ibn ʿĪsā – narrated to us; Muḥammad ibn Thābit al-ʿAbdī narrated to me, from Jabalah ibn ʿAṭiyyah, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in the house of one of his wives, he put down his head and slept, and he laughed in his sleep. When he woke, one of his wives said to him: You laughed in your sleep; what made you laugh? He said: “I am amazed at people from my ummah who ride this sea, [in the face of] the terror of the enemy, striving in the path of Allah.” Then he mentioned to them much good.
items.ma-3010: Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to present the Qurʾān to Jibrīl every Ramaḍān, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would wake in the morning, after the night in which he presented what he presented, being more generous than the wind that is sent forth. He was not asked for anything except that he gave it, until, when it was the month after which he died, he presented in it two presentations.
items.ma-3091: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, the son of the brother of Ibn Shihāb narrated to us, from his paternal uncle, he said: Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to me: he heard Abū Hurayrah say: Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq entered the mosque while ʿUmar was speaking to the people … then he mentioned the ḥadīth.
items.ma-3133: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Minhāl ibn ʿAmr, he said: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr say: I passed with Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbās on one of the roads of al-Madīnah, and there were youths who had set up a hen, shooting at it, for them [being] every [arrow] that misses. He said: So he became angry, and said: Who did this? He said: So they dispersed. Then Ibn ʿUmar said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed whoever mutilates an animal.
items.ma-3321: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: {You were the best ummah brought out for the people} [Āl ʿImrān: 110], he said: They are those who made hijrah with the Prophet ﷺ from Makkah to al-Madīnah.
items.ma-3634: Ḥusayn – meaning Ibn Muḥammad – narrated it to us, Jarīr – meaning Ibn Ḥāzim – narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash … then he mentioned something like it, except that he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh stood and said: O Messenger of Allah, the enemies of Allah have called you a liar, and harmed you, and expelled you, and fought you, and you are in a valley abundant in firewood, so gather for them much firewood, then set it ablaze upon them. And he said: Sahl ibn Bayḍāʾ.
items.ma-3951: Rawḥ and ʿAffān narrated to us, [in] meaning, both said: Ḥammād ibn Salamah, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Abū ʿUbaydah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd – ʿAffān said: from his father, Ibn Masʿūd – he said: Indeed Allah ﷿ sent forth His Prophet ﷺ to cause a man to enter Paradise, and he entered the kanīsah, and behold, he was with Jews, and a Jew was reading the Torah to them. When they came to the description of the Prophet ﷺ, they held back, and in a side of it was a sick man. The Prophet ﷺ said: “What is the matter with you that you held back?” The sick man said: Indeed they came to the description of a prophet, and they held back. Then the sick man came crawling until he took the Torah, and read until he came to the description of the Prophet ﷺ and his ummah, and said: This is your description and the description of your ummah. I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah, and that you are the Messenger of Allah. Then he died. The Prophet ﷺ said to his Companions: “Lū your brother.”
items.ma-4107: Wakīʿ and Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, both said: Al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū Wāʾil, he said: ʿAbd Allāh said: It is as if I am looking at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as he relates [the story of] a prophet from among the prophets whom his people struck, and he is flicking off the blood, (Abū Muʿāwiyah said: wiping off the blood) from his forehead, and saying: “O Rabb, forgive my people, for they do not know.”
items.ma-4264: I read to my father: ʿAlī ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to us, he said: Al-Hajarī informed us, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Repentance from a sin is that he repents from it, then does not return to it.”
items.ma-4577:
I heard Sufyān say: Indeed he made a vow, meaning to observe iʿtikāf in al-Masjid al-Ḥarām, and he asked the Prophet ﷺ, and he commanded him.
It was said to Sufyān: From Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar: that ʿUmar made a vow? He said: Yes.
items.ma-4887: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from Ibn ʿUmar, he said: I have not left touching the two corners, in ease or in hardship, since I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ touching them.
items.ma-5114: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd – meaning al-Wāsiṭī – narrated to us, Ibn Thawbān informed us, from Ḥassān ibn ʿAṭiyyah, from Abū Munīb al-Jurashī, from Ibn ʿUmar, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I was sent with the sword until Allah is worshipped, with no partner for Him. My provision was made beneath the shade of my spear, and humiliation and abasement were made upon whoever opposes my command. And whoever imitates a people is one of them.”
items.ma-5197: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from ʿUbayd Allāh, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “It is not right for a man who has something to make a bequest about to spend two nights without his bequest being written down with him.”
items.ma-5505: Muḥammad narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Abū al-Ḥakam: I heard Ibn ʿUmar narrating from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Whoever keeps a dog, except a dog for crops, or sheep, or hunting, a qīrāṭ is deducted from his reward every day.”
items.ma-5813: Yaḥyā ibn Ḥabīb ibn ʿArabī narrated to us, he said: Khālid ibn al-Ḥārith narrated to us, then he mentioned something like it.
items.ma-6123: Makkī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, Ḥanẓalah narrated to us: I heard Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh say: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever drags his garment out of arrogance, Lam yanẓur Allāh ilayhi on the Day of Resurrection.”
items.ma-6433: Asbāṭ narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar: that he used to perform ramal for three [circuits], from the Stone to the Stone, and to walk four at his ease. He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to do it.
items.ma-6748: Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, Muslim – meaning Ibn Khālid – narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān – meaning Ibn Ḥarmalah –, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “One rider is a devil, two riders are two devils, and three are a riding party.”
items.ma-7069: Qutaybah ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, Rishdīn informed us, from al-Ḥajjāj ibn Shaddād, from Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Ghifārī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣī, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “The first to enter by this door will be a man from the people of Paradise.” Then Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ entered.
items.ma-7380: Sufyān narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn; it was said to Sufyān: From Abū Hurayrah? He said: Yes. It was said to him: From the Prophet ﷺ? He said: Yes. “Whoever buys a muḥaffalah or a muṣarrāh has the choice. If he wishes to return it, let him return it, and if he wishes to keep it, he keeps it.”
items.ma-7690: ʿAbd al-Razzāq and Ibn Bakr narrated to us, both said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib informed me – and Ibn Bakr said: Ibn ʿAbd al-Malik – that Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr informed him, that Abū Hurayrah informed him, that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever prays over a funeral and follows it has two qīrāṭs, each like Uḥud; and whoever prays and does not follow it has one qīrāṭ, like Uḥud.” Ibn Bakr said: The qīrāṭ is like Uḥud.
items.ma-8002: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Bishr, from Shahr ibn Ḥawshab, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “The truffle is of the manna, and its water is a cure for the eye; and the ajwa date is from Paradise, and its water is a cure from poison.”
items.ma-8315: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Abū Bakr informed us, from Hishām, from Ibn Sīrīn, from Abū Hurayrah, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed the sun was not held back for any human being except for Yūshaʿ, during the nights he marched to Bayt al-Maqdis.”
items.ma-8623: Ḥasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, ʿAyyāsh ibn ʿAbbās al-Qitbānī narrated to us, from Abū Tamīm al-Zuhrī, from Abū Hurayrah, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When the prayer is established, there is no prayer except the one that has been established.”
items.ma-8936: Muḥammad ibn Idrīs narrated to us, Mālik informed us, from Mūsā ibn Abī Tamīm, from Saʿīd ibn Yasār, from Abū Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A dinar for a dinar, and a dirham for a dirham, with no excess between them.”
items.ma-9248: Khalaf ibn al-Walīd narrated to us, he said: Ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “No servant conceals a servant in this world except that Allah will conceal him on the Day of Resurrection.”
items.ma-9556: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, he said: Muḥammad ibn Ziyād narrated to us, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Fast for its sighting, and break the fast for its sighting; and if it is overcast upon you, complete the number, thirty.”
items.ma-9867: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, he said: Layth narrated to us, he said: ʿUqayl ibn Khālid narrated to me, from Ibn Shihāb, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, that Abū Hurayrah said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “I was sent with jawāmiʿ al-kalim, and I was given victory by terror. And while I was asleep, I was brought the keys of the treasures of the earth, and they were placed in my hands.”
items.ma-10176: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, he said: Al-Aʿmash narrated to us, he said: Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, he said: Abū Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, then he mentioned its meaning.
items.ma-10484: ʿAlī narrated to us, from al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, from Ibn Sīrīn, from Abū Hurayrah, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The ʿajmāʾ is jubār, and the mine is jubār, and in the rikāz is the khumus.”
items.ma-10793:
Yaḥyā ibn Ḥammād narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Abū Hurayrah, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Be light in the prayer, for behind you are the weak, the old, and the one with a need.” He said: And Ibrāhīm al-Taymī narrated to us, from al-Ḥārith ibn Suwayd, from ʿAbd Allāh, the like of that.
He said: And Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, the like of that.
He said: And Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of that.
items.ma-11104: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Abū Isrāʾīl – meaning Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Isḥāq al-Mulāʾī – informed us, from ʿAṭiyyah, from Abū Saʿīd, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed I am leaving among you the two weighty things, one of them greater than the other: the Book of Allah, a rope extended from the heaven to the earth, and my ʿitrah, the people of my house. And they will never separate until they come to me at the Ḥawḍ.”
items.ma-11418: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Shuʿbah informed us, from Abū al-Tayyāḥ, from Abū al-Waddāk, he said: I will not drink nabīdh after what I heard Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī say: A man was brought to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: They said: Indeed he is intoxicated. So he said: I only drank raisins and dates in a gourd. He said: So he was struck with sandals and pushed with hands. And he forbade the gourd, and that raisins and dates be mixed.
items.ma-11732: Yaḥyā ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah informed us, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Jābir, that Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī informed him that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “A people will come out of the Fire, having been burned, and they were like charcoal. The people of Paradise will keep sprinkling water over them until they sprout, as flood-debris sprouts in the silt carried by the torrent.”
items.ma-12045: Ibn Abī ʿAdī narrated to us, from Ḥumayd, from Anas, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “The best of what you treat yourselves with is cupping, and al-qusṭ al-baḥrī, and do not torment your children by pressing.”
items.ma-12355: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, from ʿImrān, from Qatādah, from Anas: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote to Kisrā, and Qayṣar, and Ukaydir of Dūmah, calling them to Allah ﷿.
items.ma-12440: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, Abān narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, from Anas ibn Mālik, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Jahannam will keep saying: Is there any more? Then Rabb al-ʿĀlamīn says, and Yaḍaʿu Qadamahu fīhā, and some of it folds in upon some of it, and it says: By Your ʿIzzah, enough, enough. And there remains a surplus in Paradise until Allah brings into being another creation, and settles them in the surplus of Paradise.”
items.ma-12674: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, he said: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, he said: Anas ibn Mālik informed me, he said: There was none among them more like the Messenger of Allah ﷺ than al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī.
items.ma-12986: Bahz and ʿAffān narrated to us, both said: Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, Isḥāq ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Ṭalḥah narrated to us, from Anas ibn Mālik, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The Dajjāl will come and tread the earth, except Makkah and al-Madīnah. He will come to al-Madīnah and find at every pass of its passes rows of angels. Then he will come to Sabkhat al-Jurf and pitch his tent, and al-Madīnah will shake with three tremors, and every hypocrite, male and female, will go out to him.”
items.ma-13302: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Bilāl ibn Abī Mūsā, from Anas ibn Mālik, he said: Al-Ḥajjāj wished to appoint his son over the judgeship of al-Baṣrah. He said: So Anas said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever seeks the judgeship and seeks help for it is left to it; and whoever does not seek it and does not seek help for it, Allah sends down an angel to guide him aright.”
items.ma-13613: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, Ḥumayd informed us, from Anas: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the sale of fruit until it ripens, and the sale of grapes until they turn black, and the sale of grain until it hardens.
items.ma-13923: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Anas: that Barīrah was given a ṣadaqah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “It is ṣadaqah for her, and a gift for us.”
items.ma-14235: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Misʿar narrated to us, from Muḥārib ibn Dithār, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Prophet ﷺ owed me a debt, and he repaid me, and gave me more.
items.ma-14468: Muḥammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, Abū al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh say: When the Prophet ﷺ gave the khuṭbah, he would lean against the trunk of a date palm, one of the pillars of the mosque. When the minbar was made for him, and he took his seat upon it, the pillar shook like the yearning of a she-camel, until the people of the mosque heard it. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came down to it and held it close, and it became still. ʿAbd al-Razzāq and Rawḥ said: that pillar shook; and Rawḥ said: so he embraced it, and it became still; and ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: and it fell silent.
items.ma-14550: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAqīl, from Jābir, he said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the home of a woman of the Anṣār who had made food for him. The Prophet ﷺ said: “A man from the people of Paradise will enter upon you.” Then Abū Bakr entered, and we congratulated him. Then he said: “A man from the people of Paradise will enter upon you.” Then ʿUmar entered, and we congratulated him. Then he said: “A man from the people of Paradise will enter upon you.” And I saw the Prophet ﷺ putting his head beneath the young palm shoots and saying: “O Allah, if You will, make him ʿAlī.” Then ʿAlī entered, and we congratulated him.
items.ma-14862: ʿAbīdah narrated to us, al-Aswad ibn Qays narrated to us, from Nubayḥ al-ʿAnazī, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to forbid one of us, when he came back from a journey, from coming upon his family by night. He said: Then we came upon them by night afterwards.
items.ma-15182: Surayj narrated to us, Ḥammād – meaning Ibn Zayd – narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade renting out land. Then he mentioned that to Ibn ʿUmar, and a man said: I saw the son of Jābir seeking land by mukhābarah. So Ibn ʿUmar said: Look at this one: his father narrates from the Prophet ﷺ that he forbade renting out land, while he seeks land to practise mukhābarah on.
items.ma-15495: Ibrāhīm ibn Abī al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, Baqiyyah narrated to us, Baḥīr ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from Khālid ibn Maʿdān, from some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw a man praying, and on the back of his foot was a patch the size of a dirham that the water had not reached, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded him to repeat the ablution.
items.ma-15805: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Makhlad narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Nāfiʿ al-Kilābī, of the people of al-Baṣrah, he said: I passed by a mosque in al-Madīnah, and the prayer was established, and there was an old man, who rebuked the muʾadhdhin and said: Did you not know that my father informed me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command delaying this prayer? He said: I said: Who is this old man? They said: This is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rāfiʿ ibn Khadīj.
items.ma-16123: Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, he said: Ayyūb informed us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Mulaykah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, that ʿAlī mentioned the daughter of Abū Jahl, and it reached the Prophet ﷺ, so he said: “Indeed she is Fāṭimah, a part of me. Whatever harms her harms me, and whatever wearies her wearies me.”
items.ma-16437: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, he said: Maʿmar narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAbbād ibn Tamīm, from his paternal uncle, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out with the people to ask for rain. He prayed two rakʿahs with them, recited aloud in them, turned his cloak around, made supplication, and faced the qiblah.
items.ma-16759: ʿAffān narrated to us, he said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, al-Nuʿmān ibn Sālim said: A man whom he named informed me, from Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim – he said: I think he heard it from Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim – he said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, the people claim that we have no rewards in Makkah. He said: And I think he said: “They have lied. Your rewards will surely come to you, even if you were in the burrow of a fox.”
items.ma-17072: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, he said: And Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn al-Ḥārith al-Taymī narrated to me – concerning the ṣalāh upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when a Muslim sends ṣalāh upon him in his prayer – from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zayd ibn ʿAbd Rabbih al-Anṣārī, the brother of Balḥārith ibn al-Khazraj, from Abū Masʿūd ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmr, he said: A man came until he sat before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while we were with him, and said: O Messenger of Allah, as for the salām upon you, we have come to know it; so how do we send ṣalāh upon you when we pray in our prayer – ṣallā Allāh ʿalayk? He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ fell silent, until we wished that the man had not asked him. Then he said: “When you send ṣalāh upon me, say: O Allah, send ṣalāh upon Muḥammad, the Prophet al-Ummī, and upon the family of Muḥammad, as You sent ṣalāh upon Ibrāhīm and the family of Ibrāhīm; and bless Muḥammad, the Prophet al-Ummī, as You blessed Ibrāhīm and the family of Ibrāhīm. Indeed You are Ḥamīd, Majīd.”
items.ma-17384: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, from Saʿīd, from Qatādah, from al-Ḥasan, from ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “The ʿuhdah of the slave is three.”
items.ma-17703: Ḥasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, Sulaymān ibn Ziyād al-Ḥaḍramī narrated to us that he heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Jazʾ al-Zubaydī, a Companion of the Prophet ﷺ, say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade us from any one of us urinating facing the qiblah.
items.ma-18019: Ḥasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hubayrah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Jubayr, he said: I was in a gathering in which were al-Mustawrid ibn Shaddād and ʿAmr ibn Ghaylān, and I heard al-Mustawrid say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever takes charge of some work for us,” then he mentioned the like of the ḥadīth of al-Ḥārith.
items.ma-18336: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Khālid narrated to us, from Abū al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Shikhkhīr, from his brother Muṭarrif, from ʿIyāḍ ibn Ḥimār, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever picks up a luqaṭah, let him have one just person or two just persons witness it, then let him not conceal it and not hide it away. If its owner comes, he has more right to it; and if not, then it is the property of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills.”
items.ma-18653: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Barāʾ. He said: And Ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, that he heard al-Barāʾ say: When {Not equal are those who sit among the believers and the strivers in the path of Allah} was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called Zayd, and he came with a shoulder-blade and wrote it down. Then Ibn Umm Maktūm complained of his affliction, so {Not equal are those who sit among the believers, other than those with affliction} was revealed [al-Nisāʾ: 95].
items.ma-18965: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Bishr ibn al-Sarī narrated to us [ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad said]: And Abū Khaythamah narrated to me, Bishr ibn al-Sarī narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Ḥārithah ibn Muḍarrib, from Furāt ibn Ḥayyān, that the Prophet ﷺ commanded that he be killed – he was a spy for Abū Sufyān and an ally – and he passed by a circle of the Anṣār and said: I am a Muslim. They said: O Messenger of Allah, he claims he is a Muslim. So he said: “Among you are men whom we leave to their īmān; among them is Furāt ibn Ḥayyān.”
items.ma-19277: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, Ḥasan ibn Muslim informed me, from Abū al-Minhāl – and he did not hear it from him – that he heard Zayd and al-Barāʾ. Then he mentioned the ḥadīth.
items.ma-19594: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from Abū Qilābah and from al-Qāsim al-Tamīmī, from Zahdam al-Jarmī, he said: There was a bond of brotherhood between us and al-Ashʿarī. Then he mentioned the ḥadīth and its meaning.
items.ma-19911: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Jaʿfar ibn Ḥayyān narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan, from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The begging of a rich man is a blemish on his face.”
items.ma-20224: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar and ʿAffān narrated to us, both said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Ibn Abī Laylā – ʿAffān said in his ḥadīth: Al-Ḥakam informed us, he said: I heard Ibn Abī Laylā – from Samurah ibn Jundub, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Whoever narrates a ḥadīth from me while he thinks that it is a lie, he is one of the liars.” And ʿAffān also said: the liars.
items.ma-20539:
Yūnus narrated to us, Ḥammād – meaning Ibn Zayd – narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from Abū Qilābah, from Mālik ibn al-Ḥuwayrith al-Laythī: that he said to his companions one day: Shall I not show you how the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was? He said: And that was at a time other than the time of prayer. So he stood and made the standing settled, then bowed and made the bowing settled, then raised his head and stood upright for a short while, then prostrated, then raised his head, and says the takbīr in the sitting, then waited a short while, then prostrated. Abū Qilābah said: So he prayed a prayer like the prayer of this shaykh of ours – meaning: ʿAmr ibn Salimah al-Jarmī, who used to lead the prayer in the time of the Prophet ﷺ.
Ayyūb said: I saw ʿAmr ibn Salimah doing something I do not see you doing: when he raised his head from the two prostrations he sat upright, then stood up from the first rakʿah and the third.
items.ma-20849: Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, from Simāk, from Jābir ibn Samurah, he said: Bilāl used to call the adhān when the sun passed its zenith, without fail; then he would not give the iqāmah until the Prophet ﷺ came out. He said: When he came out, he gave the iqāmah as soon as he saw him.
items.ma-21164: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us; Suwayd ibn Saʿīd narrated to me; al-Walīd ibn Muḥammad al-Muwaqqarī narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, he said: I heard Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān say: I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghūth say: I heard Ubayy ibn Kaʿb say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say … then he mentioned it. And he did not mention Marwān in it.
items.ma-21487: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Shimr ibn ʿAṭiyyah, from his shaykhs, from Abū Dharr, he said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, advise me. He said: “When you commit an evil deed, follow it with a good deed; it will wipe it out.” He said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, is “There is no deity except Allah” among the good deeds? He said: “It is the best of the good deeds.”
items.ma-21805:
ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Maʿmar narrated to us, Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd narrated to us, Ibn Shihāb narrated to us, from a cousin of Usāmah ibn Zayd who was called ʿIyāḍ – the daughter of Usāmah was with him – and he mentioned the ḥadīth like it.
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: And some of them said: ʿIyāḍ ibn Ḍamrī.
items.ma-22123: Yūnus narrated to us, Fulayḥ narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Abī Unaysah, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, from Muʿādh: that the prayer was transformed through three states; then he mentioned its states – qaṭṭ.
items.ma-22350: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Sulaymān, from Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, from his father, from Abū Masʿūd: that he was beating a slave of his, and the Prophet ﷺ said to him: “By Allah, Allah is more capable over you than you are over him.” He said: O Prophet of Allah, then I have freed him for Wajh Allāh ﷿.
items.ma-22438: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, from Thawbān, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed a servant is deprived of provision because of a sin that befalls him; and nothing repels the Qadar except duʿāʾ, and nothing increases lifespan except birr.”
items.ma-22757: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd al-Hāshimī narrated to us, Ismāʿīl informed us, ʿAmr informed us, from al-Muṭṭalib, from ʿUbādah ibn al-Ṣāmit, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Guarantee me six things from yourselves, and I will guarantee you Paradise: be truthful when you speak, fulfil when you promise, discharge when you are entrusted, guard your private parts, lower your gazes, and restrain your hands.”
items.ma-23079: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim al-Laythī, from a man from among them, that he came to the Prophet ﷺ and accepted Islam on the condition that he pray two prayers, and he accepted it from him.
items.ma-23393: Muʾammal narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz – meaning Ibn Muslim – narrated to us, Ḥuṣayn narrated to us, from Abū Wāʾil, from Ḥudhayfah, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Peoples will surely come to me at the Ḥawḍ, and when I see them, they are snatched away from before me. Then I say: O my Rabb, my Companions, my Companions! Then it is said: Indeed you do not know what they innovated after you.”
items.ma-23710: Ḥajjāj ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, Ibn Abī Dhiʾb narrated to us, from Saʿīd al-Maqburī, he said: My father informed me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wadīʿah, from Salmān al-Khayr, from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: “No man bathes on the day of Friday, and purifies himself as much as he is able of purification, and applies oil from his oil, or touches some of the perfume of his house, then goes out to the mosque and does not separate between two [persons], then prays what Allah has written for him, then listens in silence to the imām when he speaks, except that he is forgiven for what is between him and the other Friday.”
items.ma-24044: Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, he said: Yūnus ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, from al-ʿAyzār ibn Ḥurayth, from ʿĀʾishah, she said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to stand and pray, with one edge of the quilt upon him and one edge of it upon ʿĀʾishah; then he would pray.
items.ma-24356: Yūnus narrated to us, he said: Layth narrated to us, from Yazīd, from Mūsā ibn Sarjis, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from ʿĀʾishah, she said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was dying, with a cup of water by him, and he would put his hand into the cup, then wipe his face with the water, then say: “O Allah, help me against the agonies of death.”
items.ma-24666: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, he said: ʿAwf narrated to us, from Awfā ibn Dalham, from Muʿādhah, from ʿĀʾishah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to take something from our faces while he was fasting.
items.ma-24975:
Rawḥ narrated to us, he said: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said: Ibn Shihāb informed me, from ʿUrwah, from ʿĀʾishah, that she said: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ and ʿAbd ibn Zamʿah brought a dispute to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Saʿd said: O Messenger of Allah, the son of my brother ʿUtbah ibn Abī Waqqāṣ – he charged me that he is his son. Look at his resemblance.
And ʿAbd ibn Zamʿah said: This is my brother, O Messenger of Allah, born on the bed of my father. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at his resemblance, and saw a clear resemblance to ʿUtbah, and said: “He is yours, O ʿAbd ibn Zamʿah. The child belongs to the bed, and for the adulterer is the stone. And veil yourself from him, O Sawdah daughter of Zamʿah.” She said: And he never saw Sawdah.
items.ma-25287: Ḥammād narrated to us, Hishām informed us, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿUrwah, he said: I heard ʿUrwah narrating: from ʿĀʾishah, she said: I used to perfume the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with the finest perfume I was able to, before he entered iḥrām; then he would enter iḥrām.
items.ma-25596: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from al-Miqdām ibn Shurayḥ ibn Hāniʾ, from his father, ʿĀʾishah said: Whoever narrates to you that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ urinated standing, do not believe him; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not urinate standing since the Qurʾān was sent down upon him.
items.ma-25912: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, he said: Hishām informed us, from Ibn Sīrīn, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaqīq, he said: I asked ʿĀʾishah about the prayer of the Prophet ﷺ, and she said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed standing, then he mentioned the meaning of the ḥadīth of Muḥammad ibn Salamah.
items.ma-26223: Yūnus narrated to us, he said: Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, he said: Maʿmar narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwah, from ʿĀʾishah, she said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Five are fawāsiq, to be killed in the Ḥaram: the mouse, the scorpion, the crow, the kite, and the biting dog.”
items.ma-26540: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, he said: ʿAwf narrated to us, from Abū al-Muʿadhdhal ʿAṭiyyah al-Ṭufāwī, from his father, that Umm Salamah narrated to him, she said: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in my house one day, the servant said: ʿAlī and Fāṭimah are at the doorway. She said: He said to me: “Rise and move aside for me from the people of my house.” She said: So I rose and moved aside, close by in the house. Then ʿAlī and Fāṭimah entered, and with them al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn, two small boys. He took the two boys and put them in his lap and kissed them. He said: And he embraced ʿAlī with one hand and Fāṭimah with the other hand, and kissed Fāṭimah and kissed ʿAlī. Then he drew a black cloak over them and said: “O Allah, to You, not to the Fire – I and the people of my house.” She said: I said: And I, O Messenger of Allah? He said: “And you.”
items.ma-26853: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, he said: Maʿmar narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Nudbah, the mawlāh of Maymūnah, from Maymūnah, she said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to have contact with one of his wives while she was menstruating, with a cloth upon her down to the knee, or to the middle of the thighs.
items.ma-27173: Surayj and Abū Jaʿfar al-Madāʾinī narrated to us, both said: ʿAbbād narrated to us, from Sufyān ibn Ḥusayn, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik, from his father, that the Prophet ﷺ passed by him while he was keeping hold of a man, and said: “What is this?” He said: O Messenger of Allah, a debtor of mine. And he gestured with his hand that he take the half. I said: O Messenger of Allah, yes. He said: So he took the half and left the half.
items.ma-27491: Ḥasan narrated to us, he said: Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, from Wāhib ibn ʿAbd Allāh, that Abū al-Dardāʾ said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever says: There is no deity except Allah, alone, having no partner, enters Paradise.” He said: I said: Even if he commits zinā and even if he steals?! He said: “Even if he commits zinā and even if he steals.” I said: Even if he commits zinā and even if he steals?! He said: “Even if he commits zinā and even if he steals.” I said: Even if he commits zinā and even if he steals?! He said: “Even if he commits zinā and even if he steals, in spite of the nose of Abū al-Dardāʾ.” He said: So I went out to proclaim it among the people. He said: ʿUmar met me and said: Go back, for if the people learn of this, they will rely upon it. So I went back and informed him ﷺ, and he ﷺ said: “ʿUmar has spoken truly.”
items.ma-1: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥanbal narrated to us, he said: My father Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Ḥanbal ibn Hilāl ibn Asad narrated to me, from his book, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr narrated to us, he said: Ismāʿīl – meaning Ibn Abī Khālid – informed us, from Qays, he said: Abū Bakr ﵁ stood, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: O people, you recite this verse: {O you who believe, upon you are your own selves; he who has gone astray will not harm you when you are guided} [al-Māʾidah: 105], and indeed we heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Indeed, when the people see the munkar and do not change it, it is near that Allah will encompass them all with His punishment.”
items.ma-2: Wakīʿ narrated to us, he said: Misʿar and Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿUthmān ibn al-Mughīrah al-Thaqafī, from ʿAlī ibn Rabīʿah al-Wālibī, from Asmāʾ ibn al-Ḥakam al-Fazārī, from ʿAlī ﵁, he said: Whenever I heard a ḥadīth from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Allah benefited me by it as He willed; and when someone other than me narrated to me from him, I would make him swear an oath, and when he swore to me I believed him. And Abū Bakr ﵁ narrated to me – and Abū Bakr spoke truly – that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “There is no man who commits a sin, then performs ablution and perfects the ablution – Misʿar said: and prays; and Sufyān said: then prays two rakʿahs – and seeks forgiveness from Allah ﷿, except that he is forgiven.”
items.ma-3:
ʿAmr ibn Muḥammad Abū Saʿīd – meaning al-ʿAnqazī – narrated to us, he said: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib, he said: Abū Bakr bought a saddle from ʿĀzib for thirteen dirhams. He said: Abū Bakr said to ʿĀzib: Tell al-Barāʾ to carry it to my house. He said: No, not until you tell us what you did when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left, while you were with him.
He said: Abū Bakr said: We set out and travelled by night, and we pressed on through our day and our night until it was noon, and the sun stood at its height. I cast my gaze about: do I see a shade we can take refuge in? And behold, a rock. I made for it, and there was a remnant of its shade, so I levelled it for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and spread a sheepskin for him, and said: Lie down, O Messenger of Allah. So he lay down. Then I went out looking: do I see anyone of the pursuers? And behold, a shepherd of sheep. I said: To whom do you belong, O boy? He said: To a man of Quraysh. He named him, and I knew him. I said: Is there any milk in your sheep? He said: Yes. He said: I said: Will you milk for me? He said: Yes. He said: I commanded him, and he held one of the ewes; then I commanded him, and he wiped the dust from its udder; then I commanded him, and he wiped the dust from his palms. And with me was a leather water-container with a cloth over its mouth. He milked for me a small quantity of milk, and I poured [water] over the cup until its bottom cooled. Then I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and found him awake, and I said: Drink, O Messenger of Allah. So he drank until I was content. Then I said: Has the time for departure come?
He said: So we set off, with the people seeking us, and none of them overtook us except Surāqah ibn Mālik ibn Juʿshum, on a horse of his. I said: O Messenger of Allah, this is the pursuit; it has caught up with us. He said: “Do not grieve; Allah is with us.” Until, when he came near to us, and between us and him was the distance of a spear, or two spears, or three, I said: O Messenger of Allah, this is the pursuit; it has caught up with us. And I wept. He said: “Why do you weep?” I said: By Allah, it is not for myself that I weep, but I weep for you. He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made supplication against him and said: “O Allah, suffice us against him by whatever You will.” Then the legs of his horse sank into its belly in hard ground, and he leapt off it and said: O Muḥammad, I know that this is your doing, so supplicate Allah that He rescue me from what I am in. By Allah, I will surely mislead those behind me among the pursuers. And this is my quiver, so take an arrow from it, for you will pass by my camels and my sheep in such and such a place, so take from them what you need. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I have no need of them.” He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ supplicated for him, and he was released, and returned to his companions.
And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went on, and I with him, until we reached al-Madīnah. The people met him and went out on the road and onto the rooftops, and the servants and the boys ran hard along the road, saying: Allāhu akbar! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has come! Muḥammad has come! He said: And the people disputed over which of them he would stay with. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Tonight I will stay with Banū al-Najjār, the maternal uncles of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, to honour them by that.” When morning came, he went out to where he was commanded.
Al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib said: The first of the Muhājirūn to come to us was Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr, the brother of Banū ʿAbd al-Dār; then Ibn Umm Maktūm the blind, the brother of Banū Fihr, came to us; then ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb came to us with twenty riders. We said: What has the Messenger of Allah ﷺ done? He said: He is on my trail. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came, and Abū Bakr with him.
Al-Barāʾ said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had not yet come when I had recited surahs of the Mufaṣṣal.
Isrāʾīl said: And al-Barāʾ was of the Anṣār, from Banū Ḥārithah.
items.ma-4: Wakīʿ narrated to us, he said: Isrāʾīl said, Abū Isḥāq said: from Zayd ibn Yuthayʿ, from Abū Bakr: that the Prophet ﷺ sent him with Barāʾah to the people of Makkah: No polytheist shall perform Ḥajj after this year, no naked person shall circumambulate the House, and none shall enter Paradise except a Muslim soul. Whoever has a period of treaty between him and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, his term runs until the end of his period. And Allah is free of the polytheists, and [so is] His Messenger. He said: He travelled with it for three days, then he said to ʿAlī, رَضِيَ اللهُ تَعَالَى عَنْهُ: “Catch up with him and send Abū Bakr back to me, and you deliver it.” He said: So he did. He said: When Abū Bakr came to the Prophet ﷺ, he wept. He said: O Messenger of Allah, has something happened concerning me? He said: “Nothing has happened concerning you but good; but I was commanded that none deliver it except me or a man from me.”
items.ma-5: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, he said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn Khumayr, from Sulaym ibn ʿĀmir, from Awsaṭ, he said: Abū Bakr addressed us and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood in this place of mine last year – and Abū Bakr wept – then Abū Bakr said: Ask Allah for muʿāfāh – or he said: ʿāfiyah – for no one has ever been given, after certainty, anything better than ʿāfiyah – or muʿāfāh. Hold to truthfulness, for it is with birr, and the two are in Paradise; and beware of lying, for it is with fujūr, and the two are in the Fire. And do not envy one another, do not hate one another, do not sever ties with one another, do not turn your backs on one another, and be brothers, as Allah has commanded you.
items.ma-6: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī and Abū ʿĀmir narrated to us, both said: Zuhayr – meaning Ibn Muḥammad – narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh – meaning Ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAqīl –, from Muʿādh ibn Rifāʿah ibn Rāfiʿ al-Anṣārī, from his father, Rifāʿah ibn Rāfiʿ, he said: I heard Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq ﵁ say on the minbar of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say – and Abū Bakr wept when he mentioned the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then it was lifted from him – then he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say, in this heat last year: “Ask Allah for pardon and ʿāfiyah, and for certainty in the Hereafter and the first.”
items.ma-7: Abū Kāmil narrated to us, he said: Ḥammād – meaning Ibn Salamah – narrated to us, from Ibn Abī ʿAtīq, from his father, from Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “The siwāk is a purifier for the mouth, [a means of] Riḍā for the Rabb.”
items.ma-8:
Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim narrated to us, he said: Al-Layth narrated to us, he said: Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb narrated to me, from Abū al-Khayr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, from Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, that he said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Teach me a supplication to make in my prayer. He said: “Say: O Allah, I have wronged myself with much wrong, and none forgives sins except You; so forgive me with a forgiveness from You, and have mercy on me; indeed You are al-Ghafūr al-Raḥīm.”
And Yūnus said: great. Ḥasan al-Ashyab narrated it to us, from Ibn Lahīʿah, he said: great.
items.ma-9: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, he said: Maʿmar narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwah, from ʿĀʾishah: that Fāṭimah and al-ʿAbbās came to Abū Bakr ﵁, seeking their inheritance from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they were at that time asking for his land at Fadak and his share at Khaybar. Abū Bakr said to them: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “We are not inherited from; what we leave is ṣadaqah. The family of Muḥammad only eat from this property.” And by Allah, I will not leave any matter that I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ doing concerning it except that I do it.
items.ma-10: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Muqriʾ narrated to us, he said: Ḥaywah ibn Shurayḥ narrated to us, he said: I heard ʿAbd al-Malik ibn al-Ḥārith say: that Abū Hurayrah said: I heard Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq say on this minbar: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on this day last year – then Abū Bakr shed tears and wept – then he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “You have not been given anything after the word of ikhlāṣ like ʿāfiyah, so ask Allah for ʿāfiyah.”
items.ma-11: ʿAffān narrated to us, he said: Hammām narrated to us, he said: Thābit informed us, from Anas, that Abū Bakr narrated to him, he said: I said to the Prophet ﷺ while he was in the cave – and once he said: while we were in the cave –: If one of them were to look at his feet, he would see us beneath his feet. He said: He said: “O Abū Bakr, what do you think of two, of whom Allah is the third?”
items.ma-12: Rawḥ narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abī ʿArūbah narrated to us, from Abū al-Tayyāḥ, from al-Mughīrah ibn Subayʿ, from ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth, from Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ narrated to us: “The Dajjāl will emerge from a land in the east called Khurāsān; peoples will follow him whose faces are like hammered shields.”
items.ma-13: Abū Saʿīd, the mawlā of Banū Hāshim, narrated to us, he said: Ṣadaqah ibn Mūsā, the flour-seller, narrated to us, from Farqad, from Murrah ibn Sharāḥīl, from Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There shall not enter Paradise a miser, nor a deceiver, nor a traitor, nor one who treats badly those he owns. And the first to knock at the door of Paradise are slaves, when they act well in what is between them and Allah ﷿, and in what is between them and their masters.”
items.ma-14: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to us – and I heard it from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Shaybah – he said: Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, from al-Walīd ibn Jumayʿ, from Abū al-Ṭufayl, he said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken, Fāṭimah sent to Abū Bakr: Are you the heir of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, or his family? He said: No, rather his family. She said: Then where is the share of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? He said: Abū Bakr said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Indeed Allah ﷿, when He feeds a prophet a provision, then takes him, makes it for the one who stands after him.” So I saw fit to return it to the Muslims. She said: Then you, and what you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, know best.
items.ma-15:
Ibrāhīm ibn Isḥāq al-Ṭālaqānī narrated to us, he said: Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl al-Māzinī narrated to me, he said: Abū Naʿāmah narrated to me, he said: Abū Hunaydah al-Barāʾ ibn Nawfal narrated to me, from Wālān al-ʿAdawī, from Ḥudhayfah, from Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq ﵁, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose one day and prayed the morning prayer, then sat, until, when it was forenoon, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed. Then he sat in his place until he prayed the first [prayer], and the ʿAṣr and the Maghrib, all that time not speaking, until he prayed the last ʿishāʾ, then rose to his family. The people said to Abū Bakr: Will you not ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what is the matter with him? He did today something he has never done. He said: So he asked him, and he said:
“Yes. There was presented to me what is going to be of the affair of this world and the affair of the Hereafter. The first and the last were gathered on one plain, and the people were terrified by that, until they went to Ādam ﵇, with the sweat almost bridling them. They said: O Ādam, you are the father of mankind, and Allah ﷿ chose you; intercede for us with your Rabb. He said: I have met with the like of what you have met. Go to your father after your father, to Nūḥ: {Indeed Allah chose Ādam and Nūḥ and the family of Ibrāhīm and the family of ʿImrān over the worlds} [Āl ʿImrān: 33]. He said: So they go to Nūḥ ﵇ and say: Intercede for us with your Rabb, for Allah chose you, and answered you in your supplication, and did not leave upon the earth any inhabitant of the disbelievers. He says: That is not with me. Go to Ibrāhīm ﵇, for Allah ﷿ took him as a khalīl. So they go to Ibrāhīm, and he says: That is not with me, but go to Mūsā ﵇, for Allah ﷿ spoke to him directly. Then Mūsā ﵇ says: That is not with me, but go to ʿĪsā ibn Maryam, for he heals the one blind from birth and the leper, and gives life to the dead. Then ʿĪsā ﵇ says: That is not with me, but go to the master of the children of Ādam, for he is the first from whom the earth will split open on the Day of Resurrection. Go to Muḥammad ﷺ, and he will intercede for you with your Rabb ﷿.
He said: So he goes, and Jibrīl ﵇ comes to his Rabb, and Allah ﷿ says: Permit him, and give him glad tidings of Paradise. He said: Then Jibrīl goes with him, and he falls prostrate for the length of a week, and Allah ﷿ says: Raise your head, O Muḥammad, speak and you will be heard, and intercede and your intercession will be accepted. He said: So he raises his head, and when he looks at his Rabb ﷿, he falls prostrate for the length of another week. Then Allah ﷿ says: Raise your head, speak and you will be heard, and intercede and your intercession will be accepted. He said: Then he goes to fall prostrate, and Jibrīl ﵇ takes him by his upper arms, and Allah ﷿ opens for him of supplication something He has never opened for any human. Then he says: O my Rabb, You created me the master of the children of Ādam, and no boast; and the first from whom the earth will split open on the Day of Resurrection, and no boast; until there come to me at the Ḥawḍ more than what is between Ṣanʿāʾ and Aylah. Then it is said: Call the ṣiddīqūn, and they intercede. Then it is said: Call the prophets. He said: So there comes a prophet with a band, and a prophet with five and six, and a prophet with no one. Then it is said: Call the shuhadāʾ, and they intercede for whom they wish. He said: When the shuhadāʾ have done that, he said: Allah ﷿ says: I am Arḥam al-Rāḥimīn; enter into My Paradise whoever did not associate anything with Me. He said: So they enter Paradise.
He said: Then Allah ﷿ says: Look into the Fire: do you find anyone who ever did any good? He said: So they find in the Fire a man, and He says to him: Did you ever do any good? He says: No, except that I used to be lenient with people in sale. Then Allah ﷿ says: Be lenient with My servant as he was lenient to My servants.
Then they bring out of the Fire a man, and He says to him: Did you ever do any good? He says: No, except that I commanded my children: When I die, burn me in the fire, then grind me, until I am like kohl, then take me to the sea and scatter me in the wind. For by Allah, Rabb al-ʿĀlamīn will never have power over me. Allah ﷿ said to him: Why did you do that? He said: Out of fear of You. He said: Then Allah ﷿ says: Look at the kingdom of the greatest king, for you will have the like of it and ten times its like. He said: Then he says: Why do you mock me, when You are al-Malik? He said: And that is what I laughed at in the forenoon.”
items.ma-17: Hāshim narrated to us, he said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: Yazīd ibn Khumayr informed me, he said: I heard Sulaym ibn ʿĀmir – a man from Ḥimyar – narrating from Awsaṭ ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Awsaṭ al-Bajalī, narrating from Abū Bakr: that he heard him, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died, say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood last year in this place of mine – then he wept – then said: “Hold to truthfulness, for it is with birr, and the two are in Paradise; and beware of lying, for it is with fujūr, and the two are in the Fire. And ask Allah for muʿāfāh, for no man has been given, after certainty, anything better than muʿāfāh.” Then he said: “Do not sever ties with one another, do not turn your backs on one another, do not hate one another, do not envy one another, and be brothers, O servants of Allah.”
items.ma-18:
ʿAffān narrated to us, he said: Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Dāwūd ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Awdī, from Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ died while Abū Bakr was in a district of al-Madīnah. He said: So he came and uncovered his face and kissed him, and said: May my father and my mother be a ransom for you; how good you are, alive and dead. Muḥammad ﷺ has died, by the Rabb of the Kaʿbah … then he mentioned the ḥadīth.
He said: Then Abū Bakr and ʿUmar set off, leading one another, until they came to them. Abū Bakr spoke, and he left out nothing that had been revealed concerning the Anṣār, nor anything the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had mentioned of their standing, except that he mentioned it, and said: You know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “If the people took one valley and the Anṣār took another valley, I would take the valley of the Anṣār.” And you know, O Saʿd, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, while you were sitting: “Quraysh are the guardians of this matter: the righteous among the people follow their righteous, and the wicked among them follow their wicked.” He said: Saʿd said to him: You have spoken truly; we are the ministers and you are the commanders.
items.ma-19: ʿAlī ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to us, he said: Al-ʿAṭṭāf ibn Khālid narrated to us, he said: A man from the people of al-Baṣrah narrated to me, from Ṭalḥah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, he said: I heard my father mention that his father heard Abū Bakr say: I said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: O Messenger of Allah, do we act on what has been finished with, or on a matter newly begun? He said: “Rather on a matter that has been finished with.” He said: I said: Then what is the point of action, O Messenger of Allah? He said: “Everyone is made ready for that for which he was created.”
items.ma-20:
Abū al-Yamān narrated to us, he said: Shuʿayb informed us, from al-Zuhrī, he said: A man of the Anṣār, of the people of fiqh, informed me that he heard ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān ﵀ narrating: that men from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, when the Prophet ﷺ died, grieved for him, until some of them nearly succumbed to waswasah. ʿUthmān said: And I was among them. While I was sitting in the shade of one of the fortresses, ʿUmar ﵁ passed by me and greeted me with salām, and I did not notice that he had passed by or greeted. ʿUmar went on until he entered upon Abū Bakr ﵁ and said to him: Does it not amaze you that I passed by ʿUthmān and greeted him, and he did not return the greeting to me? He came, he and Abū Bakr – during the rule of Abū Bakr ﵁ – until they both greeted me. Then Abū Bakr said: Your brother ʿUmar came to me and mentioned that he passed by you and greeted you and you did not return it ﵇ – what made you do that? He said: I said: I did not do so. ʿUmar said: Yes, by Allah, you did, but it is your ʿubbiyyah, O Banū Umayyah. He said: I said: By Allah, I did not notice that you passed by me or greeted. Abū Bakr said: ʿUthmān has spoken truly, and some matter has preoccupied you from that? I said: Yes. He said: What is it?
Then ʿUthmān ﵁ said: Allah ﷿ took His Prophet ﷺ before we asked him about the deliverance of this matter. Abū Bakr said: I have asked him about that. He said: So I stood up to him and said: May my father and my mother be a ransom for you; you are more deserving of it. Abū Bakr said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, what is the deliverance of this matter? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever accepts from me the word that I presented to my uncle, and he rejected it to me, it is for him deliverance.”
items.ma-21: Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Rabbih narrated to us, he said: Baqiyyah ibn al-Walīd narrated to us, he said: A shaykh of Quraysh narrated to me, from Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywah, from Junādah ibn Abī Umayyah, from Yazīd ibn Abī Sufyān, he said: Abū Bakr ﵁ said, when he sent me to al-Shām: O Yazīd, you have relatives whom you may well favour with authority, and that is what I fear most for you. For the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever is put in charge of anything of the affairs of the Muslims and appoints someone over them out of favouritism, upon him is the curse of Allah; Allah will not accept from him any ṣarf or ʿadl until He enters him into Jahannam. And whoever gives anyone the ḥimā of Allah has violated something of the ḥimā of Allah without right, and upon him is the curse of Allah” – or he said: “the dhimmah of Allah ﷿ is free of him.”
items.ma-22: Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim narrated to us, he said: Al-Masʿūdī narrated to us, he said: Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas narrated to me, from a man, from Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I was given seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without reckoning, their faces like the moon on the night of the full moon, and their hearts upon the heart of one man. So I asked my Rabb ﷿ for more, and He increased me by seventy thousand with each one.” Abū Bakr ﵁ said: So I saw that that would come upon the people of the villages, and strike those at the edges of the deserts.
items.ma-23: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn ʿAṭāʾ narrated to us, from Ziyād al-Jaṣṣāṣ, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿUmar, he said: I heard Abū Bakr say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it in this world.”
items.ma-24: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ, he said: Ibn Shihāb said: A man of the Anṣār, not suspected, informed me that he heard ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān narrating: that men from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died, grieved for him, until some of them nearly succumbed to waswasah. ʿUthmān said: And I was among them … then he mentioned the meaning of the ḥadīth of Abū al-Yamān, from Shuʿayb.
items.ma-25:
Yaʿqūb narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ, Ibn Shihāb said: ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, informed him: that Fāṭimah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, asked Abū Bakr, after the death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, to divide for her her inheritance from what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left, of what Allah had granted him as fayʾ. Abū Bakr said to her: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “We are not inherited from; what we leave is ṣadaqah.” Fāṭimah ﵍ became angry, and forsook Abū Bakr ﵁, and she continued to forsake him until she died. He said: And she lived after the death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ six months.
He said: And Fāṭimah ﵂ used to ask Abū Bakr for her share of what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left from Khaybar and Fadak, and his ṣadaqah in al-Madīnah, but Abū Bakr refused her that and said: I will not leave anything that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to act upon except that I act upon it; I fear that if I leave anything of his affair, I will deviate.
As for his ṣadaqah in al-Madīnah, ʿUmar handed it to ʿAlī and ʿAbbās, and ʿAlī prevailed over him concerning it. As for Khaybar and Fadak, ʿUmar ﵁ kept them and said: They are the ṣadaqah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; they were for his rights that befell him, and his needs, and their affair is for whoever is put in charge of the matter. He said: And they are so to this day.
items.ma-26:
Ḥasan ibn Mūsā and ʿAffān narrated to us, both said: Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from ʿĀʾishah: that she quoted this verse while Abū Bakr ﵁ was passing judgment: A fair-faced one, by whose face rain is sought from the clouds … spring of the orphans, protection for the widows.
Then Abū Bakr ﵁ said: By Allah, that is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-27: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, he said: Ibn Jurayj informed me, he said: My father informed me: that the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ did not know where to bury the Prophet ﷺ, until Abū Bakr ﵁ said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “A prophet is never buried except where he dies.” So they moved his bedding aside and dug for him beneath his bedding.
items.ma-28: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, he said: Layth narrated to us, he said: Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb narrated to me, from Abū al-Khayr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, from Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq: that he said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Teach me a supplication to make in my prayer. He said: “Say: O Allah, I have wronged myself with much wrong, and none forgives sins except You; so forgive me with a forgiveness from You, and have mercy on me; indeed You are al-Ghafūr al-Raḥīm.”
items.ma-29: Ḥammād ibn Usāmah narrated to us, he said: Ismāʿīl informed us, from Qays, he said: Abū Bakr stood, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: O people, you recite this verse {O you who believe, upon you are your own selves} – until he reached the end of the verse – Beware! When the people see the wrongdoer and do not take hold of his hands, it is near that Allah will encompass them all with His punishment. Beware! And I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Indeed the people …” And on another occasion he said: And indeed we heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ….
items.ma-30: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us, he said: Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid informed us, from Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim, from Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, he said: O people, you recite this verse {O you who believe, upon you are your own selves; he who has gone astray will not harm you when you are guided}. And I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Indeed, when the people see the wrongdoer and do not take hold of his hands, it is near that Allah will encompass them all with His punishment.”
items.ma-31: Yazīd narrated to us, he said: Hammām informed us, from Farqad al-Sabakhī. And ʿAffān, he said: Hammām narrated to us, he said: Farqad informed us, from Murrah al-Ṭayyib, from Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “One who treats badly those he owns shall not enter Paradise.”
items.ma-32: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us, Ṣadaqah ibn Mūsā informed us, from Farqad al-Sabakhī, from Murrah al-Ṭayyib, from Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq ﵁, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “There shall not enter Paradise a deceiver, nor a miser, nor one who reminds others of his favours, nor one who treats badly those he owns. And the first to enter Paradise is the slave, when he obeys Allah and obeys his master.”
items.ma-33: Rawḥ narrated to us, he said: Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūbah narrated to us, from Abū al-Tayyāḥ, from al-Mughīrah ibn Subayʿ, from ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth: that Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq ﵁ recovered from an illness of his, and went out to the people, and excused himself for something, and said: We intended only good. Then he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ narrated to us: “The Dajjāl will emerge from a land in the east called Khurāsān; peoples will follow him whose faces are like hammered shields.”
items.ma-34: Rawḥ narrated to us, he said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn Khumayr, he said: I heard Sulaym ibn ʿĀmir – a man of the people of Ḥimṣ, who had met the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, and once he said: he said – I heard Awsaṭ al-Bajalī, from Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, he said: I heard him addressing the people – and once he said: when he was made caliph – and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood last year in this place of mine – and Abū Bakr ﵁ wept – and said: “I ask Allah for pardon and ʿāfiyah, for the people have not been given, after certainty, anything better than ʿāfiyah. And hold to truthfulness, for it is in Paradise; and beware of lying, for it is with fujūr, and the two are in the Fire. And do not sever ties with one another, do not hate one another, do not envy one another, do not turn your backs on one another, and be brothers, as Allah ﷿ has commanded you.”
items.ma-35: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, he said: Abū Bakr – meaning Ibn ʿAyyāsh – narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr, from ʿAbd Allāh: that Abū Bakr and ʿUmar gave him glad tidings that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever is pleased to recite the Qurʾān fresh, as it was sent down, let him recite it according to the recitation of Ibn Umm ʿAbd.”
items.ma-36:
Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Abū Bakr and Yazīd ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of it.
He said: fresh or moist.
items.ma-37: Abū Saʿīd, the mawlā of Banū Hāshim, narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muḥammad and Saʿīd ibn Salamah ibn Abī al-Ḥusām narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Abī ʿAmr, from Abū al-Ḥuwayrith, from Muḥammad ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, that ʿUthmān said: I wished that I had asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: What will save us from what Shayṭān casts into our selves? Abū Bakr said: I have asked him about that, and he said: “What saves you from that is that you say what I commanded my uncle to say, which he did not say.”
items.ma-38: Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, from Yūnus, from al-Ḥasan, that Abū Bakr addressed the people and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O people, the people have not been given in this world anything better than certainty and muʿāfāh, so ask Allah ﷿ for them.”
items.ma-39: Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, he said: And Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to me, from ʿIkrimah, the mawlā of Ibn ʿAbbās, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When they wanted to dig for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ – and Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ used to dig a ḍarīḥ, like the digging of the people of Makkah, and Abū Ṭalḥah Zayd ibn Sahl used to dig for the people of al-Madīnah, and he used to dig a laḥd – ʿAbbās called two men, and said to one of them: Go to Abū ʿUbaydah, and to the other: Go to Abū Ṭalḥah. O Allah, choose well for Your Messenger. He said: The one sent to Abū Ṭalḥah found Abū Ṭalḥah and brought him, and he dug a laḥd for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-40:
Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, ʿUmar ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, ʿUqbah ibn al-Ḥārith informed me, he said: I went out with Abū Bakr ﵁ from the ʿAṣr prayer some nights after the death of the Prophet ﷺ, with ʿAlī ﵇ walking beside him. He passed by al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī playing with some boys, and lifted him onto his neck, saying:
By my father, the likeness of the Prophet … not a likeness of ʿAlī.
He said: And ʿAlī was laughing.
items.ma-41: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Jābir, from ʿĀmir, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abzā, from Abū Bakr, he said: I was sitting with the Prophet ﷺ, and Māʿiz ibn Mālik came and confessed to him once, and he sent him back; then he came to him and confessed a second time, and he sent him back; then he came to him and confessed a third time, and he sent him back. So I said to him: If you confess a fourth time, he will stone you. He said: So he confessed a fourth time, and he detained him, then asked about him, and they said: We know only good. He said: So he commanded his stoning.
items.ma-42: ʿAlī ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to us, al-Walīd ibn Muslim narrated to us, he said: And Yazīd ibn Saʿīd ibn Dhī ʿAṣwān al-ʿAnsī informed me, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr al-Lakhmī, from Rāfiʿ al-Ṭāʾī, the companion of Abū Bakr on the expedition of al-Salāsil, he said: And I asked him about what was said concerning their pledge of allegiance, and he said – while narrating to him what the Anṣār had said, and what he said to them, and what ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said to the Anṣār, and what he reminded them of concerning my leading them in prayer by the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in his illness –: So they pledged allegiance to me for that, and I accepted it from them, and I feared that there would be a fitnah, and after it an apostasy.
items.ma-43: ʿAlī ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to us, al-Walīd ibn Muslim narrated to us, Waḥshī ibn Ḥarb ibn Waḥshī ibn Ḥarb narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather Waḥshī ibn Ḥarb: that Abū Bakr ﵁ gave Khālid ibn al-Walīd the banner to fight the people of apostasy, and said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “What an excellent servant of Allah, and brother of the clan, is Khālid ibn al-Walīd, and a sword from among the swords of Allah, which Allah ﷿ has drawn against the disbelievers and the hypocrites.”
items.ma-44: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, Muʿāwiyah – meaning Ibn Ṣāliḥ – narrated to us, from Sulaym ibn ʿĀmir al-Kalāʿī, from Awsaṭ ibn ʿAmr, he said: I came to al-Madīnah a year after the death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and found Abū Bakr addressing the people. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among us last year, and tears choked him three times. Then he said: “O people, ask Allah for muʿāfāh, for no one has been given the like of certainty after muʿāfāh, nor anything more severe than doubt after disbelief. Hold to truthfulness, for it guides to birr, and the two are in Paradise; and beware of lying, for it guides to fujūr, and the two are in the Fire.”
items.ma-45: Muḥammad ibn Muyassar Abū Saʿd al-Ṣāghānī, the blind, narrated to us, Hishām ibn ʿUrwah narrated to us, from his father, from ʿĀʾishah, she said: When death came to Abū Bakr, he said: What day is this? They said: Monday. He said: If I die tonight, do not wait with me for tomorrow, for the dearest of days and nights to me is the nearest of them to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-46: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, ʿAmr ibn Murrah narrated to us, from Abū ʿUbaydah, he said: Abū Bakr stood a year after the death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood in my place last year and said: “Ask Allah for ʿāfiyah, for no servant has been given anything better than ʿāfiyah. Hold to truthfulness and birr, for the two are in Paradise; and beware of lying and fujūr, for the two are in the Fire.”
items.ma-47: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿUthmān ibn al-Mughīrah, he said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Rabīʿah, of Banū Asad, narrating from Asmāʾ or Ibn Asmāʾ of Banū Fazārah, he said: ʿAlī ﵁ said: Whenever I heard something from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Allah benefited me by it as much as He willed to benefit me from it. And Abū Bakr narrated to me – and Abū Bakr spoke truly – he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no Muslim who commits a sin, then performs ablution and prays two rakʿahs, then seeks forgiveness from Allah for that sin, except that He forgives him.” And he recited these two verses: {And whoever does evil or wrongs himself, then seeks forgiveness of Allah, will find Allah Ghafūr, Raḥīm} [al-Nisāʾ: 110], {and those who, when they commit an indecency or wrong themselves} [Āl ʿImrān: 135].
items.ma-48: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: I heard ʿUthmān, of the family of Abū ʿAqīl al-Thaqafī … except that he said: Shuʿbah said: And he recited one of these two verses: {Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it} [al-Nisāʾ: 123], {and those who, when they commit an indecency}.
items.ma-49:
Bahz ibn Asad narrated to us, Salīm ibn Ḥayyān narrated to us, he said: I heard Qatādah narrating, from Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, that ʿUmar said:
Abū Bakr addressed us and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among us the year before and said: “Beware! Nothing has been apportioned among the people that is better than muʿāfāh after certainty. Beware! Truthfulness and birr are in Paradise. Beware! Lying and fujūr are in the Fire.”
items.ma-50: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: I heard Abū Isḥāq say: I heard al-Barāʾ say: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was coming from Makkah to al-Madīnah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ became thirsty, and they passed by a shepherd of sheep. Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq said: So I took a cup and milked into it for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a small quantity of milk, and brought it to him, and he drank until I was content.
items.ma-51: Bahz narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, Yaʿlā ibn ʿAṭāʾ informed me, he said: I heard ʿAmr ibn ʿĀṣim say: I heard Abū Hurayrah say: Abū Bakr said: O Messenger of Allah, teach me something to say when I rise in the morning, when I enter the evening, and when I take to my bed. He said: “Say: O Allah, Fāṭir of the heavens and the earth, ʿĀlim of the unseen and the witnessed – or he said: O Allah, ʿĀlim of the unseen and the witnessed, Fāṭir of the heavens and the earth – Rabb of everything and its Malīk, I bear witness that there is no deity except You; I seek refuge in You from the evil of my self, and from the evil of Shayṭān and his shirk.”
items.ma-52: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Yaʿlā ibn ʿAṭāʾ, he said: I heard ʿAmr ibn ʿĀṣim ibn ʿAbd Allāh … then he mentioned its meaning.
