items.ma-53: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl, he said: I heard Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim narrating from Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq: that he addressed the people and said: O people, you recite this verse and you place it other than where Allah placed it: {O you who believe, upon you are your own selves; he who has gone astray will not harm you when you are guided}. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Indeed, when the people see the munkar among them and do not deny it, it is near that Allah will encompass them all with punishment.”
items.ma-54: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Tawbah al-ʿAnbarī, he said: I heard Abū Sawwār the judge say: from Abū Barzah al-Aslamī, he said: A man spoke harshly to Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq. He said: Abū Barzah said: Shall I not strike his neck? So he rebuked him and said: It is not for anyone after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-55:
Ḥajjāj ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, ʿUqayl narrated to me, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, that she informed him: that Fāṭimah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, sent to Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq ﵁, asking him for her inheritance from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, of what Allah had granted him as fayʾ in al-Madīnah and Fadak, and what remained of the khumus of Khaybar. Abū Bakr said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “We are not inherited from; what we leave is ṣadaqah. The family of Muḥammad only eat from this property.” And by Allah, I will not change anything of the ṣadaqah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from the state it was in during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I will act concerning it as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ acted.
So Abū Bakr refused to give Fāṭimah anything of it, and Fāṭimah felt resentment toward Abū Bakr over that. And Abū Bakr said: By Him in Whose Yad is my soul, the kin of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ are dearer to me to keep ties with than my own kin. As for what has arisen between me and you concerning these properties, I have not fallen short in it from the truth, and I have not left any matter that I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ doing concerning it except that I did it.
items.ma-56: Abū Kāmil narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, ʿUthmān ibn Abī Zurʿah narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Rabīʿah, from Asmāʾ ibn al-Ḥakam al-Fazārī, he said: I heard ʿAlī say: Whenever I heard a ḥadīth from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Allah benefited me by it as much as He willed to benefit me from it; and when someone other than me narrated to me, I made him swear an oath, and when he swore to me I believed him. And Abū Bakr narrated to me – and Abū Bakr spoke truly – he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no believing servant who commits a sin, then performs ablution and perfects the purification, then prays two rakʿahs and seeks forgiveness from Allah, except that Allah forgives him.” Then he recited: {and those who, when they commit an indecency or wrong themselves}.
items.ma-57: Abū Kāmil narrated to us, Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd narrated to us, Ibn Shihāb narrated to us, from ʿUbayd ibn al-Sabbāq, from Zayd ibn Thābit, he said: Abū Bakr ﵁ sent for me after the killing of the people of al-Yamāmah, and Abū Bakr said: O Zayd ibn Thābit, you are a young man, intelligent; we do not suspect you. You used to write the revelation for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so seek out the Qurʾān and collect it.
items.ma-58: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwah, from ʿĀʾishah: that Fāṭimah and al-ʿAbbās came to Abū Bakr, seeking their inheritance from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they were at that time asking for his land at Fadak and his share at Khaybar. Abū Bakr said to them both: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “We are not inherited from; what we leave is ṣadaqah, and the family of Muḥammad ﷺ only eat from this property.” And by Allah, I will not leave any matter that I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ doing concerning it except that I do it.
items.ma-59: Mūsā ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, Nāfiʿ – meaning Ibn ʿUmar – narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, he said: It was said to Abū Bakr: O Khalīfat Allāh. He said: I am the khalīfah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I am content with it.
items.ma-60: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr, from Abū Salamah, that Fāṭimah said to Abū Bakr: Who will inherit from you when you die? He said: My children and my family. She said: Then why do we not inherit from the Prophet ﷺ? He said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “The Prophet is not inherited from”; but I support those whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to support, and I spend on those on whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to spend.
items.ma-61: ʿAffān narrated to us, Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, from Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muṭarrif ibn al-Shikhkhīr, that he narrated to them from Abū Barzah al-Aslamī, that he said: We were with Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq in his work, and he became angry with a man of the Muslims, and his anger against him grew very intense. When I saw that, I said: O Khalīfah of the Messenger of Allah, shall I strike his neck? When I mentioned killing, he turned away from that whole conversation to something else of its kind. When we dispersed, Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq sent for me after that and said: O Abū Barzah, what did you say? He said: And I had forgotten what I had said. I said: Remind me. He said: Do you not remember what you said? I said: No, by Allah. He said: Do you not recall when you saw me angry with the man and you said: Shall I strike his neck, O Khalīfah of the Messenger of Allah? Do you not remember that? Would you have done that? I said: Yes, by Allah; and now, if you command me, I will do it. He said: Alas for you – or: Woe to you – by Allah, that is not for anyone after Muḥammad ﷺ.
items.ma-62: ʿAffān narrated to us, he said: Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abī ʿAtīq narrated to us, from his father, he said: Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq ﵁ said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The siwāk is a purifier for the mouth, [a means of] Riḍā for the Rabb.”
items.ma-63: ʿAffān narrated to us, he said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Yaʿlā ibn ʿAṭāʾ, he said: I heard ʿAmr ibn ʿĀṣim ibn ʿAbd Allāh say: I heard Abū Hurayrah say: Abū Bakr said: O Messenger of Allah, tell me something to say when I rise in the morning and when I enter the evening. He said: “Say: O Allah, ʿĀlim of the unseen and the witnessed, Fāṭir of the heavens and the earth, Rabb of everything and its Malīk, I bear witness that there is no deity except You; I seek refuge in You from the evil of my self, and from the evil of Shayṭān and his shirk.” And he commanded him to say it when he rose in the morning and when he entered the evening, and when he took to his bed.
items.ma-64: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd narrated to us, Nāfiʿ ibn ʿUmar al-Jumaḥī narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Mulaykah, he said: It was said to Abū Bakr: O Khalīfat Allāh. He said: No, rather the khalīfah of Muḥammad ﷺ, and I am content with it.
items.ma-65: Mūsā ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Muʾammal narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, he said: Sometimes the rein would fall from the hand of Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq ﵁. He said: Then he would strike the foreleg of his she-camel and make her kneel, and take it. He said: They said to him: Why did you not command us to hand it to you? He said: My beloved, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, commanded me not to ask people for anything.
items.ma-66: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Abū ʿUbaydah – from Abū Bakr – he said: Abū Bakr stood a year after the death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among us last year and said: “The son of Ādam has not been given anything better than ʿāfiyah, so ask Allah for ʿāfiyah. Hold to truthfulness and birr, for the two are in Paradise; and beware of lying and fujūr, for the two are in the Fire.”
items.ma-67:
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd narrated to us, he said: Sufyān ibn Ḥusayn informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah ibn Masʿūd, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “I was commanded to fight the people until they say: There is no deity except Allah. When they say it, they protect from me their blood and their wealth, except by its right, and their reckoning is upon Allah.”
He said: When the apostasy came, ʿUmar said to Abū Bakr: Will you fight them, when you have heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say such and such? Abū Bakr ﵁ said: By Allah, I will not separate between the ṣalāh and the zakāh, and I will surely fight whoever separates between them. He said: So we fought with him, and we saw that as right guidance.
items.ma-68: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr narrated to us, he said: Ismāʿīl informed us, from Abū Bakr ibn Abī Zuhayr, he said: I was informed that Abū Bakr said: O Messenger of Allah, how can there be any good after this verse: {It is not by your wishes, nor the wishes of the People of the Book; whoever does evil will be recompensed for it} [al-Nisāʾ: 123] – so every evil we do, we are recompensed for it? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “May Allah forgive you, O Abū Bakr. Do you not fall ill? Do you not become weary? Do you not grieve? Do you not suffer hardship?” He said: Yes indeed. He said: “Then that is what you are recompensed with.”
items.ma-69: Sufyān narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abī Khālid narrated to us, from Abū Bakr ibn Abī Zuhayr – I think he said: Abū Bakr said –: O Messenger of Allah, how can there be any good after this verse? He said: “May Allah have mercy on you, O Abū Bakr. Do you not fall ill? Do you not grieve? Do you not suffer hardship? Do you not …” He said: Yes indeed. He said: “Then that is for that.”
items.ma-70: Yaʿlā ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, Ismāʿīl narrated to us, from Abū Bakr al-Thaqafī, he said: Abū Bakr said: O Messenger of Allah, how can there be any good after this verse: {Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it}? Then he mentioned the ḥadīth.
items.ma-71: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Ibn Abī Khālid narrated to us, from Abū Bakr ibn Abī Zuhayr al-Thaqafī, he said: When {It is not by your wishes, nor the wishes of the People of the Book; whoever does evil will be recompensed for it} was revealed, Abū Bakr said: O Messenger of Allah, are we really recompensed for every evil we do? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “May Allah have mercy on you, O Abū Bakr. Do you not become weary? Do you not grieve? Do you not suffer hardship? That is what you are recompensed with.”
items.ma-72:
Abū Kāmil narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, he said: I took this document from Thumāmah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Anas, from Anas ibn Mālik: that Abū Bakr wrote for them: Indeed these are the farāʾiḍ of ṣadaqah which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made obligatory upon the Muslims, which Allah ﷿ commanded His Messenger ﷺ with. Whoever among the Muslims is asked for it in its proper manner, let him give it; and whoever is asked for more than that, let him not give it:
In what is less than twenty-five camels, in every five dhawd is a sheep. When it reaches twenty-five, in it is an ibnat makhāḍ, until thirty-five; if there is no ibnat makhāḍ, then a male ibn labūn. When it reaches thirty-six, in it is an ibnat labūn, until forty-five. When it reaches forty-six, in it is a ḥiqqah ṭarūqat al-faḥl, until sixty. When it reaches sixty-one, in it is a jadhaʿah, until seventy-five. When it reaches seventy-six, in it are two bintā labūn, until ninety. When it reaches ninety-one, in it are two ḥiqqatān ṭarūqatā al-faḥl, until one hundred and twenty. If it exceeds one hundred and twenty, then in every forty is an ibnat labūn, and in every fifty a ḥiqqah. When the ages of the camels differ in the farāʾiḍ of the ṣadaqāt: whoever has reached the ṣadaqah of a jadhaʿah and has no jadhaʿah but has a ḥiqqah, it is accepted from him, and he adds with it two sheep, if they are easy for him, or twenty dirhams.
And whoever has reached the ṣadaqah of a ḥiqqah and has none but a jadhaʿah, it is accepted from him, and the muṣaddiq gives him twenty dirhams or two sheep; and whoever has reached the ṣadaqah of a ḥiqqah and does not have it but has an ibnat labūn, it is accepted from him, and he adds with it two sheep, if they are easy for him, or twenty dirhams.
And whoever has reached the ṣadaqah of an ibnat labūn and has none but a ḥiqqah, it is accepted from him, and the muṣaddiq gives him twenty dirhams or two sheep; and whoever has reached the ṣadaqah of an ibnat labūn and does not have an ibnat labūn but has an ibnat makhāḍ, it is accepted from him, and he adds with it two sheep, if they are easy for him, or twenty dirhams.
And whoever's ṣadaqah reaches an ibnat makhāḍ and he has only a male ibn labūn, it is accepted from him and nothing accompanies it. And whoever has only four camels, there is nothing in them unless their owner wishes.
And in the ṣadaqah of sheep, in their grazing herds, when they are forty, in them is a sheep, until one hundred and twenty; if it exceeds, in them are two sheep, until two hundred; if it exceeds by one, in them are three sheep, until three hundred; if it exceeds, then in every hundred a sheep. And there is not taken in ṣadaqah an aged one, nor one with a defect, nor a billy goat, unless the one giving the ṣadaqah wishes. And what is separate is not gathered together, and what is gathered together is not separated, for fear of the ṣadaqah. And what belongs to two khalīṭayn, they settle accounts between them equally. And if a man's grazing herd is short of forty sheep by one, there is nothing in it unless its owner wishes.
And in the raqqah is a quarter of a tenth; if the wealth is only one hundred and ninety dirhams, there is nothing in it unless its owner wishes.
items.ma-73: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, he said: The people of Makkah say: Ibn Jurayj took the prayer from ʿAṭāʾ, and ʿAṭāʾ took it from Ibn al-Zubayr, and Ibn al-Zubayr took it from Abū Bakr, and Abū Bakr took it from the Prophet ﷺ. I have not seen anyone pray better than Ibn Jurayj.
items.ma-74: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, he said: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from Ibn ʿUmar, from ʿUmar, he said: Ḥafṣah bint ʿUmar was widowed from Khunays ibn Ḥudhāfah or Ḥudhayfah – ʿAbd al-Razzāq doubted – who was among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, of those who witnessed Badr, and he died in al-Madīnah. He said: I met ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān and offered Ḥafṣah to him, saying: If you wish, I will marry you to Ḥafṣah. He said: I will consider that. I waited some nights, and he met me and said: I do not wish to marry on this day of mine. ʿUmar said: Then I met Abū Bakr and said: If you wish, I will marry you to Ḥafṣah daughter of ʿUmar. But he gave me no reply, and I was more resentful toward him than toward ʿUthmān. I waited some nights, then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ proposed to her to me, and I married her to him. Then Abū Bakr met me and said: Perhaps you felt resentment toward me when you offered me Ḥafṣah and I gave you no reply? He said: I said: Yes. He said: Nothing prevented me from replying to you when you offered her to me except that I had heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mention her, and I was not one to disclose the secret of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; had he left her, I would have married her.
items.ma-75: Isḥāq ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Mughīrah ibn Muslim Abū Salamah, from Farqad al-Sabakhī, from Murrah al-Ṭayyib, from Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “One who treats badly those he owns shall not enter Paradise.” A man said: O Messenger of Allah, did you not inform us that this ummah has the most slaves and orphans of all the nations? He said: “Yes indeed; so honour them as you honour your children, and feed them from what you eat.” They said: Then what benefits us in this world, O Messenger of Allah? He said: “A good horse that you tie up and fight upon in the path of Allah, and your slave who suffices you; and when he prays, he is your brother; when he prays, he is your brother.”
items.ma-76:
ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, he said: Yūnus informed us, from al-Zuhrī, he said: Ibn al-Sabbāq informed me, he said: Zayd ibn Thābit informed me: that Abū Bakr sent for him after the killing of the people of al-Yamāmah, and ʿUmar was with him. Abū Bakr said: ʿUmar came to me and said: Killing has become intense among the people of al-Yamāmah, among the reciters of the Qurʾān of the Muslims, and I fear that killing will become intense among the reciters in the various places, so that much of the Qurʾān will go and not be preserved. And I think that you should command that the Qurʾān be collected. I said to ʿUmar: How can I do something the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not do? He said: By Allah, it is good. He kept returning to me about that until Allah opened my chest for it, and I saw in it what ʿUmar saw. Zayd said: And ʿUmar was sitting with him, not speaking.
Abū Bakr said: You are an intelligent young man, we do not suspect you, and you used to write the revelation for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so collect it. Zayd said: By Allah, had they charged me with moving one of the mountains, it would not have been heavier on me than what he commanded me concerning the collecting of the Qurʾān. I said: How can you do something the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not do?
items.ma-77: Yaḥyā ibn Ḥammād narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ismāʿīl ibn Rajāʾ, from ʿUmayr, the mawlā of al-ʿAbbās, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken, and Abū Bakr was made khalīfah, al-ʿAbbās disputed with ʿAlī over things that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had left. Abū Bakr said: Something the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left and did not move, I will not move. When ʿUmar was made khalīfah, they brought their dispute to him, and he said: Something Abū Bakr did not move, I will not move. He said: When ʿUthmān was made khalīfah, they brought their dispute to him. He said: ʿUthmān fell silent and bowed his head. Ibn ʿAbbās said: I feared that he would take it, so I struck my hand between the shoulders of al-ʿAbbās and said: O my father, I adjure you to hand it over to ʿAlī. He said: So he handed it over to him.
items.ma-78:
Yaḥyā ibn Ḥammād narrated to us, he said: Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Kulayb, he said: A shaykh of Quraysh from Banū Taym narrated to me, he said: So-and-so, and so-and-so, and so-and-so narrated to me – he counted six or seven, all of them of Quraysh, among them ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr – he said: While we were sitting with ʿUmar, ʿAlī and al-ʿAbbās entered, their voices raised. ʿUmar said: Stop, O ʿAbbās! I know what you say: you say, “My brother's son, and I have half of the property.” And I know what you say, O ʿAlī: you say, “His daughter is with me, and she has half of the property.” And this is what was in the hands of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we saw how he used to act with it. Abū Bakr took charge of it after him and acted with it according to the practice of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then I took charge of it after Abū Bakr, and I swear by Allah that I will strive to act with it according to the practice of the Messenger of Allah and the practice of Abū Bakr.
Then he said: Abū Bakr narrated to me – and he swore by Allah that he was truthful – that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “The Prophet is not inherited from; his inheritance is only for the poor of the Muslims and the needy.” And Abū Bakr narrated to me – and he swore by Allah that he was truthful – that the Prophet ﷺ said: “A prophet does not die until some of his ummah lead him in prayer.”
And this is what was in the hands of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we saw how he used to act with it. If you both wish, I will give it to you so that you act with it according to the practice of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the practice of Abū Bakr, until I hand it over to you. He said: So they withdrew in private, then came, and al-ʿAbbās said: Hand it to ʿAlī, for I am content in my soul with it for him.
items.ma-79: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb ibn ʿAṭāʾ narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr informed us, from Abū Salamah, from Abū Hurayrah: that Fāṭimah ﵂ came to Abū Bakr and ʿUmar ﵄, seeking her inheritance from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they said: We heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “I am not inherited from.”
items.ma-80: Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim narrated to us, he said: ʿĪsā – meaning Ibn al-Musayyab – narrated to us, from Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim, he said: I was sitting with Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, the khalīfah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, a month after the death of the Prophet ﷺ – then he mentioned an account – and it was called out among the people: Al-ṣalāh jāmiʿah! And it was the first prayer among the Muslims for which it was called: Al-ṣalāh jāmiʿah! So the people gathered, and he ascended the minbar – something that had been made for him, upon which he used to give the khuṭbah – and it was the first khuṭbah he gave in Islam. He said: He praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: O people, I would have liked that someone other than me had spared me this. And if you hold me to the sunnah of your Prophet ﷺ, I cannot bear it: he was protected from Shayṭān, and revelation used to descend upon him from the heaven.
items.ma-81: Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim narrated to us, Shaybān narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujāhid, he said: Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me to say, when I rise in the morning, when I enter the evening, and when I take to my bed at night: “O Allah, Fāṭir of the heavens and the earth, ʿĀlim of the unseen and the witnessed, You are Rabb of everything and its Malīk. I bear witness that there is no deity except You alone, no partner for You, and that Muḥammad is Your servant and Your Messenger. I seek refuge in You from the evil of my self, and the evil of Shayṭān and his shirk, and from committing any evil against myself or dragging it to a Muslim.”
items.ma-82: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Abū Isḥāq, from Ḥārithah, he said: Some people from the people of al-Shām came to ʿUmar and said: We have acquired wealth, horses and slaves, and we would like to have zakāh and purification in them. He said: What my two companions before me did not do, I will not do. And he consulted the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ, among them ʿAlī, and ʿAlī said: It is good, as long as it is not a fixed jizyah that is taken from them after you.
items.ma-83:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, he said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Abū Wāʾil: that al-Ṣubayy ibn Maʿbad was a Christian of Taghlib, a bedouin, and he accepted Islam, and asked: Which deed is best? He was told: Jihād in the path of Allah ﷿. So he wished to fight in jihād, and it was said to him: Have you performed Ḥajj? He said: No. It was said: Perform Ḥajj and ʿumrah, then fight in jihād. So he set off, until, when he was at al-Ḥawāʾiṭ, he raised the talbiyah for both together. Zayd ibn Ṣūḥān and Salmān ibn Rabīʿah saw him and said: He is more astray than his camel – or: He is no better guided than his she-camel. So he went to ʿUmar ﵁ and told him what they had said, and he said: You have been guided to the sunnah of your Prophet ﷺ.
Al-Ḥakam said: I said to Abū Wāʾil: Did al-Ṣubayy narrate that to you? He said: Yes.
items.ma-84: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, he said: I heard ʿAmr ibn Maymūn say: ʿUmar prayed the Ṣubḥ with us at Jamʿ, then stood and said: The polytheists would not depart until the sun rose, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ opposed them; then he departed before the sun rose.
items.ma-85: ʿAffān narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ziyād narrated to us, he said: ʿĀṣim ibn Kulayb narrated to us, he said: My father said: I narrated it to Ibn ʿAbbās, and he said: And what amazed you about that? When ʿUmar ﵁ called the elders of the Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ, he would call me with them, and he said: Do not speak until they speak. He said: He called us one day, or one night, and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said about Laylat al-Qadr what you know, so seek it in the last ten, in the odd nights. In which of the odd nights do you see it?
items.ma-86: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: I heard ʿĀṣim ibn ʿAmr al-Bajalī narrating from a man of the group who asked ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and they said to him: We only came to you to ask you about three things: about a man's voluntary prayer in his house, about the ghusl from janābah, and about what is permissible for a man with his wife when she is menstruating. He said: Are you sorcerers?! You have asked me about something no one has asked me since I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about it. He said: “A man's voluntary prayer in his house is a light, so whoever wishes, let him light his house.” And about the ghusl from janābah he said: “He washes his private part, then performs ablution, then pours water over his head three times.” And about the menstruating woman he said: “He may have what is above the izār.”
items.ma-87: Qutaybah ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, from Abū al-Naḍr, from Abū Salamah, from Ibn ʿUmar, that he said: I saw Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ wiping over his khuffs in Iraq when he performed ablution, and I denounced that to him. He said: When we gathered with ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, he said to me: Ask your father about what you denounced to me concerning wiping over the khuffs. He said: So I mentioned that to him, and he said: When Saʿd narrates something to you, do not reject it, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to wipe over the khuffs.
items.ma-88: Hārūn ibn Maʿrūf narrated to us, he said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith, from Abū al-Naḍr, from Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: that he wiped over the khuffs; and that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar asked ʿUmar about that, and he said: Yes. When Saʿd narrates something to you from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, do not ask anyone else about it.
items.ma-89:
ʿAffān narrated to us, Hammām ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, he said: Qatādah narrated to us, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd al-Ghaṭafānī, from Maʿdān ibn Abī Ṭalḥah al-Yaʿmarī: that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb stood upon the minbar on the day of Jumuʿah, praised Allah and extolled Him, then mentioned the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned Abū Bakr, then said: I saw a dream which I consider to be only for the arrival of my appointed time: I saw as if a rooster pecked me two pecks. He said: And it was mentioned to me that it was a red rooster. So I related it to Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays, the wife of Abū Bakr ﵄, and she said: A man of the ʿAjam will kill you. He said: And the people command me to appoint a successor, but Allah would not let His religion go to waste, nor His khilāfah with which He sent His Prophet ﷺ; and if some matter hastens me away, then the shūrā is among these six with whom the Prophet of Allah ﷺ was pleased when he died. So whomever of them you pledge allegiance to, listen to him and obey. And I know that some people will find fault with this matter; I fought them with this hand of mine for Islam; those are the enemies of Allah, the disbelievers, the astray.
By Allah, of what my Rabb entrusted to me when He made me successor, I leave nothing more important to me than the kalālah. By Allah, the Prophet of Allah ﷺ was not as stern with me about anything since I accompanied him as he was stern with me about the kalālah, until he poked his finger into my chest and said: “The verse of the summer suffices you, which was sent down at the end of Sūrat al-Nisāʾ.” And if I live, I will judge concerning it with a judgment that will be known to the one who reads and the one who does not read.
And I call Allah to witness against the governors of the provinces that I only sent them to teach the people their religion, to make clear to them the sunnah of their Prophet ﷺ, and to raise to me what is obscure to them.
Then you, O people, eat from two plants that I consider only foul: this garlic and onion. By Allah, I used to see the Prophet of Allah ﷺ find their smell on a man, so he would command concerning him, and he would be taken by the hand and brought out of the mosque until he was brought to al-Baqīʿ. So whoever must eat them, let him kill them by cooking. He said: So he gave the khuṭbah to the people on the day of Jumuʿah, and he was struck on the day of Wednesday.
items.ma-90:
Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, he said: Nāfiʿ, the mawlā of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, narrated to me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, he said: I went out, together with al-Zubayr and al-Miqdād ibn al-Aswad, to our properties at Khaybar to look after them. When we arrived there, we separated among our properties. He said: I was attacked under the night while I was asleep on my bed, and my hands were dislocated from my elbows. When morning came, a cry for help was raised over me and my two companions came to me, and they asked me: Who did this to you? I said: I do not know. He said: They set my hands right, then they came with me to ʿUmar, and he said: This is the work of the Jews.
Then he stood among the people to give a khuṭbah and said: O people, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dealt with the Jews of Khaybar on the condition that we may expel them whenever we wish. And they attacked ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar and dislocated his hands, as it has reached you, in addition to their attack upon the Anṣārī before him. We have no doubt that they are their companions; we have no enemy there other than them. So whoever has property in Khaybar, let him join it, for I am expelling the Jews. So he expelled them.
items.ma-91: Ḥasan ibn Mūsā and Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, they both said: Shaybān narrated to us, from Yaḥyā, from Abū Salamah, from Abū Hurayrah: that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, while he was giving the khuṭbah on the day of Jumuʿah, a man came. ʿUmar said: Why do you hold yourselves back from the prayer? The man said: It was only that I heard the call and performed ablution. He said: Also?! Did you not hear that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ says: “When one of you goes to the Jumuʿah, let him perform ghusl”?
items.ma-92: Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, he said: Zuhayr narrated to us, he said: ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal narrated to us, from Abū ʿUthmān, he said: The letter of ʿUmar ﵁ came to us while we were in Adharbayjān: O ʿUtbah ibn Farqad, and beware of luxury, of the dress of the people of shirk, and of wearing silk, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade us from wearing silk, and said: “Except thus,” and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his two fingers for us.
items.ma-93: Ḥasan narrated to us, he said: Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, Abū al-Aswad narrated to us, that he heard Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān Ibn Labībah narrating from Abū Sinān al-Du'alī: that he entered upon ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, with whom was a group of the first Muhājirūn. ʿUmar sent for a casket that had been brought from a fortress in Iraq, and in it was a ring. One of his sons took it and put it in his mouth, and ʿUmar pulled it out from him. Then ʿUmar ﵁ wept. Those who were with him said to him: Why do you weep when Allah has opened for you, has made you prevail over your enemy, and has cooled your eye? ʿUmar said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “The world is not opened to anyone but that Allah ﷿ casts enmity and hatred between them until the Day of Resurrection,” and I fear that.
items.ma-94: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, Nāfiʿ narrated to me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, from his father, he said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: How should one of us act if he is in a state of janābah, then wishes to sleep before he performs ghusl? He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Let him perform his ablution for the prayer, then let him sleep.”
items.ma-95:
Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, he said: al-Zuhrī narrated to me, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah ibn Masʿūd, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb say: When ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy died, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was called to pray over him, and he stood toward him. When he stood over him, wanting to pray, I turned until I stood at his chest and said: O Messenger of Allah, over the enemy of Allah, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy, the one who said on such-and-such a day such-and-such – he enumerated his days? He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was smiling, until, when I had said much to him, he said: “Move back from me, O ʿUmar; I was given a choice and I chose. It was said: {Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will never forgive them} [al-Tawbah: 80]. If I knew that were I to exceed seventy he would be forgiven, I would exceed.” He said: Then he prayed over him, walked with him, and stood at his grave until it was finished.
He said: So [it is] a wonder to me, and my boldness toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; and Allah and His Messenger know best. He said: By Allah, it was only a short time until these two verses were revealed: {And never pray over any one of them who has died, ever, and do not stand at his grave; indeed they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger and died while they were defiantly disobedient}. After that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not pray over a hypocrite, nor stand at his grave, until Allah ﷿ took him.
items.ma-96:
Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, as Nāfiʿ, his mawlā, narrated to me from him, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar used to say: If a man has only one garment, let him wrap it around himself as an izār, then pray, for I heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb say that; and he used to say: Do not wrap yourselves in the garment when it is alone, as the Jews do.
Nāfiʿ said: And if I were to say to you that he attributed that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I would hope that I would not have lied.
items.ma-97: Muʾammal narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, he said: Ziyād ibn Mikhrāq narrated to us, from Shahr, from ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir, he said: ʿUmar narrated to me that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever dies believing in Allah and the Last Day, it will be said to him: Enter Paradise from whichever of the eight doors of Paradise you wish.”
items.ma-98: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, he said: Jaʿfar – meaning al-Aḥmar – informed us, from Muṭarrif, from al-Ḥakam, from Mujāhid, he said: A man struck at his son with a sword and killed him, and the matter was brought to ʿUmar, and he said: Had I not heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “A father is not retaliated against for his child,” I would have killed you before you left.
items.ma-99: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, he said: Zuhayr narrated to us, from Sulaymān al-Aʿmash, Ibrāhīm narrated to us, from ʿĀbis ibn Rabīʿah, he said: I saw ʿUmar look at the Stone, and he said: By Allah, had I not seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kissing you, I would not have kissed you. Then he kissed it.
items.ma-100: Abū al-Yamān narrated to us, he said: Shuʿayb informed us, from al-Zuhrī, he said: al-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd, the son of the sister of Namir, informed me that Ḥuwayṭib ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā informed him that ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Saʿdī informed him: that he came to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb in his khilāfah, and ʿUmar said to him: Was I not told that you are in charge of some of the works of the people, and when you are given the wage you dislike it? He said: I said: Indeed. ʿUmar said: What do you want by that? He said: I said: I have horses and slaves, and I am well-off, and I want my wage to be ṣadaqah for the Muslims. ʿUmar said: Do not do so, for I had wanted what you want, and the Prophet ﷺ would give me the grant, and I would say: Give it to one more in need of it than I, until once he gave me wealth and I said: Give it to one more in need of it than I. He said: And the Prophet ﷺ said to him: “Take it, and make it your property, and give it in ṣadaqah; and whatever comes to you of this wealth while you are not eagerly looking out for it nor asking, take it; and what [is] not [so], do not make your soul follow it.”
items.ma-101: Sakan ibn Nāfiʿ al-Bāhilī narrated to us, he said: Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, he said: Rabīʿah ibn Darrāj narrated to me: that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib prayed two rakʿahs of voluntary prayer after the ʿAṣr on the road to Makkah. ʿUmar saw him and became angry with him, then said: By Allah, you certainly knew that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade it.
items.ma-102: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, he said: al-ʿAlāʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yaʿqūb narrated to us, from a man of Quraysh from Banū Sahm, from a man of them called Mājidah, he said: I scuffled with a boy in Makkah, and he bit my ear and cut part of it off – or: I bit his ear and cut part of it off – and when Abū Bakr ﵁ came to us on Ḥajj, we were brought to him, and he said: Take the two of them to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb; if the one who wounded has reached [the point] where retaliation is taken from him, let retaliation be taken. He said: When we were brought to ʿUmar, he looked at us and said: Yes, this one has reached [the point] where retaliation is taken from him. Call a cupper for me. When he mentioned the cupper, he said: Indeed, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “I have given my maternal aunt a boy, and I hope that Allah will bless her in him; and I have forbidden her to make him a cupper, a butcher or a goldsmith.”
items.ma-103: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, he said: and al-ʿAlāʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to me, from a man of Banū Sahm, from Ibn Mājidah al-Sahmī, that he said: Abū Bakr performed Ḥajj [coming] to us in his khilāfah … then he mentioned the hadith.
items.ma-104: ʿUbaydah ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, from Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind, from Abū Naḍrah, from Abū Saʿīd, he said: ʿUmar gave a khuṭbah to the people and said: Indeed Allah ﷿ gave His Prophet ﷺ a concession in whatever He willed, and the Prophet of Allah ﷺ has gone his way. So complete the Ḥajj and the ʿumrah as Allah ﷿ commanded you, and fortify the private parts of these women.
items.ma-105: ʿUbaydah ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar narrated to me, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked: May a man sleep if he is in a state of janābah? He said: Yes, if he performs ablution.
items.ma-106: al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, he said: Ibn al-Mubārak informed us, he said: Maʿmar narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Rabīʿah ibn Darrāj: that ʿAlī ﵁ prayed two rakʿahs after the ʿAṣr, and ʿUmar became angry with him and said: Did you not know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to forbid it?
items.ma-107: Abū al-Mughīrah narrated to us, Ṣafwān narrated to us, Shurayḥ ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, he said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: I went out to place myself in the path of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ before I accepted Islam, and found that he had preceded me to the mosque, so I stood behind him. He began Sūrat al-Ḥāqqah, and I kept wondering at the composition of the Qurʾān. He said: I said: This, by Allah, is a poet, as Quraysh said. He said: Then he recited: {Indeed it is the speech of a noble Messenger. And it is not the speech of a poet; little do you believe.} He said: I said: A soothsayer. He said: {Nor is it the speech of a soothsayer; little do you remember. A revelation from the Rabb of the worlds. And if he had made up about Us some of the sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand. Then We would have cut from him the aorta. And there is none of you who could be a barrier from him} to the end of the sūrah [al-Ḥāqqah: 40–47]. He said: And Islam fell into every place in my heart.
items.ma-108: Abū al-Mughīrah and ʿIṣām ibn Khālid narrated to us, they both said: Ṣafwān narrated to us, from Shurayḥ ibn ʿUbayd and Rāshid ibn Saʿd and others than them, they said: When ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb reached Sargh, it was related to him that in al-Shām there was a severe epidemic. He said: It has reached me that the severity of the epidemic is in al-Shām, and I said: If my appointed time reaches me while Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ is alive, I will appoint him as successor; and if Allah asks me: Why did you appoint him as successor over the ummah of Muḥammad ﷺ? I will say: I heard Your Messenger ﷺ say: “Every prophet has an amīn, and my amīn is Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ.” The people denied that and said: What of the upper ones of Quraysh?! – they meant Banū Fihr. Then he said: And if my appointed time reaches me, and Abū ʿUbaydah has died, I will appoint Muʿādh ibn Jabal as successor; and if my Rabb ﷿ asks me: Why did you appoint him as successor? I will say: I heard Your Messenger ﷺ say: “He will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection ahead of the scholars by a nabdhah.”
items.ma-109: Abū al-Mughīrah narrated to us, Ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to us, he said: al-Awzāʿī and others narrated to me, from al-Zuhrī, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, he said: A boy was born to the brother of Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, and they named him al-Walīd. The Prophet ﷺ said: “You have named him with the names of your pharaohs. There will be in this ummah a man called al-Walīd; he will be worse for this ummah than Firʿawn was for his people.”
items.ma-110: Bahz narrated to us, Abān narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Men with whom I am satisfied testified before me, among them ʿUmar, and the one with whom I am most satisfied is ʿUmar: that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ used to say: “There is no prayer after the ʿAṣr prayer until the sun sets, and no prayer after the Ṣubḥ prayer until the sun rises.”
items.ma-111:
Abū al-Mughīrah narrated to us, Ṣafwān narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr narrated to us, from al-Ḥārith ibn Muʿāwiyah al-Kindī: that he rode to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb to ask him about three matters. He said: So he came to al-Madīnah, and ʿUmar asked him: What brought you? He said: To ask you about three matters. He said: And what are they? He said: Sometimes I and a woman are in a narrow building and the prayer arrives; if I and she pray, she is alongside me, and if she prays behind me, she goes out of the building. ʿUmar said: You screen between you and her with a garment, then [she] prays alongside you if you wish.
And about the two rakʿahs after the ʿAṣr. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade me from them.
He said: And about storytelling – for they wanted me to engage in storytelling. He said: As you wish – as though he disliked to prevent him. He said: I only wanted to end at your word. He said: I fear for you that you will tell stories and become exalted above them in your own self, then tell stories and become exalted, until it appears to you that you are above them in the position of al-Thurayyā, so Allah will put you beneath their feet on the Day of Resurrection by the measure of that.
items.ma-112: Bishr ibn Shuʿayb ibn Abī Ḥamzah narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to me, from al-Zuhrī, he said: Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh informed me that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar informed him that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Indeed Allah ﷿ forbids you to swear by your fathers.” ʿUmar said: By Allah, I have not sworn by them since I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbid it, nor have I spoken of it, mentioning it or relating it.
items.ma-113: Abū al-Yamān narrated to us, Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, from Rāshid ibn Saʿd, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān: that the Prophet ﷺ did not take ṣadaqah from horses and slaves.
items.ma-114: ʿAlī ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh – meaning Ibn al-Mubārak – informed us, Muḥammad ibn Sūqah informed us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dīnār, from Ibn ʿUmar: that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb gave a khuṭbah at al-Jābiyah and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among us as I stand among you, and said: “Treat my Companions well; then those who follow them; then those who follow them; then lying will spread, until a man will begin to give testimony before he is asked for it. So whoever among you wants the midst of Paradise, let him keep to the jamāʿah, for Shayṭān is with the one, and from two he is farther. Let none of you be alone with a woman, for Shayṭān is the third of them. And whoever is pleased by his good deed and grieved by his evil deed, he is a believer.”
items.ma-115: Abū al-Yamān narrated to us, Abū Bakr narrated to us, from Ḥakīm ibn ʿUmayr and Ḍamrah ibn Ḥabīb, they both said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: Whoever would be pleased to look at the way of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, let him look at the way of ʿAmr ibn al-Aswad.
items.ma-116: Abū Saʿīd, the mawlā of Banū Hāshim, narrated to us, he said: Zāʾidah narrated to us, Simāk narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: ʿUmar said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in a riding party, and a man said: No, by my father! And a man said: “Do not swear by your fathers.” I turned, and it was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-117:
ʿIṣām ibn Khālid and Abū al-Yamān narrated to us, they both said: Shuʿayb ibn Abī Ḥamzah informed us, from al-Zuhrī, he said: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah ibn Masʿūd narrated to us that Abū Hurayrah said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died, and Abū Bakr came after him, and those of the Arabs who disbelieved disbelieved, ʿUmar said: O Abū Bakr, how can you fight the people when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I have been commanded to fight the people until they say: There is no deity except Allah; so whoever says: There is no deity except Allah has protected from me his wealth and his life, except by its right, and his reckoning is upon Allah”? Abū Bakr said: By Allah, I will fight – Abū al-Yamān said: I will kill – whoever separates between the prayer and the zakāh, for the zakāh is the right of the wealth. By Allah, if they withheld from me a young female goat that they used to pay to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I would fight them for withholding it.
ʿUmar said: By Allah, it was only that I saw that Allah ﷿ had opened the chest of Abū Bakr for fighting, so I knew that it was the truth.
items.ma-118: Abū al-Mughīrah narrated to us, al-Awzāʿī narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no prayer after the Ṣubḥ prayer until the sun rises, nor after the ʿAṣr until the sun sets.”
items.ma-119: al-Ḥakam ibn Nāfiʿ narrated to us, Ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to us, from Abū Sabaʾ ʿUtbah ibn Tamīm, from al-Walīd ibn ʿĀmir al-Yazanī, from ʿUrwah ibn Mughīth al-Anṣārī, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, he said: The Prophet ﷺ ruled that the owner of the riding animal has more right to its front.
items.ma-120: Abū al-Yamān al-Ḥakam ibn Nāfiʿ narrated to us, Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, from Rāshid ibn Saʿd, from Ḥumrah ibn ʿAbd Kulāl, he said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb travelled to al-Shām after his first journey to it, until, when he was close to it, it reached him and those with him that the plague was widespread in it. His companions said to him: Go back and do not plunge into it, for if you were to descend upon it while it is in it, we would not see it right for you to depart from it. So he turned back, returning to al-Madīnah, and halted for the night that same night. And I was the closest of the people to him; when he set out, I set out with him, following his tracks, and I heard him say: They turned me back from al-Shām after I was close to it, because the plague is in it. Indeed, my turning back from it does not delay my appointed time, and my coming from it did not hasten me from my appointed time. Indeed, if I had arrived at al-Madīnah and finished the needs that I must attend to, I would surely travel until I enter al-Shām, then descend at Ḥimṣ, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Allah will surely raise up from it on the Day of Resurrection seventy thousand, upon whom there is no reckoning and upon whom there is no punishment; the place of their raising is between the olive trees and its wall, in al-Barth al-Aḥmar of it.”
items.ma-121:
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd narrated to us, Ḥaywah narrated to us, Abū ʿAqīl informed us, from his cousin, from ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir: that he went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the expedition of Tabūk, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat one day speaking to his Companions, and said: “Whoever rises when the sun has risen, performs ablution and does the ablution well, then rises and prays two rakʿahs, his sins will be forgiven and he will be as his mother bore him.”
ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir said: I said: Praise be to Allah who provided me to hear this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, who was sitting opposite me, said to me: Are you amazed at this? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said something more amazing than this before you came. I said: And what is that, may my father and my mother be a ransom for you? ʿUmar said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever performs ablution and does the ablution well, then raises his gaze to the sky and says: I bear witness that there is no deity except Allah alone, no partner for Him, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger, the eight doors of Paradise are opened for him; he enters by whichever of them he wishes.”
items.ma-122: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd – meaning Abū Dāwūd al-Ṭayālisī – narrated to us, he said: Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Dāwūd al-Awdī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Muslī, from al-Ashʿath ibn Qays, he said: I was ʿUmar's guest, and he reached for his wife and struck her, and said: O Ashʿath, memorize from me three things that I memorized from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: “Do not ask a man why he struck his wife, and do not sleep except upon a witr.” And I forgot the third.
items.ma-123: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Yazīd – meaning al-Rishk – narrated to us, from Muʿādhah, from Umm ʿAmr daughter of ʿAbd Allāh, that she heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr say: She heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb say in his khuṭbah that he heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saying: “Whoever wears silk in this world will not be clothed in it in the Hereafter.”
items.ma-124:
Yaḥyā ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Jābir, he said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb informed me, he said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “A rider will surely travel through the outskirts of al-Madīnah, then he will say: There was in this a large settled community of the believers.”
My father Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal said: Ḥasan al-Ashyab did not take it beyond Jābir.
items.ma-125: Hārūn narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith narrated to me that ʿUmar ibn al-Sāʾib narrated to him that al-Qāsim ibn Abī al-Qāsim al-Sabāʾī narrated to him, from the storyteller of the armies in Constantinople, that he heard him narrate that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: O people, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not sit at a table around which wine is passed; and whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not enter the bathhouse except in an izār; and whoever [of women] believes in Allah and the Last Day, let her not enter the bathhouse.”
items.ma-126: Abū Salamah al-Khuzāʿī narrated to us, Layth and Yūnus informed us, Layth narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Usāmah ibn al-Hād, from al-Walīd ibn Abī al-Walīd, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh – meaning Ibn Surāqah –, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever shades the head of a fighter, Allah will shade him on the Day of Resurrection; and whoever equips a fighter until he sets off, he will have the like of his reward until he dies – Yūnus said: or returns – and whoever builds a mosque for Allah in which the name of Allah Taʿālā is mentioned, Allah will build for him because of it a house in Paradise.”
items.ma-127: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Sulaymān al-Aʿmash, from Shaqīq, from Salmān ibn Rabīʿah, he said: I heard ʿUmar say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a distribution, and I said: O Messenger of Allah, others than these are more deserving of it than they: the People of the Ṣuffah. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed you give me the choice between asking me with indecency and between declaring me stingy, and I am not stingy.”
items.ma-128: ʿAffān narrated to us, Khālid narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, from ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from his father, or from his grandfather, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, he said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ after ḥadath perform ablution and wipe over the khuffs.
items.ma-129: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Abū Rāfiʿ: that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was leaning on Ibn ʿAbbās, and with him were Ibn ʿUmar and Saʿīd ibn Zayd, and he said: Know that I have not said anything about the kalālah, and I have not appointed anyone as successor after me, and that whoever of the captives of the Arabs reaches my death is free from the wealth of Allah ﷿. Saʿīd ibn Zayd said: Indeed, if you were to point to a man from the Muslims, the people would trust you; and Abū Bakr did that and the people trusted him. ʿUmar said: I have seen from my Companions an evil eagerness, and I am placing this matter with these six men with whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was pleased when he died. Then ʿUmar said: If one of two men had reached me, and I placed this matter with him, I would trust him: Sālim, the mawlā of Abū Ḥudhayfah, and Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ.
items.ma-130: ʿAffān narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, Abū al-ʿĀliyah narrated to me, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Men with whom I am satisfied testified before me, among them ʿUmar – and the one with whom I am most satisfied is ʿUmar – that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no prayer after the Ṣubḥ until the sun rises, and no prayer after the ʿAṣr until the sun sets.”
items.ma-131: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb bent over the Rukn and said: I know that you are a stone, and had I not seen my beloved ﷺ kiss you and touch you, I would not have touched you nor kissed you. There was for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent example.
items.ma-132: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, ʿAmmār ibn Abī ʿAmmār informed us that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw on the hand of a man a ring of gold, and said: “Throw this away.” So he threw it away, then wore a ring of iron, and he said: “This is worse than it.” So he wore a ring of silver, and he was silent about it.
items.ma-133: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, Zāʾidah narrated to us, ʿĀṣim narrated to us. And Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, from Zāʾidah, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr, from ʿAbd Allāh, he said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken, the Anṣār said: From us a commander, and from you a commander. So ʿUmar came to them and said: O assembly of the Anṣār, do you not know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded Abū Bakr to lead the people [in prayer]? Which of you is content in himself to go ahead of Abū Bakr? The Anṣār said: We seek refuge with Allah from going ahead of Abū Bakr.
items.ma-134: Mūsā ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Jābir, that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb informed him: that he saw a man perform ablution for the prayer and leave the place of a nail on the top of his foot, and the Prophet ﷺ saw him and said: “Go back and make your ablution good.” So he went back, performed ablution, then prayed.
items.ma-135:
Abū Saʿīd, the mawlā of Banū Hāshim, narrated to us, al-Haytham ibn Rāfiʿ al-Ṭāṭarī, a Baṣrī, narrated to us, Abū Yaḥyā, a man of the people of Makkah, narrated to me, from Farrūkh, the mawlā of ʿUthmān: that ʿUmar – and he was at that time Commander of the Believers – went out to the mosque and saw food scattered about, and said: What is this food? They said: Food that was brought to us. He said: May Allah bless it and the one who brought it. It was said: O Commander of the Believers, it has been hoarded. He said: And who hoarded it? They said: Farrūkh, the mawlā of ʿUthmān, and so-and-so, the mawlā of ʿUmar. So he sent for the two of them and called them, and said: What made you hoard the food of the Muslims? They both said: O Commander of the Believers, we buy with our wealth and sell. ʿUmar said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever hoards the food of the Muslims, Allah will strike him with bankruptcy or with leprosy.” At that, Farrūkh said: O Commander of the Believers, I make a covenant with Allah and with you that I will never return to [dealing in] food. As for the mawlā of ʿUmar, he said: We only buy with our wealth and sell.
Abū Yaḥyā said: I saw the mawlā of ʿUmar leprous.
items.ma-136: Abū al-Yamān narrated to us, Shuʿayb informed us, from al-Zuhrī, Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said: I heard ʿUmar say: The Prophet ﷺ used to give me the grant, and I would say: Give it to one more in need of it than I, until once he gave me wealth and I said: Give it to one more in need of it than I. The Prophet ﷺ said: “Take it and make it your property and give it in ṣadaqah; and whatever comes to you of this wealth while you are not eagerly looking out for it nor asking, take it; and what [is] not [so], do not make your soul follow it.”
items.ma-137: Hārūn narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Yūnus informed me, from Ibn Shihāb, from Sālim, from his father, he said: I heard ʿUmar say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to give me the grant … then he mentioned its meaning.
items.ma-138: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, Bukayr narrated to me, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Saʿīd al-Anṣārī, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, he said: One day I became cheerful and kissed while I was fasting. I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: I did a great thing today: I kissed while I was fasting. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “What do you think: if you were to rinse your mouth with water while you were fasting?” I said: There is no harm in that. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Then in what?”
items.ma-139: Yūnus ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, Dāwūd – meaning Ibn Abī al-Furāt – narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Buraydah, from Abū al-Aswad, that he said: I came to al-Madīnah and arrived while a sickness had befallen it, and they were dying rapidly. I sat with ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb ﵁, and a funeral procession passed by him, and good was said of its occupant, and ʿUmar said: It is obligatory. Then another passed, and good was said of its occupant, and ʿUmar said: It is obligatory. Then a third passed, and evil was said of it, and ʿUmar said: It is obligatory. Abū al-Aswad said: What is obligatory, O Commander of the Believers? He said: I said as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Any Muslim for whom four testify to good, Allah will admit him to Paradise.” He said: We said: And three? He said: “And three.” He said: We said: And two? He said: “And two.” He said: Then we did not ask him about one.
items.ma-140: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, Bukayr narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from ʿUmar, he said: We went on campaign with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Ramaḍān, and the Conquest was in Ramaḍān, and we broke the fast in both.
items.ma-141: Abū Saʿīd, the mawlā of Banū Hāshim, narrated to us, al-Muthannā ibn ʿAwf al-ʿAnazī, a Baṣrī, narrated to us, he said: al-Ghaḍbān ibn Ḥanẓalah apprised me: that his father Ḥanẓalah ibn Nuʿaym came as part of a delegation to ʿUmar, and whenever a person of the delegation passed by ʿUmar, he would ask him who he was from, until my father passed by him, and he asked him: Who are you from? He said: From ʿAnazah. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “A tribe from here, transgressed against and aided.”
items.ma-142: Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, he said: Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb narrated to us, from Maʿmar: that he asked Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab about fasting while travelling, and he narrated to him from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb that he said: We went on two campaigns with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the month of Ramaḍān: the day of Badr and the day of the Conquest, and we broke the fast in both.
items.ma-143: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Daylam ibn Ghazwān, an ʿAbdī, narrated to us, Maymūn al-Kurdī narrated to us, Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī narrated to me, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The thing I fear most for my ummah is every hypocrite learned of tongue.”
items.ma-144: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, Ṣāliḥ ibn Muḥammad ibn Zāʾidah narrated to us, from Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh: that he was with Maslamah ibn ʿAbd al-Malik in the land of the Romans, and ghulūl was found among the goods of a man. He asked Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh, and he said: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to me, from ʿUmar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever you find ghulūl among his goods, burn it – he said: and I think he said: and strike him –.” He said: So he took his goods out to the market. He said: And he found in them a muṣḥaf, so he asked Sālim, and he said: Sell it, and give its price in ṣadaqah.
items.ma-145: Abū Saʿīd and Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, they both said: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, from ʿUmar: that the Prophet ﷺ used to seek refuge from five: from stinginess, cowardice, the fitnah of the chest, the punishment of the grave, and an evil lifespan.
items.ma-146: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, he said: I heard ʿAṭāʾ ibn Dīnār, from Abū Yazīd al-Khawlānī, that he heard Faḍālah ibn ʿUbayd say: I heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “The shuhadāʾ are three: a believer of excellent īmān who met the enemy and was true to Allah until he was killed – that is the one to whom the people will raise their necks on the Day of Resurrection – and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his head until his cap fell, or the cap of ʿUmar – and a believer of excellent īmān who met the enemy, as though his skin were being struck with the thorns of the acacia, a stray arrow came to him and killed him; he is in the second rank; and a believer of excellent īmān who mixed a righteous deed with another, evil one, met the enemy and was true to Allah until he was killed; he is in the third rank.”
items.ma-147: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from ʿUmar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A father is not retaliated against for a child.” And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The wealth is inherited by the one who inherits the walāʾ.”
items.ma-148: Ḥasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb narrated to us, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, he said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Retaliation is not taken for a child from his father.”
items.ma-149: Ḥasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Sharaḥbīl narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, that he said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform ablution once, once.
items.ma-150: Yaḥyā ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Dīnār, from Abū Yazīd al-Khawlānī, he said: I heard Faḍālah ibn ʿUbayd say: I heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “The shuhadāʾ are four: a believer of excellent īmān who met the enemy and was true to Allah and was killed – that is the one at whom the people look like this – and he raised his head until the cap of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fell, or the cap of ʿUmar – and the second: a believer who met the enemy, as though his back were being struck with the thorns of the acacia, a stray arrow came to him and killed him; he is in the second rank; and the third: a believer who mixed a righteous deed with another, evil one, met the enemy and was true to Allah ﷿ until he was killed; he is in the third rank; and the fourth: a believer who was excessive against himself, greatly excessive, met the enemy and was true to Allah until he was killed; he is in the fourth rank.”
items.ma-151: Yaḥyā ibn Ghaylān narrated to us, Rishdīn ibn Saʿd narrated to us, Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ghāfiqī narrated to me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: that he performed ablution in the year of Tabūk once, once.
items.ma-152: Ḥasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, Abū al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Jābir, that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb ﵁ informed him that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “The people of Makkah will go out, then it will not be passed through – or: none but a few will pass through it – then it will fill up and be built, then they will go out from it and never return to it.”
items.ma-153: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, Abū al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Jābir that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb informed him: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw a man who had performed ablution for the Ẓuhr prayer and left the place of a nail on the top of his foot, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw him and said: “Go back and make your ablution good.” So he went back, performed ablution, then prayed.
items.ma-154: Hushaym narrated to us, he said: al-Zuhrī claimed, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah ibn Masʿūd, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿUmar that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do not praise me excessively as the Christians praised ʿĪsā ibn Maryam; I am only the servant of Allah and His Messenger.”
items.ma-155: Hushaym narrated to us, Abū Bishr informed us, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: This verse was revealed while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in hiding in Makkah: {And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be hushed in it} [al-Isrāʾ: 110]. He said: When he prayed with his Companions, he would raise his voice with the Qurʾān. He said: When the polytheists heard that, they reviled the Qurʾān, and the one who sent it down, and the one who brought it. So Allah ﷿ said to His Prophet ﷺ: {And do not be loud in your prayer}, that is, in your recitation, so that the polytheists hear and revile the Qurʾān; {nor be hushed in it} from your Companions, so that you do not let them hear the Qurʾān, until they take it from you; {and seek between that a way}.
items.ma-156: Hushaym narrated to us, ʿAlī ibn Zayd informed us, from Yūsuf ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb gave a khuṭbah – and Hushaym once said: gave us a khuṭbah – praised Allah and extolled Him, then mentioned the rajm, and said: Do not be deceived away from it, for it is a ḥadd from the ḥudūd of Allah. Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stoned, and we stoned after him. And had it not been that some would say: ʿUmar added to the Book of Allah ﷿ what is not part of it, I would have written it on one side of the muṣḥaf. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb bears witness – and Hushaym once said: and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf and so-and-so and so-and-so – that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stoned, and we stoned after him. Indeed, after you there will be a people who deny the rajm, and the Dajjāl, and the intercession, and the punishment of the grave, and a people who will be brought out of the Fire after they have been scorched.
items.ma-157: Hushaym narrated to us, Ḥumayd informed us, from Anas, he said: ʿUmar said: I agreed with my Rabb in three: I said: O Messenger of Allah, if only we took the Maqām Ibrāhīm as a place of prayer? So there was revealed: {And take from the Maqām of Ibrāhīm a place of prayer} [al-Baqarah: 125]. And I said: O Messenger of Allah, your women are entered upon by the righteous and the wicked – if only you would command them to veil themselves? So the verse of the ḥijāb was revealed. And his women gathered against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in jealousy, so I said to them: {Perhaps his Rabb, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you} [al-Taḥrīm: 5]. He said: So it was revealed just so.
items.ma-158: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: I heard Hishām ibn Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām reciting Sūrat al-Furqān, and he recited in it letters that the Prophet of Allah had not taught me to recite. He said: So I wanted to pounce on him while I was in the prayer. When he finished, I said: Who taught you to recite this recitation? He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I said: You have lied. By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not teach you to recite like this. So I took him by the hand, leading him, and went with him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and said: O Messenger of Allah, you taught me to recite Sūrat al-Furqān, and I heard this one reciting in it letters that you had not taught me to recite. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Recite, O Hishām.” So he recited as he had recited. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Thus it was revealed.” Then he said: “Recite, O ʿUmar.” So I recited. He said: “Thus it was revealed.” Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed the Qurʾān was sent down upon seven aḥruf.”
items.ma-159: ʿAmr ibn al-Haytham narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr, from ʿUmar, he said: I certainly saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ writhing, not finding enough inferior dates to fill his belly.
items.ma-160: Ibn Abī ʿAdī narrated to us, from Ḥumayd, from Anas, he said: ʿUmar said: I agreed with my Rabb ﷿ in three – or: my Rabb agreed with me in three – he said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, if only you took the Maqām as a place of prayer? He said: So Allah ﷿ revealed: {And take from the Maqām of Ibrāhīm a place of prayer}. And I said: If only you would screen [yourself] from the Mothers of the Believers, for the righteous and the wicked enter upon you? So the verse of the ḥijāb was revealed. He said: And something reached me about the Mothers of the Believers, so I went through them one after another, saying to them: You will surely refrain from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, or Allah will surely substitute for him wives better than you, Muslim women – until I came to one of the Mothers of the Believers, and she said: O ʿUmar, does the Messenger of Allah ﷺ not have what admonishes his women, that you admonish them? So I desisted. Then Allah ﷿ revealed: {Perhaps his Rabb, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you, Muslim, believing, devout} – the verse.
items.ma-162: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, he heard Mālik ibn Aws ibn al-Ḥadathān, he heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said – and Sufyān once said: he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ –: “Gold for silver is ribā except hāʾa wa-hāʾa, wheat for wheat is ribā except hāʾa wa-hāʾa, barley for barley is ribā except hāʾa wa-hāʾa, dates for dates are ribā except hāʾa wa-hāʾa.”
items.ma-163: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, he heard Abū ʿUbayd, he said: I attended the ʿĪd with ʿUmar, and he began with the prayer before the khuṭbah, and said: Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade fasting on these two days. As for the Day of al-Fiṭr, it is your breaking of the fast from your fasting; and as for the Day of al-Aḍḥā, eat from the meat of your nusuk.
items.ma-164: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿUmar, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do not praise me excessively as the Christians praised ʿĪsā ibn Maryam; I am only a servant, so say: His servant and His Messenger.”
items.ma-165: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dīnār, from Ibn ʿUmar, from ʿUmar: that he asked the Prophet ﷺ: May one of us sleep while he is in a state of janābah? He said: “He performs ablution and sleeps, if he wishes.” And Sufyān once said: “Let him perform ablution and let him sleep.”
items.ma-166: Sufyān narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father: that ʿUmar gave a horse to carry [someone] in the path of Allah ﷿, then saw it – or some of its offspring – being sold, and wanted to buy it, so he asked the Prophet ﷺ about it, and he said: “Leave it; it will meet you, or you will meet it, all together.” And once he said: He forbade him, and said: “Do not buy it, and do not return to your ṣadaqah.”
items.ma-167: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir ibn Rabīʿah, narrating from ʿUmar, conveying it to the Prophet ﷺ – and Sufyān once said: from the Prophet ﷺ – he said: “Perform the Ḥajj and the ʿumrah in succession, for following them one after the other removes poverty and sins, as the bellows remove the dross.”
items.ma-168: Sufyān narrated to us, from Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, from ʿAlqamah ibn Waqqāṣ, he said: I heard ʿUmar say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Deeds are only by intention, and for every person is only what he intended. So whoever's hijrah is to Allah ﷿, his hijrah is to what he emigrated to; and whoever's hijrah is for a worldly [gain] that he will obtain, or a woman he will marry, his hijrah is to what he emigrated to.”
items.ma-169: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbdah ibn Abī Lubābah, from Abū Wāʾil, he said: al-Ṣubayy ibn Maʿbad said: I was a Christian man and I accepted Islam, and I raised the talbiyah for Ḥajj and ʿumrah, and Zayd ibn Ṣūḥān and Salmān ibn Rabīʿah heard me while I was raising the talbiyah for both, and they said: This one is certainly more astray than the camel of his family. It was as though a mountain had been placed upon me by their word. So I came to ʿUmar and informed him, and he turned to them and rebuked them, and turned to me and said: You have been guided to the sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ, you have been guided to the sunnah of your Prophet ﷺ. ʿAbdah said: Abū Wāʾil said: Many a time I and Masrūq went to al-Ṣubayy, asking him about it.
items.ma-170: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās: It was mentioned to ʿUmar that Samurah – and once he said: It reached ʿUmar that Samurah – sold wine. He said: May Allah fight Samurah! Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “May Allah curse the Jews: the fats were prohibited to them, so they melted them and sold them.”
items.ma-171: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr and Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Mālik ibn Aws ibn al-Ḥadathān, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, he said: The wealth of Banū al-Naḍīr was of what Allah bestowed as fayʾ upon His Messenger ﷺ, for which the Muslims did not press with horses or riding camels, so it was exclusively for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he would spend on his family from it the expense of his year – and once he said: the sustenance of his year – and what remained he placed in horses and weapons, as preparation in the path of Allah ﷿.
items.ma-172: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from al-Zuhrī, from Mālik ibn Aws, he said: I heard ʿUmar say to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, Ṭalḥah, al-Zubayr and Saʿd: I adjure you by Allah, by whom the heaven and the earth stand: do you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “We are not inherited from; what we leave is ṣadaqah”? They said: O Allah, yes.
items.ma-173: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Yazīd, from his father, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The child belongs to the firāsh.”
items.ma-174: Ibn Idrīs narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, from Ibn Abī ʿAmmār, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bābayh, from Yaʿlā ibn Umayyah, he said: I asked ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, I said: {There is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer if you fear that those who disbelieve will subject you to fitnah} [al-Nisāʾ: 101], though Allah has made the people secure?! ʿUmar said to me: I was amazed at what you were amazed at, so I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about that, and he said: “A ṣadaqah with which Allah has given ṣadaqah to you, so accept His ṣadaqah.”
items.ma-175:
Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, he said: A man came to ʿUmar while he was at ʿArafah – Abū Muʿāwiyah said: and al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Khaythamah, from Qays ibn Marwān, that he came to ʿUmar – and said: I have come, O Commander of the Believers, from al-Kūfah, and I left there a man dictating the maṣāḥif from the back of his heart. He became angry and swelled until he almost filled what is between the two branches of the saddle, and said: And who is he, woe to you? He said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd. He kept being cooled and the anger relieved from him until he returned to the state he had been in.
Then he said: Woe to you, by Allah, I do not know that anyone remains among the people more deserving of that than he, and I will tell you about that. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would continue to converse at night with Abū Bakr, on nights like that, about a matter of the affairs of the Muslims, and he conversed with him one night, and I was with him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out, and we went out with him, and there was a man standing praying in the mosque. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood listening to his recitation, and when we almost recognized him, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever is pleased to recite the Qurʾān fresh as it was sent down, let him recite it according to the recitation of Ibn Umm ʿAbd.” He said: Then the man sat down making supplication, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began to say to him: “Ask and you will be given; ask and you will be given.” ʿUmar said: I said: By Allah, I will go to him early and give him glad tidings. He said: So I went early to him to give him glad tidings, and found that Abū Bakr had preceded me to him and had given him glad tidings. And no, by Allah, I never raced him to any good except that he preceded me to it.
items.ma-176: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, he said: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿĀbis ibn Rabīʿah, he said: I saw ʿUmar kiss the Stone, and he said: I kiss you although I know that you are a stone, and had I not seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kiss you, I would not have kissed you.
items.ma-177: Jarīr narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from Jābir ibn Samurah, he said: ʿUmar gave a khuṭbah to the people at al-Jābiyah and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood in a place like this standing place of mine and said: “Be good to my Companions, then those who follow them, then those who follow them. Then a people will come, one of whom will swear an oath before he is asked to swear it, and will testify to a testimony before he is asked to testify. So whoever among you loves to attain the midst of Paradise, let him keep to the jamāʿah, for Shayṭān is with the one, and from two he is farther. And let no man be alone with a woman, for the third of them is Shayṭān. And whoever among you is pleased by his good deed and grieved by his evil deed, he is a believer.”
items.ma-178: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿUmar, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to converse at night with Abū Bakr, on nights like that, about a matter of the affairs of the Muslims, and I was with him.
