items.ma-179: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūbah, from Qatādah, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, from Maʿdān ibn Abī Ṭalḥah, he said: ʿUmar said: I did not ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about anything more than I asked him about the kalālah, until he poked his finger into my chest and said: “The verse of the summer suffices you, the one at the end of Sūrat al-Nisāʾ.”
items.ma-180: Yaḥyā narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from Ibn ʿUmar, from ʿUmar, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “The dead is punished in his grave by the wailing over him.”
items.ma-181: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik, ʿAbd Allāh, the mawlā of Asmāʾ, narrated to us, he said: Asmāʾ sent me to Ibn ʿUmar: that it had reached her that you prohibit three things: the marking on the garment, the crimson cushion, and fasting the whole of Rajab. He said: As for what you mentioned of fasting Rajab, then how about the one who fasts perpetually? And as for what you mentioned of the marking on the garment, I heard ʿUmar ﵁ say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever wears silk in this world will not wear it in the Hereafter.”
items.ma-182: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us – I asked him – Sulaymān ibn al-Mughīrah narrated to us, Thābit narrated to us, from Anas, he said: We were with ʿUmar between Makkah and al-Madīnah, and we looked out for the new moon, and I had sharp sight, so I saw it, and I began saying to ʿUmar: Do you not see it? He said: I will see it while I am lying on my bed. Then he began to narrate to us about the people of Badr. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to show us their places of falling the day before, saying: “This is the falling place of so-and-so tomorrow, if Allah wills, and this is the falling place of so-and-so tomorrow, if Allah wills.” He said: And they began to be struck down at them. He said: I said: By Him who sent you with the truth, they did not miss that [spot]; they were struck down at them. Then he commanded about them, and they were thrown into a well, and he went to them and said: “O so-and-so, O so-and-so, have you found what Allah promised you to be true? For I have found what Allah promised me to be true.” ʿUmar said: O Messenger of Allah, are you speaking to a people who have become carrion? He said: “You are not more hearing of what I say than they are, but they cannot answer.”
items.ma-183: Yaḥyā narrated to us, Ḥusayn al-Muʿallim narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, he said: When ʿAmr returned, the sons of Maʿmar ibn Ḥabīb came disputing with him before ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb about the walāʾ of their sister. He said: I will judge between you by what I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whatever the son or the father secures belongs to his ʿaṣabah, whoever he may be.” So he ruled in our favour with it.
items.ma-184:
I read to Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd: ʿUthmān ibn Ghiyāth said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Buraydah narrated to me, from Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar and Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥimyarī, they both said: We met ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, and we mentioned al-qadar and what they say about it. He said: When you return to them, say: Ibn ʿUmar is free of you, and you are free of him – three times. Then he said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb informed me that while they were sitting – or: seated – with the Prophet ﷺ, a man came to him walking, handsome of face, handsome of hair, upon him white garments, and the people looked at one another: We do not know this one, and this is not a traveller.
Then he said: O Messenger of Allah, may I come to you? He said: “Yes.” So he came and placed his knees against his knees and his hands on his thighs, and said: What is Islam? He said: “The testimony that there is no deity except Allah and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah, and that you establish the prayer, give the zakāh, fast Ramaḍān, and perform Ḥajj to the House.” He said: Then what is īmān? He said: “That you believe in Allah, His angels, Paradise and the Fire, the resurrection after death, and al-qadar, all of it.” He said: Then what is iḥsān? He said: “That you work for Allah as though you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then indeed He Yarāka.” He said: Then when is the Hour? He said: “The one asked about it is not more knowing than the one asking.” He said: Then what are its signs? He said: “When the naked, barefoot, destitute shepherds of sheep compete in the height of buildings, and slave-women give birth to their masters.” He said: Then he said: “Bring the man to me.” So they sought him but saw nothing. He remained two or three days, then said: “O Ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, do you know who the questioner was about such-and-such?” He said: Allah and His Messenger know best. He said: “That was Jibrīl; he came to you to teach you your religion.”
He said: And a man from Juhaynah or Muzaynah asked him, saying: O Messenger of Allah, in what are we working: in something that has finished and passed, or in something that is begun now? He said: “In something that has finished, or passed.” A man, or some of the people, said: O Messenger of Allah, then in what are we working? He said: “The people of Paradise are eased toward the deeds of the people of Paradise, and the people of the Fire are eased toward the deeds of the people of the Fire.”
He said: Yaḥyā said: It is thus.
items.ma-185:
Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, Salamah ibn Kuhayl narrated to me, he said: I heard Abū al-Ḥakam say: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās about nabīdh of the jar, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade nabīdh of the jar and the gourd. And he said: Whoever is pleased to prohibit what Allah and His Messenger prohibited, let him prohibit nabīdh. He said: And I asked Ibn al-Zubayr, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the gourd and the jar. He said: And I asked Ibn ʿUmar, and he narrated from ʿUmar that the Prophet ﷺ forbade the gourd and the pitch-coated vessel.
He said: And my brother narrated to me, from Abū Saʿīd: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the jar, the gourd, the pitch-coated vessel, the unripe dates, and the dates.
items.ma-186:
Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us – I asked him – Hishām narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, from Maʿdān ibn Abī Ṭalḥah: that ʿUmar gave a khuṭbah on a day of Jumuʿah, mentioned the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, mentioned Abū Bakr ﵁, and said: I have seen as if a rooster pecked me two pecks, and I consider it only to be for the arrival of my appointed time. And some people command me to appoint a successor, but Allah would not let His religion go to waste, nor His khilāfah, and that with which He sent His Prophet ﷺ. If a matter hastens me away, the khilāfah is a shūrā among these six with whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was pleased when he died. And I know that some people will find fault with this matter; I struck them with this hand of mine for Islam; if they do so, those are the enemies of Allah, the disbelievers, the astray.
And I do not leave anything after me more important to me than the kalālah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was not as stern with me about anything since I accompanied him as he was stern with me about the kalālah, and I did not go back to him about anything as I went back to him about the kalālah, until he poked his finger into my chest and said: “O ʿUmar, does the verse of the summer, which is at the end of Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, not suffice you?” If I live, I will give a judgment concerning it, by which will judge the one who recites the Qurʾān and the one who does not recite the Qurʾān.
Then he said: O Allah, I call You to witness against the governors of the provinces, for I only sent them to teach the people their religion and the sunnah of their Prophet ﷺ, to distribute among them their fayʾ, to act justly toward them, and to raise to me what is unclear to them of their affairs.
O people, you eat from two plants that I consider only foul. I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he found their smell on a man in the mosque, command about him, and he would be taken by the hand and brought out to al-Baqīʿ. And whoever eats them, let him kill them by cooking.
items.ma-187: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Mujālid, from ʿĀmir, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, he said: I heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb say to Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh: What is the matter that I see you dishevelled and dust-covered since the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died? Perhaps the leadership of your cousin has displeased you, O Ṭalḥah? He said: I seek refuge with Allah! I am the most fitting of you not to do that. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Indeed I know a word that no man says at the presence of death except that he finds in it a relief for his soul when it leaves his body, and it will be a light for him on the Day of Resurrection.” I did not ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about it, and he did not inform me of it, and that is what entered me. ʿUmar said: I know it. He said: Then praise be to Allah! He said: Then what is it? He said: It is the word that he said to his uncle: There is no deity except Allah. Ṭalḥah said: You have spoken truly.
items.ma-188: Jaʿfar ibn ʿAwn narrated to us, Abū ʿUmays narrated to us, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Ṭāriq ibn Shihāb, he said: A man of the Jews came to ʿUmar and said: O Commander of the Believers, you recite a verse in your Book which, had it been revealed upon us, the assembly of the Jews, we would have taken that day as an ʿĪd. He said: And which verse is it? He said: His saying ﷿: {Today I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favour upon you} [al-Māʾidah: 3]. ʿUmar said: By Allah, I know the day on which it was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the hour in which it was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: the evening of ʿArafah, on a Friday.
items.ma-189: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAyyāsh ibn Abī Rabīʿah, from Ḥakīm ibn Ḥakīm ibn ʿAbbād ibn Ḥunayf, from Abū Umāmah ibn Sahl ibn Ḥunayf: that a man shot a man with an arrow and killed him, and he had no heir except a maternal uncle. Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ wrote about that to ʿUmar, and he wrote: that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Allah and His Messenger are the mawlā of the one who has no mawlā, and the maternal uncle is the heir of the one who has no heir.”
items.ma-190: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Yaʿfūr al-ʿAbdī, he said: I heard a shaykh in Makkah during the governorship of al-Ḥajjāj narrating from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb that the Prophet ﷺ said to him: “O ʿUmar, you are a strong man; do not crowd at the Stone and harm the weak. If you find it clear, touch it; otherwise face it and make tahlīl and takbīr.”
items.ma-191: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Kahmas narrated to us, from Ibn Buraydah, from Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar, from Ibn ʿUmar: from ʿUmar: that Jibrīl ﵇ said to the Prophet ﷺ: What is īmān? He said: “That you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and in al-qadar, its good and its evil.” Jibrīl said to him: You have spoken truly. He said: We were amazed at him, asking him and affirming his truthfulness. He said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “That was Jibrīl; he came to you to teach you the landmarks of your religion.”
items.ma-192: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Hishām ibn ʿUrwah narrated to us, from his father, from ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUmar, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When the night approaches – and once he said: the night comes – from here, and the day goes from here, then the fasting person has broken his fast” – meaning the east and the west.
items.ma-193: Yazīd narrated to us, Isrāʾīl ibn Yūnus informed us, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā al-Thaʿlabī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, he said: I was with ʿUmar, and a man came to him and said: I saw the new moon, the new moon of Shawwāl. ʿUmar said: O people, break your fast. Then he stood to a large bowl in which there was water and performed ablution, and wiped over his khuffs. The man said: By Allah, O Commander of the Believers, I came to you only to ask you about this: have you seen anyone other than yourself do it? He said: Yes, one better than me and the best of the ummah: I saw Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ do the like of what I did, and he was wearing a Shāmī cloak, tight in the sleeves, and he put his hand in from under the cloak. Then ʿUmar prayed the Maghrib.
items.ma-194:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Sulaymān, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ did not prohibit the desert lizard, but he found it repulsive.
One other than Muḥammad said: from Sulaymān al-Yashkurī.
items.ma-195: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from Sālim, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, from ʿUmar, from the Prophet ﷺ: that he asked his permission for the ʿumrah, and he permitted him, and said: “O my little brother, do not forget us in your supplication.” And later, in al-Madīnah, he said: “O my little brother, include us in your supplication.” ʿUmar said: I would not like to have in exchange for it all that the sun has risen upon, because of his saying: “O my little brother.”
items.ma-196: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us. And Ḥajjāj, he said: I heard Shuʿbah, from ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from Sālim, from Ibn ʿUmar, from ʿUmar: that he said to the Prophet ﷺ: Do you see that in which we work: has it been finished with, or is it in something started afresh, or an originated matter? He said: “In what has been finished with.” ʿUmar said: Should we not rely? He said: “Work, O Ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, for each is made ready. As for the one who is of the people of happiness, he works for happiness; and as for the people of wretchedness, he works for wretchedness.”
items.ma-197: Hushaym narrated to us, al-Zuhrī informed us, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah ibn Masʿūd, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās informed me, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf narrated to me: that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb gave a khuṭbah to the people, and he heard him say: Indeed, some people say: What of the rajm? In the Book of Allah is the flogging! But the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stoned, and we stoned after him. And had it not been that some would say, or some would speak, that ʿUmar added to the Book of Allah what is not part of it, I would have affirmed it as it was sent down.
items.ma-198: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: I heard Yazīd ibn Khumayr narrating from Ḥabīb ibn ʿUbayd, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from Ibn al-Simṭ: that he came to a land called Dawmīn, at a distance of eighteen miles from Ḥimṣ, and prayed two rakʿahs. I said to him: Do you pray two rakʿahs? He said: I saw ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah praying two rakʿahs, so I asked him, and he said: I only do as I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do – or he said: as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did.
items.ma-199: I read to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī: Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb, from Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿUmar, he said: A man from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the mosque on the day of Jumuʿah while ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was giving the khuṭbah to the people, and ʿUmar said: What hour is this? He said: O Commander of the Believers, I returned from the market, heard the call, and did no more than perform ablution. ʿUmar said: And ablution also, when you certainly knew that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command ghusl?!
items.ma-200: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, he said: The polytheists would not depart from Jamʿ until the sun shone upon Thabīr, so the Prophet ﷺ opposed them and departed before the sun rose.
items.ma-201: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, Abū al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh say: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb informed me that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “I will surely expel the Jews and the Christians from the Arabian Peninsula, until I leave none but a Muslim.”
items.ma-202: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from his father: that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, while he was standing giving the khuṭbah on the day of Jumuʿah, a man from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ entered, and ʿUmar called out to him: What hour is this? He said: I was busy today and did not return to my family until I heard the call, and I did no more than perform ablution. ʿUmar said: Ablution also, when you [all] knew – and in another place: when you knew – that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command ghusl?!
items.ma-203: Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim narrated to us, ʿIkrimah – meaning Ibn ʿAmmār – narrated to us, Simāk al-Ḥanafī Abū Zumayl narrated to me, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās narrated to me, ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb narrated to me, he said: On the day of Khaybar a group of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ came forward and said: So-and-so is a shahīd, so-and-so is a shahīd, until they passed by a man and said: So-and-so is a shahīd. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “No. I saw him in the Fire, in a cloak that he took as ghulūl, or a robe.” Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O Ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, go and call out among the people: None enters Paradise except the believers.” He said: So I went out and called out: Indeed, none enters Paradise except the believers.
items.ma-204: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd narrated to us, Dāwūd – meaning Ibn Abī al-Furāt – narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Buraydah narrated to me, from Abū al-Aswad al-Dīlī, he said: I came to al-Madīnah while a sickness had befallen it, and they were dying rapidly. I sat with ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and a funeral procession passed by him, and good was said of its occupant, and ʿUmar said: It is obligatory. Then another passed by, and good was said of its occupant, and he said: It is obligatory. Then a third passed by, and evil was said of its occupant, and ʿUmar said: It is obligatory. I said: What is obligatory, O Commander of the Believers? He said: I said as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Any Muslim for whom four testify to good, Allah will admit him to Paradise.” He said: We said: Or three? He said: “Or three.” We said: Or two? He said: “Or two.” Then we did not ask him about one.
items.ma-205: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Ḥaywah narrated to us, Bakr ibn ʿAmr informed me that he heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hubayrah say that he heard Abū Tamīm al-Jayshānī say: he heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb say: that he heard the Prophet of Allah ﷺ say: “If you were to rely upon Allah with the due reliance upon Him, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds: they go out in the morning empty-bellied and return in the evening full-bellied.”
items.ma-206:
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Saʿīd ibn Abī Ayyūb narrated to me, ʿAṭāʾ ibn Dīnār narrated to me, from Ḥakīm ibn Sharīk al-Hudhalī, from Yaḥyā ibn Maymūn al-Ḥaḍramī, from Rabīʿah al-Jurashī, from Abū Hurayrah, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Do not sit with the people of al-qadar, and do not open conversation with them.”
And Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān once said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-207: Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn Khumayr al-Hamdānī Abū ʿUmar, he said: I heard Ḥabīb ibn ʿUbayd narrating from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from Ibn al-Simṭ: that he went out with ʿUmar to Dhū al-Ḥulayfah and he prayed two rakʿahs, and I asked him about that, and he said: I only do as I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do.
items.ma-208:
Abū Nūḥ Qurād narrated to us, ʿIkrimah ibn ʿAmmār informed us, Simāk al-Ḥanafī Abū Zumayl narrated to us, Ibn ʿAbbās narrated to me, ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb narrated to me, he said: On the day of Badr – he said – the Prophet ﷺ looked at his Companions, and they were three hundred and some, and he looked at the polytheists, and they were a thousand and more. The Prophet ﷺ faced the qiblah, then stretched out his hands, and upon him were his cloak and his izār, then said: “O Allah, where is what You promised me? O Allah, fulfil what You promised me. O Allah, if You destroy this band of the people of Islam, You will not be worshipped on the earth ever.” He said: He kept appealing for help to his Rabb ﷿ and supplicating to Him until his cloak fell. Abū Bakr came to him, took his cloak and put it on him, then clung to him from behind and said: O Prophet of Allah, thus is your entreaty of your Rabb, for He will fulfil for you what He promised you. And Allah ﷿ sent down: {When you were appealing to your Rabb for help, so He responded to you: Indeed I am reinforcing you with a thousand of the angels, following one another} [al-Anfāl: 9].
When it was that day, and they met, Allah ﷿ defeated the polytheists; seventy men of them were killed and seventy men of them were taken captive. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ consulted Abū Bakr, ʿAlī and ʿUmar. Abū Bakr said: O Prophet of Allah, these are the cousins, the clan and the brothers; I think you should take the ransom from them, so that what we take from them becomes strength for us against the disbelievers, and perhaps Allah will guide them and they will be a support for us. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “What do you think, O Ibn al-Khaṭṭāb?” He said: I said: By Allah, I do not think what Abū Bakr thinks, but I think you should give me power over so-and-so – a relative of ʿUmar – so that I strike his neck, and give ʿAlī power over ʿAqīl so that he strikes his neck, and give Ḥamzah power over so-and-so, his brother, so that he strikes his neck, so that Allah knows that there is no leniency in our hearts for the polytheists. These are their chiefs, their leaders and their commanders. But the Messenger of Allah ﷺ inclined to what Abū Bakr said, and did not incline to what I said, and he took the ransom from them.
When it was the next day, ʿUmar said: I went early to the Prophet ﷺ, and he was sitting with Abū Bakr, and they were both weeping. I said: O Messenger of Allah, tell me what makes you weep, you and your companion? If I find weeping, I will weep, and if I do not find weeping, I will feign weeping because of your weeping. He said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “[It is] what your Companions presented to me of the ransom; your punishment was certainly presented to me nearer than this tree” – referring to a nearby tree – and Allah ﷿ sent down: {It is not for a prophet to have captives until he has thoroughly prevailed in the land} up to: {Were it not for a decree from Allah that preceded, there would have touched you, for what you took} [al-Anfāl: 67–68] – of the ransom; then the spoils were made lawful for them.
When it was the day of Uḥud, in the following year, they were punished for what they did on the day of Badr in taking the ransom: seventy of them were killed, the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ fled from the Prophet ﷺ, his incisor was broken, the helmet was smashed on his head, and blood flowed down his face. And Allah Taʿālā sent down: {Is it that when a calamity struck you, though you had struck twice the like of it, you said: How is this? Say: It is from yourselves. Indeed Allah is Qadīr over all things} [Āl ʿImrān: 165] – through your taking the ransom.
items.ma-209: Abū Nūḥ narrated to us, Mālik ibn Anas narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, he said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey. He said: I asked him about something three times and he did not reply to me. He said: I said to myself: May your mother lose you, O Ibn al-Khaṭṭāb! You importuned the Messenger of Allah ﷺ three times and he did not reply to you. He said: So I mounted my mount and went ahead, fearing that something had been revealed about me. He said: Then there was a caller calling: O ʿUmar, where is ʿUmar? He said: I went back, thinking that something had been revealed about me. He said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “A sūrah was revealed to me last night that is dearer to me than the world and what is in it: {Indeed We have opened for you an evident opening. That Allah may forgive for you what preceded of your sin and what came after} [al-Fatḥ: 1–2].”
items.ma-210: Abū al-Naḍr narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī narrated to us, from Ḥakīm ibn Jubayr, from Mūsā ibn Ṭalḥah, from Ibn al-Ḥawtakiyyah, he said: Food was brought to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and he invited a man to it, and he said: I am fasting. Then he said: And which fast do you fast? Were it not for my dislike of adding or subtracting, I would narrate to you the hadith of the Prophet ﷺ when the bedouin came to him with the hare; but send for ʿAmmār. When ʿAmmār came, he said: Were you present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day the bedouin came to him with the hare? He said: Yes. He said: I saw blood on it. He said: “Eat it.” He said: I am fasting. He said: “And which fast do you fast?” He said: The beginning of the month and its end. He said: “If you are fasting, then fast the thirteenth, the fourteenth and the fifteenth.”
items.ma-211: Abū al-Naḍr narrated to us, Abū ʿAqīl narrated to us, Mujālid ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, ʿĀmir informed us, from Masrūq ibn al-Ajdaʿ, he said: I met ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and he said to me: Who are you? I said: Masrūq ibn al-Ajdaʿ. ʿUmar said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Al-Ajdaʿ is a devil.” But you are Masrūq ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān. ʿĀmir said: Then I saw him written in the register: Masrūq ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and I said: What is this? He said: ʿUmar ﵁ named me thus.
items.ma-212: Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, from Jaʿfar ibn Rabīʿah, from al-Zuhrī, from Muḥarrar ibn Abī Hurayrah, from his father, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb: that the Prophet ﷺ forbade ʿazl with a free woman except with her permission.
items.ma-213: Abū ʿĀmir ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, he said: Hishām – meaning Ibn Saʿd – narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, he said: I heard ʿUmar say: If I live to this coming year, no town will be opened for the people but I will divide it among them as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ divided Khaybar.
items.ma-214: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Zubayrī narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿUmar, he said: I was with the Prophet ﷺ on a campaign, and I swore: No, by my father! A man called out to me from behind me and said: “Do not swear by your fathers.” And it was the Prophet ﷺ.
items.ma-215: Abū Aḥmad al-Zubayrī narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Jābir, from ʿUmar, he said: If I live, if Allah wills, I will surely expel the Jews and the Christians from the Arabian Peninsula.
items.ma-216: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd Abū Dāwūd narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from his father, from ʿUmar, he said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wipe over the khuffs.
items.ma-217: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd Abū Dāwūd narrated to us, Sallām – meaning Abū al-Aḥwaṣ – narrated to us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from Sayyār ibn al-Maʿrūr, he said: I heard ʿUmar giving a khuṭbah, saying: Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ built this mosque while we were with him, the Muhājirūn and the Anṣār. When the crowding becomes severe, let a man among you prostrate on the back of his brother. And he saw some people praying in the road, and said: Pray in the mosque.
items.ma-218: I read to Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd: Zuhayr said: Abū Isḥāq narrated to us, from Ḥārithah ibn Muḍarrib: that he performed Ḥajj with ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and the nobles of the people of al-Shām came to him and said: O Commander of the Believers, we have acquired slaves and animals, so take from our wealth a ṣadaqah by which you purify us, and which will be zakāh for us. He said: This is something that neither of my two predecessors did, but wait until I ask the Muslims.
items.ma-219: Rawḥ and Muʾammal narrated to us, they both said: Sufyān al-Thawrī narrated to us, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “If I live, I will surely expel the Jews and the Christians from the Arabian Peninsula, until I leave in it none but a Muslim.”
items.ma-220: ʿAttāb ibn Ziyād narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh – meaning Ibn al-Mubārak – informed us, Yūnus informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from al-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd and ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb – ʿAbd Allāh said: and my father took it up to the Prophet ﷺ – he said: “Whoever misses something of his wird – or he said: of his ḥizb – from the night, and recites it between the Fajr prayer and the Ẓuhr, it is as though he recited it during his night.”
items.ma-221:
Abū Nūḥ Qurād narrated to us, ʿIkrimah ibn ʿAmmār narrated to us, Simāk al-Ḥanafī Abū Zumayl narrated to us, Ibn ʿAbbās narrated to me, ʿUmar narrated to me, he said: On the day of Badr – he said – the Prophet ﷺ looked at his Companions, and they were three hundred and some, and he looked at the polytheists, and they were a thousand and more. The Prophet ﷺ faced the qiblah, then stretched out his hands, and upon him were his cloak and his izār, then said: “O Allah, where is what You promised me? O Allah, fulfil what You promised me. O Allah, if You destroy this band of the people of Islam, You will not be worshipped on the earth ever.” He said: He kept appealing for help to his Rabb and supplicating to Him until his cloak fell. Abū Bakr came to him and took his cloak [and put it on him, then clung to him from behind, and said: O Prophet of Allah, thus is your entreaty of your Rabb, for He will fulfil for you what He promised you]. And Allah Taʿālā sent down: {When you were appealing to your Rabb for help, so He responded to you: Indeed I am reinforcing you with a thousand of the angels, following one another}.
When it was that day, and they met, Allah defeated the polytheists; seventy men of them were killed and seventy men of them were taken captive. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ consulted Abū Bakr, ʿAlī and ʿUmar. Abū Bakr said: O Prophet of Allah, these are the cousins, the clan and the brothers; I think you should take the ransom from them, so that what we take from them becomes strength for us against the disbelievers, and perhaps Allah will guide them and they will be a support for us. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “What do you think, O Ibn al-Khaṭṭāb?” He said: I said: By Allah, I do not think what Abū Bakr thinks, but I think you should give me power over so-and-so – a relative of ʿUmar – so that I strike his neck, and give ʿAlī power over ʿAqīl so that he strikes his neck, and give Ḥamzah power over so-and-so, his brother, so that he strikes his neck, so that Allah knows that there is no leniency in our hearts for the polytheists. These are their chiefs, their leaders and their commanders. But the Messenger of Allah ﷺ inclined to what Abū Bakr said, and did not incline to what I said, and he took the ransom from them.
When it was the next day, ʿUmar said: I went early to the Prophet ﷺ, and he was sitting with Abū Bakr, and they were both weeping. I said: O Messenger of Allah, tell me what makes you weep, you and your companion? If I find weeping, I will weep, and if I do not find weeping, I will feign weeping because of your weeping. He said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “[It is] what your Companions presented to me of the ransom, and your punishment was certainly presented to me nearer than this tree” – referring to a nearby tree – and Allah Taʿālā sent down: {It is not for a prophet to have captives until he has thoroughly prevailed in the land} up to His saying: {would have touched you for what you took} – of the ransom; then the spoils were made lawful for them.
When it was the day of Uḥud, in the following year, they were punished for what they did on the day of Badr in taking the ransom: seventy of them were killed, the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ fled from the Prophet ﷺ, his incisor was broken, the helmet was smashed on his head, and blood flowed down his face. So Allah sent down: {Is it that when a calamity struck you} up to His saying: {Indeed Allah is Qadīr over all things} – through your taking the ransom.
items.ma-222:
ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Thawr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I kept being eager to ask ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb about the two women of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ about whom Allah Taʿālā said: {If you two repent to Allah, your hearts have indeed inclined} [al-Taḥrīm: 4], until ʿUmar performed Ḥajj and I performed Ḥajj with him. When we were on part of the road, ʿUmar turned aside, and I turned aside with him with the water-skin; he went to relieve himself, then came to me, and I poured upon his hands, and he performed ablution. I said: O Commander of the Believers, who are the two women of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ about whom Allah Taʿālā said: {If you two repent to Allah, your hearts have indeed inclined}? ʿUmar said: How astonishing of you, O Ibn ʿAbbās! – al-Zuhrī said: By Allah, he disliked what he asked him about, yet he did not conceal it from him – He said: They are Ḥafṣah and ʿĀʾishah.
He said: Then he began to relate the hadith. He said: We, the assembly of Quraysh, were a people who dominated women. When we came to al-Madīnah, we found a people whose women dominated them, and our women began to learn from their women. He said: And my house was among Banū Umayyah ibn Zayd in al-ʿAwālī. He said: I became angry with my wife one day, and she was answering me back, and I denounced that she answered me back. She said: What do you denounce in my answering you back? By Allah, the wives of the Prophet ﷺ answer him back, and one of them forsakes him for the day until the night. He said: So I went off and entered upon Ḥafṣah and said: Do you answer back the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? She said: Yes. I said: And does one of you forsake him for the day until the night? She said: Yes. I said: He has failed and lost, whoever of you does that. Does one of you feel safe that Yaghḍaba Allāh ʿalayhā because of the anger of His Messenger, so that she is destroyed? Do not answer back the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and do not ask him for anything, and ask me whatever occurs to you; and do not let it deceive you that your neighbour is more beautiful and dearer to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ than you – he means ʿĀʾishah.
He said: And I had a neighbour from the Anṣār, and we used to take turns going down to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: he would go down one day, and I would go down one day; he would bring me news of the revelation and other things, and I would bring him the like of that. He said: And we used to say that Ghassān was shoeing horses to attack us. My companion went down one day, then came to me in the evening and knocked on my door, then called me, and I went out to him, and he said: A great matter has occurred. I said: What is it? Has Ghassān come? He said: No, rather greater than that and longer: the Messenger has divorced his wives. I said: Ḥafṣah has failed and lost; I had thought this would happen.
When I had prayed the Ṣubḥ, I tightened my garments about me, then went down and entered upon Ḥafṣah, and she was weeping. I said: Has the Messenger of Allah ﷺ divorced you? She said: I do not know; he is secluded in that upper room. So I went to a black boy of his and said: Ask permission for ʿUmar. The boy entered, then came out to me and said: I mentioned you to him, and he was silent. I went off until I came to the minbar, and there was a group sitting by it, some of them weeping. I sat a little, then what I felt overcame me. I went to the boy and said: Ask permission for ʿUmar. He entered, then came out to me and said: I mentioned you to him, and he was silent. So I went out and sat by the minbar; then what I felt overcame me. I went to the boy and said: Ask permission for ʿUmar. He entered, then came out to me and said: I mentioned you to him, and he was silent. So I turned my back to leave, and the boy was calling me. He said: Enter, he has given you permission. I entered and greeted the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he was reclining on the plaiting of a mat – and Yaʿqūb narrated it to us in the hadith of Ṣāliḥ, he said: rumāl of a mat – which had left a mark on his side. I said: Have you divorced your wives, O Messenger of Allah? He raised his head to me and said: “No.” I said: Allāhu akbar! If you had seen us, O Messenger of Allah – we, the assembly of Quraysh, were a people who dominated women; when we came to al-Madīnah, we found a people whose women dominated them, and our women began to learn from their women. I became angry with my wife one day, and she was answering me back, and I denounced that she answered me back. She said: What do you denounce in my answering you back? By Allah, the wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ answer him back, and one of them forsakes him for the day until the night. I said: He has failed and lost, whoever of them does that. Does one of them feel safe that Yaghḍaba Allāh ʿalayhā because of the anger of His Messenger, so that she is destroyed? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled. I said: O Messenger of Allah, I entered upon Ḥafṣah and said: Do not let it deceive you that your neighbour is more beautiful and dearer to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ than you. He smiled again. I said: May I be at ease, O Messenger of Allah? He said: “Yes.” So I sat, and I raised my head in the house, and by Allah, I did not see in it anything that draws back the sight except three skins. I said: Supplicate, O Messenger of Allah, that He make [things] ample for your ummah, for [things] have been made ample for Persia and Rome, and they do not worship Allah. He sat upright, then said: “Are you in doubt, O Ibn al-Khaṭṭāb? Those are a people whose good things have been hastened for them in the life of this world.” I said: Ask forgiveness for me, O Messenger of Allah. And he had sworn not to enter upon them for a month because of the intensity of his displeasure with them, until Allah ﷿ rebuked him.
items.ma-223: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Yūnus ibn Sulaym informed me, he said: Yūnus ibn Yazīd al-Aylī dictated to me, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd al-Qārī: I heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb say: When revelation descended upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, a humming like the humming of bees would be heard at his face. We remained for a while, then he faced the qiblah and raised his hands and said: “O Allah, increase us and do not diminish us; honour us and do not humiliate us; give us and do not deprive us; favour us and do not favour [others] over us; and Irḍa ʿannā, and make us pleased.” Then he said: “Ten verses have been revealed to me; whoever establishes them enters Paradise.” Then he recited to us: {Successful indeed are the believers} until he completed the ten verses.
items.ma-224: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from Abū ʿUbayd, the mawlā of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf: that he attended the ʿĪd with ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and he prayed before giving the khuṭbah, without adhān and without iqāmah, then gave the khuṭbah and said: O people, indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade fasting on these two days. As for one of them, it is the day of your breaking the fast from your fasting and your ʿĪd; and as for the other, it is a day on which you eat from your nusuk.
items.ma-225: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, al-Zuhrī narrated to me, from Saʿd Abū ʿUbayd, the mawlā of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Azhar, he said: I attended the ʿĪd with ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb … then he mentioned the hadith.
items.ma-226: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, that ʿUmar kissed the Stone, then said: I know that you are a stone, and had I not seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kiss you, I would not have kissed you.
items.ma-227: Hushaym narrated to us, Sayyār informed me, from Abū Wāʾil: that a man who was a Christian, called al-Ṣubayy ibn Maʿbad, accepted Islam, and wanted jihād, and it was said to him: Begin with Ḥajj. So he came to al-Ashʿarī, who commanded him to raise the talbiyah for the ʿumrah and the Ḥajj together, and he did so. While he was saying the talbiyah, he passed by Zayd ibn Ṣūḥān and Salmān ibn Rabīʿah, and one of them said to his companion: This one is more astray than the camel of his family. Al-Ṣubayy heard it, and it weighed heavily upon him. When he arrived, he came to ʿUmar and mentioned that to him, and ʿUmar said to him: You have been guided to the sunnah of your Prophet. He said: And I heard him another time say: You have been granted success in the sunnah of your Prophet.
items.ma-228: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿUmar, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to converse at night with Abū Bakr, on nights like that, about a matter of the affairs of the Muslims, and I was with him.
items.ma-229: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sarjis, he said: I saw al-Uṣayliʿ – meaning ʿUmar – kiss the Stone and say: I kiss you although I know that you are a stone that neither benefits nor harms, and had I not seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kiss you, I would not have kissed you.
items.ma-230: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allāh narrated to us, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, from ʿUmar: I said: O Messenger of Allah, may one of us sleep while he is in a state of janābah? He said: “Yes, if he performs ablution.”
items.ma-231: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Hishām informed us, from his father, from ʿĀṣim, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When the night approaches and the day departs and the sun has set, you have broken your fast.”
items.ma-232: Abū Kāmil narrated to us, Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd narrated to us, Ibn Shihāb narrated to us. (ḥ) And ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, in meaning, from Abū al-Ṭufayl ʿĀmir ibn Wāthilah: that Nāfiʿ ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥārith met ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb at ʿUsfān, and ʿUmar had appointed him over Makkah, and ʿUmar said to him: Whom have you appointed as successor over the people of the valley? He said: I appointed Ibn Abzā as successor over them. He said: And who is Ibn Abzā? He said: A man from our mawālī. ʿUmar said: You appointed a mawlā as successor over them! He said: He is a reciter of the Book of Allah, knowledgeable in the farāʾiḍ, a judge. ʿUmar said: Indeed your Prophet ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah raises by this Book some peoples and lowers by it others.”
items.ma-233: Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, Ismāʿīl ibn Sumayʿ narrated to us, from Muslim al-Baṭīn, from Abū al-Bakhtarī, he said: ʿUmar said to Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ: Stretch out your hand so that I may pledge allegiance to you, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “You are the amīn of this ummah.” Abū ʿUbaydah said: I would not go ahead of a man whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded to lead us [in prayer], and who led us until he died.
items.ma-234: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from Shaqīq ibn Salamah, from Salmān ibn Rabīʿah, from ʿUmar, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a distribution, and I said: O Messenger of Allah, others than these are more deserving of it than they. The Prophet ﷺ said: “They have given me the choice between asking me with indecency or declaring me stingy, and I am not stingy.”
items.ma-235: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar informed us, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar: that ʿUmar asked the Prophet ﷺ: May one of us sleep while he is in a state of janābah? He said: “Yes, and he performs his ablution for the prayer.”
items.ma-236: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar: that ʿUmar asked the Prophet ﷺ … the like of it.
items.ma-237:
ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar informed us, from Nāfiʿ, he said: Ibn ʿUmar saw Saʿd ibn Mālik wiping over his khuffs, and Ibn ʿUmar said: And you do this? Saʿd said: Yes. So the two gathered with ʿUmar, and Saʿd said: O Commander of the Believers, give a ruling to my brother's son concerning wiping over the khuffs. ʿUmar said: We, while we were with our Prophet ﷺ, used to wipe over our khuffs. Ibn ʿUmar said: Even if he has come from defecation and urination? ʿUmar said: Yes, even if he has come from defecation and urination. Nāfiʿ said: So Ibn ʿUmar after that used to wipe over them as long as he did not take them off, and he did not set a time limit for that.
I narrated it to Maʿmar, and he said: Ayyūb narrated it to me, from Nāfiʿ, the like of it.
items.ma-238: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, Mālik ibn Aws ibn al-Ḥadathān informed me, he said: I exchanged silver for gold with Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, and he said: Give me time until our treasurer comes to us from al-Ghābah. He said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb heard it and said: No, by Allah, do not part from him until you receive in full your ṣarf from him, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Gold for silver is ribā except hāʾa wa-hāʾa.”
items.ma-239: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, he said: When the people of the apostasy apostatised in the time of Abū Bakr, ʿUmar said: How will you fight the people, O Abū Bakr, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I have been commanded to fight the people until they say: There is no deity except Allah; so when they say: There is no deity except Allah, they have protected from me their blood and their wealth, except by its right, and their reckoning is upon Allah”? Abū Bakr said: By Allah, I will fight whoever separates between the prayer and the zakāh, for the zakāh is the right of the wealth. By Allah, if they withheld from me a young female goat that they used to pay to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I would fight them over it. ʿUmar said: By Allah, it was only that I saw that Allah had opened the chest of Abū Bakr for fighting, so I knew that it was the truth.
items.ma-240: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Isrāʾīl informed us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: ʿUmar said: I was in a riding party, travelling on a campaign with the Prophet ﷺ, and I swore, saying: No, by my father! A man behind me rebuked me and said: “Do not swear by your fathers.” I turned, and there was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-241: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from his father, from ʿUmar, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard me swearing by my father, and said: “Indeed Allah forbids you to swear by your fathers.” ʿUmar said: By Allah, I have not sworn by them since then, mentioning it or relating it.
items.ma-242: Khalaf ibn al-Walīd narrated to us, Khālid narrated to us, from Khālid, from Abū ʿUthmān, from ʿUmar: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave a concession regarding silk in [the measure of] two fingers.
items.ma-243:
Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, al-Taymī narrated to us, from Abū ʿUthmān, he said: We were with ʿUtbah ibn Farqad, and ʿUmar wrote to him about things, narrating from the Prophet ﷺ; among what he wrote to him was that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “None wears silk in this world except one who will have no share of it in the Hereafter, except thus,” and he said with his two fingers: the index and the middle.
Abū ʿUthmān said: I thought that it meant the buttons of the shawls, when we saw the shawls.
items.ma-244: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī ʿAmmār narrated to me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bābayh, from Yaʿlā ibn Umayyah, he said: I said to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb: People's shortening the prayer today, when Allah ﷿ only said: {if you fear that those who disbelieve will subject you to fitnah} [al-Nisāʾ: 101] – that has gone today! He said: I was amazed at what you were amazed at, so I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: “A ṣadaqah with which Allah has given ṣadaqah to you, so accept His ṣadaqah.”
items.ma-245: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us: I heard ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī ʿAmmār narrating; then he mentioned it.
items.ma-246: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ibn Abī ʿArūbah, Qatādah narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, he said: ʿUmar said: Indeed the last of the Qurʾān to be revealed was the verse of ribā, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken without having explained it, so leave ribā and doubt.
items.ma-247: Yaḥyā narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from Ibn ʿUmar, from ʿUmar, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “The dead is punished in his grave by the wailing over him.”
items.ma-248: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from ʿUbayd Allāh, Nāfiʿ informed me, from Ibn ʿUmar, from ʿUmar ﵁, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “The dead is punished by his family's weeping over him.”
items.ma-249: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Yaḥyā, he said: I heard Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab say that ʿUmar said: Beware of perishing over the verse of the rajm, [and that someone should say:] We do not find two ḥadds in the Book of Allah. For I saw the Prophet ﷺ stone, and we stoned.
items.ma-250: Yaḥyā narrated to us, Ḥumayd narrated to us, from Anas, he said: ʿUmar said: I agreed with my Rabb in three – or: my Rabb agreed with me in three – I said: O Messenger of Allah, if only you took the Maqām Ibrāhīm as a place of prayer? So Allah sent down: {And take from the Maqām of Ibrāhīm a place of prayer}. I said: O Messenger of Allah, the righteous and the wicked enter upon you; if only you commanded the Mothers of the Believers to observe ḥijāb. So Allah sent down the verse of the ḥijāb. And the Prophet's ﵇ rebuking some of his wives reached me. He said: So I went through the Mothers of the Believers, and entered upon them, and began going through them one by one: By Allah, if you do not desist, then Allah will surely substitute for His Messenger ones better than you. He said: Then I came to one of his wives, and she said: O ʿUmar, does the Messenger of Allah ﷺ not have what admonishes his wives, that you should be the one to admonish them? So Allah sent down: {Perhaps his Rabb, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you}.
items.ma-251: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, Abū Dhibyān narrated to me, I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr say: Do not clothe your women in silk, for I heard ʿUmar narrating from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: “Whoever wears silk in this world will not wear it in the Hereafter.” And ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr said, from himself: And whoever does not wear it in the Hereafter does not enter Paradise. Allah Taʿālā said: {And their clothing therein is silk}.
items.ma-252: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl, ʿĀmir narrated to us. And Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid narrated to us, from a man, from al-Shaʿbī, he said: ʿUmar passed by Ṭalḥah – then he mentioned its meaning – he said: ʿUmar passed by Ṭalḥah and saw him distressed, and said: Perhaps the leadership of your cousin has displeased you – he said: meaning Abū Bakr – He said: No, but I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Indeed I know a word that no man says at his death except that it will be a light in his page, or he will find relief in it at death.” ʿUmar said: I will inform you of it. It is the word that he wanted for his uncle: the testimony that there is no deity except Allah. He said: It was as though a covering had been removed from me. He said: You have spoken truly; had he known a word more excellent than it, he would have commanded him with it.
items.ma-253: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, Sulaymān ibn ʿAtīq narrated to me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bābayh, from Yaʿlā ibn Umayyah, he said: I performed ṭawāf with ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and when I was at the Rukn that adjoins the door, on the side that adjoins the Stone, I took his hand so that he would touch it, and he said: Did you not perform ṭawāf with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? I said: Yes. He said: Did you see him touch it? I said: No. He said: Then pass on, for you have in the Messenger of Allah an excellent example.
items.ma-254: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, Shaqīq narrated to us, al-Ṣubayy ibn Maʿbad narrated to me – and he was a man of Banū Taghlib – he said: I was a Christian and I accepted Islam, and I strove and spared no effort, so I raised the talbiyah for a Ḥajj and an ʿumrah, and I passed by al-ʿUdhayb on Salmān ibn Rabīʿah and Zayd ibn Ṣūḥān, and one of them said: With both together? His companion said to him: Leave him, he is surely more astray than his camel. He said: It was as though my camel were on my neck. I came to ʿUmar and mentioned that to him, and ʿUmar said to me: They said nothing. You have been guided to the sunnah of your Prophet ﷺ.
items.ma-255: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from ʿUbayd Allāh, Nāfiʿ narrated to me, from Ibn ʿUmar, from ʿUmar, that he said: O Messenger of Allah, I vowed in the Jāhiliyyah to observe iʿtikāf in the Masjid al-Ḥarām for a night. He said to him: “Then fulfil your vow.”
items.ma-256: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from Manṣūr, from Abū Wāʾil, from Ṣubayy ibn Maʿbad al-Taghlibī, he said: I was recent in my association with Christianity, and I wanted jihād or Ḥajj. I came to a man of my people called Hudaym, and asked him, and he commanded me to perform Ḥajj. So I combined the Ḥajj and the ʿumrah … then he mentioned it.
items.ma-257: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us. And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Sufyān, from Zubayd al-Iyāmī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿUmar, he said: The prayer of travel is two rakʿahs, the prayer of al-Aḍḥā is two rakʿahs, the prayer of al-Fiṭr is two rakʿahs, and the prayer of Jumuʿah is two rakʿahs – complete, not shortened – upon the tongue of Muḥammad ﷺ. Sufyān said: And Zubayd once said: I think it is from ʿUmar. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said it not in the form of doubt. And Yazīd – meaning Ibn Hārūn – said: Ibn Abī Laylā said: I heard ʿUmar.
items.ma-258: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Hishām ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from ʿUmar: that he found a horse that he had given to carry [someone] in the path of Allah being sold in the market, and wanted to buy it, so he asked the Prophet ﷺ, and he forbade him and said: “Do not return to your ṣadaqah.”
items.ma-259: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Khālid, from Qays, he said: I saw ʿUmar with a palm-frond in his hand, making the people sit, saying: Listen to the word of the khalīfah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then a mawlā of Abū Bakr called Shadīd came with a page and read it to the people, saying: Abū Bakr says: Listen and obey the one in this page, for by Allah, I have not fallen short with you. Qays said: Then I saw ʿUmar after that on the minbar.
items.ma-260: Muʾammal narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Salamah, from ʿImrān al-Sulamī, he said: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās about nabīdh, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade nabīdh of the jar and the gourd. Then I met Ibn ʿUmar and asked him, and he informed me – as I think – from ʿUmar: that the Prophet ﷺ forbade nabīdh of the jar and the gourd – Sufyān doubted. He said: Then I met Ibn al-Zubayr and asked him, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade nabīdh of the jar and the gourd.
items.ma-261:
Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Abū Sinān, from ʿUbayd ibn Ādam, Abū Maryam and Abū Shuʿayb: that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was at al-Jābiyah … then he mentioned the conquest of Bayt al-Maqdis.
He said: Abū Salamah said: Abū Sinān narrated to me, from ʿUbayd ibn Ādam, he said: I heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb say to Kaʿb: Where do you think I should pray? He said: If you take from me, you will pray behind the Rock, so that all of al-Quds is in front of you. ʿUmar said: You have imitated Judaism. No, but I will pray where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed. He went forward toward the qiblah and prayed, then came and spread his cloak and swept the sweepings into his cloak, and the people swept.
items.ma-262: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, Mālik – meaning Ibn Mighwal – narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿAmr, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿUmar, he said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the kalālah, and he said: “The verse of the summer suffices you.” He said: That I should have asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about it is dearer to me than that I should have red camels.
items.ma-263: Abū Aḥmad Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dīnār, from Ibn ʿUmar, from ʿUmar: that he came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: Janābah comes upon me. So he commanded him to wash his private part and to perform his ablution for the prayer.
items.ma-264: ʿAffān narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Qazaʿah, he said: I said to Ibn ʿUmar: Does Allah punish this dead person by the weeping of this living? He said: ʿUmar ﵁ narrated to me from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; I have not lied about ʿUmar, and ʿUmar did not lie about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-265: ʿAffān narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ziyād narrated to us, al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUbayd Allāh narrated to us, Ibrāhīm narrated to us, from ʿAlqamah, from al-Qarthaʿ, from Qays or Ibn Qays – a man of Juʿfī – from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed – and I was with him, and Abū Bakr – by ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd while he was reciting, and he stood and listened to his recitation, then ʿAbd Allāh bowed and prostrated. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Ask and you will be given; ask and you will be given.” He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went on and said: “Whoever is pleased to recite the Qurʾān fresh as it was sent down, let him recite it from Ibn Umm ʿAbd.” He said: So I set out in the night to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd to give him glad tidings of what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said. He said: When I knocked on the door – or he said: when he heard my voice – he said: What brought you at this hour? I said: I came to give you glad tidings of what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said. He said: Abū Bakr has preceded you. I said: If he has done so, he is a great racer to good deeds; we never raced to any good except that Abū Bakr preceded us to it.
items.ma-266: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Saʿīd al-Jurayrī, from Abū Naḍrah, from Usayr ibn Jābir, he said: When the people of Yemen came, ʿUmar began going through the companies, saying: Is there anyone among you from Qaran? until he came to Qaran, and said: Who are you? They said: Qaran. Then the rein of ʿUmar fell – or the rein of Uways – and one of them handed it to the other – or: he handed – and he recognised him. ʿUmar said: What is your name? He said: I am Uways. He said: Do you have a mother? He said: Yes. He said: Was there any whiteness in you? He said: Yes, so I supplicated Allah ﷿ and He removed it from me except for a place the size of a dirham at my navel, that I might remember my Rabb by it. ʿUmar said to him: Ask forgiveness for me. He said: You are more deserving that you ask forgiveness for me, you are a Companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. ʿUmar said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Indeed the best of the Tābiʿūn is a man called Uways; he has a mother, and he had whiteness, so he supplicated Allah ﷿ and He removed it from him except for a place the size of a dirham at his navel.” So he asked forgiveness for him, then entered into the crowds of people, and it was not known where he ended up. He said: Then he came to al-Kūfah. He said: We used to gather in a circle and remember Allah, and he would sit with us, and when he spoke, his speech would fall in our hearts in a place that the speech of no one else falls … then he mentioned the hadith.
items.ma-267: Narrated to us [ʿAbd Allāh; Muḥammad ibn narrated to me] ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abī al-Shawārib, ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ziyād narrated to us, al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUbayd Allāh narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, [from ʿAlqamah], from al-Qarthaʿ, from Qays, or Ibn Qays – a man of Juʿfī – from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, then he mentioned the like of the hadith of ʿAffān.
items.ma-268: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, Thābit narrated to us, from Anas: that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, when Ḥafṣah wailed over him, said: O Ḥafṣah, did you not hear the Prophet ﷺ say: “The one who is wailed over is punished.” He said: And Ṣuhayb wailed, and ʿUmar said: O Ṣuhayb, did you not know that the one who is wailed over is punished?
items.ma-269: ʿAffān narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Wāḥid narrated to us, Yazīd al-Rishk narrated to us, from Muʿādhah, from Umm ʿAmr daughter of ʿAbd Allāh, that she heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr narrating that he heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb giving a khuṭbah; he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever wears silk in this world will not be clothed in it in the Hereafter.”
items.ma-270: ʿAffān narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, Abū al-ʿĀliyah narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAbbās: Men with whom I am satisfied narrated to me, among them ʿUmar – and ʿAffān once said: Men with whom I am satisfied testified before me, and the one with whom I am most satisfied is ʿUmar – that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no prayer after two prayers: after the Ṣubḥ until the sun rises, and after the ʿAṣr until the sun sets.”
items.ma-271: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abān narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, with the like of this: Men with whom I am satisfied testified before me.
items.ma-272: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Ṭāriq ibn Shihāb: that the Jews said to ʿUmar: You recite a verse which, had it been revealed about us, we would have taken that day as an ʿĪd. He said: I know where it was revealed, and on what day it was revealed, and where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was when it was revealed: it was revealed on the day of ʿArafah while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was standing at ʿArafah – Sufyān said: and I doubt whether it was Friday or not – meaning: {Today I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favour upon you, and Raḍītu for you Islam as religion} [al-Māʾidah: 3].
items.ma-273: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Ṭāriq ibn Shihāb, from Abū Mūsā, he said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was at al-Baṭḥāʾ, and he said: “With what did you raise the talbiyah?” I said: With a talbiyah like the talbiyah of the Prophet ﷺ. He said: “Did you drive any sacrificial animal?” I said: No. He said: “Perform ṭawāf of the House and of Ṣafā and Marwah, then come out of iḥrām.” So I performed ṭawāf of the House and of Ṣafā and Marwah, then I came to a woman of my people and she combed my hair and washed my head. I used to give people a fatwā with that during the leadership of Abū Bakr and the leadership of ʿUmar. While I was standing at the season, a man came to me and said: You do not know what the Commander of the Believers has newly introduced concerning the nusuk. I said: O people, whoever we have given a fatwā, this is the Commander of the Believers coming to you, so take him as your leader. When he arrived I said: What is this that you have newly introduced concerning the nusuk? He said: If we take by the Book of Allah, then Allah said: {And complete the Ḥajj and the ʿumrah for Allah} [al-Baqarah: 196]; and if we take by the sunnah of our Prophet ﷺ, he did not come out of iḥrām until he slaughtered the sacrificial animal.
items.ma-274: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Suwayd ibn Ghafalah, he said: I saw ʿUmar kissing the Stone and saying: Indeed I know that you are a stone, you neither harm nor benefit, but I saw Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ showing you great kindness.
items.ma-275: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān. And ʿAbd al-Razzāq: Sufyān informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, he said: ʿUmar said – ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: I heard ʿUmar –: Indeed the polytheists used not to depart from Jamʿ until the sun shone upon Thabīr – ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: and they used to say: Shine, Thabīr, that we may raid – meaning: so the Prophet ﷺ opposed them and set off before the sun rose.
items.ma-276: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Mālik narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: ʿUmar said: Indeed Allah Taʿālā sent Muḥammad ﷺ and sent down the Book upon him, and among what He sent down upon him was the verse of the rajm. We recited it, understood it, and preserved it. I fear that a long time will pass over the people and they will say: We do not find the verse of the rajm, so an obligation that Allah sent down will be left. And the rajm in the Book of Allah Taʿālā is a right upon whoever commits zinā when he is muḥṣan, among men and women, when the proof is established, or there is pregnancy, or confession.
items.ma-277: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Mālik, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, he said: I heard Hishām ibn Ḥakīm reciting Sūrat al-Furqān in the prayer in a way other than I recite it, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had taught me to recite it. So I took hold of his garment and went with him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and said: O Messenger of Allah, I heard him reciting Sūrat al-Furqān in a way other than you taught me to recite it. He said: “Recite.” So he recited the recitation that I had heard from him, and he said: “Thus it was sent down.” Then he said to me: “Recite.” So I recited, and he said: “Thus it was sent down. Indeed this Qurʾān was sent down upon seven aḥruf, so recite what is easy.”
items.ma-278: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwah, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd al-Qārī: that they both heard ʿUmar say: I passed by Hishām ibn Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām reciting Sūrat al-Furqān … then he mentioned its meaning.
items.ma-279: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from al-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Saʿdī, he said: ʿUmar said to me: Was I not told that you take charge of some of the work of the people, and when you are given the wage you do not accept it? He said: Yes. He said: Then what do you want by that? He said: I am wealthy; I have slaves and I have horses; I want my work to be a ṣadaqah upon the Muslims. He said: Do not do so, for I used to do what you are doing. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would give me the gift, and I would say: Give it to one more in need of it than I. He said: “Take it, then either make it wealth of your own or give it in ṣadaqah; and whatever Allah gives you of this wealth while you are neither eager for it nor asking for it, take it; and what is not so, do not let your self follow after it.”
items.ma-280: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from al-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd, he said: ʿUmar met ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Saʿdī; then he mentioned its meaning, except that he said: “Give it in ṣadaqah, and do not let your self follow after it.”
items.ma-281: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Mālik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, he said: I gave a horse to carry [someone] in the path of Allah, and its owner wasted it. I wanted to buy it, and I thought that he would sell it cheaply, so I said: Not until I ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: “Do not buy it, even if he gives it to you for a dirham, for the one who returns to his ṣadaqah is like the dog that returns to its vomit.”
items.ma-282: I read to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān: from Mālik, from Ibn Shihāb, from Abū ʿUbayd, the mawlā of Ibn Azhar, that he said: I witnessed the ʿĪd with ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb. He came and prayed, then turned away and gave a khuṭbah to the people, and said: Indeed these are two days on which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade fasting: the day of your breaking your fast from your fasting, and the other, a day on which you eat from your nusuk.
items.ma-283: Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Isḥāq, from Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh, he said: ʿUmar was a man of fierce protective jealousy, and when he went out to the prayer, ʿĀtikah daughter of Zayd would follow him. He disliked her going out, and disliked preventing her. And he used to narrate that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When your women ask your permission for the prayer, do not prevent them.”
items.ma-284: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Mālik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from ʿUmar, he said: Were it not for the last of the Muslims, no town would be conquered except that I would divide it as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ divided Khaybar.
items.ma-285:
Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Salamah ibn ʿAlqamah narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn, he said: I was told from Abū al-ʿAjfāʾ al-Sulamī, he said: I heard ʿUmar say: Beware, do not inflate the dowers of women; beware, do not inflate the dowers of women. For if it were an honour in this world, or taqwā with Allah, the Prophet ﷺ would have been the most deserving of you in it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not give a dower to any of his wives, nor was any of his daughters given a dower, of more than twelve ūqiyahs. And a man is tried by the dower of his wife – and once he said: a man inflates the dower of his wife – until there is enmity toward her in his self, and until he says: I have been burdened for you with the strap of the waterskin. He said: And I was an Arab youth of mixed origin, and I did not know what the strap of the waterskin was.
He said: And another thing you say of one who is killed in your campaigns, or dies: So-and-so was killed a shahīd, and so-and-so died a shahīd – and perhaps he had loaded the rear of his animal, or the side of his riding-beast, with gold or silver, seeking trade. Do not say that, but say as the Prophet said – or as Muḥammad ﷺ said: “Whoever is killed or dies in the path of Allah is in Paradise.”
items.ma-286:
Ismāʿīl narrated to us, al-Jurayrī Saʿīd informed us, from Abū Naḍrah, from Abū Firās, he said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb gave a khuṭbah and said: O people, beware! We used only to know you when the Prophet ﷺ was among us, when the revelation was coming down, and when Allah would apprise us of your news. Beware! The Prophet ﷺ has departed and the revelation has ceased, and we know you only by what we say to you: whoever among you shows good, we think good of him and love him for it, and whoever among you shows evil to us, we think evil of him and hate him for it. Your secrets are between you and your Rabb. Beware! There came upon me a time when I reckoned that whoever recited the Qurʾān desired Allah and what is with Him, and then it was imagined to me at last – beware! – that men have recited it desiring by it what is with the people. So desire Allah by your recitation, and desire Him by your deeds.
Beware! By Allah, I do not send my officials to you to strike your skins, nor to take your wealth, but I send them to you to teach you your religion and your sunnah. So whoever has anything done to him other than that, let him raise it to me, for by Him in whose hand is my self, I will then surely have retaliation taken from him. ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ leapt up and said: O Commander of the Believers, do you see, if a man of the Muslims is over some subjects and disciplines one of his subjects, will you indeed take retaliation from him? He said: Yes, by Him in whose hand is the self of ʿUmar, I will then surely have retaliation taken from him. How could I not have retaliation taken from him when I have seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ give retaliation against himself? Beware! Do not strike the Muslims so that you humiliate them, do not keep them long [in the field] so that you put them to fitnah, do not withhold their rights from them so that you make them ungrateful, and do not make them settle in the thickets so that you lose them.
items.ma-287:
Ismāʿīl narrated to us another time, Salamah ibn ʿAlqamah informed us, from Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn, he said: I was told from Abū al-ʿAjfāʾ, he said: I heard ʿUmar say: Beware, do not inflate the dowers of women … then he mentioned the hadith.
Ismāʿīl said: Ayyūb, Hishām and Ibn ʿAwn mentioned, from Muḥammad, from Abū al-ʿAjfāʾ, from ʿUmar, something like the hadith of Salamah, except that they said: Muḥammad did not say: I was told from Abū al-ʿAjfāʾ.
items.ma-288:
Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Mulaykah, he said: I was with ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, and we were waiting for the funeral of Umm Abān daughter of ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, and with him was ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān. Ibn ʿAbbās came, led by his guide. He said: I think he informed him of the place of Ibn ʿUmar. He came and sat beside me, and I was between them. Then there was a voice from the house, and Ibn ʿUmar said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Indeed the dead is punished by the weeping of his family over him.” ʿAbd Allāh left it unqualified. Ibn ʿAbbās said: We were with the Commander of the Believers ʿUmar, until, when we were at al-Baydāʾ, there was a man dismounted in the shade of a tree. He said to me: Go and find out who that is. I went, and it was Ṣuhayb. I returned to him and said: You commanded me to find out for you who that is, and it is Ṣuhayb. He said: Order him to join us. I said: He has his family with him. He said: Even if he has his family with him – and Ayyūb once said: Let him join us – When we reached al-Madīnah, the Commander of the Believers was not long before he was struck. Ṣuhayb came and said: Oh my brother! Oh my companion! ʿUmar said: Did you not know, or did you not hear – or he said: did you not know, did you not hear – that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed the dead is punished by some of the weeping of his family over him”? As for ʿAbd Allāh, he left it unqualified, and as for ʿUmar, he said: “by some of the weeping.”
So I came to ʿĀʾishah and mentioned to her the saying of ʿUmar, and she said: No, by Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not say that the dead is punished by the weeping of anyone, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah ﷿ increases the disbeliever in punishment by the weeping of his family.” And indeed Allah, it is He who made laugh and made weep, {and no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another} [al-Anʿām: 164].
Ayyūb said: And Ibn Abī Mulaykah said: al-Qāsim narrated to me, he said: When the saying of ʿUmar and Ibn ʿUmar reached ʿĀʾishah, she said: You narrate to me from two who are neither liars nor denied, but hearing errs.
items.ma-289: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Mulaykah informed me … then he mentioned the meaning of the hadith of Ayyūb, except that he said: Ibn ʿUmar said to ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, who was facing him: Will you not forbid weeping? For the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed the dead is punished by the weeping of his family over him.”
items.ma-290: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Mulaykah informed me, he said: A daughter of ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān died in Makkah, and Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbās attended her, and I was sitting between them. Ibn ʿUmar said to ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān, who was facing him: Will you not forbid weeping? For the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed the dead is punished by the weeping of his family over him” … then he mentioned something like the hadith of Ismāʿīl, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah.
items.ma-291: Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: ʿUmar said: I was in a riding party, travelling on a campaign with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I swore, saying: No, by my father! A man behind me called out to me: “Do not swear by your fathers.” I turned, and there was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-292: Muḥammad ibn Muyassar Abū Saʿd al-Ṣāghānī narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from Mālik ibn Aws ibn al-Ḥadathān, he said: ʿUmar used to swear three oaths, saying: By Allah, no one is more entitled to this wealth than another, and I am not more entitled to it than anyone; by Allah, there is none of the Muslims except that he has a share in this wealth, except an owned slave; but we are according to our ranks from the Book of Allah, and our division from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: the man and his trial in Islam, the man and his precedence in Islam, the man and his usefulness in Islam, and the man and his need. And by Allah, if I remain for them, his share of this wealth will surely come to the shepherd at the mountain of Ṣanʿāʾ while he is grazing in his place.
items.ma-293: ʿAbd al-Quddūs ibn al-Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Ṣafwān narrated to us, Abū al-Mukhāriq Zuhayr ibn Sālim narrated to me that ʿUmayr ibn Saʿd al-Anṣārī, whom ʿUmar had appointed over Ḥimṣ … then he mentioned the hadith. ʿUmar said – meaning to Kaʿb: Indeed I ask you about a matter, so do not conceal it from me. He said: By Allah, I will not conceal from you anything I know. He said: What is the thing you fear most for the Ummah of Muḥammad ﷺ? He said: Misleading imams. ʿUmar said: You have spoken truly; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ confided that to me and let me know it.
items.ma-294: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ, Ibn Shihāb said: Sālim said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar say: ʿUmar said: Send me a physician to look at this wound of mine. He said: So they sent for a physician of the Arabs, who gave ʿUmar nabīdh to drink, and the nabīdh was likened to blood when it came out of the stab that was beneath the navel. He said: Then I called another physician, from the Anṣār, of Banū Muʿāwiyah, who gave him milk to drink, and the milk came out of the stab solid white. The physician said to him: O Commander of the Believers, make your will. ʿUmar said: The brother of Banū Muʿāwiyah has told me the truth, and had you said other than that, I would have called you a liar. He said: The people wept over him when they heard that. He said: Do not weep for us. Whoever is weeping, let him go out. Did you not hear what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said? He said: “The dead is punished by the weeping of his family over him.” For that reason ʿAbd Allāh would not approve of weeping being done in his presence over one who had perished, of his children or others.
items.ma-295: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, al-Thawrī informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, he said: I heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb say: The people of the Jāhiliyyah used not to depart from Jamʿ until they saw the sun upon Thabīr, and they used to say: Shine, Thabīr, that we may raid. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ departed before the rising of the sun.
items.ma-296: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwah, from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd al-Qārī: that they both heard ʿUmar say: I passed by Hishām ibn Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām reciting Sūrat al-Furqān during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and I listened to his recitation, and he was reciting in many ḥurūf that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had not taught me to recite. I nearly leapt upon him in the prayer, but I waited until he gave the salām. When he gave the salām, I seized him by his cloak and said: Who taught you to recite this sūrah that you recite? He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught it to me. He said: I said to him: You lied! By Allah, the Prophet ﷺ himself taught me this sūrah that you recite. He said: So I set off, leading him to the Prophet ﷺ, and said: O Messenger of Allah, I heard this one reciting Sūrat al-Furqān in ḥurūf that you did not teach me, and you taught me Sūrat al-Furqān! The Prophet ﷺ said: “Release him, O ʿUmar.
