Recite, O Hishām.” So he recited to him the recitation that I had heard, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “Thus it was sent down.” Then the Prophet ﵇ said: “Recite, O ʿUmar.” So I recited the recitation that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had taught me, and he said: “Thus it was sent down.” Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed the Qurʾān was sent down upon seven aḥruf, so recite of it what is easy.”
items.ma-297: Al-Ḥakam ibn Nāfiʿ narrated to us, Shuʿayb informed us, from al-Zuhrī, ʿUrwah narrated to me from the hadith of al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd al-Qārī: that they both heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb say: I heard Hishām ibn Ḥakīm ibn Ḥizām reciting Sūrat al-Furqān during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ, and I listened to his recitation, and he was reciting in many ḥurūf that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had not taught me to recite. I nearly leapt upon him in the prayer, but I waited until he gave the salām. When he gave the salām … then he mentioned its meaning.
items.ma-298: Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, from Zāʾidah, from ʿĀṣim, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: ʿUmar said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever of you is seeking Laylat al-Qadr, let him seek it in the last ten, in the odd [nights].”
items.ma-299: Muḥammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, Hishām ibn ʿUrwah narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn ʿUmar: that it was said to ʿUmar: Will you not appoint a successor? He said: If I leave it, then one who is better than I left it: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; and if I appoint a successor, then one who is better than I appointed a successor: Abū Bakr.
items.ma-300: Yazīd narrated to us, Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd informed us that Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm informed him that he heard ʿAlqamah ibn Waqqāṣ al-Laythī say: that he heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, while he was giving a khuṭbah to the people, saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Action is only by intention, and each man will have only what he intended. So whoever's hijrah was to Allah and to His Messenger, his hijrah is to Allah and to His Messenger; and whoever's hijrah was for some worldly [gain] that he will obtain, or a woman whom he will marry, his hijrah is to that to which he made hijrah.”
items.ma-301: Yazīd narrated to us, ʿĀṣim informed us, from Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb that he said: Wear a waist-wrapper and wear a cloak, and wear sandals, and throw off the khuffs and the trousers, and throw off the stirrups and leap with a leap, and keep to the Maʿaddiyyah, and shoot at the targets, and leave luxury and the dress of the non-Arabs, and beware of silk, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has forbidden it and said: “Do not wear of silk except what is like this,” and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pointed with his two fingers.
items.ma-302: Yazīd narrated to us, Yaḥyā informed us, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: Beware of perishing over the verse of the rajm, and of someone saying: We do not find two ḥadds in the Book of Allah. For I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stone, and we stoned after him.
items.ma-303: Yazīd narrated to us, al-ʿAwwām informed us, a shaykh who was keeping guard at the coast narrated to me, he said: I met Abū Ṣāliḥ, the mawlā of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and he said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb narrated to us, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: “There is no night but that the sea looks out three times over the land, asking Allah's permission to burst upon them, and Allah ﷿ restrains it.”
items.ma-304: Yazīd narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Malik informed us, from Anas ibn Sīrīn, he said: I said to Ibn ʿUmar: Narrate to me about your divorcing your wife. He said: I divorced her while she was menstruating. He said: I mentioned that to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and he mentioned it to the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “Order him to take her back, and when she is pure, let him divorce her in her purity.” He said: I said to him: Did you count the one you divorced while she was menstruating? He said: Why would I not count it, even if I was incapable and acted foolishly?
items.ma-305: Yazīd narrated to us, Aṣbagh informed us, from Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Shāmī, he said: Abū Umāmah put on a new garment, and when it reached his collarbone he said: Praise be to Allah who clothed me with what I cover my ʿawrah with and adorn myself with in my life. Then he said: I heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever acquires a new garment and wears it, and says when it reaches his collarbone: Praise be to Allah who clothed me with what I cover my ʿawrah with and adorn myself with in my life, then goes to the garment that had become worn – or he said: that he cast off – and gives it in ṣadaqah, will be in the dhimmah of Allah, in the neighbourhood of Allah, and in the shelter of Allah, living and dead, living and dead, living and dead.”
items.ma-306: Yazīd narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq informed us, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, he said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I said: O Messenger of Allah, when one of us wants to sleep while in janābah, what should he do before he bathes? He said: “He performs his ablution as for the prayer, then sleeps.”
items.ma-307:
Yazīd narrated to us, Warqāʾ informed us. And Abū al-Naḍr said: Warqāʾ narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā al-Thaʿlabī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, he said: I was with al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib, and ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was at al-Baqīʿ looking at the new moon. A rider came, and ʿUmar met him and said: Where have you come from? He said: From the west. He said: Did you sight the new moon? He said: Yes. ʿUmar said: Allāhu Akbar, one man suffices for the Muslims. Then ʿUmar stood and performed ablution, and wiped over his khuffs, then prayed the Maghrib, then said: Thus I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do.
Abū al-Naḍr said: And he was wearing a cloak with narrow sleeves, so he took his hand out from beneath it and wiped.
items.ma-308: Yazīd narrated to us, Jarīr informed us, al-Zubayr ibn al-Khirrīt informed us, from Abū Labīd, he said: A man from Ṭāḥiyah went out as a muhājir, called Bayraḥ ibn Asad, and he came to al-Madīnah some days after the death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. ʿUmar saw him and knew that he was a stranger, and said to him: Who are you? He said: From the people of ʿUmān. He said: From the people of ʿUmān? He said: Yes. He said: So he took him by the hand and brought him in to Abū Bakr ﵁, and said: This one is from the people of the land about which I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Indeed I know a land called ʿUmān; the sea splashes at its side; in it is a tribe of the Arabs; had my messenger come to them, they would not have thrown at him an arrow or a stone.”
items.ma-309: Yazīd narrated to us, ʿĀṣim ibn Muḥammad informed us, from his father, from Ibn ʿUmar, from ʿUmar – he said: I do not know it except that he raised it – he said: “Allah ﵎ says: Whoever humbles himself to Me thus – and Yazīd began to put the inside of his palm toward the ground, bringing it near to the ground – I raise him thus – and he put the inside of his palm toward the sky, and raised it toward the sky –.”
items.ma-310: Yazīd narrated to us, Daylam ibn Ghazwān al-ʿAbdī informed us, Maymūn al-Kurdī narrated to us, from Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī, he said: I was sitting beneath the minbar of ʿUmar while he was giving a khuṭbah to the people, and he said in his khuṭbah: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Indeed what I fear most for this Ummah is every hypocrite learned of tongue.”
items.ma-311: Rawḥ narrated to us, Mālik narrated to us (ḥ) And Isḥāq narrated to us, Mālik informed me. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad said: And Muṣʿab al-Zubayrī narrated to us, Mālik narrated to me, from Zayd ibn Abī Unaysah, that ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn al-Khaṭṭāb informed him, from Muslim ibn Yasār al-Juhanī, that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was asked about this verse: {And when your Rabb took from the children of Ādam, from their loins, their offspring} – the verse [al-Aʿrāf: 172]. ʿUmar said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ being asked about it, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah created Ādam, then wiped his back with His Yamīn and brought forth from him offspring, and said: I created these for Paradise, and by the deeds of the people of Paradise they will act. Then He wiped his back and brought forth from him offspring, and said: I created these for the Fire, and by the deeds of the people of the Fire they will act.” A man said: O Messenger of Allah, then what is the deed for? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah ﷿, when He creates a servant for Paradise, employs him in the deeds of the people of Paradise until he dies upon one of the deeds of the people of Paradise, and enters him by it into Paradise; and when He creates a servant for the Fire, He employs him in the deeds of the people of the Fire until he dies upon one of the deeds of the people of the Fire, and enters him by it into the Fire.”
items.ma-312: Rawḥ narrated to us, Mālik ibn Anas narrated to us, from Ibn Shihāb, from Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, from his father: that a man of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the mosque on the day of Jumuʿah while ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was standing giving a khuṭbah. ʿUmar said: What hour is this? He said: O Commander of the Believers, I turned back from the market and heard the call, and I did no more than perform ablution and come. ʿUmar said: Ablution also?! And you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command us to bathe.
items.ma-313: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, Sulaymān ibn ʿAtīq informed me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bābayh, from some of the sons of Yaʿlā, from Yaʿlā ibn Umayyah, he said: I performed ṭawāf with ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and he touched the Rukn. Yaʿlā said: I was on the side next to the House, and when I reached the western Rukn that adjoins the Black [Stone], I pulled his hand so that he would touch, and he said: What is the matter with you? I said: Will you not touch? He said: Did you not perform ṭawāf with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? I said: Yes. He said: Did you see him touch these two western Arkān? I said: No. He said: Do you not have in him an excellent example? I said: Yes. He said: Then move on.
items.ma-314: ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmar and Abū ʿĀmir narrated to us, both said: Mālik narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Mālik ibn Aws ibn al-Ḥadathān, he said: I came with dinars of mine, wanting to exchange them, and Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh met me, and he exchanged them and took them, and said: Until my treasurer comes – Abū ʿĀmir said: from al-Ghābah, and he said throughout it: hāʾa wa-hāʾa – so I asked ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb about that, and he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Gold for silver is ribā except hāʾa wa-hāt, wheat for wheat is ribā except hāʾa wa-hāt, barley for barley is ribā except hāʾa wa-hāt, and dates for dates is ribā except hāʾa wa-hāt.”
items.ma-315: ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, Yūnus informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, that ʿUmar said: Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The dead is punished by the weeping of his family over him.”
items.ma-316: Bakr ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from al-Mughīrah, from al-Shaʿbī, from ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim, he said: I came to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb with some people of my tribe, and he began to assign an allowance to a man of Ṭayyiʾ of two thousand, and to turn away from me. He said: So I faced him, and he turned away from me, then I came to him from in front of his face, and he turned away from me. He said: I said: O Commander of the Believers, do you know me? He said: He laughed until he fell back on his neck, then said: Yes, by Allah, I know you. You believed when they disbelieved, you came forward when they turned back, and you were faithful when they betrayed. And the first ṣadaqah that whitened the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the faces of his Companions was the ṣadaqah of Ṭayyiʾ; you brought it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then he began to excuse himself, and then said: I only assigned [allowances] to a people whom want had ravaged, and they are the chiefs of their clans, because of the rights that befall them.
items.ma-317: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, Hishām ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, he said: I heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb say: Why the ramal now, and the uncovering of the shoulders, when Allah has made Islam firm and driven out kufr and its people? Yet with that we do not leave anything we used to do in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-318: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad and ʿAffān narrated to us, both said: Dāwūd ibn Abī al-Furāt narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Buraydah narrated to us – ʿAffān said: from Ibn Buraydah –, from Abū al-Aswad al-Dīlī, he said: I came to al-Madīnah, and a sickness had broken out there – ʿAbd al-Ṣamad said: they were dying rapidly – so I sat with ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and a funeral passed by him, and its owner was praised with good, and he said: It has become obligatory. Then another passed, and its owner was praised with good, and he said: It has become obligatory. Then another passed, and it was praised with evil, and ʿUmar said: It has become obligatory. Abū al-Aswad said: I said to him: O Commander of the Believers, what has become obligatory? He said: I said as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Any Muslim for whom four bear witness to good, Allah will enter him into Paradise.” He said: We said: And three? He said: “And three.” We said: And two? He said: “And two.” He said: And we did not ask him about one.
items.ma-319: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, Ḥarb – meaning Ibn Shaddād – narrated to us, Yaḥyā narrated to us, Abū Salamah narrated to us, Abū Hurayrah narrated to us, he said: While ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was giving a khuṭbah, a man came and sat. ʿUmar said: Why do you hold yourselves back from the Jumuʿah? The man said: O Commander of the Believers, it was only that I heard the call, so I performed ablution, then came. ʿUmar said: And also?! Did you not hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “When one of you goes out to the Jumuʿah, let him bathe”?
items.ma-320: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, my father narrated to me, al-Ḥusayn al-Muʿallim narrated to us, Yaḥyā narrated to us, Abū Salamah informed me that Abū Hurayrah informed him: that ʿUmar, while he was giving a khuṭbah … then he mentioned it.
items.ma-321: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, Ḥarb narrated to us, Yaḥyā narrated to us, from ʿImrān ibn Ḥiṭṭān – as Ḥarb thinks –: that he asked Ibn ʿAbbās about wearing silk, and he said: Ask ʿĀʾishah about it. So he asked ʿĀʾishah, and she said: Ask Ibn ʿUmar. So he asked Ibn ʿUmar, and he said: Abū Ḥafṣ narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever wears silk in this world has no share in the Hereafter.”
items.ma-322: Yaḥyā ibn Ḥammād and ʿAffān narrated to us, both said: Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Dāwūd ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Awdī, from Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥimyarī, Ibn ʿAbbās narrated to us in al-Baṣrah, he said: I was the first to come to ʿUmar when he was stabbed, and he said: Preserve from me three things, for I fear that the people will not reach me: As for me, I have not issued a ruling on the kalālah, I have not appointed a khalīfah over the people, and every slave of his is freed. The people said to him: Appoint a successor. He said: Whichever of that I do, one who is better than I has done it. If I leave to the people their affair, the Prophet of Allah ﵊ left it, and if I appoint a successor, one who is better than I appointed a successor: Abū Bakr. I said to him: Receive glad tidings of Paradise: you accompanied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and prolonged his companionship, and you were given charge of the affair of the Believers, and you became strong and discharged the trust. He said: As for your giving me glad tidings of Paradise, by Allah, if I had – ʿAffān said: no, by Allah, there is no deity except Him, if I had – the world and what is in it, I would ransom myself with it from the terror of what is before me, before I know the outcome. And as for your saying about the affair of the Believers, by Allah, I would love that it be even, neither for me nor against me. And as for what you mentioned of the companionship of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, that is so.
items.ma-323: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAyyāsh, from Ḥakīm ibn Ḥakīm, from Abū Umāmah ibn Sahl, he said: ʿUmar wrote to Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ: Teach your boys swimming and your fighters archery. They used to go back and forth to the targets, and a stray arrow came to a boy and killed him, and no kin was found for him, and he was in the care of a maternal uncle of his. So Abū ʿUbaydah wrote about him to ʿUmar [[To whom shall I give his blood-money?]] (*), and ʿUmar wrote to him: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say: “Allah and His Messenger are the mawlā of one who has no mawlā, and the maternal uncle is the heir of one who has no heir.”
items.ma-324: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zayd narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “The walāʾ is inherited by whoever inherits the wealth from a father or a child.”
items.ma-325: Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿĀbis ibn Rabīʿah, he said: I saw ʿUmar come to the Stone and say: By Allah, I know that you are a stone, you neither harm nor benefit, and had I not seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kiss you, I would not have kissed you. Then he drew near and kissed it.
items.ma-326: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Dujayn Abū al-Ghuṣn, a Baṣran, narrated to us, he said: I came to al-Madīnah and met Aslam, the mawlā of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and said: Narrate to me from ʿUmar. He said: I cannot; I fear that I would add or omit. When we said to ʿUmar: Narrate to us from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: I fear that I would add a letter or omit one. Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever lies about me is in the Fire.”
items.ma-327: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, the mawlā of the family of al-Zubayr, from Sālim, from his father, from ʿUmar, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever says in a market: There is no deity except Allah alone, He has no partner; to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs the praise; in His Yad is the good; He gives life and causes death, and He is over everything Qadīr, Allah writes for him by it a thousand thousand good deeds, effaces from him by it a thousand thousand evil deeds, and builds for him a house in Paradise.”
items.ma-328: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, ʿIkrimah ibn ʿAmmār narrated to us, Abū Zumayl narrated to us, Ibn ʿAbbās narrated to me, ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb narrated to me, he said: On the day of Khaybar, a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came saying: So-and-so is a shahīd, and so-and-so is a shahīd, until they passed by a man and said: So-and-so is a shahīd. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “No! I saw him being dragged to the Fire in a cloak that he had taken in ghulūl. Go out, O ʿUmar, and call out among the people: None enters Paradise except the believers.” So I went out and called out: None enters Paradise except the believers.
items.ma-329: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, Saʿīd ibn Masrūq narrated to us, from Saʿd ibn ʿUbaydah, from Ibn ʿUmar, from ʿUmar, that he said: No, by my father! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Stop! Whoever swears by anything other than Allah has committed shirk.”
items.ma-330: Ḥammād al-Khayyāṭ narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, from Nāfiʿ: that ʿUmar enlarged the mosque from the pillar to the maqṣūrah, and ʿUthmān enlarged it; and ʿUmar said: Had I not heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “We ought to enlarge our mosque,” I would not have enlarged it.
items.ma-331:
ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah ibn Masʿūd, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿUmar, that he said: Indeed Allah ﷿ sent Muḥammad ﷺ with the truth and sent down the Book with him, and among what was sent down upon him was the verse of the rajm, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stoned, and we stoned after him. Then he said: We used to recite: And do not turn away from your fathers, for it is kufr in you – or: indeed kufr in you – to turn away from your fathers.
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do not praise me excessively as Ibn Maryam was praised excessively; I am only a servant, so say: His servant and His Messenger.”
And Maʿmar sometimes said: “as the Christians praised Ibn Maryam excessively.”
items.ma-332: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Sālim, from Ibn ʿUmar, that he said to ʿUmar: I heard the people saying a statement, and I swore that I would say it to you: they claimed that you are not going to appoint a successor. He lowered his head for a while, then raised it and said: Indeed Allah ﷿ protects His religion. If I do not appoint a successor, then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not appoint a successor; and if I appoint a successor, then Abū Bakr appointed a successor. He said: By Allah, it was only that he mentioned the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abū Bakr, and I knew that he would not equate anyone with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and that he was not going to appoint a successor.
items.ma-333: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Mālik ibn Aws ibn al-Ḥadathān, he said: ʿUmar sent for me … then he mentioned the hadith, and I said to you both: Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “We are not inherited from; what we leave is ṣadaqah.”
items.ma-334: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Ibn al-Musayyab, he said: When Abū Bakr died, he was wept over, and ʿUmar said: Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The dead is punished by the weeping of the living.”
items.ma-335: Ibrāhīm ibn Khālid narrated to us, Rabāḥ narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, from Abū Hurayrah, he said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died, and those who disbelieved disbelieved, ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: O Abū Bakr, how will you fight the people when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I have been commanded to fight the people until they say: There is no deity except Allah; so whoever says: There is no deity except Allah has protected from me his wealth and his self, and his reckoning is upon Allah ﷿”? Abū Bakr said: I will surely fight whoever separates between the prayer and the zakāh; indeed the zakāh is the right of the wealth. By Allah, if they withheld from me a young female goat that they used to pay to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I would fight them over it. ʿUmar said: By Allah, it was only that I saw that Allah had opened the chest of Abū Bakr for fighting, so I knew that it was the truth.
items.ma-336: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from al-Zuhrī, from Mālik ibn Aws, from ʿUmar, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “We are not inherited from; what we leave is ṣadaqah.”
items.ma-337: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from al-Zuhrī, from Mālik ibn Aws, he said: ʿUmar sent for me … then he mentioned the hadith, and said: Indeed the wealth of Banū al-Naḍīr was among what Allah bestowed as fayʾ upon His Messenger, that for which the Muslims had not urged on horses or riding-camels; so he would spend on his family from it the provision of their year, and what remained he put into horses and weapons as preparation in the path of Allah ﷿.
items.ma-338: Sufyān narrated to us, from Hishām, from his father, from ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUmar, from his father, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “When the night comes forward, the day turns back, and the sun sets, the one fasting has broken his fast.”
items.ma-339: Sufyān narrated to us, from Yaḥyā – meaning Ibn Saʿīd – from ʿUbayd ibn Ḥunayn, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: I wanted to ask ʿUmar, but I did not find an opening, so I waited two years. When we were at Marr al-Ẓahrān, and he went to relieve himself, and came back having relieved himself, I went to pour water on him, and I said: O Commander of the Believers, who were the two women who backed one another against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? He said: ʿĀʾishah and Ḥafṣah.
items.ma-340:
Sufyān narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from Ibn Sīrīn, he heard it from Abū al-ʿAjfāʾ: I heard ʿUmar say: Do not inflate the dowers of women, for if it were an honour in this world, or taqwā in the Hereafter, the Prophet ﷺ would have been the most deserving of you in it; he did not marry off any of his daughters, nor any of his wives, for more than twelve ūqiyahs.
And another thing you say in your campaigns: So-and-so was killed a shahīd, so-and-so died a shahīd – and perhaps he had loaded the rear of his animal, or the side of his riding-beast, with gold and silver, seeking trade. Do not say that, but say as Muḥammad ﷺ said: “Whoever is killed in the path of Allah is in Paradise.”
items.ma-341:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūbah narrated to us – he dictated it to me – from Qatādah, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd al-Ghaṭafānī, from Maʿdān ibn Abī Ṭalḥah al-Yaʿmarī: that ʿUmar stood giving a khuṭbah, and praised Allah and extolled Him, and mentioned the Prophet of Allah ﷺ and Abū Bakr, then said: I saw a dream: it was as though a rooster pecked me two pecks, and I do not see that as anything but the arrival of my appointed time. People command me to appoint a successor, and Allah ﷿ would not let His khilāfah and His religion be lost, nor that with which He sent His Prophet ﷺ. So if a matter hastens upon me, the khilāfah is a consultation among these six, with whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was pleased when he died. So whichever of them you pledge allegiance to, listen to him and obey. I know that men will attack this matter, and I fought them with this hand of mine for Islam; so if they do so, those are the enemies of Allah, the disbelievers, the astray.
By Allah, I do not leave after me anything of greater concern to me than the matter of the kalālah. I asked the Prophet of Allah ﷺ about it, and he was never harsher with me about anything than he was about it, until he poked with his hand – or with his finger – in my chest – or my side – and said: “O ʿUmar, the verse that was revealed in the summer suffices you, the one at the end of Sūrat al-Nisāʾ.” And if I live, I will pass a judgment on it about which no one will differ, whether he recites the Qurʾān or does not recite the Qurʾān.
Then he said: O Allah, I call You to witness against the governors of the regions, for I sent them to teach the people their religion and the sunnah of their Prophet, to divide among them their fayʾ, to deal justly with them, and to raise to me what is unclear to them.
Then he said: O people, you eat from two plants which I consider only foul: this garlic and onion. I used to see a man in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ whose smell was found on him, and he would be taken by the hand until he was taken out to al-Baqīʿ. So whoever must eat them, let him kill them by cooking.
He said: ʿUmar gave this khuṭbah on the day of Jumuʿah, and he was struck on the day of Wednesday, four nights remaining of Dhū al-Ḥijjah.
items.ma-342: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us. He said: And Hushaym informed me, from al-Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāh, from al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtaybah, from ʿUmārah, from Abū Burdah, from Abū Mūsā, that ʿUmar said: It is the sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ – meaning the mutʿah – but I fear that they will spend the wedding night with them under the arāk trees, then set out with them as pilgrims.
items.ma-343: ʿAlī ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to us, Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād informed us, from ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from his father, or his grandfather – the doubt is from Yazīd –, from ʿUmar, he said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform ablution after ḥadath, and wipe over his khuffs and pray.
items.ma-344:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Simāk, he said: I heard ʿIyāḍ al-Ashʿarī say: I witnessed al-Yarmūk, and we had five commanders over us: Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ, Yazīd ibn Abī Sufyān, Ibn Ḥasanah, Khālid ibn al-Walīd, and ʿIyāḍ – and this ʿIyāḍ is not the one who narrated to Simāk – He said: And ʿUmar said: If there is fighting, then Abū ʿUbaydah is over you. He said: So we wrote to him that death had surged toward us, and we asked him for reinforcement. He wrote to us: Your letter has come to me asking me for reinforcement, and I direct you to One who is mightier in victory and more present in forces: Allah ﷿. So seek victory from Him, for Muḥammad ﷺ was given victory on the day of Badr with fewer than your number. When this letter of mine comes to you, fight them and do not return to me.
He said: So we fought them and defeated them, and killed them for four farsakhs. He said: And we took wealth, and they consulted, and ʿIyāḍ advised us to give ten for every head.
He said: And Abū ʿUbaydah said: Who will wager with me? A youth said: I, if you do not become angry. He said: He outstripped him, and I saw the two braids of Abū ʿUbaydah bouncing while he was behind him on an Arabian horse.
items.ma-345: Muḥammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, ʿUyaynah informed us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, he said: I came to al-Madīnah and entered upon Sālim ibn ʿAbd Allāh, and I was wearing a khazz cloak. Sālim said to me: What do you do with these clothes? I heard my father narrating from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Only one who has no share wears silk.”
items.ma-346: Abū al-Mundhir Asad ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, I think from Ḥajjāj, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather, he said: A man killed his son intentionally, and it was raised to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, and he imposed on him a hundred camels: thirty ḥiqqahs, thirty jadhaʿahs, and forty thaniyyahs, and he said: The killer does not inherit; and had I not heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “A father is not killed for his child,” I would have killed you.
items.ma-347: Hushaym and Yazīd narrated to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, he said: ʿUmar said: Had I not heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “The killer has nothing,” I would have made you inherit. He said: And he called the brother of the one killed and gave him the camels.
items.ma-348: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Najīḥ and ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb narrated to me, both from Mujāhid ibn Jabr, then he mentioned the hadith, and said: ʿUmar took of the camels thirty ḥiqqahs, thirty jadhaʿahs, and forty thaniyyahs up to the bāzil of its year, all of them pregnant. He said: Then he called the brother of the one killed and gave them to him rather than to his father, and said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “The killer has nothing.”
items.ma-349: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah ibn Khālid, from Mālik ibn Aws ibn al-Ḥadathān, he said: Al-ʿAbbās and ʿAlī came to ʿUmar disputing, and al-ʿAbbās said: Judge between me and this so-and-so. The people said: Decide between them, decide between them. He said: I will not decide between them; they both know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “We are not inherited from; what we leave is ṣadaqah.”
items.ma-350: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, from Ibn Abī ʿArūbah, from Qatādah, from Ibn al-Musayyab, that ʿUmar said: Indeed among the last of what was revealed is the verse of ribā, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died without having explained it, so leave ribā and doubt.
items.ma-351: Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from ʿUmārah ibn ʿUmayr, from Ibrāhīm ibn Abī Mūsā, from Abū Mūsā: that he used to give a fatwā on the mutʿah, and a man said to him: Go gently with some of your fatwā, for you do not know what the Commander of the Believers has newly introduced regarding the nusuk after you. Until he met him afterwards and asked him, and ʿUmar said: I know that the Prophet ﷺ did it, and his Companions, but I disliked that they should remain with them, spending the wedding night in the arāk trees, and then set out for the Ḥajj with their heads dripping.
items.ma-352: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar and Ḥajjāj narrated to us, both said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm, he said: I heard ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah narrating from Ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, he said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb performed Ḥajj, and wanted to give the people a khuṭbah, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf said: The riffraff of the people have gathered with you, so delay that until you come to al-Madīnah. When he came to al-Madīnah, I drew near to him, close to the minbar, and I heard him say: Some people say: What is the matter with the rajm, when what is in the Book of Allah is only the flogging? Yet the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stoned and we stoned after him. And had it not been that they would say: He has added to the Book of Allah what is not in it, I would have added it as it was sent down.
items.ma-353:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar and Ḥajjāj narrated to us, both said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, he said: I heard al-Nuʿmān – meaning Ibn Bashīr – giving a khuṭbah, saying:
ʿUmar mentioned what the people have received of this world, and said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ spending the day twisting about, not finding even inferior dates to fill his belly with.
items.ma-354:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us. And Ḥajjāj said: Shuʿbah narrated to me, he said: I heard Qatādah narrating from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from Ibn ʿUmar, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “The dead is punished in his grave for that which is wailed over him.”
And Ḥajjāj said: “for the wailing over him.”
items.ma-355: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Qatādah, he said: I heard Rufayʿ Abū al-ʿĀliyah narrating from Ibn ʿAbbās: Men narrated to me – Shuʿbah said: I think he said: of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ; he said: and the most pleasing of them to me is ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb –: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade prayer at two times: after the ʿAṣr until the sun sets, and after the Ṣubḥ until it rises.
items.ma-356: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us. And Ḥajjāj said: Shuʿbah narrated to me, from Qatādah, he said: I heard Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī say: The letter of ʿUmar came to us when we were in Adharbayjān with ʿUtbah ibn Farqad, or in al-Shām: To proceed: Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade silk except thus, two fingers. Abū ʿUthmān said: We did not delay [in realising] that it was the aʿlām.
items.ma-357: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us. And Ḥajjāj and Abū Dāwūd: Shuʿbah narrated to me, from Qatādah, he said: I heard Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī say: The letter of ʿUmar came to us.
items.ma-358: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us. And Abū Dāwūd, from Shuʿbah, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, he said: ʿUmar prayed the Ṣubḥ while at Jamʿ – Abū Dāwūd said: We were with ʿUmar at Jamʿ – and said: Indeed the polytheists used not to depart until the sun rose, and they would say: Shine, Thabīr; and the Prophet of Allah ﷺ opposed them, and departed before the rising of the sun.
items.ma-359: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dīnār, he said: I heard Ibn ʿUmar say: ʿUmar asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying: Janābah comes upon me in the night, so what should I do? He said: “Wash your private part, then perform ablution, then sleep.”
items.ma-360: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, he said: I heard Abū al-Ḥakam say: I asked Ibn ʿUmar about the jar, and he narrated to us from ʿUmar: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the jar, and the gourd, and the pitch-coated vessel.
items.ma-361: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sarjis, he said: I saw al-Uṣayliʿ – meaning ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb – kissing the Stone, and saying: Indeed I know that you are a stone, but I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kissing you.
items.ma-362:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: I heard Abū Jamrah al-Ḍubaʿī narrating from Juwayriyah ibn Qudāmah, he said: I performed Ḥajj and came to al-Madīnah in the year in which ʿUmar was struck. He said: He gave a khuṭbah and said: I saw as though a red rooster pecked me one peck or two pecks – Shuʿbah is the one in doubt –. Then what became of his affair was that he was stabbed, and the people were permitted to enter upon him. The first to enter upon him were the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, then the people of al-Madīnah, then the people of al-Shām, then the people of al-ʿIrāq were permitted, and I entered among those who entered. He said: Whenever a group entered upon him, they praised him and wept.
He said: When we entered upon him – he said: he had bound his belly with a black turban, and the blood was flowing – we said: Counsel us. He said: And no one asked him for counsel other than us. He said: Hold to the Book of Allah, for you will not go astray so long as you follow it. We said: Counsel us. He said: I counsel you regarding the Muhājirūn, for the people will increase and decrease; and I counsel you regarding the Anṣār, for they are the shiʿb of Islam, to which it took refuge; and I counsel you regarding the Bedouins, for they are your origin and your supply; and I counsel you regarding the people of your dhimmah, for they are the covenant of your Prophet and the provision of your dependants. Rise from me. He said: He added nothing to us beyond these words.
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar said: Shuʿbah said: Then I asked him after that, and he said about the Bedouins: And I counsel you regarding the Bedouins, for they are your brothers and the enemy of your enemy.
items.ma-363:
Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Shuʿbah informed us: I heard Abū Jamrah al-Ḍubaʿī narrating from Juwayriyah ibn Qudāmah, he said: I performed Ḥajj and came to al-Madīnah in the year in which ʿUmar was struck. He said: He gave a khuṭbah and said: I saw as though a red rooster pecked me one peck or two pecks – Shuʿbah is the one in doubt – He said: He stayed only a week until he was stabbed … then he mentioned the like of it, except that he said: And I counsel you regarding the people of your dhimmah, for they are the dhimmah of your Prophet.
Shuʿbah said: Then I asked him after that, and he said about the Bedouins: And I counsel you regarding the Bedouins, for they are your brothers and the enemy of your enemy.
items.ma-364: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Saʿīd narrated to us. And ʿAbd al-Wahhāb, from Saʿīd, from Qatādah, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah, from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: Men with whom I am satisfied testified before me, among them ʿUmar, and the one with whom I am most satisfied is ʿUmar: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade prayer after the Ṣubḥ prayer until the sun rises, and after the ʿAṣr until it sets.
items.ma-365: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah, from al-Shaʿbī, from Suwayd ibn Ghafalah: that ʿUmar gave the people a khuṭbah at al-Jābiyah and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade wearing silk except the place of two fingers, or three, or four, and he pointed with his palm.
items.ma-366: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, from Ibn ʿUmar, from ʿUmar, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “The dead is punished in his grave for that which is wailed over him.”
items.ma-367:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Kahmas narrated to us, from Ibn Buraydah. And Yazīd ibn Hārūn said: Kahmas narrated to us, from Ibn Buraydah, from Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar, he heard Ibn ʿUmar say: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb narrated to me, he said: While we were one day with the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, a man appeared before us, intensely white of garments, intensely black of hair, upon whom the mark of travel was not seen – Yazīd said: we did not see – and none of us knew him, until he sat by the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, and rested his knees against his knees, and placed his palms on his thighs.
Then he said: O Muḥammad, inform me about Islam: what is Islam? He said: “Islam is that you testify that there is no deity except Allah and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah, that you establish the prayer, give the zakāh, fast Ramaḍān, and perform Ḥajj to the House if you are able to find a way to it.” He said: You have spoken truly. He said: We were amazed at him, asking him and affirming him.
He said: Then he said: Inform me about īmān. He said: “Īmān is that you believe in Allah, His angels, His Books, His Messengers, and the Last Day, and in al-qadar, all of it, its good and its evil.” He said: You have spoken truly.
He said: Then inform me about iḥsān: what is iḥsān? Yazīd said: “That you worship Allah as though you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then indeed He Yarāka.”
He said: Then inform me about the Hour. He said: “The one asked about it is not more knowing of it than the one asking.” He said: Then inform me about its signs. He said: “That the slave-woman gives birth to her mistress, and that you see the barefoot, naked shepherds of sheep competing in the height of buildings.”
He said: Then he went off. He said: I remained a long while – Yazīd said: three – and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: “O ʿUmar, do you know who the questioner was?” I said: Allah and His Messenger know best. He said: “That was Jibrīl; he came to you to teach you your religion.”
items.ma-368: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd narrated to us, Kahmas narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Buraydah, from Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar, he heard Ibn ʿUmar say: ʿUmar narrated to us, he said: We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ … then he mentioned the hadith, except that he said: and the mark of travel was not seen upon him. And he said: ʿUmar said: I remained three, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: “O ʿUmar.
items.ma-369: Bahz narrated to us. He said: And ʿAffān narrated to us, both said: Hammām narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, from Abū Naḍrah, he said: I said to Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh: Ibn al-Zubayr forbids the mutʿah, and Ibn ʿAbbās commands it. He said: He said to me: The hadith passed through my hands: we performed mutʿah with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ – ʿAffān said: and with Abū Bakr – and when ʿUmar took charge, he gave the people a khuṭbah and said: Indeed the Qurʾān is the Qurʾān, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is the Messenger, and indeed there were two mutʿahs in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: one of them the mutʿah of Ḥajj, and the other the mutʿah of women.
items.ma-370: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah informed us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hubayrah, from Abū Tamīm, that he heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb say: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “If you were to rely upon Allah with the reliance due to Him, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds: they go out in the morning empty-bellied and return in the evening full-bellied.”
items.ma-371: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, Bukayr ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to me, from Busr ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn al-Sāʿidī al-Mālikī, that he said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb appointed me over the ṣadaqah, and when I had finished it and paid it to him, he ordered a wage for me. I said to him: I only worked for Allah, and my reward is upon Allah. He said: Take what you are given, for I worked in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he paid me a wage, and I said what you said, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: “When you are given something without having asked, eat and give ṣadaqah.”
items.ma-372:
Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, Bukayr narrated to me, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Saʿīd al-Anṣārī, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh,
from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb ﵁: that he said: I was delighted one day and kissed while I was fasting, so I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: I did a great thing today: I kissed while fasting. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do you see if you were to rinse your mouth with water while fasting?” I said: There is no harm in that. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Then in what?”
items.ma-373: Yaḥyā ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah informed us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hubayrah narrated to us, he said: I heard Abū Tamīm al-Jayshānī say: I heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “If you were relying upon Allah with the reliance due to Him, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds. Do you not see that they go out in the morning empty-bellied and return in the evening full-bellied?”
items.ma-374:
Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAlqamah ibn Marthad, from Sulaymān ibn Buraydah, from Ibn Yaʿmar, he said: I said to Ibn ʿUmar: We travel to far regions and meet a people who say: There is no qadar. Ibn ʿUmar said: When you meet them, inform them that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar is free of them and they are free of him – three times – then he began to narrate: While we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, a man came, and he mentioned something of his appearance, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Come near.” He came near. He said: “Come near.” He came near. He said: “Come near.” He came near, until his knees almost touched his knees.
He said: O Messenger of Allah, inform me what īmān is – or: about īmān –. He said: “You believe in Allah, His angels, His Books, His Messengers, and the Last Day, and you believe in al-qadar” – Sufyān said: I think he said: its good and its evil –.
He said: Then what is Islam? He said: “Establishing the prayer, giving the zakāh, the Ḥajj of the House, fasting the month of Ramaḍān, and bathing from janābah.” To all of that he said: You have spoken truly, you have spoken truly. The people said: We have not seen a man more reverent toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ than this one, as though he were teaching the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Then he said: O Messenger of Allah, inform me about iḥsān. He said: “That you worship Allah – or: worship Him – as though you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then indeed He Yarāka.” To all of that we said: We have not seen a man more reverent toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ than this one, and he would say: You have spoken truly, you have spoken truly.
He said: Inform me about the Hour. He said: “The one asked about it is not more knowing of it than the one asking.” He said: You have spoken truly. He said that repeatedly. We have not seen a man more reverent toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ than this one. Then he turned away.
Sufyān said: It reached me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Seek him.” They did not find him. He said: “That was Jibrīl; he came to you to teach you your religion. He never came to me in a form but that I recognised him, except this form.”
items.ma-375: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAlqamah ibn Marthad, from Sulaymān ibn Buraydah, from Ibn Yaʿmar, he said: I asked Ibn ʿUmar – or a man asked him: We travel in this land and meet a people who say: There is no qadar. Ibn ʿUmar said: When you meet those, inform them that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar is free of them and they are free of him – he said it three times – then he began to narrate to us. He said: While we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, a man came and said: O Messenger of Allah, may I come near? He said: “Come near.” So he came near a step. Then he said: O Messenger of Allah, may I come near? He said: “Come near.” So he came near a step. Then he said: O Messenger of Allah, may I come near? He said: “Come near.” So he came near a step, until his knees almost touched the knee of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: O Messenger of Allah, what is īmān? Then he mentioned its meaning.
items.ma-376: Ḥasan ibn Mūsā al-Ashyab narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, al-Walīd ibn Abī al-Walīd narrated to us, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Surāqah al-ʿAdawī, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever shades the head of a campaigner, Allah will shade him on the Day of Resurrection; and whoever equips a campaigner until he is able to set off with his equipment will have the like of his reward; and whoever builds a mosque in which the name of Allah is mentioned, Allah will build for him a house in Paradise.”
items.ma-377: ʿAttāb – meaning Ibn Ziyād – narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh – meaning Ibn al-Mubārak – narrated to us, Yūnus informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from al-Sāʾib ibn Yazīd and ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb – ʿAbd Allāh said: And my father had taken it up to the Prophet ﷺ; he said: “Whoever misses something of his wird – or he said: of his portion – from the night, and recites it between the Fajr prayer and the Ẓuhr, it is as though he recited it in his night.”
items.ma-378: Khalaf ibn al-Walīd narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū Maysarah, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, he said: When the prohibition of khamr was revealed, he said: O Allah, make clear to us concerning khamr a clear statement that is a cure. Then this verse in Sūrat al-Baqarah was revealed: {They ask you about khamr and maysir; say: In both is a great sin} [al-Baqarah: 219]. He said: So ʿUmar was called and it was recited to him, and he said: O Allah, make clear to us concerning khamr a clear statement that is a cure. Then the verse in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ was revealed: {O you who believe, do not approach the prayer while you are intoxicated} [al-Nisāʾ: 43], and the caller of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when the prayer was established, would call: Let no intoxicated person approach the prayer. So ʿUmar was called and it was recited to him, and he said: O Allah, make clear to us concerning khamr a clear statement that is a cure. Then the verse in al-Māʾidah was revealed, and ʿUmar was called and it was recited to him, and when it reached {Will you then desist?} [al-Māʾidah: 91], ʿUmar said: We have desisted, we have desisted.
items.ma-379: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Abū Wāʾil, from Ṣubayy ibn Maʿbad: that he was a Christian of Taghlib, and accepted Islam, and asked: Which deed is best? It was said to him: Jihād in the path of Allah ﷿. He wanted to fight in jihād, and it was said to him: Have you performed Ḥajj? He said: No. It was said to him: Perform Ḥajj and ʿumrah, then fight in jihād. So he raised the talbiyah for both together, and happened upon Zayd ibn Ṣūḥān and Salmān ibn Rabīʿah, who said: He is more astray than his she-camel – or: He is not more guided than his camel –, so he went to ʿUmar and informed him of what they said, and he said: You have been guided to the sunnah of your Prophet ﷺ – or: to the sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-380: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Hishām, he said: My father informed me that ʿUmar said to the Stone: You are only a stone, and had I not seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kiss you, I would not have kissed you. Then he kissed it.
items.ma-381: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Hishām, from his father, that ʿUmar came to the Stone and said: Indeed I know that you are a stone, you neither harm nor benefit, and had I not seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kiss you, I would not have kissed you. He said: Then he kissed it.
items.ma-382: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Suwayd ibn Ghafalah: that ʿUmar kissed it and clung to it, then said: I saw Abū al-Qāsim ﷺ showing you great kindness – meaning the Stone –.
items.ma-383: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Hishām ibn ʿUrwah narrated to us, from his father, from ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUmar, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When the night comes from here and the day goes from here, the one fasting has broken his fast.”
items.ma-384: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Hishām ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from ʿUmar, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The likeness of the one who returns to his ṣadaqah is like the likeness of the one who returns to his vomit.”
items.ma-385: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, from ʿUmar, he said: The people of the Jāhiliyyah used not to depart from Jamʿ until they said: Shine, Thabīr, that we may raid; so when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came, he opposed them, and he used to depart from Jamʿ at the measure of the prayer of the musfirīn with the morning prayer, before the rising of the sun.
items.ma-386: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Rabāḥ ibn Abī Maʿrūf narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, he heard Ibn ʿAbbās: ʿUmar said to me: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Indeed the dead is punished by the weeping of his family over him.”
items.ma-387: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ, from ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from Sālim, from Ibn ʿUmar, he said: ʿUmar said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wiping over his khuffs on a journey.
items.ma-388:
Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, from ʿUmar: that the Prophet ﷺ used to seek refuge from miserliness and cowardice, the punishment of the grave, the most abject age, and the fitnah of the chest.
Wakīʿ said: The fitnah of the chest: that a man dies – and Wakīʿ mentioned the fitnah – without having repented from it.
items.ma-389: Wakīʿ narrated to us, ʿUmar ibn al-Walīd al-Shannī narrated to me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Buraydah, he said: ʿUmar sat in a seat in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to sit, and funerals were passing by him. He said: They passed with a funeral and praised with good, and he said: It has become obligatory. Then they passed with a funeral and praised with good, and he said: It has become obligatory. Then they passed with a funeral and said good, and he said: It has become obligatory. Then they passed with a funeral and said: This one was the greatest liar of the people. He said: Indeed the greatest liar of the people is the greatest liar about Allah, then those who come next after them: whoever lied about his soul in his body. He said: They said: What if four testify? He said: It has become obligatory. They said: And three? He said: It has become obligatory. They said: And two? He said: It has become obligatory; and that I had said one is dearer to me than red camels. He said: It was said to ʿUmar: Is this something you say by your own opinion, or something you heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? He said: No, rather I heard it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-390: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from his father, from ʿAbāyah ibn Rifāʿah, he said: It reached ʿUmar that Saʿd, when he built the palace, said: The little voice has been cut off. So he sent Muḥammad ibn Maslamah to him, and when he arrived he took out his fire-stick and kindled his fire, and bought firewood for a dirham. It was said to Saʿd: A man has done such-and-such. He said: That is Muḥammad ibn Maslamah. So he went out to him and swore by Allah that he had not said it, and he said: We convey from you what you say, and we do what we were commanded. Then he burned the door, then turned to offering him provisions, but he refused. He went out and came to ʿUmar, setting out to him at midday, and his going and his returning took nineteen. He said: Were it not for my good opinion of you, we would think that you had not conveyed on our behalf. He said: Indeed I did; he sent, conveying the salām, and excused himself, and swore by Allah that he had not said it. He said: Did he give you any provisions? He said: No. He said: What prevented you from asking me to give you provisions? He said: I disliked to give an order for you, so that the cool would be for you and the hot for me, while around me were the people of al-Madīnah, whom hunger had killed. And I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “A man is not satisfied without his neighbour.”
items.ma-392: Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, Mālik informed me, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, that he heard Anas ibn Mālik say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Shall I not inform you of the best of the houses of the Anṣār? Banū al-Najjār, then Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal, then al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj, then Banū Sāʿidah.” And he said: “In all the houses of the Anṣār there is good.”
items.ma-393: Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, Mālik narrated to us, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The two parties to a sale have the option so long as they have not separated, or the sale is an option.”
items.ma-394: Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, Mālik informed us, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the sale of ḥabal al-ḥabalah.
items.ma-395: Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, Mālik informed us, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, he said: We used to trade foodstuff in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he would send someone to us who would order us to move it from the place in which we had bought it to another place before we sold it.
items.ma-396: Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, Mālik informed us, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever buys foodstuff, let him not sell it until he has received it in full.”
items.ma-397: Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, Mālik informed us, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever frees his share in a slave, and has what reaches the price of the slave, then he is valued at a just value, and his partners are given their right, and the slave becomes free through him; otherwise, he has freed only what he freed.”
items.ma-398: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from Saʿīd, he said: I said to Ibn ʿUmar: A man performed liʿān with his wife. He said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ separated between them … and he mentioned the hadith.
items.ma-399:
Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, ʿAwf narrated to us, Yazīd – meaning al-Fārisī – narrated to us. My father Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal said: And Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, ʿAwf narrated to us, from Yazīd, he said: Ibn ʿAbbās said to us: I said to ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān: What induced you to take al-Anfāl, which is of the mathānī, and Barāʾah, which is of the miʾīn, and join them, and not write – Ibn Jaʿfar said: between them – a line: In the name of Allah, al-Raḥmān, al-Raḥīm, and place them among the seven long ones? What induced you to that?
ʿUthmān said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, at times when time passed over him, would have sūrahs possessing a number [of verses] revealed to him, and when something was revealed to him he would call one of those who wrote with him and say: “Place this in the sūrah in which such-and-such is mentioned,” and verses would be revealed to him, and he would say: “Place these verses in the sūrah in which such-and-such is mentioned,” and a verse would be revealed to him, and he would say: Place this verse in the sūrah in which such-and-such is mentioned.” And al-Anfāl was among the first of what was revealed in al-Madīnah, and Barāʾah among the last of the Qurʾān, and its account resembled its account. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken and did not make clear to us that it was of it, and I thought that it was of it, so from that I joined them, and did not write between them a line: In the name of Allah, al-Raḥmān, al-Raḥīm. Ibn Jaʿfar said: And I placed it among the seven long ones.
items.ma-400: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, my father informed me that Ḥumrān informed him, he said: ʿUthmān performed ablution at the paved area, then said: I will narrate to you a hadith that I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; were it not for a verse in the Book of Allah, I would not narrate it to you. I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “Whoever performs ablution and does the ablution well, then enters and prays, will be forgiven what is between him and the other prayer until he prays it.”
items.ma-401: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Mālik, Nāfiʿ narrated to me, from Nubayh ibn Wahb, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “The muḥrim does not marry, nor give in marriage, nor propose.”
items.ma-402: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ibn Ḥarmalah, he said: I heard Saʿīd – meaning Ibn al-Musayyab – say: ʿUthmān went out for Ḥajj, and when he was at some point on the road, it was said to ʿAlī, riḍwān Allāh ʿalayhimā: He has forbidden tamattuʿ by ʿumrah to Ḥajj. ʿAlī said to his companions: When he sets out, set out. So ʿAlī and his companions raised the talbiyah for ʿumrah, and ʿUthmān did not speak to him about that. ʿAlī said to him: Was I not informed that you forbade tamattuʿ? He said: Yes indeed. He said: Did you not hear that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed tamattuʿ? He said: Yes indeed.
items.ma-403: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl, from ʿĀmir ibn Shaqīq, from Abū Wāʾil, from ʿUthmān: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed ablution three times, three times.
items.ma-404: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū al-Naḍr, from Abū Anas: that ʿUthmān performed ablution at al-Maqāʿid three times, three times, and with him were men from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: “Is this not how you saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform ablution? They said: Yes.
items.ma-405: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us. And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Sufyān, from ʿAlqamah ibn Marthad, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿUthmān, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The best of you is the one who learns the Qurʾān and teaches it.”
items.ma-406: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Jāmiʿ ibn Shaddād, he said: I heard Ḥumrān ibn Abān narrating from ʿUthmān, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever completes the ablution as Allah ﷿ commanded him, then the prescribed prayers are kaffārāt for what is between them.”
items.ma-407: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid, he said: Qays said: Abū Sahlah narrated to me: that ʿUthmān said on the Day of the House, when he was besieged: Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a covenant with me, and I am patient upon it. Qays said: They used to think that it was that day.
items.ma-408: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us. And ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: Sufyān informed us, from ʿUthmān ibn Ḥakīm, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAmrah, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān; ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Whoever prays the ʿIshāʾ prayer and the Ṣubḥ in congregation, it is like standing a night [in prayer],” and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: “Whoever prays the ʿIshāʾ in congregation, it is like standing half a night [in prayer], and whoever prays the Ṣubḥ in congregation, it is like standing a night [in prayer].”
items.ma-409: ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, ʿAlī ibn al-Mubārak narrated to us, from Yaḥyā – meaning Ibn Abī Kathīr – from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever prays the ʿIshāʾ in congregation is like one who stood half the night, and whoever prays the Ṣubḥ in congregation is like one who stood the whole night.”
items.ma-410: Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, Yūnus – meaning Ibn ʿUbayd – narrated to us, ʿAṭāʾ ibn Farrūkh, the mawlā of the Qurashīs, narrated to me: that ʿUthmān bought land from a man, and he was slow toward him; so he met him and said to him: What prevented you from receiving your money? He said: You cheated me, and I do not meet anyone of the people but he blames me. He said: Does that prevent you? He said: Yes. He said: Then choose between your land and your money. Then he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allah ﷿ admitted to Paradise a man who was easy-going as a buyer, a seller, a payer of what he owed, and a collector of what was owed to him.”
items.ma-411: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, from Abū Maʿshar, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlqamah, he said: I was with Ibn Masʿūd while he was with ʿUthmān, and ʿUthmān said to him: What is left in you for women? He said: When women were mentioned, Ibn Masʿūd said: Come near, O ʿAlqamah – and I was a young man – and ʿUthmān said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to a group of young men of the Muhājirūn and said: “Whoever among you has the means, let him marry, for it is more lowering to the gaze and better at guarding the private part; and whoever does not, then fasting is a restraint for him.”
items.ma-412:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar, Bahz and Ḥajjāj narrated to us, they said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: I heard ʿAlqamah ibn Marthad narrating from Saʿd ibn ʿUbaydah, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “Indeed the best of you is the one who teaches the Qurʾān or learns it.” Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar and Ḥajjāj said: He said: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: That is what seated me in this seat.
Ḥajjāj said: Shuʿbah said: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān did not hear from ʿUthmān nor from ʿAbd Allāh, but he heard from ʿAlī ﵁.
My father said: And Bahz said, from Shuʿbah, he said: ʿAlqamah ibn Marthad informed me, and he said: “The best of you is the one who learns the Qurʾān and teaches it.”
items.ma-413: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, ʿAlqamah ibn Marthad informed me, and he said in it: “Whoever learns the Qurʾān or teaches it.”
items.ma-414: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar and Ḥajjāj narrated to us, both said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, he said: I heard a man narrating from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “There was a man who was easy-going as a seller and as a buyer, as a payer and as a collector, so he entered Paradise.”
items.ma-415: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Muslim ibn Yasār, from Ḥumrān ibn Abān, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān: that he called for water and performed ablution, and rinsed his mouth and sniffed water into his nose, then washed his face three times, and his forearms three times each, and wiped his head and the tops of his feet, then laughed, and said to his companions: Will you not ask me what made me laugh? They said: What made you laugh, O Commander of the Believers? He said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ call for water near this spot, and he performed ablution as I performed it, then laughed and said: “Will you not ask me what made me laugh?” They said: What made you laugh, O Messenger of Allah? He said: “Indeed, when the servant calls for ablution water and washes his face, Allah removes from him every sin he committed with his face; when he washes his forearms it is the same; if he wipes his head it is the same; and when he cleanses his feet it is the same.”
items.ma-416:
Bahz narrated to us, Mahdī ibn Maymūn informed us, Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Yaʿqūb narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan ibn Saʿd, the mawlā of al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Rabāḥ, he said: My people married me to a slave-woman of theirs, a Roman, and I had relations with her, and she bore me a black boy like me, and I named him ʿAbd Allāh. Then I had relations with her, and she bore me a black boy like me, and I named him ʿUbayd Allāh. Then a Roman slave-boy of my people, called Yūḥannas, took notice of her and spoke to her in his foreign tongue. He said: And she bore a boy as though he were a lizard of the lizards. I said to her: What is this? She said: He is Yūḥannas's. He said: So we were brought up to the Commander of the Believers ʿUthmān ﵁ – Mahdī said: I think he said: he asked the two of them and they confessed – and he said: Are you both pleased that I judge between you with the judgment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? He said: Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ judged that the child belongs to the firāsh, and for the adulterer is the stone.
Mahdī said: And I think he said: he flogged her and flogged him, and they were two owned slaves.
items.ma-417: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Shaybān Abū Muḥammad narrated to us, Mahdī ibn Maymūn narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Yaʿqūb narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan ibn Saʿd, from Rabāḥ, then he mentioned the hadith, he said: So I brought the two of them up to the Commander of the Believers ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, and he said: Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ judged that the child belongs to the firāsh … then he mentioned the like of it.
items.ma-418: Abū Kāmil narrated to us, Ibrāhīm – meaning Ibn Saʿd – narrated to us, Ibn Shihāb narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yazīd, from Ḥumrān, he said: ʿUthmān called for water while he was at al-Maqāʿid, and poured it over his right hand and washed it, then put his right hand into the vessel and washed his palms three times, then washed his face three times, and rinsed his mouth and blew out his nose, and washed his forearms to the elbows three times, then wiped his head, then washed his feet to the ankles three times, then said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever performs ablution like this ablution of mine, then prays two rakʿahs in which he does not speak to himself, Allah forgives him what preceded of his sin.”
items.ma-419: Ibrāhīm ibn Naṣr al-Tirmidhī narrated to us, Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yazīd, from Ḥumrān, the mawlā of ʿUthmān: that he saw ʿUthmān call for a vessel … then he mentioned something like it.
items.ma-420:
Abū Qaṭan narrated to us, Yūnus – meaning Ibn Abī Isḥāq – narrated to us, from his father, from Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, he said: ʿUthmān looked out from the palace while he was besieged, and said: I adjure by Allah whoever was present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Ḥirāʾ, when the mountain shook and he kicked it with his foot, then said: “Be still, Ḥirāʾ, upon you is only a prophet, a ṣiddīq, or a shahīd” – and I was with him? Men testified for him.
He said: I adjure by Allah whoever was present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Bayʿat al-Riḍwān, when he sent me to the polytheists, to the people of Makkah, and he said: “This is my hand, and this is the hand of ʿUthmān,” and pledged allegiance for me? Men testified for him.
He said: I adjure by Allah whoever was present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he said: “Who will extend for us the mosque with this house, for a house in Paradise?” and I bought it from my wealth and extended the mosque with it? Men testified for him.
He said: And I adjure by Allah whoever was present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Jaysh al-ʿUsrah, when he said: “Who will spend today an accepted expenditure?” and I equipped half the army from my wealth? He said: Men testified for him.
And I adjure by Allah whoever witnessed Rūmah, whose water was being sold to the wayfarer, and I bought it from my wealth and made it permitted to the wayfarer? He said: Men testified for him.
items.ma-421: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yazīd al-Laythī, from Ḥumrān ibn Abān, he said: I saw ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān perform ablution: he poured water over his hands three times and washed them, then rinsed his mouth and blew out his nose, then washed his face three times, then washed his right hand to the elbow three times, then the left likewise, then wiped his head, then washed his right foot three times, then the left likewise. Then he said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform ablution similar to this ablution of mine, and then he said: “Whoever performs this ablution of mine, then prays two rakʿahs in which he does not speak to himself, what preceded of his sin will be forgiven him.”
items.ma-422: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from Ayyūb, from Nāfiʿ, from Nubayh ibn Wahb, he said: ʿUmar ibn ʿUbayd Allāh sent to Abān ibn ʿUthmān: May he apply kohl to his eyes while he is a muḥrim? Or with what may he apply kohl to them while he is a muḥrim? He sent back to him: that he should bandage them with aloe, for I heard ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān narrating that from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-423: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, ʿImrān ibn Ḥudayr narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUbayd, from Ḥumrān ibn Abān, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever knows that the prayer is an obligatory right will enter Paradise.”
items.ma-424: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr al-Muqaddamī narrated to us, Abū Maʿshar – meaning al-Barrāʾ, whose name is Yūsuf ibn Yazīd – narrated to me, Ibn Ḥarmalah narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, he said: ʿUthmān performed Ḥajj, and when he was at some point on the road, ʿAlī was informed that ʿUthmān had forbidden his companions tamattuʿ with the ʿumrah and the Ḥajj. ʿAlī said to his companions: When he sets out in the afternoon, set out. So ʿAlī and his companions raised the talbiyah for ʿumrah, and ʿUthmān did not speak to them. ʿAlī said: Was I not informed that you forbade tamattuʿ? Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ not perform tamattuʿ? He said: I do not know what ʿUthmān ﵁ answered him.
items.ma-425:
ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Mālik ibn Aws ibn al-Ḥadathān, he said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb sent for me, and while I was thus, his mawlā Yarfaʾ came to him and said: Here are ʿUthmān, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Saʿd and al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām – he said: and I do not know whether he mentioned Ṭalḥah or not – asking permission to see you. He said: Permit them. Then he stayed an hour, then came and said: Here are al-ʿAbbās and ʿAlī asking permission to see you. He said: Permit them. When al-ʿAbbās entered, he said: O Commander of the Believers, judge between me and this one. And they were then disputing about what Allah bestowed as fayʾ upon His Messenger of the wealth of Banū al-Naḍīr. The people said: Judge between them, O Commander of the Believers, and relieve each of them of the other, for their dispute has gone on long. ʿUmar said: I adjure you by Allah, by whose permission the heavens and the earth stand: do you know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “We are not inherited from; what we leave is ṣadaqah”? They said: He said that. And he said the same to the two of them, and they said: Yes.
He said: I will inform you about this fayʾ. Indeed Allah ﷿ singled out His Prophet ﷺ with something of it that He gave to no one else, and He said: {And whatever Allah bestowed as fayʾ upon His Messenger from them, you did not urge on against it any horses or riding-camels} [al-Ḥashr: 6], and it was for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ specifically. By Allah, he did not take it to the exclusion of you, nor did he prefer himself over you with it; he divided it among you and distributed it among you, until this wealth remained of it, and he would spend from it on his family for a year, then put what remained of it where the wealth of Allah is put. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken, Abū Bakr said: I am the walī of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ after him; I act in it as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to act in it.
items.ma-426: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Ismāʿīl Abū Maʿmar narrated to us, Yaḥyā ibn Sulaym al-Ṭāʾifī narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Umayyah, from Mūsā ibn ʿImrān ibn Mannāḥ, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿUthmān: that he saw a funeral and stood for it, and said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ see a funeral and stand for it.
items.ma-427: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr narrated to us, Khālid ibn al-Ḥārith narrated to us, Ibn Abī Dhiʾb narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qāriẓ, from Abū ʿUbayd, he said: I witnessed ʿAlī and ʿUthmān ﵄ on the day of al-Fiṭr and the day of al-Naḥr, praying, then turning away and reminding the people, and I heard them both say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade fasting on these two days.
items.ma-428: Muḥammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, Ibn Shihāb narrated to me, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yazīd al-Jundaʿī, that he heard Ḥumrān, the mawlā of ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, say: I saw the Commander of the Believers ʿUthmān perform ablution: he poured water over his hands three times, then blew out his nose three times and rinsed his mouth three times … and he mentioned the hadith like the meaning of the hadith of Maʿmar.
items.ma-429: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us, al-Jurayrī informed us, from ʿUrwah ibn Qabīṣah, from a man of the Anṣār, from his father, that ʿUthmān said: Shall I not show you how the ablution of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was? They said: Yes. So he called for water, and rinsed his mouth three times, blew out his nose three times, washed his face three times, and his forearms three times each, and wiped his head, and washed his feet. Then he said: And know that the two ears are part of the head. Then he said: I have taken careful pains for you over the ablution of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-430: Isḥāq ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, ʿAwf al-Aʿrābī narrated to us, from Maʿbad al-Juhanī, from Ḥumrān ibn Abān, he said: We were with ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, and he called for water and performed ablution, and when he finished his ablution he smiled and said: Do you know what I laughed at? He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed ablution as I performed it, then smiled, then said: “Do you know what I laughed at?” We said: Allah and His Messenger know best. He said: “Indeed the servant, when he performs ablution and completes his ablution, then enters his prayer and completes his prayer, comes out of his prayer from his sins as he came out of the belly of his mother.”
items.ma-431:
Rawḥ narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Qatādah, he said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaqīq say: ʿUthmān used to forbid the mutʿah, and ʿAlī would raise the talbiyah for it. ʿUthmān said something to him, and ʿAlī said to him: You know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did that? ʿUthmān said: Indeed, but we were afraid.
Shuʿbah said: I said to Qatādah: What was their fear? He said: I do not know.
items.ma-432: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Qatādah, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaqīq said: ʿUthmān used to forbid the mutʿah, and ʿAlī used to command it. ʿUthmān said something to ʿAlī, then ʿAlī said: You know that we performed tamattuʿ with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? He said: Indeed, but we were afraid.
items.ma-433: Rawḥ narrated to us, Kahmas narrated to us, from Muṣʿab ibn Thābit ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, he said: ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān said, while giving a khuṭbah on his minbar: I am going to narrate to you a hadith that I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; nothing prevented me from narrating it to you except stinginess toward you. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Guarding for a night in the path of Allah Taʿālā is better than a thousand nights whose nights are spent in prayer and whose days in fasting.”
items.ma-434: ʿAbd al-Kabīr ibn ʿAbd al-Majīd Abū Bakr al-Ḥanafī narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd – meaning Ibn Jaʿfar – narrated to us, from his father, from Maḥmūd ibn Labīd, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever builds a mosque for Allah ﷿, Allah builds for him the like of it in Paradise.”
items.ma-435:
ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, Ibn Abī Dhiʾb narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Khālid ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qāriẓ, from Abū ʿUbayd, the mawlā of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Azhar, he said: I saw ʿAlī and ʿUthmān praying on the day of al-Fiṭr and al-Aḍḥā, then turning away, reminding the people. He said: And I heard them both say: Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade fasting on these two days.”
He said: And I heard ʿAlī say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade that anything of your nusuk should remain with you after three.
items.ma-436: Ṣafwān ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Maryam, he said: I entered upon Ibn Dārah, the mawlā of ʿUthmān, and he heard me rinsing my mouth, and he said: O Muḥammad. I said: At your service. He said: Shall I not inform you about the ablution of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?
