items.ma-585: Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, al-Mughīrah narrated to us, from Umm Mūsā, from ʿAlī, he said: The last words of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were: “The prayer, the prayer! Fear Allah regarding what your right hands possess.”
items.ma-586: Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Kulayb, from Abū Burdah ibn Abī Mūsā, from Abū Mūsā, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade me to put my ring on this index finger, or the one next to it.
items.ma-587: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, al-Zuhrī informed us, from Abū ʿUbayd, the mawlā of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, he said: Then I witnessed ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib after that on a day of ʿīd; he began with the prayer before the khuṭbah, and prayed without adhān or iqāmah. Then he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbid anyone to keep anything of his nusuk beyond three days.
items.ma-588: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Surayj ibn Yūnus narrated to me, ʿAlī ibn Hāshim – meaning Ibn al-Barīd – narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Rāfiʿ, from ʿUmar ibn ʿAlī ibn Ḥusayn, from his father, from ʿAlī: that the Prophet ﷺ gave his wives the choice of the world and the Hereafter, and did not give them the choice of divorce.
items.ma-589: ʿAbd Allāh said: And Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb narrated it to us, ʿAlī ibn Hāshim ibn al-Barīd narrated to us, then he mentioned the like of it, and said: He gave his wives the choice between the world and the Hereafter, and did not give them the choice of divorce.
items.ma-590: Abū Yūsuf al-Muʾaddib Yaʿqūb, our neighbor, narrated to us, Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn al-Muṭṭalib, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith, from Zayd ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from his father, from his grandfather, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever is killed defending his property is a shahīd.”
items.ma-591: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿAdī narrated to us, from Saʿīd, from Qatādah, from Abū Ḥassān, from ʿUbaydah, from ʿAlī, that the Prophet ﷺ said on the day of al-Aḥzāb: “May Allah fill their houses and their graves with fire, as they kept us occupied from the middle prayer until the sun had set.”
items.ma-592: Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Ḥasan and ʿAbd Allāh, the two sons of Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from their father – and Ḥasan was the more pleasing of the two to us – that ʿAlī said to Ibn ʿAbbās: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the marriage of mutʿah, and the meat of domestic donkeys at the time of Khaybar.
items.ma-593: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from Mujāhid, from Ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me to distribute his sacrificial camels, to oversee them, and to distribute their hides and their coverings, and he commanded me not to give the butcher anything of it, and said: “We give him from ourselves.”
items.ma-594: Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Zayd ibn Uthayʿ – a man of Hamdān: We asked ʿAlī: With what were you sent? – meaning the day the Prophet ﷺ sent him with Abū Bakr on the Ḥajj – he said: I was sent with four: none will enter Paradise except a believing soul; no naked person may perform ṭawāf of the House; whoever has a treaty between him and the Prophet ﷺ, his treaty is until its term; and the polytheists and the Muslims shall not perform Ḥajj together after this year of theirs.
items.ma-595: Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī: Muḥammad ﷺ judged that debt comes before bequest, though you recite the bequest before the debt, and that full brothers inherit from one another to the exclusion of paternal half-brothers.
items.ma-596: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from his father, from ʿAlī, he said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “I will not give to you and leave the People of the Ṣuffah with their bellies writhing from hunger.” And once he said: “I will not provide you two with a servant and leave the People of the Ṣuffah with their bellies shriveled.”
items.ma-597: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Ziyād al-Qaṭawānī narrated to me, Zayd ibn al-Ḥubāb narrated to us, Ḥarb Abū Sufyān al-Minqarī informed me, Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī Abū Jaʿfar narrated to us, my uncle narrated to me, from my father: that he saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performing saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah in the masʿā, with his garment pulled back, up to his knees.
items.ma-598: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Kurayb Muḥammad ibn al-ʿAlāʾ narrated to me, Ibn al-Mubārak narrated to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Zaḥr, from ʿAlī ibn Yazīd, from al-Qāsim, from Abū Umāmah, he said: ʿAlī said: I used to come to the Prophet ﷺ and ask permission; if he was in prayer he would say “Subḥān Allāh,” and if he was not in prayer he gave me permission.
items.ma-599: Sufyān narrated to us, from Muṭarrif, from al-Shaʿbī, from Abū Juḥayfah, he said: We asked ʿAlī: Do you have anything from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ besides the Qurʾān? He said: No, by the One who split the grain and created the soul, except an understanding that Allah ﷿ gives a man in the Qurʾān, or what is in the ṣaḥīfah. I said: And what is in the ṣaḥīfah? He said: The blood-money, the ransoming of the captive, and that a Muslim is not killed for a disbeliever.
items.ma-600: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr, he said: Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī informed me, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Rāfiʿ informed me – and once he said: that ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Rāfiʿ informed him – that he heard ʿAlī say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me, along with al-Zubayr and al-Miqdād, and said: “Go until you come to Rawḍat Khākh, for there is a woman in a howdah there with a letter; take it from her.” So we set out, our horses racing with us, until we came to the Rawḍah, and there we found the woman in the howdah. We said: Bring out the letter. She said: I have no letter. We said: You will bring out the letter, or we will strip off the clothes. He said: So she brought the letter out from her braids. We took the letter and brought it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and in it was: From Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿah to some of the polytheists in Makkah, informing them of some of the affair of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O Ḥāṭib, what is this?” He said: Do not hasten against me. I was a man attached to Quraysh, and was not of their own selves, while those who were with you of the Muhājirūn have kinsfolk who protect their families in Makkah. So, since that connection of lineage with them had escaped me, I wished to place a favor with them by which they would protect my kin. I did not do this out of kufr, nor apostasy from my religion, nor contentment with kufr after Islam. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “He has told you the truth.” ʿUmar said: Let me strike the neck of this hypocrite. He said: “He witnessed Badr, and what do you know – perhaps Allah Iṭṭalaʿa upon the people of Badr and said: Do what you wish, for I have forgiven you.”
items.ma-601: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Ḥajjāj ibn Yūsuf al-Shāʿir narrated to me, Yaḥyā ibn Ḥammād narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Mūsā ibn Sālim Abū Jahḍam, that Abū Jaʿfar narrated to him from his father, that ʿAlī narrated to them: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade me three things – he said: I do not know whether it was for him specifically or for the people generally: he forbade me the qassī, and the mīthara, and that I recite while I am bowing.
items.ma-602: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Wahb ibn Baqiyyah al-Wāsiṭī narrated to me, ʿUmar ibn Yūnus – meaning al-Yamāmī – narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar al-Yamāmī, from al-Ḥasan ibn Zayd ibn Ḥasan, my father narrated to me, from his father, from ʿAlī, he said: I was with the Prophet ﷺ when Abū Bakr and ʿUmar approached, and he said: “O ʿAlī, these two are the masters of the middle-aged men of the people of Paradise and of its youths, after the Prophets and Messengers.”
items.ma-603: Sufyān informed us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from his father, from a man who heard ʿAlī say: I wanted to propose to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for his daughter, and I said: I have nothing, so how? Then I remembered his kindness and his generosity, and I proposed to her from him. He said: “Do you have anything?” I said: No. He said: “Then where is your Ḥuṭamiyyah coat of mail that I gave you on such-and-such a day?” He said: It is with me. He said: “Give it to me.” He said: So I gave it to him.
items.ma-604: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Yazīd, from Mujāhid, from Ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAlī: that Fāṭimah came to the Prophet ﷺ asking for a servant, and he said: “Shall I not guide you to what is better for you than that? You glorify thirty-three times, magnify thirty-three times, and praise thirty-three times” – one of them thirty-four.
items.ma-605: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Aʿlā ibn Ḥammād al-Narsī narrated to me, Dāwūd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Abū ʿAbd Allāh Maslamah al-Rāzī narrated to us, from Abū ʿAmr al-Bajalī, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Sufyān al-Thaqafī, from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah Yuḥibbu the believing servant who is tried and repents often.”
items.ma-606: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr narrated to me, Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from al-Mundhir, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAlī, he said: I was a man who emitted madhy often, and I was shy to ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ because of the position of his daughter, so I told al-Miqdād to ask him, and he said: “He washes his private part and performs ablution.”
items.ma-607: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿUqbah ibn Mukram al-Kūfī narrated to me, Yūnus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Saʿīd al-Maqburī, from Abū Hurayrah; and from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Rāfiʿ, from his father, from ʿAlī, both said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Were it not that I would burden my ummah, I would command them to use the siwāk at every prayer.”
items.ma-608: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to us, Mughīrah ibn Miqsam narrated to us, al-Ḥārith al-ʿUklī narrated to me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nujayy, he said: ʿAlī said: I had two entries to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, by night and by day, and when I entered upon him while he was praying, he would clear his throat. I came to him one night, and he said: “Do you know what the angel did this night? I was praying, and I heard a rustling in the house, so I went out, and it was Jibrīl ﵇, and he said: I have been waiting for you all this night; there is a dog in your house, so I could not enter, and we do not enter a house in which there is a dog, or a person in janābah, or a statue.”
items.ma-609: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq narrated to us, from Shurayḥ ibn al-Nuʿmān al-Hamdānī, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade sacrificing an animal whose ear is cut at the front, or cut at the back, or split, or pierced, or cut off.
items.ma-610: Jarīr ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Hilāl, from Wahb ibn al-Ajdaʿ, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “No prayer is to be offered after the ʿaṣr prayer unless the sun is white and high.”
items.ma-611: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAjlān, Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥunayn narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade me to recite while I am bowing, and the gold ring, and the qassī and the safflower-dyed cloth.
items.ma-612: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtaybah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, he said: Abū Mūsā came to al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī to visit him, and ʿAlī said to him: Have you come as a visitor, or to gloat? He said: No, rather as a visitor. ʿAlī said to him: If you have come as a visitor, then I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “When a man visits his Muslim brother, he walks among the fruit-gatherings of Paradise until he sits; and when he sits, mercy envelops him. If it is morning, seventy thousand angels pray for him until evening; and if it is evening, seventy thousand angels pray for him until morning.”
items.ma-613:
ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Suwayd ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, in the year two hundred and twenty-six, Muslim ibn Khālid al-Zanjī narrated to us – Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: I said to Suwayd: Why was he called al-Zanjī? He said: He was extremely black – from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith, from Zayd ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from his father, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Rāfiʿ, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood at ʿArafah, with Usāmah ibn Zayd riding behind him, and said: “This is a standing place, and all of ʿArafah is a standing place.” Then he moved on, proceeding at a brisk pace, while the people were striking their mounts to the right and left, and he was turning and saying: “Tranquility, O people! Tranquility, O people!” until he came to al-Muzdalifah, and combined the two prayers.
Then he stood at al-Muzdalifah, and had al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās ride behind him, then stood at Quzaḥ and said: “This is the standing place, and all of al-Muzdalifah is a standing place.” Then he moved on and proceeded at a brisk pace, while the people were striking their mounts to the right and left, and he was turning and saying: “Tranquility, O people! Tranquility, O people!” When he stopped at Muḥassir he struck his mount, and she trotted with him until she had come out of the valley; then he went on his way until he came to the Jamrah, then entered the place of slaughter and said: “This is the place of slaughter, and all of Minā is a place of slaughter” … then he mentioned the like of the hadith of Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdah, from al-Mughīrah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, like it, or similar.
items.ma-614: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Ismāʿīl Abū Maʿmar narrated to me, Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Jabīrah, from Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Rāfiʿ, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “None hates the Arabs except a hypocrite.”
items.ma-615: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, from his father, he said: ʿAlī gave us a khuṭbah and said: Whoever claims that we have anything we recite except the Book of Allah and this ṣaḥīfah – a ṣaḥīfah in which are the ages of camels and certain matters concerning wounds – has lied. He said: And in it: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Al-Madīnah is a ḥaram between ʿAyr and Thawr. Whoever introduces a ḥadath in it, or shelters one who introduces a ḥadath, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels, and all the people; Allah will not accept from him on the Day of Resurrection any ʿadl or ṣarf. And whoever claims descent from other than his father, or takes as his mawlā other than his own mawālī, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels, and all the people; Allah will not accept from him on the Day of Resurrection any ṣarf or ʿadl. And the dhimmah of the Muslims is one; the least of them strives to uphold it.”
items.ma-616: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Khaythamah, from Suwayd ibn Ghafalah, he said: ʿAlī said: When I narrate to you a hadith from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, falling from the sky is dearer to me than lying about him; and when I narrate to you from other than him, I am only a man at war, and war is deception. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “In the last time there will emerge people young in years, foolish in their thinking, who speak from the best speech of creation; their īmān does not pass beyond their throats. Wherever you meet them, kill them, for killing them is a reward on the Day of Resurrection for whoever kills them.”
items.ma-617: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Muslim, from Shutayr ibn Shakal, from ʿAlī ﵁, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of al-Aḥzāb: “They kept us occupied from the middle prayer, the ʿaṣr prayer; may Allah fill their graves and their houses with fire.” Then he prayed it between the two ʿishāʾs: between Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ.
items.ma-618: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Mundhir Abū Yaʿlā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah, from ʿAlī, he said: He was a man who emitted madhy often, and was shy to ask the Prophet ﷺ about madhy. He said: So he said to al-Miqdād: Ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for me about madhy. He said: So he asked him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “In it is ablution.”
items.ma-619: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr narrated to us, Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade a man to recite while he is bowing or prostrating.
items.ma-620: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Saʿd ibn ʿUbaydah, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿAlī, he said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, what is it with you that you choose so carefully among Quraysh and leave us? He said: “Do you have something?” I said: Yes, the daughter of Ḥamzah. He said: “She is not lawful for me; she is my brother's daughter by suckling.”
items.ma-621: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Saʿd ibn ʿUbaydah, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting one day with a stick in his hand, scratching the ground with it. He said: Then he raised his head and said: “There is no soul among you but its station in Paradise and the Fire is already known.” He said: They said: O Messenger of Allah, then why do we act? He said: “Act, for each is made easy for what he was created for: {As for he who gives and fears Allah and believes in the best, We will ease him toward ease. But as for he who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient and denies the best, We will ease him toward difficulty}” [al-Layl: 5–10].
items.ma-622: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Saʿd ibn ʿUbaydah, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent out an expedition and appointed over them a man of the Anṣār. He said: When they set out, he became angry with them over something. He said to them: Has the Messenger of Allah ﷺ not commanded you to obey me? They said: Yes. He said: Then gather firewood. Then he called for fire and kindled it in the wood, then said: I order you: you will enter it. He said: The people were about to enter it, but a young man among them said to them: You only fled to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from the Fire, so do not hasten until you meet the Prophet ﷺ; if he commands you to enter it, then enter it. He said: So they returned to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him, and he said to them: “Had you entered it, you would never have come out of it. Obedience is only in what is right.”
items.ma-623: Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr, he said: Wāqid ibn ʿAmr ibn Saʿd ibn Muʿādh narrated to me, he said: I attended a funeral among Banū Salimah and stood, and Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr said to me: Sit, for I will inform you of this with certainty: Masʿūd ibn al-Ḥakam al-Zuraqī narrated to me that he heard ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib at the open square of al-Kūfah saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to stand for the funeral, then sat after that and commanded us to sit.
items.ma-624: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, from Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūbah, from ʿAbd Allāh al-Dānāj, from Ḥuḍayn Abū Sāsān al-Raqāshī, he said: Some people of al-Kūfah came to ʿUthmān and informed him of what had happened with al-Walīd – that is, his drinking of khamr – and ʿAlī spoke to him about it. He said: Here is your cousin; carry out the ḥadd on him. He said: O Ḥasan, stand and flog him. He said: You have nothing to do with this; give it to someone other than you. He said: Rather, you have become weak and feeble and incapable; stand, O ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar. So ʿAbd Allāh began to strike him, and ʿAlī counted, until he reached forty. Then he said: Hold – or he said: Stop – the Messenger of Allah ﷺ flogged forty, and Abū Bakr forty, and ʿUmar completed it to eighty, and each is Sunnah.
items.ma-625: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥah ibn Yazīd ibn Rukānah narrated to me, from ʿUbayd Allāh al-Khawlānī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: ʿAlī entered upon me in my house and called for ablution water, so we brought a wooden bowl that takes a mudd or near it, until it was placed before him, and he had urinated. He said: O Ibn ʿAbbās, shall I not perform for you the ablution of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? I said: Yes, may my father and mother be your ransom. He said: A vessel was placed for him, and he washed his hands, then rinsed his mouth, sniffed water into his nose and blew it out. Then he took water with his hands and dashed it on his face, and pressed his thumbs into the front parts of his ears. He said: Then he repeated the like of that three times. Then he took a handful of water in his right hand and poured it over his forelock, then let it run down over his face. Then he washed his right hand to the elbow three times, then the other hand likewise. Then he wiped his head and his ears, on their backs. Then he took water in his two palms and dashed it on his feet, while the sandals were on them, then turned it over with them; then on the other foot likewise. He said: I said: Even on the sandals? He said: Even on the sandals. I said: Even on the sandals? He said: Even on the sandals. I said: Even on the sandals? He said: Even on the sandals.
items.ma-626: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from Muḥammad, from ʿAbīdah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Khawārij were mentioned, and he said: Among them is a man with a deformed hand – or a stunted hand, or a breast-like hand. Were it not that you would become arrogant, I would narrate to you what Allah promised those who kill them, on the tongue of Muḥammad. I said: Did you hear it from Muḥammad? He said: Yes, by the Rabb of the Kaʿbah; yes, by the Rabb of the Kaʿbah; yes, by the Rabb of the Kaʿbah.
items.ma-627: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salamah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to have us recite the Qurʾān as long as he was not in janābah.
items.ma-628: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Sufyān, Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, from ʿAlī, he said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, when you send me, should I be like the heated iron spike, or does the one who is present see what the absent one does not see? He said: “The one who is present sees what the absent one does not see.”
items.ma-629: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, Manṣūr narrated to us, he said: I heard Ribʿī say: I heard ʿAlī say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do not lie about me, for whoever lies about me will enter the Fire.”
items.ma-630: Ḥusayn narrated it to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Ribʿī ibn Ḥirāsh, he said: I heard ʿAlī say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do not lie about me, for whoever lies about me will enter the Fire.”
items.ma-631: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir narrated to us, from Masʿūd ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAlī, he said: We saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stand, so we stood, and sit, so we sat.
items.ma-632: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, ʿAlī ibn Mudrik narrated to me, from Abū Zurʿah, from Ibn Nujayy, from his father, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ: “The angels do not enter a house in which there is a person in janābah, or an image, or a dog.”
items.ma-633: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Hishām, Qatādah narrated to us, from Jurayy ibn Kulayb, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade sacrificing an animal with a broken horn or a cut ear.
items.ma-634: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Sufyān, Sulaymān narrated to me, from Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, from al-Ḥārith ibn Suwayd, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the gourd and the pitch-coated vessel. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: I heard my father say: There is no hadith in al-Kūfah from ʿAlī sounder than this.
items.ma-635: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Mujālid, ʿĀmir narrated to me, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed ten: the one who consumes ribā, the one who feeds it, the one who writes it, its two witnesses, the ḥāll and the one for whom it is made lawful, the one who withholds ṣadaqah, the woman who tattoos and the woman who has herself tattooed.
items.ma-636: Yaḥyā narrated to me, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Abū al-Bakhtarī, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me to Yemen while I was young in age. I said: You are sending me to a people among whom disputes will arise, and I have no knowledge of judging? He said: “Allah will guide your tongue and make your heart firm.” He said: So I never doubted in a judgment between two people after that.
items.ma-637: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, ʿAmr ibn Murrah narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salamah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by me while I was in pain, and I was saying: O Allah, if my appointed time has come, give me rest; and if it is delayed, raise me up; and if it is an affliction, make me patient. He said: “What did you say?” So I repeated it to him, and he struck me with his foot and said: “What did you say?” He said: So I repeated it to him, and he said: “O Allah, grant him well-being,” or: “heal him.” He said: And I did not complain of that pain after that.
items.ma-638: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, he said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salamah, from ʿAlī, he said: I was ailing, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by me … then he mentioned its meaning, except that he said: “O Allah, grant him well-being; O Allah, heal him.”
items.ma-639: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, ʿAmr ibn Murrah narrated to me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salamah, he said: I came to ʿAlī, I and two men, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would relieve himself, then go out and recite the Qurʾān, and eat meat with us, and nothing would keep him – and perhaps he said: veil him – from the Qurʾān except janābah.
items.ma-640: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr narrated to us, Hishām narrated to us, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, from ʿAlī, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “The best of its women is Maryam, daughter of ʿImrān, and the best of its women is Khadījah.”
items.ma-641: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to us, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥīm al-Kindī, from Zādhān Abū ʿUmar, he said: I heard ʿAlī at al-Raḥbah, adjuring the people: Who witnessed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Ghadīr Khumm, when he said what he said? Thirteen men stood and testified that they heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever I am his mawlā, ʿAlī is his mawlā.”
items.ma-642: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from ʿAdī ibn Thābit, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, he said: ʿAlī said: By Allah, it is among what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entrusted to me: that none hates me except a hypocrite, and none loves me except a believer.
items.ma-643: Abū Usāmah narrated to us, Zāʾidah informed us, ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib narrated to us, from his father, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ furnished Fāṭimah with a khamīl, a waterskin, and a leather pillow stuffed with idhkhir fiber.
items.ma-644: Asbāṭ ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, Nuʿaym ibn Ḥakīm al-Madāʾinī narrated to us, from Abū Maryam, from ʿAlī, he said: The Prophet ﷺ and I set out until we came to the Kaʿbah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: “Sit,” and climbed onto my shoulders. I went to rise with him, but he saw weakness in me, so he came down, and the Prophet of Allah ﷺ sat for me and said: “Climb onto my shoulders.” He said: So I climbed onto his shoulders. He said: And he rose with me. He said: It seemed to me that if I wished I could reach the horizon of the sky, until I climbed onto the House, and on it was a statue of brass or copper. I began to work it loose, to its right and to its left, in front of it and behind it, until, when I had a hold on it, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: “Throw it down.” So I threw it down, and it shattered as glass vessels shatter. Then I came down, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and I set off racing until we were hidden among the houses, for fear that any of the people might meet us.
items.ma-645: Faḍl ibn Dukayn narrated to us, Yāsīn al-ʿIjlī narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah, from his father, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The Mahdī is from us, the people of the House; Allah will set him right in a single night.”
items.ma-646:
Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, Hāshim ibn al-Barīd narrated to us, from Ḥusayn ibn Maymūn, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, the judge of al-Rayy, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, he said: I heard the Commander of the Believers ʿAlī say: Fāṭimah, al-ʿAbbās, Zayd ibn Ḥārithah and I gathered with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and al-ʿAbbās said: O Messenger of Allah, my age has advanced, my bones have grown weak, and my expenses have grown many; so if you see fit, O Messenger of Allah, to order for me so-and-so many wasqs of food, do so. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “We will.” Fāṭimah said: O Messenger of Allah, if you see fit to order for me as you ordered for your uncle, do so. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “We will do that.” Then Zayd ibn Ḥārithah said: O Messenger of Allah, you had given me land from which was my livelihood, then you took it back; so if you see fit to return it to me, do so. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “We will do that.”
He said: So I said: O Messenger of Allah, if you see fit to put me in charge of this right that Allah has made for us in His Book, of this khumus, so that I distribute it in your lifetime and no one disputes it with me after you. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “We will do that.” So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ put me in charge of it and I distributed it in his lifetime; then Abū Bakr put me in charge of it and I distributed it in his lifetime; then ʿUmar put me in charge of it and I distributed it in his lifetime, until it was the last of the years of ʿUmar, when much wealth came to him.
items.ma-647: Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, Shuraḥbīl ibn Mudrik al-Juʿfī narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nujayy al-Ḥaḍramī, from his father, he said: ʿAlī said to me: I had from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a station that no one among creation had: I used to come to him every pre-dawn and greet him until he cleared his throat. One night I came and greeted him, saying: Peace be upon you, O Prophet of Allah. He said: “Take your time, O Abū Ḥasan, until I come out to you.” When he came out to me, I said: O Prophet of Allah, has someone angered you? He said: “No.” I said: Then why did you not speak to me before, until you spoke to me tonight? He said: “I heard a movement in the room, and I said: Who is this? He said: I am Jibrīl. I said: Enter. He said: No, come out to me. When I came out, he said: In your house is something that no angel will enter as long as it is in it. I said: I do not know of it, O Jibrīl. He said: Go and look. So I opened the house and found nothing in it except a puppy with which al-Ḥasan was playing. I said: I found only a puppy. He said: There are three things; no angel will ever enter as long as one of them is in it: a dog, or janābah, or an image of a living creature.”
items.ma-648: Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, Shuraḥbīl ibn Mudrik narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nujayy, from his father: that he travelled with ʿAlī, and was in charge of his vessel for ablution water, and when he came alongside Nīnawā, as he was going toward Ṣiffīn, ʿAlī called out: Be patient, Abū ʿAbd Allāh; be patient, Abū ʿAbd Allāh, at the bank of the Euphrates. I said: What is this? He said: I entered upon the Prophet ﷺ one day while his eyes were overflowing. I said: O Prophet of Allah, has someone angered you? What is the matter with your eyes, that they are overflowing? He said: “Rather Jibrīl got up from me a short while ago, and told me that al-Ḥusayn will be killed at the bank of the Euphrates.” He said: And he said: “Would you like me to let you smell some of his soil?” I said: Yes. So he stretched out his hand, took a handful of earth, and gave it to me, and I could not keep my eyes from overflowing.
items.ma-649: Marwān ibn Muʿāwiyah al-Fazārī narrated to us, al-Azhar ibn Rāshid al-Kāhilī informed us, from al-Khiḍr ibn al-Qawwās, from Abū Sukhaylah, he said: ʿAlī said: Shall I not tell you of the most excellent verse in the Book of Allah Taʿālā, which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ narrated to us: {Whatever misfortune befalls you is for what your hands have earned, and He pardons much} [al-Shūrā: 30] – “And I will explain it to you, O ʿAlī: whatever sickness, or punishment, or affliction befalls you in this world is for what your hands have earned, and Allah Taʿālā is too generous to repeat the punishment for them in the Hereafter; and whatever Allah Taʿālā has pardoned in this world, Allah Taʿālā is too forbearing to return to it after His pardon.”
items.ma-650:
Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān, Isrāʾīl and my father narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, he said: We asked ʿAlī about the voluntary prayer of the Prophet ﷺ by day, and he said: You cannot bear it. He said: We said: Tell us of it, and we will take from it what we are able. He said: When the Prophet ﷺ prayed Fajr, he would wait until the sun was from here – meaning from the direction of the east – at the same measure as it is at the time of ʿaṣr from there – from the direction of the west – then he stood and prayed two rakʿahs. Then he would wait until the sun was from here – meaning from the direction of the east – at the same measure as it is at the time of Ẓuhr from there – meaning from the direction of the west – then he stood and prayed four; and four before Ẓuhr when the sun had declined, and two after it, and four before ʿAṣr, separating every two rakʿahs with the salutation upon the angels brought near, and the Prophets, and those who follow them among the believers and the Muslims. And he said: ʿAlī said: That is sixteen rakʿahs, the voluntary prayer of the Prophet ﷺ by day, and few keep up with them.
Wakīʿ narrated to us, from his father, he said: Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit said to Abū Isḥāq, when he narrated it to him: O Abū Isḥāq, this hadith of yours is worth a mosque-full of gold.
items.ma-651: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥusayn narrated to us, both said: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, he said: From every part of the night the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed witr: from its beginning, its middle and its end; and the witr became fixed at the end of the night.
items.ma-652: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, he said: The witr is not obligatory like the prayer, but it is a Sunnah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ established.
items.ma-653: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed witr at the beginning of the night, its end and its middle, and his witr ended at the pre-dawn.
items.ma-654: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Ḥārithah ibn Muḍarrib, from ʿAlī, he said: I saw us on the day of Badr taking refuge with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he was the nearest of us to the enemy, and he was among the strongest of the people in might that day.
items.ma-655: Wakīʿ narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Muslim al-Ḥanafī narrated to us, from his father, from ʿAlī, he said: A Bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, we are out in the desert, and a little wind comes out of one of us? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah ﷿ does not Yastaḥyī of the truth. When one of you does that, let him perform ablution; and do not come to women in their hindquarters.” And once he said: “in their rears.”
items.ma-656:
Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā al-Ṭabbāʿ narrated to us, Yaḥyā ibn Sulaym narrated to me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿIyāḍ ibn ʿAmr al-Qārī, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād came and entered upon ʿĀʾishah while we were sitting with her, on his return from al-ʿIrāq, in the nights when ʿAlī was killed. She said to him: O ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād, will you be truthful with me about what I ask you? Tell me about these people whom ʿAlī killed. He said: And why would I not be truthful with you? She said: Then tell me their story. He said: When ʿAlī wrote to Muʿāwiyah and appointed the two arbitrators, eight thousand of the Qurrāʾ of the people came out against him, and camped in a land called Ḥarūrāʾ, on the side of al-Kūfah. They blamed him and said: You stripped yourself of a shirt that Allah Taʿālā clothed you in, and a name that Allah Taʿālā named you by, then you went and appointed arbitrators in the religion of Allah; and there is no judgment except for Allah Taʿālā.
When what they blamed him for reached ʿAlī, and they had parted from him over it, he commanded a mu'adhdhin to call out that none was to enter upon the Commander of the Believers except a man who had memorized the Qurʾān. When the house had filled with the Qurrāʾ of the people, he called for a great imām muṣḥaf and placed it before him, and began to strike it with his hand and say: O muṣḥaf, speak to the people! The people called out to him and said: O Commander of the Believers, what are you asking of it? It is only ink on paper, and we speak by what we have narrated from it. What do you want? He said: These companions of yours who have come out – between me and them is the Book of Allah ﷿. Allah Taʿālā says in His Book, concerning a woman and a man: {And if you fear a breach between the two, send an arbiter from his people and an arbiter from her people; if they desire reconciliation, Allah will bring about agreement between them} [al-Nisāʾ: 35]. So the ummah of Muḥammad ﷺ is greater in blood and sanctity than one woman and one man.
And they resented that I wrote to Muʿāwiyah. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib wrote – and Suhayl ibn ʿAmr had come to us while we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at al-Ḥudaybiyah, when he made peace with his people, Quraysh, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote: In the name of Allah, al-Raḥmān, al-Raḥīm. Suhayl said: Do not write: In the name of Allah, al-Raḥmān, al-Raḥīm. He said: “How shall we write?” He said: Write: In Your name, O Allah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Then write: Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah.” He said: If I knew that you were the Messenger of Allah, I would not oppose you. So he wrote: This is what Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh made peace with Quraysh upon. Allah Taʿālā says in His Book: {There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent example for whoever hopes in Allah and the Last Day} [al-Aḥzāb: 21].
Then ʿAlī sent ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās to them, and I went out with him, until when we were in the middle of their camp, Ibn al-Kawwāʾ stood up to address the people. He said: O bearers of the Qurʾān, this is ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās; whoever does not know him, I will make him known to you from the Book of Allah: he is one of those about whom, and about whose people, it was revealed: {a people who are contentious} [al-Zukhruf: 58]. So send him back to his companion, and do not debate the Book of Allah with him. Their orators stood up and said: By Allah, we will debate the Book of Allah with him; if he brings a truth we recognize, we will follow it, and if he brings falsehood, we will confront him with his falsehood. So they debated the Book with ʿAbd Allāh for three days, and four thousand of them returned, every one of them repentant, among them Ibn al-Kawwāʾ, until he brought them in to ʿAlī at al-Kūfah. Then ʿAlī sent to the rest of them and said: What has happened between us and the people you have seen; so stay wherever you wish, until the ummah of Muḥammad ﷺ is united. Between us and you is that you do not shed unlawful blood, or cut off a road, or wrong anyone under the dhimmah; for if you do, we have thrown the war back at you on equal terms; indeed Allah does not Yuḥibbu the treacherous.
ʿĀʾishah said to him: O Ibn Shaddād, so he did kill them! He said: By Allah, he did not send to them until they had cut off the road, shed blood, and treated the people of the dhimmah as lawful. She said: By Allah? He said: By Allah, besides whom there is no deity, it was so. She said: Then what is this that has reached me from the people of al-ʿIrāq, which they are narrating? They say: Dhū al-Thudayy, Dhū al-Thudayy. He said: I saw him, and I stood with ʿAlī over him among the slain. He called the people and said: Do you recognize this man? How many came saying: I saw him in the mosque of Banū so-and-so, praying; and I saw him in the mosque of Banū so-and-so, praying; and they brought no proof by which he could be known other than that. She said: And what did ʿAlī say when he stood over him, as the people of al-ʿIrāq claim? He said: I heard him say: Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth. She said: Did you hear him say anything other than that? He said: O Allah, no. She said: Yes, Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth. May Allah have mercy on ʿAlī. It was part of his way of speaking that he would not see anything that pleased him except that he said: Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth. And the people of al-ʿIrāq go on lying about him and adding to the hadith about him.
items.ma-657: Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from al-Ḥakam, from Abū Muḥammad al-Hudhalī, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was at a funeral, and he said: “Which of you will go to al-Madīnah and not leave any idol there without breaking it, nor any grave without leveling it, nor any image without smearing it over?” A man said: I, O Messenger of Allah. So he went, but he was afraid of the people of al-Madīnah and returned. ʿAlī said: I will go, O Messenger of Allah. He said: “Then go.” So he went and returned, and said: O Messenger of Allah, I did not leave any idol there without breaking it, nor any grave without leveling it, nor any image without smearing it over. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever returns to making anything of this has disbelieved in what was sent down to Muḥammad ﷺ.” Then he said: “Do not be a tempter, nor a conceited man, nor a merchant except a merchant of good, for those are the ones outstripped in deeds.”
items.ma-658: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from a man of the people of al-Baṣrah, he said: The people of al-Baṣrah give him the kunyah Abū Muwarriʿ, he said: and the people of al-Kūfah give him the kunyah Abū Muḥammad, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was at a funeral – then he mentioned the hadith, and did not say: from ʿAlī. And he said: “nor any image without smearing it over.” He said: I did not come to you, O Messenger of Allah, until I had left no image without smearing it over. And he said: “Do not be a tempter, nor a conceited man.”
items.ma-659: Ibrāhīm ibn Abī al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: He used to pray witr at the adhān, and to pray the two rakʿahs at the iqāmah.
items.ma-660: Khalaf ibn al-Walīd narrated to us, Abū Jaʿfar – meaning al-Rāzī – narrated to us, from Ḥuṣayn ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from al-Shaʿbī, from al-Ḥārith, from a man of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ – I have no doubt that it was ʿAlī – he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the one who consumes ribā, the one who feeds it, its two witnesses, its writer, the woman who tattoos, the woman who has herself tattooed, the muḥill, the muḥallal lahu, and the one who withholds ṣadaqah; and he used to forbid wailing.
items.ma-661: Khalaf narrated to us, Qays narrated to us, from al-Ashʿath ibn Sawwār, from ʿAdī ibn Thābit, from Abū Ẓabyān, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O ʿAlī, if you take charge of the matter after me, expel the people of Najrān from the Arabian Peninsula.”
items.ma-662: Khalaf narrated to us, Abū Jaʿfar – meaning al-Rāzī – and Khālid – meaning al-Ṭaḥḥān – narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: I was a man who emitted madhy often, so I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: “As for semen, in it is bathing; and as for madhy, in it is ablution.”
items.ma-663: Khalaf narrated to us, Khālid narrated to us, from Muṭarrif, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī: that the Messenger ﷺ forbade a man to raise his voice in recitation before ʿishāʾ and after it, confusing his companions while they are praying.
items.ma-664: Khalaf narrated to us, Khālid narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Kulayb, from Abū Burdah ibn Abī Mūsā, that ʿAlī said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Ask Allah Taʿālā for guidance and rectitude; and by guidance remember your guiding of the road, and by rectitude remember your aiming of the arrow.”
items.ma-665: Muḥammad ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ narrated to us – ʿAbd Allāh said: and I heard it myself from Muḥammad ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ – Ismāʿīl ibn Zakariyyā narrated to us, from Kathīr al-Nawwāʾ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mulayl, he said: I heard ʿAlī say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “There was no prophet before me but that he was given seven chiefs, ministers, noble ones; and I have been given fourteen: ministers, chiefs, noble ones – seven from Quraysh, and seven from the Muhājirūn.”
items.ma-666: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Ḥārithah ibn Muḍarrib, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me to Yemen, and I said: O Messenger of Allah, you are sending me to a people older than I am, to judge between them. He said: “Go, for Allah Taʿālā will make your tongue firm and guide your heart.”
items.ma-667: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, Abān – meaning Ibn ʿAbd Allāh – narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn Ghuzayy narrated to me, my uncle ʿIlbāʾ narrated to me, from ʿAlī, he said: The ṣadaqah camels passed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: And he reached out his hand to a tuft of hair from the side of a camel and said: “I have no more right to this hair than a man among the Muslims.”
items.ma-668: Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, al-Ḥārith ibn Yazīd narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zurayr al-Ghāfiqī, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: While we were praying with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he turned away while we were standing, then came back with his head dripping, and prayed the prayer for us. Then he said: “I remembered that I was in janābah when I stood to the prayer and had not bathed; so whoever among you feels a rumbling in his belly, or is in the same condition I was in, let him leave until he has finished his need, or his bath, then return to his prayer.”
items.ma-669: Yaḥyā ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, from al-Ḥārith ibn Yazīd, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zurayr, from ʿAlī, then he mentioned the like of it.
items.ma-670: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, al-Rabīʿ – meaning Ibn Abī Ṣāliḥ al-Aslamī – narrated to us, Ziyād ibn Abī Ziyād narrated to me, I heard ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib adjuring the people, and he said: I adjure by Allah any Muslim man who heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Ghadīr Khumm say what he said. So twelve men of Badr stood and testified.
items.ma-671: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the one who deals in ribā, the one who consumes it, its writer, its two witnesses, the muḥill and the muḥallal lahu.
items.ma-672: Abū Saʿīd, the mawlā of Banū Hāshim, narrated to us, Ismāʿīl ibn Muslim al-ʿAbdī narrated to us, Abū Kathīr, the mawlā of the Anṣār, narrated to us, he said: I was with my master with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib when he killed the people of al-Nahrawān, and it seemed the people felt something in themselves about killing them. ʿAlī said: O people, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ narrated to us about people who will pass out of the religion as the arrow passes out of the game, then never return to it, until the arrow returns to its notch; and the sign of that is that among them is a black man with a deformed hand, one of whose hands is like the breast of a woman, with a nipple like the nipple of a woman's breast, around which are seven coarse hairs. So search for him, for I see him among them. They searched for him and found him at the edge of the river under the slain, and brought him out. ʿAlī said takbīr, and said: Allāhu akbar; Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth. He was wearing an Arab bow, and he took it in his hand and began to prod his deformed hand with it, saying: Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth. And the people said takbīr when they saw him, and rejoiced, and what they had been feeling left them.
items.ma-673: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A Muslim has six rights over a Muslim in what is good: he greets him with salām when he meets him; he says a blessing for him when he sneezes; he visits him when he is ill; he answers him when he invites him; he attends his funeral when he dies; he loves for him what he loves for himself; and he gives him sincere counsel in his absence.”
items.ma-674: Ḥusayn narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, then he mentioned the like of it with its chain and its meaning.
items.ma-675: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq narrated to us, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The Hour will not come until a man from among my Companions is searched for, as a stray animal is searched for or sought, and is not found.”
items.ma-676: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Ḥārithah ibn Muḍarrib, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of Badr: “Whoever of Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib you are able to take captive, take him captive, for they came out unwillingly.”
items.ma-677: Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning {and you make your provision that you deny} [al-Wāqiʿah: 82], he said: “Your shirk – ‘We were given rain by the nawʾ of such-and-such, by the star of such-and-such.’”
items.ma-678: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr and Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, both said: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray witr with nine surahs from the Mufaṣṣal. Aswad said: He would recite in the first rakʿah: {Competition in increase has diverted you}, and {Indeed, We sent it down on Laylat al-Qadr}, and {When the earth is shaken with its shaking}; and in the second rakʿah: {By the ʿaṣr}, and {When the victory of Allah and the conquest come}, and {Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar}; and in the third rakʿah: {Say: O disbelievers}, and {Perish the two hands of Abū Lahab}, and {Say: He is Allah, One}.
items.ma-679: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, I heard ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrating from Abū Jamīlah, from ʿAlī: that a slave-woman of theirs committed zinā and became pregnant, so ʿAlī came to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him, and he said: “Leave her until she gives birth – or delivers – then flog her.”
items.ma-680: Hāshim and Ḥasan narrated to us, both said: Shaybān narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, he said: Ibn Jurmūz asked permission to see ʿAlī, and he said: Who is this? They said: Ibn Jurmūz, asking permission. He said: Permit him, and let the killer of al-Zubayr enter the Fire. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Every prophet has a ḥawārī, and my ḥawārī is al-Zubayr.”
items.ma-681:
Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, Zāʾidah narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, he said: Ibn Jurmūz asked permission to see ʿAlī while I was with him, and ʿAlī said: Give the killer of the son of Ṣafiyyah the glad tidings of the Fire. Then ʿAlī said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Every prophet has a ḥawārī, and my ḥawārī is al-Zubayr.”
ʿAbd Allāh said: My father said: I heard Sufyān say: The ḥawārī is the helper.
items.ma-682: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, Shuʿbah informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, he heard ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray some of the Ḍuḥā prayer.
items.ma-683: Yūnus ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, Ḥammād – meaning Ibn Salamah – narrated to us, from Yūnus ibn Khabbāb, from Jarīr ibn Ḥayyān, from his father, that ʿAlī said: I am sending you on what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me on: he commanded me to level every grave, and to efface every idol.
items.ma-684: Yūnus narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAqīl, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had a large head and large eyes, long eyelashes, a reddish tinge in the whites of his eyes, a thick beard, and a radiant complexion. When he walked he leaned forward, as if walking down a slope, and when he turned he turned with his whole body. His hands and feet were thick-boned.
items.ma-685: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Abū Bakr informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī: that the Prophet ﷺ used to pray witr with three.
items.ma-686: Aswad narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited after he had broken ablution, before touching water. And at times Isrāʾīl said: from a man, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ.
items.ma-687: Aswad narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Mūsā al-Ṣaghīr al-Ṭaḥḥān, from Mujāhid, he said: ʿAlī said: I went out and came to an orchard. He said: And he said: “A bucket for a date.” He said: So I drew until I had filled my palm, then I came to the water and drank my fill of the sweet water – meaning: I drank – then I came to the Prophet ﷺ, and fed him some of it, and I ate some of it myself.
items.ma-688: Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Jābir, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from his father, from ʿAlī, he said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: I vowed to slaughter my she-camel, and such and such. He said: “As for your she-camel, slaughter it; and as for such and such, it is from Shayṭān.”
items.ma-689: Abū Nūḥ – meaning Qurād – narrated to us, Shuʿbah informed us, from Abū al-Tayyāḥ, I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī al-Hudhayl narrating from a man of Banū Asad, he said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib came out to us, and they asked him about witr. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to pray witr at this hour. Make the tathwīb, O Ibn al-Nabbāḥ, or call the adhān, or the iqāmah.
items.ma-690: Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, from Zāʾidah, from Simāk, from Ḥanash, from ʿAlī, he said: The Prophet ﷺ said to me: “When two disputants come before you, do not listen to the words of the first until you have heard the words of the other; then you will see how you judge.” He said: ʿAlī said: I have been a judge ever since.
items.ma-691: Abū al-Naḍr Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim narrated to us, Abū Sallām ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Muslim al-Ḥanafī narrated to us, from ʿImrān ibn Ẓabyān, from Ḥukaym ibn Saʿd Abū Tiḥyā, from ʿAlī, he said: When the Prophet ﷺ intended a journey he would say: “O Allah, with You I attack, with You I move about, and with You I travel.”
items.ma-692: Abū al-Naḍr Hāshim and Abū Dāwūd narrated to us, both said: Warqāʾ informed us, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā al-Thaʿlabī, from Abū Jamīlah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had himself cupped, and commanded me to give the cupper his wage.
items.ma-693: Bakr ibn ʿĪsā al-Rāsibī narrated to us, ʿUmar ibn al-Faḍl narrated to us, from Nuʿaym ibn Yazīd, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: The Prophet ﷺ commanded me to bring him a tray on which he would write what would keep his ummah from going astray after him. He said: I feared that his life would slip away from me. He said: I said: I will remember and retain it. He said: “I counsel you regarding the ṣalāh, the zakāh, and those whom your right hands own.”
items.ma-694: Ḥujayn narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Whoever lies about a dream he claims to have seen will be made to tie a grain of barley on the Day of Resurrection.”
items.ma-695: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr al-Muqaddamī narrated to me, Fuḍayl ibn Sulaymān – meaning al-Numayrī – narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Abī Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Iyās ibn ʿAmr al-Aslamī, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “After me there will be disagreement, or a matter; so if you are able to be at peace, then do so.”
items.ma-696: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Warkānī and Ismāʿīl ibn Mūsā al-Suddī narrated to me, and Zakariyyā ibn Yaḥyā Zaḥmawayh narrated to us, they said: Sharīk informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Saʿīd ibn Dhī Ḥuddān, from ʿAlī, he said: Allah ﷿ named war, upon the tongue of His Prophet: khudʿah (deception). Zaḥmawayh said in his hadith: upon the tongue of your Prophet.
items.ma-697: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, my father and ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar al-Qawārīrī narrated to me, both said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Abū Isḥāq, from Saʿīd ibn Dhī Ḥuddān, one who heard ʿAlī narrated to me, saying: War is deception, upon the tongue of your Prophet ﷺ.
items.ma-698: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Isḥāq ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to me, Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbbād narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Maysarah, he heard Zayd ibn Wahb, from ʿAlī: that the Prophet ﷺ was given a silk-striped ḥullah as a gift, and sent it to me, so I went off wearing it, and I recognized anger in the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: So I divided it among my women.
items.ma-699:
ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Walīd and Abū Aḥmad al-Zubayrī narrated to us, both said: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib – Sufyān said: I only know that he raised it – he said: “Whoever lies about a dream he claims to have seen will be made, on the Day of Resurrection, to tie a grain of barley.”
Abū Aḥmad said: He said: I think it was from the Prophet ﷺ.
items.ma-700: Ḥujayn ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to fast continuously until the last part of the night.
items.ma-701: Rawḥ narrated to us, Usāmah ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād ibn al-Hād, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught me to say, when distress befell me: “There is no deity but Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous. Glory be to Allah, and blessed is Allah, Rabb of the Mighty Throne. And all praise is for Allah, Rabb of the worlds.”
items.ma-702: ʿUbaydah ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, Thuwayr ibn Abī Fākhitah narrated to me, from his father, he said: Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī visited al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī while he was ill. He said: Then ʿAlī entered and said: Have you come as a visitor of the sick, O Abū Mūsā, or as a caller? He said: O Commander of the Believers, no, rather as a visitor of the sick. ʿAlī said: Then I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “No Muslim visits a sick Muslim but seventy thousand angels send blessings upon him from morning until evening, and Allah Taʿālā makes for him a kharīf in Paradise.” He said: We said: O Commander of the Believers, what is the kharīf? He said: “The channel that waters the date palms.”
items.ma-703: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿAlī ibn Ḥakīm al-Awdī narrated to me, Sharīk informed us, from ʿUthmān ibn Abī Zurʿah, from Zayd ibn Wahb, he said: A group of the Khawārij from the people of al-Baṣrah came to ʿAlī, among them a man called al-Jaʿd ibn Baʿjah. He said to him: Fear Allah, O ʿAlī, for you will die. ʿAlī said: Rather, I will be killed – a blow upon this will dye this – meaning his beard from his head – a covenant covenanted, a decree decreed, and he who invents falsehood has failed. And he reproached him about his clothing. He said: What concern is my clothing of yours? It is further from arrogance, and more fitting for a Muslim to follow me in it.
items.ma-704: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, he said: And Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī mentioned from al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Aʿwar, he said: I said: I will surely go to the Commander of the Believers and ask him about what I heard this evening. He said: So I came to him after ʿishāʾ and entered upon him, and he mentioned the hadith. He said: Then he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Jibrīl came to me and said: O Muḥammad, your ummah will be in disagreement after you. He said: I said to him: Then where is the way out, O Jibrīl? He said: The Book of Allah Taʿālā, by which Allah shatters every tyrant. Whoever holds fast to it is saved, and whoever abandons it is destroyed – twice – a decisive word, not a jest; tongues do not fabricate it, and its wonders do not end. In it is the news of those before you, the judgment of what is between you, and the report of what will come after you.”
items.ma-705: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, Ḥakīm ibn Ḥakīm ibn ʿAbbād ibn Ḥunayf narrated to me, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Shihāb, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥusayn, from his father, from his grandfather ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon me and Fāṭimah at night and woke us for the ṣalāh. He said: Then he returned to his house and prayed for a good while of the night. He said: He heard no sound from us, so he returned to us, woke us, and said: “Get up and pray.” He said: I sat up rubbing my eyes and said: By Allah, we pray only what has been written for us; our souls are only in the Yad of Allah, and when He wills to raise us, He raises us. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned away, saying and striking his thigh with his hand: “We pray only what has been written for us, we pray only what has been written for us!” {And man has ever been, more than anything, argumentative}.
items.ma-706: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Aḥmad ibn Jamīl Abū Yūsuf narrated to us, Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Ḥumayd ibn Abī Ghaniyyah informed us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abī Sulaymān, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Zayd ibn Wahb, he said: When the Khawārij rose at al-Nahrawān, ʿAlī stood among his companions and said: These people have shed unlawful blood and raided the grazing herds of the people, and they are the nearest enemy to you; and if you march against your enemy, I fear these will take your place behind you. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “A group will come out from my ummah; your ṣalāh is nothing beside their ṣalāh, your fasting nothing beside their fasting, your recitation nothing beside their recitation. They recite the Qurʾān thinking it is for them, while it is against them; it does not pass beyond their throats. They pass out of Islam as the arrow passes out of the game.” And the sign of that is that among them is a man with an upper arm but no forearm, upon which is something like the nipple of a breast, with white hairs on it. If the army that overcomes them knew what is theirs upon the tongue of their Prophet, they would rely on the deed. So march in the name of Allah … and he mentioned the hadith at length.
items.ma-707: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbbād ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr narrated to me, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, he said: By Allah, we were with ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān at al-Juḥfah, and with him a group of the people of al-Shām, among them Ḥabīb ibn Maslamah al-Fihrī, when ʿUthmān said – tamattuʿ by ʿumrah up to Ḥajj having been mentioned to him – The most complete way for Ḥajj and ʿumrah is that they not be in the months of Ḥajj; so if you delay this ʿumrah until you visit this House twice, it would be better, for Allah Taʿālā has made ample the good. And ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib was in the bottom of the valley feeding a camel of his. He said: What ʿUthmān had said reached him, so he came until he stood before ʿUthmān and said: Have you set out against a Sunnah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ established, and a concession that Allah Taʿālā granted the servants in His Book, restricting them in it and forbidding it, when it was for the needy and for those from distant lands? Then he made the talbiyah for Ḥajj and ʿumrah together. ʿUthmān turned to the people and said: Did I forbid it? I did not forbid it; it was only an opinion I suggested, so whoever wishes may take it, and whoever wishes may leave it.
items.ma-708: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Salamah narrated to me, from Masʿūd ibn al-Ḥakam al-Anṣārī, then al-Zuraqī, from his mother, that she narrated to him, she said: It is as though I am looking at ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib on the white mule of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he stopped at the mountain pass of the Anṣār during the Farewell Ḥajj, saying: O people, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ says: “These are not days of fasting; they are days of eating, drinking, and remembrance.”
items.ma-709: Yaʿqūb and Saʿd narrated to us, both said: My father narrated to us, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād – Saʿd said: Ibn al-Hād – I heard ʿAlī say: I never heard the Prophet ﷺ join his father and mother for anyone other than Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, for I heard him say on the day of Uḥud: “Shoot, O Saʿd, may my father and mother be your ransom.”
items.ma-710: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥunayn narrated to me, from his father, he said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade me – I do not say, forbade you – from wearing a gold ring, from wearing qassī and safflower-dyed garments, and from reciting the Qurʾān while I am in rukūʿ. And he clothed me in a silk-striped ḥullah and I went out in it, and he said: “O ʿAlī, I did not clothe you in it for you to wear it.” He said: So I returned with it to Fāṭimah and gave her a portion of it; she took it to fold it with me, and I tore it in two. He said: She said: May your hands be covered in dust, O Ibn Abī Ṭālib, what have you done? He said: I said to her: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade me to wear it, so wear it and clothe your women.
items.ma-711: Surayj ibn al-Nuʿmān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I have pardoned you the horses and the slaves, so bring the ṣadaqah of silver: from every forty dirhams, one dirham; there is nothing in a hundred and ninety, and when it reaches two hundred, in it are five dirhams.”
items.ma-712: Abū Aḥmad al-Zubayrī narrated to us, ʿAlī ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salamah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Prophet ﷺ said to me: “Shall I not teach you words which, if you say them, you will be forgiven, even though you are already forgiven? There is no deity but Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous; there is no deity but Allah, the Most High, the Most Great; glory be to Allah, Rabb of the seven heavens and Rabb of the Mighty Throne; all praise is for Allah, Rabb of the worlds.”
items.ma-713: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from ʿImrān ibn Ẓabyān, from Abū Tiḥyā, he said: When Ibn Muljam struck ʿAlī the blow, ʿAlī said: Do to him as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wished to be done to a man who intended to kill him; he said: “Kill him, then burn him.”
items.ma-714: Muḥammad ibn Sābiq narrated to us, Ibrāhīm ibn Ṭahmān narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from al-Minhāl ibn ʿAmr, from Nuʿaym ibn Dijājah, that he said: Abū Masʿūd ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmr al-Anṣārī entered upon ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, and ʿAlī said to him: Are you the one who says: A hundred years will not come upon the people while an eye still blinks on the earth? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only said: “A hundred years will not come upon the people while an eye still blinks on the earth from among those who are alive today.” By Allah, the ease of this ummah is after a hundred years.
items.ma-715: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmr and Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, both said: Zāʾidah narrated to us, ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib narrated to us, from his father, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ furnished Fāṭimah with a khamīl, a waterskin, and a leather pillow stuffed with idhkhir. Abū Saʿīd said: palm fibre.
items.ma-716: Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Salamah and al-Mujālid, from al-Shaʿbī, that both heard him narrating: that when ʿAlī stoned the woman from the people of al-Kūfah, he flogged her on Thursday and stoned her on Friday, and said: I flog her by the Book of Allah and stone her by the Sunnah of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-717: Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān – meaning Ibn Abī al-Zinād – narrated to us, from Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn so-and-so ibn Rabīʿah ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib al-Hāshimī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aʿraj, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Rāfiʿ, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: that when he stood for the obligatory ṣalāh he would say takbīr and raise his hands level with his shoulders; and he would do the same when he finished his recitation and wished to go into rukūʿ, and he would do it when he raised his head from rukūʿ; and he would not raise his hands in any part of his ṣalāh while sitting; and when he stood up after the two prostrations he would raise his hands likewise, and say takbīr.
items.ma-718: ʿAlī ibn Ḥafṣ narrated to us, Warqāʾ informed us, from Manṣūr, from al-Minhāl, from Nuʿaym ibn Dijājah, he said: Abū Masʿūd entered upon ʿAlī and said: Are you the one who says: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: A hundred years will not come upon the people while a living soul is on the earth? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only said: “A hundred years will not come upon the people while a living soul is on the earth from among those who are alive today.” And the ease of this ummah is after the hundred.
items.ma-719: ʿAlī ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh informed us, al-Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāh informed us, from ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī, that he narrated to him from the mawlā of his wife, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: “When it is the day of Jumuʿah, the shayāṭīn go out holding the people back and discouraging them in their markets, with banners in their hands, and the angels sit at the doors of the mosques writing down the people according to their ranks: the first to come, the one who prays, and the one after him, until the imām comes out. Whoever draws near the imām, keeps silent, listens and does not speak idly, will have two shares of reward; and whoever stays far from him, listens, keeps silent and does not speak idly, will have one share of reward. Whoever draws near the imām and speaks idly, and does not keep silent or listen, will bear two shares of burden; and whoever stays far from him and speaks idly, and does not keep silent or listen, will bear one share of burden. And whoever says ‘Hush’ has indeed spoken, and whoever speaks has no Jumuʿah.” Then he said: Thus I heard your Prophet.
items.ma-720: Khalaf ibn al-Walīd narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, he said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “The Hour will not come until a man from among my Companions is searched for, as a stray animal is searched for, and is not found.”
items.ma-721: Khalaf ibn al-Walīd narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the one who deals in ribā, the one who consumes it, its two witnesses, the muḥill and the muḥallal lahu.
items.ma-722: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: Abū Isḥāq informed us, he said: I heard Hubayrah say: I heard ʿAlī say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade – or the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade me – the gold ring, qassī, and the mīthara.
items.ma-723: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “The mukātab is paid blood-money according to the amount he has paid.”
items.ma-724: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Zubayd al-Iyāmī, from Saʿd ibn ʿUbaydah, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAlī: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent an army and appointed a man over them; he kindled a fire and said: Enter it. Some people wanted to enter it, and others said: We only fled from it. That was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said to those who wanted to enter it: “Had you entered it, you would have remained in it until the Day of Resurrection.” And he said something good to the others, and said: “There is no obedience in disobedience to Allah; obedience is only in what is right.”
items.ma-725: Wahb ibn Jarīr narrated to us, my father narrated to us, I heard al-Aʿmash narrating from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Abū al-Bakhtarī, from ʿAlī, he said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said to the people: What do you think of the surplus that remains with us from this wealth? The people said: O Commander of the Believers, we have kept you from your family, your estate and your trade, so it is yours. Then he said to me: What do you say? I said: They have advised you. He said: Speak. I said: Why do you turn your certainty into conjecture? He said: You must make good what you have said. I said: Yes, by Allah, I will. Do you remember when the Prophet of Allah ﷺ sent you to collect ṣadaqah, and you came to al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and he withheld his ṣadaqah from you, and something passed between you? You said to me: Come with me to the Prophet ﷺ. We found him heavy-hearted, so we returned; then we went to him the next morning and found him in good spirits. You told him what al-ʿAbbās had done, and he said to you: “Do you not know that a man's paternal uncle is the twin of his father?” And we told him what we had seen of his heaviness on the first day, and what we had seen of his good spirits on the second day. He said: “You came to me on the first day while two dīnārs of the ṣadaqah remained with me, and what you saw of my heaviness was because of them; and you came to me today after I have sent them off, and that is what you saw of my good spirits.” ʿUmar said: You have spoken the truth. By Allah, I will thank you for the first and the last.
items.ma-726: Yūnus narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAjlān, from Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād ibn al-Hād, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught me these words and commanded me, if distress or hardship befell me, to say them: “There is no deity but Allah, the Generous, the Forbearing. Glory be to Him, and blessed is Allah, Rabb of the Mighty Throne. And all praise is for Allah, Rabb of the worlds.”
items.ma-727: Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Zādhān, from ʿAlī, he said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “Whoever leaves the place of a single hair from janābah that water did not reach, Allah Taʿālā will do such-and-such to him of the Fire.” ʿAlī said: From that time I have been hostile to my hair.
items.ma-728: Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAqīl, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī Ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah, from his father, he said: The Prophet ﷺ was shrouded in seven garments.
items.ma-729:
Abū Saʿīd narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Mājishūn narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Faḍl and al-Mājishūn narrated to us, from al-Aʿraj, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Rāfiʿ, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib: that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said takbīr, he would begin the ṣalāh and then say: “I have turned my face to Him who originated the heavens and the earth, as a ḥanīf and a Muslim, and I am not of the polytheists. Indeed my ṣalāh, my nusuk, my living and my dying are for Allah, Rabb of the worlds. He has no partner; with that I have been commanded, and I am of the Muslims – and Abū al-Naḍr said: and I am the first of the Muslims. O Allah, there is no deity but You; You are my Rabb and I am Your servant. I have wronged myself and acknowledged my sin, so forgive me all my sins; none forgives sins but You. Guide me to the best of character; none guides to the best of it but You; and turn away from me its evil; none turns away its evil from me but You. You are blessed and exalted; I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance.”
And when he went into rukūʿ he would say: “O Allah, to You I have bowed, in You I have believed, and to You I have submitted; my hearing, my sight, my marrow, my bones and my sinews have humbled themselves to You.”
And when he raised his head from the rukūʿ he would say: “Samiʿa Allāhu liman ḥamidah. Our Rabb, to You is all praise, filling the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and filling whatever You will beyond that.”
And when he prostrated he would say: “O Allah, to You I have prostrated, in You I have believed, and to You I have submitted. My face has prostrated to Him who created it, fashioned it, and made its form beautiful, and split its hearing and sight. Blessed is Allah, the best of creators.”
And when he gave the salām at the end of the ṣalāh he would say: “O Allah, forgive me what I have sent ahead and what I have left behind, what I have concealed and what I have made public, what I have been extravagant in, and what You know better than I. You are the One who advances and the One who delays; there is no deity but You.”
items.ma-730: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Fiṭr narrated to us, from Mundhir, from Ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah, he said: ʿAlī said: O Messenger of Allah, what if a son is born to me after you; may I name him with your name and give him your kunyah? He said: “Yes.” So it was a concession from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to ʿAlī.
items.ma-731: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from ʿAdī ibn Thābit, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, from ʿAlī, he said: The Prophet ﷺ made a covenant with me: that none loves you but a believer, and none hates you but a hypocrite.
items.ma-732: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Salamah, from Ḥujayyah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to examine the eye and the ear closely.
items.ma-733: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Muslim al-Baṭīn, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam, he said: We were travelling with ʿUthmān, and there was a man making the talbiyah for both together. ʿUthmān said: Who is this? They said: ʿAlī. He said: Do you not know that I have forbidden this? He said: Indeed, but I would not leave the word of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for your word.
items.ma-734: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Ḥujayyah, he said: A man asked ʿAlī about the cow. He said: On behalf of seven. He said: And one with a broken horn? He said: It does not harm you. He said: And a lame one? He said: If it reaches the place of sacrifice, slaughter it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to examine the eye and the ear closely.
