items.ma-735: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim and Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ narrated to us, from Ibn Sīrīn, both heard it from ʿAbīdah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A people will come out, among them a man with a stunted hand – or with a small hand, or with a deformed hand. Were it not that you would become arrogant, I would inform you of what Allah has promised those who kill them, upon the tongue of His Prophet ﷺ.” ʿAbīdah said: I said to ʿAlī: Did you hear it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? He said: Yes, by the Rabb of the Kaʿbah; yes, by the Rabb of the Kaʿbah; yes, by the Rabb of the Kaʿbah.
items.ma-736: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā al-Thaʿlabī, from Abū Jamīlah al-Ṭuhawī, from ʿAlī: that a female servant of the Prophet ﷺ committed an offence, and the Prophet ﷺ commanded me to carry out the ḥadd upon her. I went to her and found that she had not yet stopped bleeding. I came to him and told him, and he said: “When her bleeding has stopped, carry out the ḥadd upon her. Carry out the ḥudūd upon those whom your right hands own.”
items.ma-737: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd Khayr, from ʿAlī, he said: I used to think the underside of the feet more deserving of wiping than their top, until I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wipe over their top.
items.ma-738: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿUthmān al-Thaqafī, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade us to let a donkey mount a mare.
items.ma-739: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “If I were to appoint a successor without consultation, I would appoint Ibn Umm ʿAbd.”
items.ma-740: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, ʿAlī narrated to us: that Fāṭimah complained to the Prophet ﷺ of the mark of the dough on her hand. Captives came to the Prophet ﷺ, and she went to him to ask for a servant, but did not find him, and returned. He said: He came to us when we had already taken to our beds. He said: I went to get up, and he said: “Stay where you are.” He came and sat until I felt the coolness of his feet. He said: “Shall I not guide you to something better for you than a servant? When you take to your bed, glorify Allah thirty-three times, praise Him thirty-three times, and say takbīr thirty-four times.”
items.ma-741: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Ḥabīb, from Abū Wāʾil, from Abū al-Hayyāj al-Asadī, he said: ʿAlī said to me: Shall I send you on what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me on? That you not leave any image without effacing it, nor any raised grave without leveling it.
items.ma-742: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Thuwayr ibn Abī Fākhitah, from his father, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to love this surah: {Exalt the name of your Rabb, the Most High}.
items.ma-743: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, he said: Three men came to the Prophet ﷺ. One of them said: O Messenger of Allah, I had a hundred dīnārs and gave ten dīnārs of it in ṣadaqah. The other said: O Messenger of Allah, I had ten dīnārs and gave one dīnār of it in ṣadaqah. And the other said: O Messenger of Allah, I had one dīnār and gave a tenth of it in ṣadaqah. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “You are all equal in reward; each of you gave a tenth of his wealth.”
items.ma-744: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī and Misʿar narrated to us, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hurmuz, from Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had thick hands and feet, and large joints.
items.ma-745: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sharīk, from Simāk, from Ḥanash, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When two disputants sit before you, do not speak until you have heard from the other as you heard from the first.”
items.ma-746: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Masʿūdī informed us, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hurmuz, from Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was neither tall nor short; he had a large head and beard, thick hands and feet, a reddish tinge in his face, a long line of hair from chest to navel, and large joints. When he walked he leaned forward as if descending a slope. I never saw anyone like him before him or after him ﷺ.
items.ma-747: Yazīd narrated to us, Isrāʾīl informed us, from Thuwayr ibn Abī Fākhitah, from his father, from ʿAlī, he said: Kisrā sent a gift to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he accepted it from him; Qayṣar sent him a gift and he accepted it from him; and the kings sent him gifts and he accepted them from them.
items.ma-748: Yazīd narrated to us, from al-Ḥajjāj, from al-Ḥakam, from al-Qāsim ibn Mukhaymirah, from Shurayḥ ibn Hāniʾ, he said: I asked ʿĀʾishah about wiping, and she said: Ask ʿAlī, for he knows better than I; he used to travel with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: So I asked ʿAlī and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “For the traveller, three days and their nights; and for the resident, a day and a night.”
items.ma-749: Yazīd narrated to us, from al-Ḥajjāj, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAlī ibn Rabīʿah, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ, like it.
items.ma-750: Yazīd narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq informed us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Abī al-Ṣaʿbah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zurayr al-Ghāfiqī, he said: I heard ʿAlī say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took gold in his right hand and silk in his left, then raised his hands with them and said: “These two are forbidden to the males of my ummah.”
items.ma-751: Yazīd narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah informed us, from Hishām ibn ʿAmr, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām, from ʿAlī: that the Prophet ﷺ used to say at the end of his witr: “O Allah, I seek refuge in Your riḍā from Your sakhaṭ, and in Your pardon from Your punishment, and I seek refuge in You from You. I cannot count praise of You; You are as You have praised Yourself.”
items.ma-752: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us, Khālid ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, from Muṭarrif, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade people to raise their voices in recitation of the Qurʾān over one another between al-Maghrib and al-ʿIshāʾ.
items.ma-753: Yazīd narrated to us, Sharīk ibn ʿAbd Allāh informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAlī ibn Rabīʿah, he said: I saw ʿAlī, to whom a mount was brought for him to ride. When he put his foot in the stirrup he said: In the name of Allah. When he settled upon it he said: Praise be to Allah. {Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could never have subdued it. And indeed, to our Rabb we will return.} Then he praised Allah three times and said takbīr three times, then said: Glory be to You, there is no deity but You; I have wronged myself, so forgive me. Then he laughed. I said: What are you laughing at, O Commander of the Believers? He said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do as I have done, then laugh, and I said: What are you laughing at, O Messenger of Allah? He said: “The Rabb Yaʿjabu at His servant when he says: My Rabb, forgive me, and He says: My servant knew that none forgives sins but Me.”
items.ma-754:
Yazīd narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Yaʿlā ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yasār: that ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth visited al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, and ʿAlī said to him: Do you visit al-Ḥasan while in your heart is what is in it? ʿAmr said to him: You are not my Rabb that you may turn my heart wherever you wish. ʿAlī said: That does not prevent us from giving you sincere advice. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “There is no Muslim who visits his brother but Allah sends seventy thousand angels who send blessings upon him, whatever hour of the day it is until evening, and whatever hour of the night it is until morning.”
ʿAmr said to him: What do you say about walking with the funeral: in front of it or behind it? ʿAlī said: The merit of walking behind it over walking in front of it is like the merit of the obligatory ṣalāh in congregation over praying alone. ʿAmr said: But I saw Abū Bakr and ʿUmar walking in front of the funeral. ʿAlī said: They disliked to put the people in difficulty.
items.ma-755: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Maysarah, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ clothed me in a silk-striped ḥullah, and I went out in it, and I saw anger in his face. He said: So I tore it up among my women.
items.ma-756: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Qatādah, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaqīq said: ʿUthmān used to forbid the mutʿah, and ʿAlī used to command it. ʿUthmān said to ʿAlī: You are such-and-such. Then ʿAlī said: You know that we performed tamattuʿ with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: Indeed, but we were afraid.
items.ma-757: Muʿādh ibn Hishām narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Qatādah, from Abū Ḥarb ibn Abī al-Aswad, from Abū al-Aswad al-Dīlī, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said concerning the nursing infant: “The urine of the boy is sprinkled, and the urine of the girl is washed.” Qatādah said: This is as long as they have not eaten food; once they have eaten, both are washed.
items.ma-758: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Ribʿī ibn Ḥirāsh, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “No servant believes until he believes in four: until he testifies that there is no deity but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah, whom He sent with the truth; and until he believes in the resurrection after death; and until he believes in al-qadar.”
items.ma-759: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, he said: I heard Nājiyah ibn Kaʿb narrating from ʿAlī: that he came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: Abū Ṭālib has died. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: “Go and bury him.” He said: He died a polytheist. He said: “Go and bury him.” He said: When I had buried him I returned to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said to me: “Bathe.”
items.ma-760: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Saʿīd – meaning Ibn Abī ʿArūbah – narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtaybah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me to sell two boys who were brothers, and I sold them, separating them. I mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ and he said: “Catch up with them and bring them back, and do not sell them except together.”
items.ma-761: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, he said: Witr is not obligatory like the form of the ṣalāh, but it is a Sunnah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ established.
items.ma-762: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Sufyān, Shuʿbah and Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Hubayrah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Prophet ﷺ used to wake his family in the last ten nights of Ramaḍān.
items.ma-763: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh – meaning Ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAqīl – from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī that he heard ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I have been given what none of the prophets was given.” We said: O Messenger of Allah, what is it? He said: “I have been aided with terror; I have been given the keys of the earth; I have been named Aḥmad; earth has been made a means of purification for me; and my ummah has been made the best of nations.”
items.ma-764: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Isrāʾīl informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray witr at the adhān, and pray the two rakʿahs of al-Fajr at the iqāmah.
items.ma-765: Abū al-Naḍr narrated to us, al-Ashjaʿī narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Jābir, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nujayy, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: We mentioned al-Dajjāl in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ while he was asleep. He woke with his colour flushed and said: “Something other than that I fear more for you.” He mentioned a word.
items.ma-766: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from ʿUthmān ibn Abī Zurʿah, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAlqamah, from ʿAlī, he said: A mule, or a she-mule, was given as a gift to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I said: What is this? He said: “A mule, or a she-mule.” I said: And from what is it? He said: “A donkey is made to cover a mare, and this comes out of the two of them.” I said: Should we not make so-and-so cover so-and-so? He said: “No; only those who do not know do that.”
items.ma-767: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubārak narrated to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Zaḥr, from ʿAlī ibn Yazīd, from al-Qāsim, from Abū Umāmah, from ʿAlī, he said: Whenever I asked permission to see the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, if he was in ṣalāh he would say subḥān Allāh, and if he was not, he would give permission.
items.ma-768: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, from Sufyān ibn Saʿīd, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith, from Zayd ibn ʿAlī, from his father, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Rāfiʿ, from ʿAlī: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to the place of sacrifice at Minā and said: “This is the place of sacrifice, and all of Minā is a place of sacrifice.”
items.ma-769: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Hāniʾ ibn Hāniʾ, from ʿAlī, he said: When al-Ḥasan was born I named him Ḥarb. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and said: “Show me my son; what have you named him?” I said: Ḥarb. He said: “Rather he is Ḥasan.” When al-Ḥusayn was born I named him Ḥarb. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and said: “Show me my son; what have you named him?” I said: Ḥarb. He said: “Rather he is Ḥusayn.” When the third was born I named him Ḥarb. The Prophet ﷺ came and said: “Show me my son; what have you named him?” I said: Ḥarb. He said: “Rather he is Muḥassin.” Then he said: “I have named them with the names of the sons of Hārūn: Shabbar, Shabbīr and Mushabbir.”
items.ma-770: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Hāniʾ ibn Hāniʾ and Hubayrah ibn Yarīm, from ʿAlī, he said: When we left Makkah, the daughter of Ḥamzah followed us calling: O uncle, O uncle. He said: I took her by her hand and handed her to Fāṭimah, saying: Here is your cousin. He said: When we reached al-Madīnah, we disputed over her, I, Jaʿfar and Zayd ibn Ḥārithah. Jaʿfar said: She is the daughter of my uncle and her maternal aunt is with me – meaning Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays. Zayd said: She is the daughter of my brother. And I said: I took her, and she is the daughter of my uncle. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “As for you, Jaʿfar, you resemble me in my form and my character. As for you, ʿAlī, you are from me and I am from you. As for you, Zayd, you are our brother and our mawlā. The girl is to be with her maternal aunt, for the maternal aunt is a mother.” I said: O Messenger of Allah, will you not marry her? He said: “She is the daughter of my brother through nursing.”
items.ma-771: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Khalīl, from ʿAlī, he said: I heard a man asking forgiveness for his parents while they were both polytheists. I said: Does a man ask forgiveness for his parents while they are polytheists? He said: Did Ibrāhīm not ask forgiveness for his father? I mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and there was revealed: {It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists} up to His saying: {he disassociated himself from him} [al-Tawbah: 113–114]. He said: “When he died.” I do not know whether Sufyān said it, or Isrāʾīl said it, or whether it is in the hadith: “When he died”?
items.ma-772: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Mūsā ibn Ayyūb narrated to us, my uncle Iyās ibn ʿĀmir narrated to me, I heard ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray during the night, with ʿĀʾishah lying across between him and the qiblah.
items.ma-773: Ḥajjāj and Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, both said: Fiṭr narrated to us, from al-Qāsim ibn Abī Bazzah, from Abū al-Ṭufayl – Ḥajjāj said: I heard ʿAlī say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Even if only one day of the world remained, Allah ﷿ would send a man from us who would fill it with justice as it was filled with injustice.” Abū Nuʿaym said: “a man from me.” He said: And I heard him once mention it from Ḥabīb, from Abū al-Ṭufayl, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ.
items.ma-774: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to me, from Abū Isḥāq, from Hāniʾ, from ʿAlī, he said: Al-Ḥasan most resembled the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from the chest to the head, and al-Ḥusayn most resembled the Prophet ﷺ in what was below that.
items.ma-775: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, he said: Yūnus ibn Abī Isḥāq informed me, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū Juḥayfah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever commits a sin in this world and is punished for it, Allah is too just to double His punishment upon His servant; and whoever commits a sin in this world, and Allah conceals it for him and pardons him, Allah is too generous to go back on something He has pardoned.”
items.ma-776: Abū Saʿīd, the mawlā of Banū Hāshim, narrated to us, Yaḥyā ibn Salamah – meaning Ibn Kuhayl – narrated to us, he said: I heard my father narrating from Habbah al-ʿUranī, he said: I saw ʿAlī laugh on the minbar; I had not seen him laugh more than that, until his molars showed. Then he said: I remembered the words of Abū Ṭālib. Abū Ṭālib came upon us while I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and we were praying at Baṭn Nakhlah, and he said: What are you two doing, O son of my brother? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called him to Islam, and he said: There is no harm in what you two are doing, or in what you two are saying, but by Allah, my rear will never be raised above me. And he laughed in wonder at his father's words. Then he said: O Allah, I do not acknowledge that any servant of Yours from this ummah worshipped You before me other than Your Prophet – three times – I prayed seven years before the people prayed.
items.ma-777: ʿAbd Allāh said: I found this hadith in my father's book, and most of my knowledge – if Allah wills – is that I heard it from him: Abū Saʿīd, the mawlā of Banū Hāshim, narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hubayrah narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zurayr al-Ghāfiqī, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in ṣalāh one day and then turned away; then he came back with his head dripping water and led us in ṣalāh. Then he said: “I led you in ṣalāh a moment ago while I was in janābah; so whoever is afflicted as I was afflicted, or finds a rumbling in his belly, let him do as I have done.”
items.ma-778: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Laylā, from al-Minhāl, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, he said: My father used to converse at night with ʿAlī, and ʿAlī would wear summer clothes in winter and winter clothes in summer. It was said to him: Why do you not ask him? So he asked him, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for me on the day of Khaybar while I had sore eyes, and I said: O Messenger of Allah, my eyes are sore. He spat in my eye and said: “O Allah, remove from him heat and cold.” I have not felt heat or cold since that day. And he said: “I will give the banner to a man who loves Allah and His Messenger, and whom Allah and His Messenger Yuḥibbu; he is not one who flees.” The Companions of the Prophet ﷺ strained to be chosen for it, and he gave it to me.
items.ma-779: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, he said: Abū Isḥāq, from Hāniʾ ibn Hāniʾ, from ʿAlī, he said: I was sitting with the Prophet ﷺ when ʿAmmār came and asked permission. He said: “Give him permission; welcome to the good, the purified.”
items.ma-780: Abū Saʿīd, the mawlā of Banū Hāshim, narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam and another, from al-Qāsim ibn Mukhaymirah, from Shurayḥ ibn Hāniʾ, he said: I asked ʿĀʾishah about wiping over the khuffs, and she said: Ask ʿAlī. I asked him and he said: Three days and their nights – meaning for the traveller – and a day and a night for the resident.
items.ma-781: Ibn al-Ashjaʿī narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Sufyān, from ʿAbdah ibn Abī Lubābah, from al-Qāsim ibn Mukhaymirah, from Shurayḥ ibn Hāniʾ, he said: ʿAlī commanded me to wipe over the khuffs.
items.ma-782: Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Mukhāriq, from Ṭāriq ibn Shihāb, he said: I witnessed ʿAlī saying on the minbar: By Allah, we have no book to recite to you except the Book of Allah Taʿālā and this ṣaḥīfah – hanging from his sword – which I took from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; in it are the obligations of ṣadaqah. It was hanging from a sword of his whose fittings were iron – or he said: whose rings were iron.
items.ma-783:
Hāshim narrated to us, Sulaymān – meaning Ibn al-Mughīrah – narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal al-Hāshimī narrated to us, he said: My father al-Ḥārith was in charge of one of the affairs of Makkah in the time of ʿUthmān, and ʿUthmān came to Makkah. ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith said: I met ʿUthmān with hospitality at Qudayd. The people of the water had hunted partridge, and we cooked it in water and salt and made it bones for tharīd, and presented it to ʿUthmān and his companions, but they held back. ʿUthmān said: Game I did not hunt, and we did not command it to be hunted; a people not in iḥrām hunted it and fed it to us – what is the harm? Then ʿUthmān said: Who says anything about this? They said: ʿAlī.
So he sent for ʿAlī, and he came. ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith said: It is as though I am looking at ʿAlī when he came, brushing the leaves off his palms. ʿUthmān said to him: Game we did not hunt and did not command to be hunted; a people not in iḥrām hunted it and fed it to us – what is the harm? ʿAlī became angry and said: I adjure by Allah any man who was present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when a leg of a wild donkey was brought to him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “We are people in iḥrām; feed it to those not in iḥrām.” He said: Twelve men of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ testified. Then ʿAlī said: I adjure by Allah any man who was present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when ostrich eggs were brought, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “We are people in iḥrām; feed it to those not in iḥrām.” He said: Fewer than the twelve testified. He said: Then ʿUthmān turned his hip away from the food and went into his lodging, and the people of the water ate that food.
items.ma-784: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Hudbah ibn Khālid narrated to me, Hammām narrated to us, ʿAlī ibn Zayd narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith: that his father was in charge of ʿUthmān's food. He said: It is as though I am looking at the partridge around the bowls. A man came and said: ʿAlī dislikes this. So he sent for ʿAlī, who had his hands smeared with leaves, and said: You disagree with us a great deal. ʿAlī said: I remind by Allah whoever was present with the Prophet ﷺ when the hindquarter of a wild donkey was brought to him while he was in iḥrām, and he said: “We are in iḥrām; feed it to those not in iḥrām.” Men stood and testified. Then he said: I remind by Allah any man who was present with the Prophet ﷺ when five eggs were brought – ostrich eggs – and he said: “We are in iḥrām; feed it to those not in iḥrām.” Men stood and testified. Then ʿUthmān stood and entered his tent, and they left the food to the people of the water.
items.ma-785: Hāshim narrated to us, Layth – meaning Ibn Saʿd – narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from Abū al-Khayr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zurayr al-Ghāfiqī, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, that he said: A she-mule was given as a gift to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. We said: O Messenger of Allah, what if we had donkeys cover our mares so that they bore us the like of this? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Only those who do not know do that.”
items.ma-786: Hāshim narrated to us, Abū Khaythamah narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, he said: Witr is not obligatory, but it is a Sunnah from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; and Allah ﷿ is Witr, and Yuḥibbu the witr.
items.ma-787: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, my father Isḥāq ibn Yasār narrated to me, from Miqsam Abū al-Qāsim, the mawlā of ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal, from his master ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith, he said: I performed ʿumrah with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib in the time of ʿUmar, or the time of ʿUthmān, and he stayed with his sister Umm Hāniʾ bint Abī Ṭālib. When he finished his ʿumrah he returned, and water was poured for him for a bath, and he bathed. When he had finished his bath a group of the people of al-ʿIrāq came in to him and said: O Abū Ḥasan, we have come to ask you about a matter we would like you to tell us about. He said: I think al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah has been telling you that he was the last of the people in time with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? They said: Yes, it is about that we have come to ask you. He said: The last of the people in time with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was Quthum ibn al-ʿAbbās.
items.ma-788: ʿAffān narrated to us, Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, ʿUtaybah narrated to us, from Burayd ibn Aṣram, he said: I heard ʿAlī say: A man of Ahl al-Ṣuffah died and left two dīnārs, or two dirhams, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Two brandings. Pray over your companion.”
items.ma-789: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Aʿlā al-Thaʿlabī narrated to us, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “Whoever lies deliberately about a dream will be made to tie a grain of barley on the Day of Resurrection.”
items.ma-790: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān Luwayn narrated to me, Muḥammad ibn Jābir narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from ʿUmārah ibn Ruwaybah, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: My two ears heard and my heart retained it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: “The people are followers of Quraysh; their righteous follow their righteous, and their wicked follow their wicked.”
items.ma-791: ʿAffān narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, Qatādah narrated to us, a man of Banū Sadūs called Jurayy ibn Kulayb narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib: that the Prophet ﷺ forbade an animal with a cut ear or broken horn. He said: I asked Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib and he said: “Half, or more than that.”
items.ma-792: ʿAffān narrated to us, Muʿādh ibn Muʿādh narrated to us, Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ narrated to us, from Abū al-Miqdām, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Azraq, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in to me while I was sleeping on the sleeping-mat, and al-Ḥasan or al-Ḥusayn asked for something to drink. He said: The Prophet ﷺ got up and went to a ewe of ours that gave little milk, and milked her, and she gave milk. Al-Ḥasan came, and the Prophet ﷺ moved him aside. Fāṭimah said: O Messenger of Allah, is he the dearer of the two to you? He said: “No, but he asked for a drink before him.” Then he said: “I, you, these two, and this sleeper will be in one place on the Day of Resurrection.”
items.ma-793: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān Luwayn narrated to me, Ḥudayj narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū Ḥudhayfah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “I went out when the moon rose, as though it were half of a bowl, and he said: Tonight is Laylat al-Qadr.”
items.ma-794: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib informed us, from Zādhān, that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “Whoever leaves the place of a single hair on his body from janābah that water did not reach, such-and-such will be done to him of the Fire.” ʿAlī said: From that time I have been hostile to my head; from that time I have been hostile to my head.
items.ma-795: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Zādhān, that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib drank standing, and the people looked at him as though they disapproved. He said: What are you looking at? If I drink standing, I have seen the Prophet ﷺ drink standing; and if I drink sitting, I have seen the Prophet ﷺ drink sitting.
items.ma-796: ʿAffān and Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, both said: Ḥammād narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh – meaning Ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAqīl – from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had a large head and large eyes, long eyelashes – Ḥasan said: shifār – a reddish tinge in the whites of his eyes, a thick beard, and a radiant complexion; his hands and feet were thick-boned. When he walked it was as though he were walking down a slope – Ḥasan said: he leaned forward – and when he turned he turned with his whole body.
items.ma-797: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū ʿUbaydah ibn Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ narrated to us – and he said to me: it is my name and my kunyah – Mālik ibn Suʿayr – meaning Ibn al-Khims – narrated to us, Furāt ibn Aḥnaf narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ribʿī ibn Ḥirāsh: that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib stood to give a khuṭbah in al-Raḥabah. He praised Allah and extolled Him, then said what Allah willed him to say, then called for a jug of water, rinsed his mouth from it, wiped himself, and drank the remainder of his jug while standing. Then he said: It has reached me that one of you dislikes to drink while standing. This is the ablution of one who has not broken ablution, and I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do like this.
items.ma-798: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Warkānī narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Mukhāriq, from Ṭāriq, he said: ʿAlī gave us a khuṭbah and said: We have nothing of revelation – or he said: of a writing from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ – except what is in the Book of Allah and this ṣaḥīfah tied to my sword – and he had a sword whose fittings were iron – and in it are the obligations of ṣadaqah.
items.ma-799: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, ʿĀṣim ibn Bahdalah informed us, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, that it was said to ʿAlī: The killer of al-Zubayr is at the door. He said: Let the killer of the son of Ṣafiyyah enter the Fire. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Every prophet has a ḥawārī, and my ḥawārī is al-Zubayr.”
items.ma-800: ʿAffān and Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, both said: Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from al-Ḥajjāj, from al-Ḥakam, from Maymūn ibn Abī Shabīb, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave me two boys who were brothers, and I sold one of them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “What became of the two boys?” I said: I sold one of them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Take him back.”
items.ma-801: ʿAffān and Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, both said: Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAqīl – ʿAffān said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAqīl narrated to us – from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī Ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah, from his father: that the Prophet ﷺ was shrouded in seven garments.
items.ma-802: Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim narrated to us, Muḥammad – meaning Ibn Rāshid – narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAqīl, from Faḍālah ibn Abī Faḍālah al-Anṣārī – and Abū Faḍālah was one of the people of Badr – he said: I went out with my father to visit ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib in an illness that had afflicted him and grown heavy upon him. He said: My father said to him: What keeps you in this dwelling of yours? If your appointed time came, none but the bedouins of Juhaynah would attend to you. You should be carried to al-Madīnah, so that if your appointed time came, your companions would attend to you and pray over you. ʿAlī said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a covenant with me that I would not die until I was made commander, and then this – meaning his beard – would be dyed from the blood of this – meaning the crown of his head. He was killed, and Abū Faḍālah was killed with ʿAlī on the day of Ṣiffīn.
items.ma-803:
Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz – meaning Ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Salamah – narrated to us, from his uncle al-Mājishūn ibn Abī Salamah, from al-Aʿraj, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Rāfiʿ, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib: that when the Prophet ﷺ began the ṣalāh he would say takbīr and then say: “I have turned my face to Him who originated the heavens and the earth, as a ḥanīf, and I am not of the polytheists. Indeed my ṣalāh, my nusuk, my living and my dying are for Allah, Rabb of the worlds. He has no partner; with that I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims. O Allah, You are the King; there is no deity but You. You are my Rabb and I am Your servant. I have wronged myself and acknowledged my sin, so forgive me all my sins; none forgives sins but You. Guide me to the best of character; none guides to the best of it but You. Turn away from me its evil; none turns away its evil from me but You. At Your service, and happy to serve You; all good is in Your Yadayn, and evil is not to You. I am by You and to You. You are blessed and exalted; I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance.”
And when he went into rukūʿ he would say: “O Allah, to You I have bowed, in You I have believed, and to You I have submitted; my hearing, my sight, my marrow, my bones and my sinews have humbled themselves to You.”
And when he raised his head he would say: “Samiʿa Allāhu liman ḥamidah. Our Rabb, to You is all praise, filling the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and filling whatever You will beyond that.”
And when he prostrated he would say: “O Allah, to You I have prostrated, in You I have believed, and to You I have submitted. My face has prostrated to Him who created it and fashioned it and made its form beautiful, and split its hearing and sight. Blessed is Allah, the best of creators.”
And when he had finished the ṣalāh and given the salām he would say: “O Allah, forgive me what I have sent ahead and what I have left behind, what I have concealed and what I have made public, what I have been extravagant in, and what You know better than I. You are the One who advances and the One who delays; there is no deity but You.”
ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us: He said: It has reached us from Isḥāq ibn Rāhawayh, from al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl, that he said concerning this hadith: “and evil is not to You” – he said: Evil is not drawn near to You.
items.ma-804: Ḥujayn narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us, from his uncle al-Mājishūn ibn Abī Salamah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aʿraj, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Rāfiʿ, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: that when he began the ṣalāh he would say takbīr and then say: “I have turned my face …” and he mentioned the like of it, except that he said: “and turn away from me its evil.”
items.ma-805: Ḥujayn narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Faḍl al-Hāshimī, from al-Aʿraj, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Rāfiʿ, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of it.
items.ma-807: Ibrāhīm ibn Abī al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, al-Ḥasan ibn Yazīd al-Aṣamm narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Suddī Ismāʿīl mention it, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿAlī, he said: When Abū Ṭālib died I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: Your old uncle has died. He said: “Go and bury him, then do not do anything until you come to me.” He said: I buried him and then came to him. He said: “Go and bathe, then do not do anything until you come to me.” He said: I bathed and then came to him. He said: He made some supplications for me that I would not exchange for red camels and black ones. He said: And whenever ʿAlī washed the dead, he bathed.
items.ma-808: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Warkānī narrated to us in the year two hundred and twenty-seven, Abū ʿAqīl Yaḥyā ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated to us. And Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān Luwayn narrated to us in the year two hundred and forty, Abū ʿAqīl Yaḥyā ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated to us, from Kathīr al-Nawwāʾ, from Ibrāhīm ibn Ḥasan ibn Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, from his father, from his grandfather, he said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “In the last of time a people will appear called the Rāfiḍah; they reject Islam.”
items.ma-809: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Kurayb Muḥammad ibn al-ʿAlāʾ narrated to me, Ibn al-Mubārak narrated to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Zaḥr, from ʿAlī ibn Yazīd, from al-Qāsim, from Abū Umāmah, he said: ʿAlī said: “I used to come to the Prophet ﷺ and ask permission; if he was in ṣalāh he would say subḥān Allāh, and if he was not in ṣalāh he would give me permission.”
items.ma-810: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Aʿlā ibn Ḥammād narrated to me, Dāwūd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-ʿAṭṭār narrated to us, Abū ʿAbd Allāh Maslamah al-Rāzī narrated to us, from Abū ʿAmr al-Bajalī, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Sufyān al-Thaqafī, from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad Ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah Taʿālā Yuḥibbu the servant who is tried and constantly repents.”
items.ma-811: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Warkānī narrated to me, Abū Shihāb al-Ḥannāṭ ʿAbd Rabbih ibn Nāfiʿ informed us, from al-Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāh, from Abū Yaʿlā, from Muḥammad Ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: When the matter of madhy wore me out, I commanded al-Miqdād to ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about it, and he said: “From it is ablution.” – out of shyness on account of Fāṭimah.
items.ma-812: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr al-Muqaddamī narrated to me, Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAlī: that the Prophet ﷺ forbade, on the day of Khaybar, the mutʿah and the flesh of donkeys.
items.ma-813: Yūnus narrated to us, Ḥammād – meaning Ibn Salamah – narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr, that it was said to ʿAlī: The killer of al-Zubayr is at the door. ʿAlī said: The killer of the son of Ṣafiyyah will enter the Fire. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Every prophet has a ḥawārī, and my ḥawārī is al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām.”
items.ma-814: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, ʿAlī ibn Zayd informed us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal: that ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān alighted at Qudayd, and partridges were brought in bowls with their legs sticking up. He sent for ʿAlī, who was tying up a camel of his, and he came with leaves falling from his hands. ʿAlī held back, and the people held back. ʿAlī said: Who is here from Ashjaʿ? Do you know that a bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ with ostrich eggs and dried wild-game meat, and he said: “Feed them to your family, for we are in iḥrām”? They said: Yes. ʿUthmān leaned away from his seat and got down, and said: You have spoiled it for us.
items.ma-815: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, ʿAlī ibn Mudrik informed me, he said: I heard Abū Zurʿah ibn ʿAmr ibn Jarīr narrating from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nujayy, from his father, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “The angels do not enter a house in which there is a dog or an image.”
items.ma-816: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq informed us, I heard Hubayrah say: I heard ʿAlī say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade – or the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade me – the gold ring, qassī, and the mīthara.
items.ma-817: ʿAffān narrated to us, Khālid – meaning al-Ṭaḥḥān – narrated to us, Muṭarrif narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade a man to raise his voice in the recitation of the Qurʾān before al-ʿatamah and after it, confusing his companions in the ṣalāh.
items.ma-818: ʿAffān narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “The mukātab is paid blood-money according to the amount he has paid.”
items.ma-819: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib narrated to us, from his father, from ʿAlī: that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Fāṭimah to him, he sent with him a khamīlah, a leather pillow stuffed with palm fibre, two hand-mills, a waterskin and two jars.
items.ma-820: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, al-Ḥajjāj informed us, from al-Ḥasan ibn Saʿd, from his father: that Yuḥannas and Ṣafiyyah were from the captives of the khumus. Ṣafiyyah committed zinā with a man from the khumus and gave birth to a boy, and the fornicator and Yuḥannas both claimed him. They brought their dispute to ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, who referred them to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib. ʿAlī said: I will judge between them by the judgment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: “The child belongs to the firāsh, and for the fornicator is the stone.” And he flogged each of them fifty.
items.ma-821: Yaḥyā ibn Ghaylān narrated to us, al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Faḍālah narrated to us, Yazīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Salamah, from ʿAmr ibn Sulaym al-Zuraqī, from his mother, she said: We were at Minā when a crier cried out: Beware! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ says: “Do not fast, for these are days of eating and drinking.” She said: I lifted the ropes of the tent, and the crier was ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib.
items.ma-822: Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr narrated to us, Ismāʿīl ibn Zakariyyā narrated to us, from Ḥajjāj ibn Dīnār, from al-Ḥakam, from Ḥujayyah ibn ʿAdī, from ʿAlī: that al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib asked the Prophet ﷺ about paying his ṣadaqah early, before it fell due, and he granted him a concession in that.
items.ma-823: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Aḥmad ibn ʿĪsā narrated to me, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wahb narrated to us, Makhramah ibn Bukayr informed me, from his father, from Sulaymān ibn Yasār, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: We sent al-Miqdād ibn al-Aswad to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he asked him about madhy that comes out of a person: what should he do? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Perform ablution and sprinkle your private part.”
items.ma-824: Qutaybah ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, Layth ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from Ibn al-Hād, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Salamah, from ʿAmr ibn Sulaym al-Zuraqī, from his mother, that she said: While we were at Minā, ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib was on a camel, saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ says: “These are days of eating and drinking, so let none fast.” And he made the people hear.
items.ma-825: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: Abū Isḥāq informed me more than once, he said: I heard ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed witr at every part of the night: at its beginning, its middle and its end, and his witr ended at the last part of the night.
items.ma-826: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: Salamah ibn Kuhayl informed me, he said: I heard Ḥujayyah ibn ʿAdī – a man from Kindah – say: I heard a man ask ʿAlī, saying: I bought this cow for the Aḍḥā. He said: On behalf of seven. He said: The horn? He said: It does not harm you. He said: The lameness? He said: If it reaches the place of sacrifice. Then he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to examine the eye and the ear closely.
items.ma-827: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, Ḥuṣayn narrated to us, Saʿd ibn ʿUbaydah narrated to me, he said: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī and Ḥibbān ibn ʿAṭiyyah disputed, and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said to Ḥibbān: I know what emboldened your companion – meaning ʿAlī. He said: What is it, may you have no father? He said: A statement I heard him say. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me, al-Zubayr and Abū Marthad, and each of us was a horseman. He said: “Go until you reach Rawḍat Khākh, for there is a woman there with a letter from Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿah to the polytheists; bring it to me.” So we set off on our horses until we caught up with her where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had told us, travelling on a camel of hers. He had written to the people of Makkah about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ's march. We said to her: Where is the letter you have? She said: I have no letter. So we made her camel kneel and searched her saddle, but found nothing in it. My two companions said: We do not see a letter with her. I said: You both know the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not lie. Then I swore: By Him by whom I swear, if you do not bring out the letter, I will strip you. She reached for her waistband – she had wrapped it with a cloak – and took out the letter. They brought it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and said: O Messenger of Allah, he has betrayed Allah, His Messenger and the believers; let me strike his neck. He said: “O Ḥāṭib, what made you do what you did?” He said: O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, it is not that I am not a believer in Allah and His Messenger, but I wanted to have a favour with the people by which Allah would defend my family and wealth; and there is none of your companions but has someone there from his people through whom Allah Taʿālā defends his family and wealth. He said: “He has spoken the truth, so say nothing to him but good.” ʿUmar said: O Messenger of Allah, he has betrayed Allah, His Messenger and the believers; let me strike his neck. He said: “Is he not of the people of Badr? And what do you know – perhaps Allah ﷿ Iṭṭalaʿa upon them and said: Do what you wish, for Paradise is due to you.” ʿUmar's eyes filled with tears, and he said: Allah Taʿālā and His Messenger know best.
items.ma-828: Hārūn ibn Maʿrūf narrated to us – ʿAbd Allāh said: and I heard it myself from Hārūn – Ibn Wahb informed us, Saʿīd ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Juhanī narrated to me, that Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib narrated to him, from his father, from his grandfather ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Three things, O ʿAlī, do not delay: the ṣalāh when it comes, the funeral when it is present, and the unmarried woman when she finds a suitable match.”
items.ma-829: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Dāwūd al-Mubārakī Sulaymān ibn Muḥammad, neighbour of Khalaf al-Bazzār, narrated to us, Abū Shihāb narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade me the gold ring, wearing red, and reciting in rukūʿ and sujūd.
items.ma-830: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to me, ʿImrān ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Laylā narrated to us, from his father, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: Meat of game was brought to the Prophet ﷺ while he was in iḥrām, and he did not eat it.
items.ma-831: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd ibn Muḥammad al-Muḥāribī narrated to me, ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ajlaḥ narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade me to wear qassī, mīthara and safflower-dyed garments, and to recite the Qurʾān while a man is in rukūʿ or sujūd.
items.ma-832: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Muḥammad Saʿīd ibn Muḥammad al-Jarmī, who came to us from al-Kūfah, narrated to us, Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Umawī narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh (ḥ) and Saʿīd ibn Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to me, my father narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: We disputed about a surah of the Qurʾān; we said: Thirty-five verses, thirty-six verses. He said: So we went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and found ʿAlī conversing privately with him. We said: We have differed in the recitation. The face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned red, and ʿAlī said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commands you to recite as you were taught.
items.ma-833: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Tirmidhī narrated to me, Ḥammād narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim (ḥ) and ʿUbayd Allāh al-Qawārīrī narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us; al-Qawārīrī said in his hadith: ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd narrated to us, from Zirr – meaning Ibn Ḥubaysh – from Abū Juḥayfah, he said: I heard ʿAlī say: Shall I not tell you of the best of this ummah after its Prophet? Abū Bakr. Then he said: Shall I not tell you of the best of this ummah after Abū Bakr? ʿUmar.
items.ma-834: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Ṣāliḥ Hadiyyah ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhāb narrated to me in Makkah, Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd al-Ṭanāfisī narrated to us, Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb al-Bajalī narrated to us, from al-Shaʿbī, from Wahb al-Suwāʾī, he said: ʿAlī gave us a khuṭbah and said: Who is the best of this ummah after its Prophet? I said: You, O Commander of the Believers. He said: No; the best of this ummah after its Prophet is Abū Bakr, then ʿUmar. And we do not think it far-fetched that the sakīnah speaks upon the tongue of ʿUmar.
items.ma-835: Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, Manṣūr ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān – meaning al-Ghudānī al-Ashall – informed us, from al-Shaʿbī, Abū Juḥayfah, whom ʿAlī used to call Wahb al-Khayr, narrated to me, he said: ʿAlī said to me: O Abū Juḥayfah, shall I not tell you of the best of this ummah after its Prophet? He said: I said: Yes. He said – and I did not think anyone was better than him – The best of this ummah after its Prophet is Abū Bakr, and after Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and after the two of them another, a third. And he did not name him.
items.ma-836: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū Juḥayfah, he said: ʿAlī said: The best of this ummah after its Prophet is Abū Bakr, and after Abū Bakr, ʿUmar; and had I wished I would have told you of the third.
items.ma-837: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Manṣūr ibn Abī Muzāḥim narrated to us, Khālid al-Zayyāt narrated to us, ʿAwn ibn Abī Juḥayfah narrated to me, he said: My father was one of ʿAlī's police and used to be beneath the minbar. My father narrated to me: that he ascended the minbar – meaning ʿAlī – and praised Allah Taʿālā and extolled Him, and invoked blessings on the Prophet ﷺ, and said: The best of this ummah after its Prophet is Abū Bakr, and the second is ʿUmar. And he said: Allah Taʿālā places the good wherever He Aḥabba.
items.ma-838: ʿAffān narrated to us, Ḥammād narrated to us, ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib informed us, from his father, from ʿAlī: that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Fāṭimah to him, he sent with him a khamīlah, a leather pillow stuffed with palm fibre, two hand-mills, a waterskin and two jars. One day ʿAlī said to Fāṭimah: By Allah, I have drawn water until my chest has ached. He said: Allah has brought your father captives, so go and ask for a servant. She said: And I, by Allah, have ground until my hands blistered. So she went to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “What brings you, my little daughter?” She said: I came to greet you with salām – and she felt shy to ask him and returned. He said: What did you do? She said: I felt shy to ask him. So we both went to him, and ʿAlī said: O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I have drawn water until my chest has ached, and Fāṭimah said: I have ground until my hands blistered, and Allah has brought you captives and abundance, so give us a servant. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “By Allah, I will not give you two and leave the people of al-Ṣuffah with their bellies folded in hunger, not finding what to spend on them; rather I will sell them and spend their price on them.” So they returned, and the Prophet ﷺ came to them when they had got under their blanket; if they covered their heads their feet showed, and if they covered their feet their heads showed. They got up, and he said: “Stay where you are.” Then he said: “Shall I not tell you of something better than what you asked me?” They said: Yes. He said: “Words that Jibrīl taught me: glorify Allah ten times after every ṣalāh, praise Him ten times, and say takbīr ten times; and when you go to your bed, glorify thirty-three times, praise thirty-three times, and say takbīr thirty-four times.” He said: By Allah, I have not left them since the Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught them to me. He said: Ibn al-Kawwāʾ said to him: Not even on the night of Ṣiffīn? He said: May Allah fight you, O people of al-ʿIrāq! Yes, not even on the night of Ṣiffīn.
items.ma-839: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from al-Shaʿbī: that ʿAlī flogged Shurāḥah on Thursday and stoned her on Friday, and said: I flog her by the Book of Allah and stone her by the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-840: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salimah, he said: I entered upon ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib with two men: a man of my people and a man of Banū Asad – I think. He sent them on an errand and said: You are two strong men, so strive for your religion. Then he entered the place of relief and relieved himself, then came out, took a handful of water and wiped himself with it, then began to recite the Qurʾān. He said: It was as if he saw that we disapproved of that. Then he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would relieve himself, then come out and recite the Qurʾān and eat meat with us, and nothing kept him from the Qurʾān except janābah.
items.ma-841: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salimah, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: I was ill, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by me while I was saying: O Allah, if my appointed time has come, then give me rest; and if it is delayed, then raise me up; and if it is a trial, then give me patience. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “How did you say?” So he repeated to him what he had said. He said: And he struck him with his foot and said: “O Allah, grant him well-being,” or: “O Allah, heal him” – Shuʿbah was unsure. He said: I did not suffer that pain of mine after that.
items.ma-842: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from Abū Isḥāq, I heard ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah narrating from ʿAlī, he said: Witr is not obligatory like the ṣalāh, but it is a Sunnah, so do not leave it. Shuʿbah said: And I found it written with me: and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed witr.
items.ma-843: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Sharīk informed us, from Abū al-Ḥasnāʾ, from al-Ḥakam, from Ḥanash, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me to offer a sacrifice on his behalf, so I offer a sacrifice on his behalf always.
items.ma-844: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from Jābir, from al-Shaʿbī, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the one who consumes ribā, the one who feeds it, its two witnesses, its writer, the woman who tattoos and the woman who has herself tattooed for beauty, the one who withholds ṣadaqah, and the muḥill and the muḥallal lahu; and he used to forbid wailing.
items.ma-845: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from Jābir, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nujayy, from ʿAlī, he said: I used to come to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ every morning; if he cleared his throat I would enter, and if he was silent I would not enter. He said: He came out to me and said: “Something happened last night. I heard a rustling in the house, and there was Jibrīl. I said: What kept you from entering the house? He said: There is a dog in the house. He said: I went in, and there was a puppy of al-Ḥasan under a stool of ours.” He said: And he said: “The angels do not enter a house in which there are three: a dog, an image, or a person in janābah.”
items.ma-846: Mūsā ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, from Manṣūr ibn al-Muʿtamir, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith al-Aʿwar, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “If I were to appoint anyone from my ummah as commander without consultation, I would appoint Ibn Umm ʿAbd over them.”
items.ma-847: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, Rizām ibn Saʿīd al-Taymī narrated to us, from Jawwāb al-Taymī, from Yazīd ibn Sharīk – meaning al-Taymī – from ʿAlī, he said: I was a man who emitted madhy often, so I asked the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “When you eject, bathe from janābah; and when you do not eject, do not bathe.”
items.ma-848: al-Walīd ibn al-Qāsim ibn al-Walīd al-Hamdānī narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, Ibrāhīm – meaning Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā – narrated to us, from Ṭāriq ibn Ziyād, he said: We went out with ʿAlī against the Khawārij and he killed them. Then he said: Look, for the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: “A people will come forth speaking the truth, which does not pass beyond their throats. They pass out of the truth as the arrow passes out of the game. Their sign is that among them is a black man with a deformed hand, with black hairs on his hand.” If it is he, then you have killed the worst of people; and if it is not he, then you have killed the best of people. We wept. Then he said: Search. We searched and found the deformed one, and we fell down in prostration, and ʿAlī fell down prostrating with us, except that he said: “They speak the word of truth.”
items.ma-849: Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, regarding {and you make your provision}, He says: your gratitude, {that you deny}: you say, “We were given rain by the nawʾ of such-and-such, by the star of such-and-such.”
items.ma-850: Muʾammal narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAlī, raising it: {and you make your provision}. Muʾammal said: I said to Sufyān: Isrāʾīl raised it. He said: Children, children!
items.ma-851:
Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq narrated to us, from Shurayḥ ibn al-Nuʿmān – Abū Isḥāq said: he was a truthful man – from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to examine the eye and the ear closely, and not to sacrifice an animal that is one-eyed, muqābalah, mudābarah, sharqāʾ, or kharqāʾ.
Zuhayr said: I said to Abū Isḥāq: Did he mention ʿaḍbāʾ? He said: No. I said: What is the muqābalah? He said: The edge of the ear is cut. I said: What is the mudābarah? He said: The back of the ear is cut. I said: What is the sharqāʾ? He said: The ear is split. I said: What is the kharqāʾ? He said: A brand pierces its ear.
items.ma-852: Ḥasan ibn Mūsā narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, Manṣūr ibn al-Muʿtamir narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “If I were to appoint anyone from my ummah as commander without consultation among them, I would appoint Ibn Umm ʿAbd over them.”
items.ma-853: Abū Saʿīd, the mawlā of Banū Hāshim, and Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, both said: Zāʾidah narrated to us, ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib narrated to us, from his father, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ furnished Fāṭimah with a khamīl, a waterskin, and a leather pillow stuffed with palm fibre – Muʿāwiyah said: idhkhir. My father said: The khamīlah is the napped blanket.
items.ma-854: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Isrāʾīl informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Hāniʾ ibn Hāniʾ, he said: ʿAlī said: Al-Ḥasan most resembled the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from the chest to the head, and al-Ḥusayn most resembled him in what was below that.
items.ma-855: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to us, Abū Khālid al-Aḥmar narrated to us, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥayyān, from Abū al-Ṭufayl, he said: We said to ʿAlī: Tell us something the Messenger of Allah ﷺ confided to you in secret. He said: He did not confide to me anything he concealed from the people, but I heard him say: “May Allah curse whoever slaughters for other than Allah; may Allah curse whoever gives shelter to a muḥdith; may Allah curse whoever curses his parents; and may Allah curse whoever alters the boundary markers of the land” – meaning the landmarks.
items.ma-856: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Hāniʾ ibn Hāniʾ, from ʿAlī, he said: I was a man who emitted madhy often, and when I emitted madhy I would bathe. So I commanded al-Miqdād and he asked the Prophet ﷺ, and he laughed and said: “In it is ablution.”
items.ma-857: Aswad – meaning Ibn ʿĀmir – narrated to us, Isrāʾīl informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Hāniʾ ibn Hāniʾ, from ʿAlī, he said: I came to the Prophet ﷺ with Jaʿfar and Zayd. He said: He said to Zayd: “You are my mawlā,” and he hopped on one foot. He said: And he said to Jaʿfar: “You resemble me in my form and my character,” and he hopped behind Zayd. He said: And he said to me: “You are from me and I am from you,” and I hopped behind Jaʿfar.
items.ma-858: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Sulaymān narrated to me, Sulaymān ibn Ḥayyān narrated to us, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥayyān, he said: I heard ʿĀmir ibn Wāthilah say: It was said to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib: Tell us something the Messenger of Allah ﷺ confided to you in secret. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not confide to me anything he concealed from the people, but I heard him say: “May Allah curse whoever reviles his parents; may Allah curse whoever alters the boundary markers of the land; and may Allah curse whoever gives shelter to a muḥdith.”
items.ma-859: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn Abī Jaʿfar – meaning al-Farrāʾ – narrated to me, from Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, from Zayd ibn Yuthayʿ, from ʿAlī, he said: It was said: O Messenger of Allah, whom shall we appoint as commander after you? He said: “If you appoint Abū Bakr, you will find him trustworthy, ascetic in this world, desiring the Hereafter; and if you appoint ʿUmar, you will find him strong and trustworthy, fearing in Allah the blame of no blamer; and if you appoint ʿAlī – and I do not think you will – you will find him guiding and guided, taking you on the straight path.”
items.ma-860: Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū al-Tayyāḥ, he said: I heard a man of ʿAnazah narrating from a man of Banū Asad, he said: ʿAlī came out to us and said: The Prophet ﷺ commanded witr; his witr was established at this hour. O Ibn al-Nabbāḥ, call the adhān, or make the tathwīb.
items.ma-861: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū al-Tayyāḥ, a man of ʿAnazah narrated to me, from a man of Banū Asad, he said: ʿAlī came out when the muthawwib made the tathwīb for the Ṣubḥ ṣalāh, and said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to pray witr, and it was established for him at this hour.” Then he said: Make the iqāmah, O Ibn al-Nawwāḥah.
items.ma-862: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū al-Tayyāḥ, I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī al-Hudhayl al-ʿAnazī narrating from a man of Banū Asad, he said: ʿAlī came out to us … and he mentioned the like of the hadith of Suwayd ibn Saʿīd: I was with ʿUmar, and he was laid out, covered in his garment.
items.ma-863: Hāshim narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Kulayb, he said: I heard Abū Burdah narrating from ʿAlī: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade wearing a ring on this or this: the middle finger and the index finger. And Jābir – meaning al-Juʿfī – said: It is the middle finger, there is no doubt in it.
items.ma-864: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Jābir, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nujayy, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade sacrificing an animal with a broken horn or a cut ear.
items.ma-865: ʿAlī ibn Baḥr narrated to us, ʿĪsā ibn Yūnus narrated to us, Zakariyyā narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Hāniʾ ibn Hāniʾ, from ʿAlī, he said: Abū Bakr used to lower his voice when he recited, ʿUmar used to raise his voice in his recitation, and ʿAmmār, when he recited, would take from this surah and that. That was mentioned to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said to Abū Bakr: “Why do you lower your voice?” He said: I make the One I am conversing with hear me. And he said to ʿUmar: “Why do you raise your voice in your recitation?” He said: I frighten Shayṭān and wake the drowsy. And he said to ʿAmmār: “And why do you take from this surah and that?” He said: Did you hear me mix into it anything that is not from it? He said: “No.” He said: All of it is good.
items.ma-866: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Warkānī narrated to me, Abū Maʿshar Najīḥ al-Madanī, the mawlā of Banū Hāshim, narrated to us, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, he said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was laid down between the minbar and the grave, and ʿAlī came and stood in front of the rows and said: It is he, this one – three times. Then he said: The mercy of Allah be upon you. There is no one of the creation of Allah Taʿālā whom I would rather meet with his record, after the record of the Prophet ﷺ, than this one covered in his garment.
items.ma-867: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Suwayd ibn Saʿīd al-Harawī narrated to us, Yūnus ibn Abī Yaʿfūr narrated to us, from ʿAwn ibn Abī Juḥayfah, from his father, he said: I was with ʿUmar while he was covered in his garment, having met his end. ʿAlī came and uncovered the garment from his face, then said: The mercy of Allah be upon you, O Abū Ḥafṣ. By Allah, there remains after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ no one whom I would rather meet Allah Taʿālā with his record than you.
items.ma-868: ʿUbaydah ibn Ḥumayd al-Taymī Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Rukayn narrated to me, from Ḥuṣayn ibn Qabīṣah, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: I was a man who emitted madhy often, so I kept bathing in winter until my back cracked. He said: I mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, or it was mentioned to him, and he said: “Do not do that. When you see madhy, wash your male organ and perform your ablution for the ṣalāh; and when you eject the water, bathe.”
items.ma-869: ʿUbaydah narrated to us, Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād narrated to me, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAlī, he said: I was a man who emitted madhy often, so I asked the Prophet ﷺ, or he was asked about that, and he said: “In madhy is ablution, and in semen is bathing.”
items.ma-870: ʿUbaydah narrated to us, Sulaymān al-Aʿmash narrated to me, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: ʿAlī said: I was a man who emitted madhy often, so I commanded a man to ask the Prophet ﷺ about it, and he said: “In it is ablution.”
items.ma-871: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān Luwayn narrated to me, Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr, from Abū Juḥayfah, he said: ʿAlī gave us a khuṭbah and said: Shall I not tell you of the best of this ummah after its Prophet? Abū Bakr. Then he said: Shall I not tell you of the best of this ummah after its Prophet and after Abū Bakr? He said: ʿUmar.
items.ma-872: ʿĀʾidh ibn Ḥabīb narrated to us, ʿĀmir ibn al-Simṭ narrated to me, from Abū al-Gharīf, he said: Water for ablution was brought to ʿAlī. He rinsed his mouth and snuffed water into his nose three times, washed his face three times, washed his hands and forearms three times each, then wiped his head, then washed his feet. Then he said: This is how I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform ablution. Then he recited something from the Qurʾān, then said: “This is for one who is not in janābah; as for one in janābah, no, not even a verse.”
items.ma-873: Marwān ibn Muʿāwiyah al-Fazārī narrated to us, Rabīʿah ibn ʿUtbah al-Kinānī narrated to us, from al-Minhāl ibn ʿAmr, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, he said: ʿAlī wiped his head in ablution until it almost dripped, and said: This is how I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform ablution.
items.ma-874: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Abān ibn ʿImrān al-Wāsiṭī narrated to me, Sharīk narrated to us, from Mukhāriq, from Ṭāriq – meaning Ibn Shihāb – he said: I heard ʿAlī say: We have no book to recite to you except what is in the Qurʾān and what is in this ṣaḥīfah – a ṣaḥīfah that was in the scabbard of a sword he had, whose fittings were iron – which I took from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; in it are the obligations of ṣadaqah.
items.ma-875: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Asadī Luwayn narrated to us, Yaḥyā ibn Abī Zāʾidah narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, from Ziyād ibn Zayd al-Suwāʾī, from Abū Juḥayfah, from ʿAlī, he said: Part of the Sunnah in the ṣalāh is placing the palms upon the palms below the navel.
items.ma-876: Marwān narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Salʿ al-Hamdānī narrated to us, from ʿAbd Khayr, he said: ʿAlī taught us the ablution of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The servant boy poured water over his hands until he had cleaned them, then he put his hand into the leather vessel, rinsed his mouth and snuffed water into his nose, and washed his face three times and his forearms up to the elbows three times each. Then he put his hand into the vessel and pressed its bottom with his hand, then took it out and wiped the other hand with it. Then he wiped his head with his palms once, then washed his feet up to the ankles three times each. Then he scooped up a little water in his palm and drank it, and said: This is how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to perform ablution.
items.ma-877: ʿAlī ibn Baḥr narrated to us, ʿĪsā ibn Yūnus narrated to us, Zakariyyā narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O people of the Qurʾān, pray witr, for Allah ﷿ is Witr, and Yuḥibbu the witr.”
items.ma-878: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Wahb ibn Baqiyyah al-Wāsiṭī narrated to us, Khālid ibn ʿAbd Allāh informed us, from Bayān, from ʿĀmir, from Abū Juḥayfah, he said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: Shall I not tell you of the best of this ummah after its Prophet? Abū Bakr, then ʿUmar, then another man.
items.ma-879: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Mālik ibn Mighwal narrated to us, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from ʿAbd Khayr, from ʿAlī; and from al-Shaʿbī, from Abū Juḥayfah, from ʿAlī; and from ʿAwn ibn Abī Juḥayfah, from his father, from ʿAlī, that he said: The best of this ummah after its Prophet is Abū Bakr, and the best of it after Abū Bakr is ʿUmar; and had I wished I would have named the third.
items.ma-880: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Khālid (ḥ) and Abū Muʿāwiyah, Ismāʿīl narrated to us, from al-Shaʿbī, from Abū Juḥayfah, I heard ʿAlī say: The best of this ummah after its Prophet are Abū Bakr and ʿUmar; and had I wished I would have told you of the third.
items.ma-881: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: al-Ḥakam informed me, from Abū Muḥammad, from ʿAlī, he said: The Prophet ﷺ sent him to al-Madīnah and commanded him to level the graves.
items.ma-882: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Simāk, from Ḥanash, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me to Yemen. He said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, you are sending me to a people older than I am, while I am young and do not see my way in judging? He said: He placed his hand on my chest and said: “O Allah, make his tongue firm and guide his heart. O ʿAlī, when two disputants sit before you, do not judge between them until you have heard from the other as you heard from the first, for if you do that, the judgment will become clear to you.” He said: No judgment has been unclear to me since – or: none has been confusing to me since.
items.ma-883: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Minhāl, from ʿAbbād ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Asadī, from ʿAlī, he said: When this verse was revealed: {And warn your closest kindred} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 214], he said: the Prophet ﷺ gathered some of his household, and thirty gathered; they ate and drank. He said: He said to them: “Who will take on my debt and my promises, be with me in Paradise, and be my successor among my family?” A man – Sharīk did not name him – said: O Messenger of Allah, you are a sea; who could undertake this?! He said: Then he said it to another. He said: He then put that to his household, and ʿAlī said: I.
items.ma-884: Aswad narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī: that the Prophet ﷺ used to pray witr at the adhān and pray the two rakʿahs at the iqāmah.
items.ma-885: Aswad narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray sixteen rakʿahs by day.
items.ma-886: Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Rāzī narrated to us, Salamah ibn al-Faḍl narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq narrated to me, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb, from Marthad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Yazanī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zurayr al-Ghāfiqī, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to ride a donkey named ʿUfayr.
items.ma-887: ʿAlī ibn Baḥr narrated to us, Baqiyyah ibn al-Walīd al-Ḥimṣī narrated to us, al-Waḍīn ibn ʿAṭāʾ narrated to me, from Maḥfūẓ ibn ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿĀʾidh al-Azdī, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “The anus is the binding-cord of the eye, so whoever sleeps, let him perform ablution.”
items.ma-888: Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ashqar narrated to us, the son of Qābūs ibn Abī Ẓabyān al-Janbī narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, from ʿAlī, he said: When I killed Marḥab, I brought his head to the Prophet ﷺ.
items.ma-889: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Shaybān Abū Muḥammad narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, Yūnus ibn Khabbāb informed us, from Jarīr ibn Ḥayyān, from his father, that ʿAlī said to his father: I am sending you on what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me on: to level every grave and to efface every idol.
items.ma-890: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Isḥāq ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, he said: I heard ʿAlī say: I was a man who emitted madhy often, so I asked the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “In it is ablution.”
items.ma-891: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Wahb ibn Baqiyyah al-Wāsiṭī narrated to me, Khālid informed us, from Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAlī, he said: I was a man who emitted madhy often, so I asked the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “In it is ablution, and in semen is bathing.”
items.ma-892: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Umawī narrated to us, Ibn Abī Laylā narrated to us, from Ibn al-Aṣbahānī, from a grandmother of his who had been a slave-concubine of ʿAlī, she said: ʿAlī said: I was a man who slept heavily, and when I had prayed Maghrib in my clothes I would sleep – Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd said: so I would sleep before ʿishāʾ – so I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about that, and he granted me a concession.
items.ma-893: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Shaybān Abū Muḥammad narrated to me, ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muslim – meaning Abū Zayd al-Qasmalī – narrated to us, Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAlī, he said: I was a man who emitted madhy often, so I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about that, and he said: “In madhy is ablution, and in semen is bathing.”
items.ma-894: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Bakr al-Bāhilī Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAbbās narrated to me, ʿAbd al-Wahhāb – meaning al-Thaqafī – narrated to us, Ayyūb narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Karīm and Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAlī: that the Prophet ﷺ sent his sacrificial animals with him, and commanded him to give their meat, hides and covers in ṣadaqah.
items.ma-895: Shujāʿ ibn al-Walīd narrated to us, he said: Khalaf ibn Ḥawshab mentioned, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd Khayr, from ʿAlī, he said: The Prophet ﷺ took the lead, Abū Bakr came second, and ʿUmar third; then a fitnah struck us – or befell us. Allah pardons whom He wills.
items.ma-896: Abū al-Mughīrah narrated to us, Ṣafwān narrated to us, Shurayḥ – meaning Ibn ʿUbayd – narrated to me, he said: The people of al-Shām were mentioned in the presence of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib while he was in al-ʿIrāq, and they said: Curse them, O Commander of the Believers. He said: No, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “The abdāl will be in al-Shām, and they are forty men; whenever a man dies, Allah replaces him with another. By them rain is given, by them victory is granted over enemies, and by them punishment is turned away from the people of al-Shām.”
items.ma-897: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Suwayd ibn Saʿīd al-Harawī narrated to me, Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā ibn Abī Zāʾidah narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from al-Ḥasan ibn Muslim, from Mujāhid, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me in charge of the sacrificial camels, and said: “Do not give the butcher any of it.”
items.ma-898: ʿAlī ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh – meaning Ibn al-Mubārak – informed us, ʿUmar ibn Saʿīd ibn Abī Ḥusayn informed us, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, that he heard Ibn ʿAbbās say: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was laid on his bier, and the people gathered around him, supplicating and praying before he was lifted, and I was among them. Nothing startled me but a man taking me by the shoulder from behind. I turned and it was ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib. He asked mercy for ʿUmar and said: You have left behind no one dearer to me to meet Allah Taʿālā with the like of his deeds than you. By Allah, I used to think that Allah would place you with your two companions, because I often heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “I went, and Abū Bakr and ʿUmar; I entered, and Abū Bakr and ʿUmar; I came out, and Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.” And I used to think that Allah would place you with them.
items.ma-899: ʿAlī ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh informed us, Yaḥyā ibn Ayyūb informed us, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Zaḥr, from ʿAlī ibn Yazīd, from al-Qāsim, from Abū Umāmah, that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib informed him: that he used to come to the Prophet ﷺ. He said: When I found him praying, he would say subḥān Allāh and I would enter, and when he was not praying, he would give permission.
items.ma-900: Abū al-Yamān narrated to us, Shuʿayb informed us, from al-Zuhrī, ʿAlī ibn Ḥusayn informed me, that Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī informed him that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib informed him: that the Prophet ﷺ came to him and Fāṭimah, the daughter of the Prophet ﷺ, one night and said: “Will you two not pray?” I said: O Messenger of Allah, our souls are only in the Yad of Allah, and when He wills to raise us, He raises us. He turned away when I said that, and did not say anything back to me. Then I heard him, as he was going away, striking his thigh and saying: {And man has ever been, more than anything, argumentative}.
items.ma-901: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ṣāliḥ, Ibn Shihāb said: ʿAlī ibn Ḥusayn informed me that his father Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī informed him that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib informed him: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to him and Fāṭimah at night … and he mentioned the like of it.
items.ma-902: ʿAlī ibn Baḥr narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUmar ibn Kaysān narrated to us, my father said – I heard him narrating – from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wahb, from his father, from Abū Khalīfah, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed Allah is Gentle and Yuḥibbu gentleness, and gives for gentleness what He does not give for harshness.”
items.ma-903: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿUthmān ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to me, Ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Ḥakam, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAlī, he said: The Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever narrates a hadith from me that is thought to be false is one of the liars.”
items.ma-904: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr al-Muqaddamī narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ayyūb and Hishām, from Muḥammad, from ʿAbīdah, that ʿAlī mentioned the people of al-Nahrawān and said: Among them is a man with a stunted hand – or a small hand, or a deformed hand.
