Were it not that you would become arrogant, I would inform you of what Allah has promised those who kill them, upon the tongue of Muḥammad ﷺ. I said to ʿAlī: Did you hear it? He said: Yes, by the Rabb of the Kaʿbah.
items.ma-905: Manṣūr ibn Wardān al-Asadī narrated to us, ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, from his father, from Abū al-Bakhtarī, from ʿAlī, he said: When this verse was revealed: {And for Allah, upon the people, is a pilgrimage to the House – for whoever is able to find a way to it} [Āl ʿImrān: 97], they said: O Messenger of Allah, is it every year? He was silent. They said: Every year? He was silent. He said: Then they said: Every year? He said: “No; and had I said yes, it would have become obligatory.” So Allah Taʿālā sent down: {O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were shown to you, would distress you} [al-Māʾidah: 101] to the end of the verse.
items.ma-906: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from al-Qāsim ibn Mukhaymirah, from Shurayḥ ibn Hāniʾ, he said: I asked ʿĀʾishah about wiping, and she said: Go to ʿAlī, for he knows better than I. He said: So I went to ʿAlī and asked him about wiping over the khuffs. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command us to wipe over the khuffs for a day and a night, and for the traveller three.
items.ma-907: Yazīd narrated to us, Ḥajjāj informed us, raising it.
items.ma-908: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Naṣr ibn ʿAlī al-Azdī narrated to me, Bishr ibn al-Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from ʿAbd Khayr, I heard ʿAlī say: Shall I not tell you of the best of this ummah after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.
items.ma-909: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAwn narrated to me, Mubārak ibn Saʿīd, brother of Sufyān, narrated to us, from his father, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from ʿAbd Khayr al-Hamdānī, he said: I heard ʿAlī say on the minbar: Shall I not tell you of the best of this ummah after its Prophet? He said: He mentioned Abū Bakr. Then he said: Shall I not tell you of the second? He said: He mentioned ʿUmar. Then he said: Had I wished, I would have informed you of the third. He said: And he fell silent, and we thought he meant himself. I said: Did you hear him say this? He said: Yes, by the Rabb of the Kaʿbah, or else may my two ears be made deaf.
items.ma-910: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Isḥāq ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Mushir ibn ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Salʿ narrated to us, my father ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Salʿ narrated to me, from ʿAbd Khayr, from ʿAlī: that he washed his palms three times, rinsed his mouth and snuffed water into his nose three times, and washed his face three times, and said: This is the ablution of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-911: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Muslim ibn Ṣubayḥ, from Shutayr ibn Shakal, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of al-Aḥzāb: “They have kept us from the middle ṣalāh, the ʿAṣr ṣalāh. May Allah fill their graves and their houses with fire.” He said: Then he prayed it between the two ʿishāʾs, between al-Maghrib and al-ʿIshāʾ. And Abū Muʿāwiyah said once: meaning between al-Maghrib and al-ʿIshāʾ.
items.ma-912: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Khaythamah, from Suwayd ibn Ghafalah, he said: ʿAlī said: When I narrate to you a hadith from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I would rather fall from the sky than lie about him; and when I tell you something other than that, I am only a man at war, and war is deception. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “In the last of time a people will come forth, young in years, foolish in their minds. They will speak of the best of what is said among creation, but their īmān will not pass their throats. Wherever you meet them, kill them, for killing them brings a reward on the Day of Resurrection to whoever kills them.”
items.ma-913: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “I have pardoned you the horses and the slaves, and there is no zakāh on less than two hundred.”
items.ma-914: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Saʿd ibn ʿUbaydah, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAlī, he said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, why do I see you choosing selectively among Quraysh and leaving us? He said: “And do you have something in mind?” I said: The daughter of Ḥamzah. He said: “She is the daughter of my brother through nursing.”
items.ma-915: Muḥammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from Abān ibn Ṣāliḥ, from ʿIkrimah, he said: I set out from Muzdalifah with al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, and I kept hearing him make the talbiyah until he threw the Jamrat al-ʿAqabah. I asked him, and he said: I set out from Muzdalifah with my father, and I kept hearing him make the talbiyah until he threw the Jamrat al-ʿAqabah. I asked him, and he said: I set out from Muzdalifah with the Prophet ﷺ, and I kept hearing him make the talbiyah until he threw the Jamrat al-ʿAqabah.
items.ma-916: Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Maysarah, he said: I saw ʿAlī drinking while standing. He said: I said to him: You drink standing? He said: If I drink standing, I have seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ drink standing; and if I drink sitting, I have seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ drink sitting.
items.ma-917: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Isḥāq ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd Khayr, from ʿAlī, he said: I used to think the underside of the feet more deserving of wiping than their top, until I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wipe over their top.
items.ma-918: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Isḥāq ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū al-Sawdāʾ, from the son of ʿAbd Khayr, from his father, he said: I saw ʿAlī perform ablution and wash the tops of his feet, and he said: Had I not seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wash the tops of his feet, I would have thought their undersides more deserving of washing.
items.ma-919: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Isḥāq ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUqbah Abū Kibrān narrated to us, from ʿAbd Khayr, from ʿAlī, he said: This is the ablution of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then he performed ablution three times each.
items.ma-920: Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, Mughīrah narrated to us, from Umm Mūsā, she said: I heard ʿAlī say: The Prophet ﷺ commanded Ibn Masʿūd, and he climbed a tree, having been told to bring him something from it. His Companions looked at the shins of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd as he climbed the tree, and laughed at the thinness of his legs. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “What are you laughing at? The leg of ʿAbd Allāh will be heavier in the scale on the Day of Resurrection than Uḥud.”
items.ma-921: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from al-Aswad ibn Qays, from a man, from ʿAlī, that he said on the day of al-Jamal: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not make a covenant with us that we could follow concerning leadership, but it was something we saw on our own; then Abū Bakr was made successor – the mercy of Allah be upon Abū Bakr – and he established it and was upright; then ʿUmar was made successor – the mercy of Allah be upon ʿUmar – and he established it and was upright, until the religion settled firmly in place.
items.ma-922: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Wahb ibn Baqiyyah al-Wāsiṭī narrated to me, Khālid informed us, from ʿAṭāʾ – meaning Ibn al-Sāʾib – from ʿAbd Khayr, from ʿAlī, he said: Shall I not tell you of the best of this ummah after its Prophet? Abū Bakr; and the best of it after Abū Bakr: ʿUmar; then Allah places the good wherever He Aḥabba.
items.ma-923: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from Manṣūr, from al-Ḥakam, from one who heard ʿAlī and Ibn Masʿūd saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled in favour of the neighbour.
items.ma-924: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥunayn, from his father, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade me to wear a gold ring, to wear qassī, to recite in rukūʿ and sujūd, and to wear safflower-dyed garments.
items.ma-925: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, he said: Three men came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. One of them said: I had a hundred ūqiyahs and spent ten ūqiyahs of them. The other said: I had a hundred dīnārs and gave ten dīnārs of them in ṣadaqah. The other said: I had ten dīnārs and gave one dīnār of them in ṣadaqah. The Prophet ﷺ said: “You are equal in reward; each of you gave a tenth of his wealth in ṣadaqah.”
items.ma-926: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Wahb ibn Baqiyyah al-Wāsiṭī narrated to me, Khālid ibn ʿAbd Allāh informed us, from Ḥuṣayn, from al-Musayyab ibn ʿAbd Khayr, from his father, he said: ʿAlī stood and said: The best of this ummah after its Prophet are Abū Bakr and ʿUmar. And we have brought about new matters after them, in which Allah Taʿālā will decree what He wills.
items.ma-927: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar and al-Thawrī narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, he said: Witr is not obligatory like the form of the obligatory ṣalāh, but it is a Sunnah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ established.
items.ma-928: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmmār narrated to us, al-Qāsim al-Jarmī narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Khālid ibn ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Khayr, from ʿAlī: that the Prophet ﷺ performed ablution three times each.
items.ma-929: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Isrāʾīl informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī: that the Prophet ﷺ used to pray witr at the adhān.
items.ma-930: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAlī ibn Rabīʿah, once – ʿAbd al-Razzāq said: and most of the time he says: One who was present with ʿAlī when he mounted informed me: when he put his foot in the stirrup he said: In the name of Allah. When he settled he said: Praise be to Allah. Then he said: {Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could never have subdued it. And indeed, to our Rabb we will return.} Then he praised three times and said takbīr three times, then said: O Allah, there is no deity but You; I have wronged myself, so forgive me; none forgives sins but You. Then he laughed. It was said: What makes you laugh, O Commander of the Believers? He said: I saw the Prophet ﷺ do as I have done and say as I have said, then laugh, and we said: What makes you laugh, O Prophet of Allah? He said: “The servant – or he said: I was amazed at the servant – when he says: There is no deity but You, I have wronged myself, so forgive me; none forgives sins but You; he knows that none forgives sins but He.”
items.ma-931: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Hāniʾ ibn Hāniʾ and Hubayrah ibn Yarīm, from ʿAlī: that the daughter of Ḥamzah followed them calling: O uncle, O uncle. ʿAlī took her by her hand and said to Fāṭimah: Here is your cousin; take her over. ʿAlī, Zayd and Jaʿfar disputed over her. ʿAlī said: I took her, and she is the daughter of my uncle. Jaʿfar said: She is the daughter of my uncle, and her maternal aunt is married to me. Zayd said: She is the daughter of my brother. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled her to her maternal aunt and said: “The maternal aunt is in the position of the mother.” Then he said to ʿAlī: “You are from me and I am from you,” and to Jaʿfar: “You resemble me in my form and my character,” and to Zayd: “You are our brother and our mawlā.” ʿAlī said to him: O Messenger of Allah, will you not marry the daughter of Ḥamzah? He said: “She is the daughter of my brother through nursing.”
items.ma-932: Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd Khayr, from ʿAlī: The best of this ummah after its Prophet are Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.
items.ma-933: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān and Shuʿbah, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from ʿAbd Khayr, from ʿAlī, that he said: Shall I not inform you of the best of this ummah after its Prophet? Abū Bakr, then ʿUmar.
items.ma-934: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Suwayd ibn Saʿīd narrated to me, al-Ṣubayy ibn al-Ashʿath narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd Khayr, from ʿAlī: Shall I not inform you of the best of this ummah after its Prophet? Abū Bakr, and the second is ʿUmar; and had I wished I would have named the third. Abū Isḥāq said: ʿAbd Khayr spelled it out letter by letter so that they would not dispute what ʿAlī had said.
items.ma-935: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb narrated to me, from Abū al-Ṣaʿbah, from a man of Hamdān called Abū Aflaḥ, from Ibn Zurayr that he heard ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib say: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ took silk and put it in his right hand, and took gold and put it in his left, then said: “These two are forbidden to the males of my ummah.”
items.ma-936: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, Saʿīd – meaning al-Maqburī – narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Sulaym al-Zuraqī, from ʿĀṣim ibn ʿAmr, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, that he said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until, when we were at al-Ḥarrah at al-Suqyā, which belonged to Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Bring me water for ablution.” When he had performed ablution he stood facing the qiblah, said takbīr, and then said: “O Allah, Ibrāhīm was Your servant and Your khalīl, and he supplicated for blessing for the people of Makkah; and I, Muḥammad, Your servant and Your Messenger, supplicate to You for the people of al-Madīnah, that You bless them in their mudd and their ṣāʿ twice over what You blessed the people of Makkah with – with the blessing, two blessings.”
items.ma-937: Hushaym narrated to us, Abū ʿĀmir al-Muzanī informed us, an old man of Banū Tamīm narrated to us, he said: ʿAlī gave us a khuṭbah – or he said: ʿAlī said: A biting time will come upon the people, in which the well-off will bite on what is in his hands – and he was not commanded to do so; Allah ﷿ said: {And do not forget graciousness between you} [al-Baqarah: 237] – the wicked will rise up, the good will be humiliated, and people in distress will be made to sell. He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the sale of those in distress, the sale of uncertainty, and the sale of fruit before it ripens.
items.ma-938: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Khaythamah Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb narrated to us, Wakīʿ narrated to us (ḥ) and Isḥāq ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Abū Muʿāwiyah and Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Hishām ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The best of its women is Khadījah, and the best of its women is Maryam.”
items.ma-939: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Dāwūd al-Mubārakī Sulaymān ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, Abū Shihāb narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade me the gold ring, wearing red, and reciting in rukūʿ and sujūd.
items.ma-940: Hushaym narrated to us, Yūnus informed us, from al-Ḥasan, from ʿAlī: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “The pen is lifted from three: from the young until he reaches puberty, from the sleeper until he wakes, and from the afflicted until he is relieved.”
items.ma-941: Hushaym narrated to us, Ismāʿīl ibn Sālim narrated to us, from al-Shaʿbī, he said: A muḥṣan who had committed zinā was brought to ʿAlī, and he flogged him a hundred on Thursday, then stoned him on Friday. It was said to him: You combined two ḥudūd upon him? He said: I flogged him by the Book of Allah and stoned him by the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-942: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us: My father narrated to me, Hushaym narrated to us. And Abū Ibrāhīm al-Muʿaqqib said: Hushaym narrated to us, Ḥuṣayn informed us, from al-Shaʿbī, he said: A muḥṣanah freedwoman of Saʿīd ibn Qays who had committed zinā was brought to ʿAlī. He said: So he flogged her a hundred, then stoned her. Then he said: I flogged her by the Book of Allah and stoned her by the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-943: Isḥāq ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, from Sharīk, from al-Suddī, from ʿAbd Khayr, he said: I saw ʿAlī call for water to perform ablution; he wiped himself with it lightly and wiped over the top of his feet. Then he said: This is the ablution of one who has not broken ablution. Then he said: Had I not seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wipe over the top of his feet, I would have thought their undersides more deserving. Then he drank the remainder of his ablution water while standing, and said: Where are those who claim that it is not fitting for anyone to drink standing?!
items.ma-944:
ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿAlī ibn Ḥakīm narrated to me, and Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah and Ismāʿīl, the grandson of al-Suddī, said: Sharīk narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, that he described the Prophet ﷺ, saying: He had a large head, was fair with a reddish tinge, had a large beard, large joints, thick hands and feet, a long line of hair from chest to navel, and abundant, slightly wavy hair on his head. He leaned forward as he walked, as if descending a slope; he was neither tall nor short. I never saw anyone like him before him or after him ﷺ.
And ʿAlī ibn Ḥakīm said in his hadith: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib described the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to us, saying: He had a large head and beautiful, slightly wavy hair.
items.ma-945: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmmār narrated to us, al-Qāsim al-Jarmī narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Khālid ibn ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Khayr, from ʿAlī: that the Prophet ﷺ performed ablution three times each.
items.ma-946: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Surayj ibn Yūnus narrated to me, Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Umawī narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Suʿayd – or Saʿīd – from Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was neither short nor tall, with a large head and slightly wavy hair, a large beard, a reddish tinge, a long line of hair from chest to navel, large joints, and thick hands and feet. When he walked he leaned forward as if descending a slope. I never saw anyone like him before him or after him ﷺ.
items.ma-947: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Sulaymān narrated to me, Abū Khālid al-Aḥmar Sulaymān ibn Ḥayyān narrated to us, from Ḥajjāj, from ʿUthmān, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Makkī, from Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim, he said: ʿAlī was asked about the description of the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: Neither short nor tall, his colour tinged with red, with beautiful, slightly wavy hair, large joints, thick hands, a large head, and a long line of hair from chest to navel. When he walked he leaned forward as if descending a slope. I never saw anyone like him before him or after him ﷺ.
items.ma-948:
Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Ḥārithah ibn Muḍarrib, from ʿAlī, he said: When we came to al-Madīnah we ate some of its fruit and found the climate unwholesome, and fever struck us there. The Prophet ﷺ was seeking news of Badr. When it reached us that the polytheists had advanced, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ marched to Badr – and Badr is a well – and we reached it before the polytheists, and found two of them there: a man of Quraysh and a mawlā of ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ. The Qurashī escaped; as for the mawlā of ʿUqbah, we seized him, and kept asking him: How many are the people? He would say: By Allah, they are many in number and severe in might. Whenever he said that the Muslims struck him, until they brought him to the Prophet ﷺ, who said to him: “How many are the people?” He said: By Allah, they are many in number and severe in might. The Prophet ﷺ strove to make him tell how many they were, but he refused. Then the Prophet ﷺ asked him: “How many camels do they slaughter?” He said: Ten each day. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The people are a thousand: each camel for a hundred and those who follow them.”
Then a light drizzle of rain fell on us during the night, and we went under the trees and the leather shields to take shelter beneath them from the rain. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ spent the night supplicating to his Rabb ﷿, saying: “O Allah, if You destroy this band, You will not be worshipped.” He said: When dawn broke he called: “Ṣalāh, servants of Allah!” and the people came from beneath the trees and the shields, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in ṣalāh and urged us on to the fight. Then he said: “The gathering of Quraysh is beneath this red rib of the mountain.” When the people drew near us and we had lined up against them, there was a man among them on a red camel of his, going about among the people. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O ʿAlī, call Ḥamzah for me” – he was the nearest of them to the polytheists – “who is the owner of the red camel, and what is he saying to them?” Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “If there is anyone among the people who commands good, it may be the owner of the red camel.” Ḥamzah came and said: It is ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah; he is forbidding the fight and saying to them: O my people, I see a people desperate for death whom you will not reach while there is good in you. O my people, bind it today on my head and say: ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah turned coward; and you know I am not the most cowardly of you. He said: Abū Jahl heard that and said: You say this? By Allah, if anyone other than you said this I would bite him; your lungs have filled your belly with terror. ʿUtbah said: Do you taunt me, O you with the yellowed rear? Today you will know which of us is the coward. He said: Then ʿUtbah, his brother Shaybah and his son al-Walīd came forward in fierce pride, and they said: Who will duel? Six youths of the Anṣār came out, and ʿUtbah said: We do not want these; let our cousins from Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib duel us. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Rise, O ʿAlī; rise, O Ḥamzah; rise, O ʿUbaydah ibn al-Ḥārith ibn al-Muṭṭalib.” Allah Taʿālā killed ʿUtbah and Shaybah, the sons of Rabīʿah, and al-Walīd ibn ʿUtbah, and ʿUbaydah was wounded. We killed seventy of them and took seventy captive. A short man of the Anṣār came with al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib as a captive, and al-ʿAbbās said: O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, this one did not capture me; I was captured by a bald-fronted man, among the most handsome of people in face, on a piebald horse, whom I do not see among the people. The Anṣārī said: I captured him, O Messenger of Allah. He said: “Be silent; Allah Taʿālā has aided you with a noble angel.” ʿAlī said: We captured from Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib: al-ʿAbbās, ʿAqīl, and Nawfal ibn al-Ḥārith.
items.ma-949: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from al-Miqdām ibn Shurayḥ, from his father, he said: I asked ʿĀʾishah ﵂ and said: Tell me of a man among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ whom I may ask about wiping over the khuffs. She said: Go to ʿAlī and ask him, for he used to stay close to the Prophet ﷺ. He said: So I went to ʿAlī and asked him, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to wipe over our khuffs when we travelled.
items.ma-950: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿAlī ibn Ḥakīm al-Awdī narrated to us, Sharīk informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Saʿīd ibn Wahb and from Zayd ibn Yuthayʿ, both said: ʿAlī adjured the people in al-Raḥabah: Whoever heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ speak on the day of Ghadīr Khumm, let him stand. He said: Six stood from Saʿīd's side and six from Zayd's side, and they testified that they had heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say to ʿAlī on the day of Ghadīr Khumm: “Is Allah not closer to the believers?” They said: Yes. He said: “O Allah, whoever I am the mawlā of, ʿAlī is his mawlā. O Allah, befriend whoever befriends him, and be hostile to whoever is hostile to him.”
items.ma-951:
ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿAlī ibn Ḥakīm narrated to us, Sharīk informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAmr Dhī Murr, like the hadith of Abū Isḥāq, meaning from Saʿīd and Zayd
and he added to it: “and help whoever helps him, and forsake whoever forsakes him.”
items.ma-952: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿAlī narrated to us, Sharīk informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from Abū al-Ṭufayl, from Zayd ibn Arqam, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of it.
items.ma-953: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Hāniʾ ibn Hāniʾ, from ʿAlī, he said: When al-Ḥasan was born, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and said: “Show me my son; what have you named him?” I said: I named him Ḥarb. He said: “Rather he is Ḥasan.” When al-Ḥusayn was born, he said: “Show me my son; what have you named him?” I said: I named him Ḥarb. He said: “Rather he is Ḥusayn.” When I had the third, the Prophet ﷺ came and said: “Show me my son; what have you named him?” I said: Ḥarb. He said: “Rather he is Muḥassin.” Then he said: “I have named them with the names of the sons of Hārūn: Shabbar, Shabbīr and Mushabbir.”
items.ma-954: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, I heard al-Qāsim ibn Abī Bazzah narrating from Abū al-Ṭufayl, he said: ʿAlī was asked: Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ single you out with anything? He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not single us out with anything that he did not give to all the people, except what is in the scabbard of this sword of mine. He said: Then he took out a ṣaḥīfah in which was written: “May Allah curse whoever slaughters for other than Allah; may Allah curse whoever steals the landmarks of the land; may Allah curse whoever curses his father; and may Allah curse whoever gives shelter to a muḥdith.”
items.ma-955: Bahz and ʿAffān narrated to us, both said: Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Yaʿlā ibn ʿAṭāʾ – ʿAffān said: he said: Yaʿlā ibn ʿAṭāʾ informed us – from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yasār, from ʿAmr ibn Ḥurayth, that he visited al-Ḥasan while ʿAlī was with him, and ʿAlī said: O ʿAmr, do you visit al-Ḥasan while in the heart is what is in it? He said: Yes; you are not the Rabb of my heart that you may turn it wherever you wish. He said: That does not prevent me from giving you sincere advice. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “There is no Muslim who visits a Muslim but Allah sends seventy thousand angels who send blessings upon him, whatever hour of the day it is until evening, and whatever hour of the night it is until morning.”
items.ma-956: Bahz narrated to us, and ʿAffān narrated to us, both said: Hammām narrated to us, from Qatādah, from al-Ḥasan, from ʿAlī, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “The pen is lifted from three: from the sleeper until he wakes, from the feeble-minded – or he said: the insane – until he regains his reason, and from the child until he grows up.”
items.ma-957: Bahz and Abū Kāmil narrated to us, both said: Ḥammād narrated to us – Bahz said: he said – Hishām ibn ʿAmr al-Fazārī informed us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām al-Makhzūmī, from ʿAlī: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say at the end of his witr: “O Allah, I seek refuge in Your riḍā from Your sakhaṭ, and in Your pardon from Your punishment, and I seek refuge in You from You. I cannot count praise of You; You are as You have praised Yourself.”
items.ma-958: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Bakr ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAbbās al-Bāhilī narrated to us, Abū Dāwūd narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, Abū Bishr informed me, I heard Mujāhid narrating from Ibn Abī Laylā, I heard ʿAlī say: A silk ḥullah was brought to the Prophet ﷺ, and he sent it to me and I wore it, and I saw dislike in his face. He commanded me, so I cut it up into head-coverings among the women.
items.ma-959:
Bahz narrated to us, Hammām narrated to us, Qatādah informed us, from Abū Ḥassān: that ʿAlī would command a matter, and then people would come and it would be said: We have done such-and-such. He would say: Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth. He said: Al-Ashtar said to him: This that you say has spread among the people; is it something the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entrusted to you? ʿAlī said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not entrust to me anything specifically, apart from the people, except something I heard from him, and it is in a ṣaḥīfah in the scabbard of my sword. He said: They kept at him until he brought out the ṣaḥīfah, and in it was: “Whoever introduces an innovation, or gives shelter to one who introduces an innovation, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels and all the people; neither ṣarf nor ʿadl will be accepted from him.”
He said: And in it was: “Ibrāhīm made Makkah sacred, and I make al-Madīnah sacred: what lies between its two lava fields and all its protected ground is sacred. Its grass is not to be cut, its game is not to be startled, its lost property is not to be picked up except by one who will announce it, no tree is to be cut from it except that a man may feed his camel, and no weapon is to be carried in it for fighting.”
He said: And in it was: “The believers' blood is equal; the lowest of them strives to give their protection; and they are one hand against all others. Beware: a believer is not killed for a disbeliever, nor one under a covenant during his covenant.”
items.ma-960: Rawḥ narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah informed me, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Faḍl, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aʿraj, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Rāfiʿ, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib: that when the Prophet ﷺ went into rukūʿ he would say: “O Allah, to You I have bowed, in You I have believed, and to You I have submitted. You are my Rabb. My hearing, my sight, my marrow, my bone and my sinew have humbled themselves, and what my foot bears up, to Allah, Rabb of the worlds.”
items.ma-961: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar al-Qawārīrī narrated to me, Yūnus ibn Arqam narrated to us, Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, he said: I witnessed ʿAlī in al-Raḥabah adjuring the people: I adjure by Allah whoever heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say on the day of Ghadīr Khumm: “Whoever I am the mawlā of, ʿAlī is his mawlā,” to stand and testify. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: Twelve men of Badr stood – it is as though I am looking at one of them – and they said: We testify that we heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say on the day of Ghadīr Khumm: “Am I not closer to the Muslims than they are to themselves, and my wives their mothers?” We said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: “Then whoever I am the mawlā of, ʿAlī is his mawlā. O Allah, befriend whoever befriends him, and be hostile to whoever is hostile to him.”
items.ma-962: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Mukhāriq, from Ṭāriq ibn Shihāb, he said: I saw ʿAlī on the minbar giving a khuṭbah, wearing a sword whose fittings were iron, and I heard him say: By Allah, we have no book to recite to you except the Book of Allah Taʿālā and this ṣaḥīfah, which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave me; in it are the obligations of ṣadaqah. He said: of a ṣaḥīfah hanging from his sword.
items.ma-963: ʿAlī ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to us, Ismāʿīl ibn Sumayʿ informed us, from Mālik ibn ʿUmayr, he said: I was sitting with ʿAlī when Ṣaʿṣaʿah ibn Ṣūḥān came, gave salām, then stood and said: O Commander of the Believers, forbid us what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade you. He said: He forbade us the gourd, the ḥantam, the pitch-coated vessel and the naqīr; and he forbade us qassī, the red mīthara, silk, and gold rings. Then he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ clothed me in a silk ḥullah, and I went out in it so that people would see upon me the clothing of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw me and commanded me to take it off, and he sent one part of it to Fāṭimah and tore the other among his women.
items.ma-964: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Aḥmad ibn ʿUmar al-Wakīʿī narrated to us, Zayd ibn al-Ḥubāb narrated to us, al-Walīd ibn ʿUqbah ibn Nizār al-Qaysī narrated to us, Simāk ibn ʿUbayd ibn al-Walīd al-ʿAbsī narrated to me, he said: I entered upon ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā and he narrated to me that he witnessed ʿAlī in al-Raḥabah, who said: I adjure by Allah any man who heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and was present with him on the day of Ghadīr Khumm to stand, and none is to stand except one who saw him. Twelve men stood and said: We saw him and heard him when he took his hand and said: “O Allah, befriend whoever befriends him, be hostile to whoever is hostile to him, help whoever helps him, and forsake whoever forsakes him.” All stood except three who did not stand, so he invoked against them, and his invocation struck them.
items.ma-965: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn al-Minhāl, brother of Ḥajjāj ibn Minhāl, narrated to me, ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ziyād narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Isḥāq, Abū Saʿīd narrated to me, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, he said: When ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib heard the mu'adhdhin call the adhān, he would say as he said; and when he said: I testify that there is no deity but Allah, and I testify that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah, ʿAlī said: I testify that there is no deity but Allah, and I testify that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah, and that those who denied Muḥammad are the liars.
items.ma-966:
Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, he said: al-Ḥakam narrated to me, from al-Qāsim ibn Mukhaymirah, from Shurayḥ ibn Hāniʾ, he said: I asked ʿĀʾishah about wiping over the khuffs, and she said: Ask ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, for he used to travel with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I asked him, and he said: For the traveller three days and their nights, and for the resident a day and a night.
Yaḥyā said: He used to raise it – meaning Shuʿbah – then he left that.
items.ma-967: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, Saʿīd ibn Abī Saʿīd al-Maqburī narrated to me, from ʿAṭāʾ, the mawlā of Umm Ṣubayyah, from Abū Hurayrah, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Were it not that I would burden my ummah, I would command them to use the siwāk at every ṣalāh, and I would delay ʿishāʾ al-ākhirah to the first third of the night; for when the first third of the night has passed, Allah Taʿālā Habaṭa to the lowest heaven and remains there until dawn breaks, and a speaker says: Is there no one asking, that he may be given? No one supplicating, that he may be answered? No sick person seeking healing, that he may be healed? No sinner seeking forgiveness, that he may be forgiven?”
items.ma-968: Yaʿqūb narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, my uncle ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yasār narrated to me, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Abī Rāfiʿ, the mawlā of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, from his father, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, from the Prophet ﷺ, like the hadith of Abū Hurayrah.
items.ma-969: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, he said: He was asked about witr: is it obligatory? He said: As for like the obligatory ṣalāh, no; but it is a Sunnah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions practised until they passed on in that.
items.ma-970: Ibn al-Ashjaʿī narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Sufyān, from al-Suddī, from ʿAbd Khayr, from ʿAlī: that he called for a jug of water and said: Where are those who claim that they dislike drinking standing? He said: He took it and drank while standing, then performed a light ablution and wiped over his sandals, then said: This is how the ablution of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was, for one who is pure and has not broken ablution.
items.ma-971: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Walīd narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq narrated to us, from Abū Ḥayyah ibn Qays, from ʿAlī: that he performed ablution three times each, and drank the remainder of his ablution water, then said: This is how I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do.
items.ma-972: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to us, ʿAlī ibn Musḥir narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿĪsā, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When one of you sneezes, let him say: Praise be to Allah; and let those around him say: May Allah have mercy on you; and let him say: May Allah guide you and set right your affairs.”
items.ma-973: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Dāwūd ibn ʿAmr al-Ḍabbī narrated to us, Manṣūr ibn Abī al-Aswad narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Laylā, from al-Ḥakam or ʿĪsā – Manṣūr was unsure – from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When one of you sneezes, let him say: Praise be to Allah in every state; and let those with him say to him: May Allah have mercy on you; and he replies to them: May Allah guide you and set right your affairs.”
items.ma-974: Ghassān ibn al-Rabīʿ narrated to us, Abū Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from al-Suddī, from ʿAbd Khayr, he said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib came out to us while we were in the mosque and said: Where is the one who asked about witr? Whoever of us was in a single rakʿah added another to it, until we gathered around him. Then he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray witr in the first part of the night, then he prayed witr in the middle of it, then he fixed the witr at this hour. He said: That is at the break of dawn.
items.ma-975: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nāfiʿ, he said: Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī visited al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, and ʿAlī said to him: Have you come as a visitor of the sick, or as a caller? Abū Mūsā said: Rather I came as a visitor of the sick. ʿAlī said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever visits a sick person in the early morning, seventy thousand angels accompany him, all of them asking forgiveness for him until evening, and he will have a kharīf in Paradise; and if he visits him in the evening, seventy thousand angels accompany him, all of them asking forgiveness for him until morning, and he will have a kharīf in Paradise.”
items.ma-976: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nāfiʿ, he said: Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī visited al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, and ʿAlī said to him: Have you come as a visitor of the sick, or as a caller? He said: No, rather I came as a visitor of the sick. ʿAlī said: Indeed, there is no Muslim who visits a sick person but seventy thousand angels go out with him, all of them asking forgiveness for him – if it is morning, until evening, and he will have a kharīf in Paradise; and if it is evening, seventy thousand angels go out with him, all of them asking forgiveness for him until morning, and he will have a kharīf in Paradise.
items.ma-977: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Shaybān Abū Muḥammad narrated to me, ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Muslim – meaning Abū Zayd al-Qasmalī – narrated to us, Yazīd ibn Abī Ziyād narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAlī, he said: I was a man who emitted madhy often, so I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about that, and he said: “In madhy is ablution, and in semen is bathing.”
items.ma-978: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Mujālid, ʿĀmir narrated to us, he said: Shurāḥah had a husband away in al-Shām, and she became pregnant. Her master brought her to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and said: This woman committed zinā. She confessed, and he flogged her a hundred on Thursday and stoned her on Friday, and dug for her up to the navel while I was present. Then he said: Stoning is a Sunnah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ established, and had anyone testified against this woman, he would have been the first to throw; the witness testifies and then follows his testimony with his stone. But she confessed, so I am the first to throw at her. He threw a stone at her, then the people threw, and I was among them. He said: By Allah, I was among those who killed her.
items.ma-979: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Isrāʾīl informed us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from his father, from his uncle, he said: ʿAlī said, when he was asked: May a man ride his hady? He said: There is no harm in it; the Prophet ﷺ would pass by men walking and command them to ride his hady, the hady of the Prophet ﷺ. He said: And you will not follow anything better than the Sunnah of your Prophet ﷺ.
items.ma-980: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl, ʿĀmir narrated to us, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the one who consumes ribā, the one who feeds it, its two witnesses, its writer, the one who withholds ṣadaqah, the woman who tattoos, the woman who is tattooed, the ḥāll, and the muḥallal lahu. He said: And he used to forbid wailing.
items.ma-981: Yazīd narrated to us, Hishām informed us, from Muḥammad, from ʿAbīdah, from ʿAlī, he said: It was forbidden: crimson mayāthir, wearing qassī, and the gold ring. Muḥammad said: I mentioned that to my brother Yaḥyā ibn Sīrīn, and he said: Did you not hear this? Yes, and the borders of brocade.
items.ma-982: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar al-Qawārīrī narrated to me, Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us, Ayyūb informed us, from Muḥammad, from ʿAbīdah, he said: ʿAlī mentioned the people of al-Nahrawān and said: Among them is a man with a stunted hand – or a small hand, or a deformed hand. Were it not that you would become arrogant, I would inform you of what Allah has promised those who kill them, upon the tongue of Muḥammad ﷺ. He said: I said: Did you hear it from him? He said: Yes, by the Rabb of the Kaʿbah.
items.ma-983: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr al-Muqaddamī narrated to me, Ḥammād ibn Yaḥyā al-Abaḥḥ narrated to us, Ibn ʿAwn narrated to us, from Muḥammad, from ʿAbīdah, he said: When ʿAlī killed the people of al-Nahrawān, he said: Look for him. They found him in a pit beneath the slain and brought him out. ʿAlī turned to his companions and said: Were it not that you would become arrogant, I would inform you of what Allah has promised whoever kills these, upon the tongue of Muḥammad ﷺ. I said: Did you hear it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? He said: Yes, by the Rabb of the Kaʿbah.
items.ma-984: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I have pardoned you the ṣadaqah on horses and slaves; and on silver, a quarter of a tenth.”
items.ma-985: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Abū al-Bakhtarī, from ʿAlī, he said: When a hadith is narrated to you from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, think of it what is most guided, what is most modest, and what is most God-fearing.
items.ma-986: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Misʿar, ʿAmr ibn Murrah narrated to us, from Abū al-Bakhtarī, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAlī, he said: When a hadith is narrated to you from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, think of it what is most modest, most guided, and most God-fearing.
items.ma-987: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Abū al-Bakhtarī, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿAlī, he said: When a hadith is narrated to you from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, think of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what is most modest, most God-fearing and most guided. And ʿAlī came out to us when the muthawwib made the tathwīb, and said: Where is the one who asked about witr? This is a good time for witr.
items.ma-988: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr ibn ʿAlī al-Muqaddamī narrated to us, Ḥammād – meaning Ibn Zayd – narrated to us, from Ayyūb and Hishām, from Muḥammad, from ʿAbīdah: that ʿAlī mentioned the people of al-Nahrawān and said: Among them is a man with a stunted hand – or a small hand, or a deformed hand. Were it not that you would become arrogant, I would inform you of what Allah has promised those who kill them, upon the tongue of Muḥammad ﷺ. I said to ʿAlī: Did you hear it? He said: Yes, by the Rabb of the Kaʿbah.
items.ma-989:
Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, Mālik ibn ʿUrfuṭah narrated to me, I heard ʿAbd Khayr say: I was with ʿAlī when a chair and a basin were brought. He said: He washed his palms three times, his face three times, and his forearms three times, and wiped his head – Yaḥyā described: he began with the front of his head to the back, and said: I do not know whether he brought his hand back or not – and washed his feet. Then he said: Whoever would like to look at the ablution of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, this is the ablution of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: Shuʿbah erred in this; it is rather from Khālid ibn ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Khayr.
items.ma-990: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq al-Tirmidhī narrated to me, al-Ashjaʿī narrated to us, from Sufyān, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, from ʿAbīdah al-Salmānī, from ʿAlī, he said: We used to think it was Fajr, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “It is the ʿAṣr ṣalāh” – meaning the middle ṣalāh.
items.ma-991: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar al-Qawārīrī narrated to me, Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Abī Ḥazm narrated to us, ʿUmar ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Abū Ḥassān, from ʿAlī, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The believers' blood is equal; they are one hand against all others; the lowest of them strives to give their protection. Beware: a believer is not killed for a disbeliever, nor one under a covenant during his covenant.”
items.ma-992: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from Yūsuf ibn Masʿūd, from his grandmother: that a man passed by them on a camel, hurrying it, at Minā in the days of al-Tashrīq: These are days of eating and drinking. I asked about him, and they said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib.
items.ma-993: Yaḥyā narrated to us, Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūbah narrated to us, from Qatādah, from al-Ḥasan, from Qays ibn ʿUbād, he said: I went with al-Ashtar to ʿAlī and we said: Did the Prophet of Allah ﷺ entrust to you anything he did not entrust to the people in general? He said: No, except what is in this writing of mine. He said: And there was a writing in the scabbard of his sword, and in it was: “The believers' blood is equal; they are one hand against all others; the lowest of them strives to give their protection. Beware: a believer is not killed for a disbeliever, nor one under a covenant during his covenant. Whoever introduces an innovation, or gives shelter to one who introduces an innovation, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels and all the people.”
items.ma-994: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Hishām, from Muḥammad, from ʿAbīdah, from ʿAlī, that the Prophet ﷺ said on the day of al-Khandaq: “They have kept us from the middle ṣalāh until the sun set – or the sun was about to set. May Allah fill their bellies – or their graves – with fire.”
items.ma-995: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Laylā, my brother narrated to me, from my father, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “When one of you sneezes, let him say: Praise be to Allah in every state; and let it be said to him: May Allah have mercy on you; and let him say: May Allah guide you and set right your affairs.” I said to him: From Abū Ayyūb? He said: ʿAlī.
items.ma-996: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān narrated to me, Azhar ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAwn, from Muḥammad, from ʿAbīdah, from ʿAlī, he said: Fāṭimah complained to me of the blisters on her hands from grinding. We came to the Prophet ﷺ and I said: O Messenger of Allah, Fāṭimah complains to you of the blisters on her hands from grinding and asks you for a servant. He said: “Shall I not guide you to something better for you than a servant?” And he commanded us at our sleep to say thirty-three, and three, and thirty, and thirty-four of glorification, praise and takbīr.
items.ma-997: ʿAbd Allāh said: I found in my father's book, he said: I was informed from Sinān ibn Hārūn, Bayān narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: When the Prophet ﷺ went into rukūʿ, if a cup of water had been placed on his back it would not have spilled.
items.ma-998: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to me, Sharīk narrated to us, from Khālid ibn ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Khayr, from ʿAlī, he said: He performed ablution: he rinsed his mouth three times, snuffed water into his nose three times from one palm, and washed his face three times. Then he put his hand into the leather vessel, wiped his head and washed his feet. Then he said: This is the ablution of your Prophet ﷺ.
items.ma-999: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, Abū Isḥāq narrated to me, from Hāniʾ ibn Hāniʾ, from ʿAlī: that ʿAmmār asked permission to see the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “The good, the purified.”
items.ma-1000:
Yaḥyā – meaning Ibn Saʿīd – narrated to us, from Shuʿbah (ḥ) and Ḥajjāj, Shuʿbah informed us, from Manṣūr – Yaḥyā said: he said: Manṣūr narrated to me – from Ribʿī, he said: I heard ʿAlī say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do not lie about me, for whoever lies about me will enter the Fire.”
Ḥajjāj said: I said to Shuʿbah: Did he meet ʿAlī? He said: Yes, he narrated to me from ʿAlī, and did not say: he heard.
items.ma-1001: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Ribʿī ibn Ḥirāsh: that he heard ʿAlī giving a khuṭbah, saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said … and he mentioned the like of it.
items.ma-1002: Yaḥyā narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, Ḥasan ibn Muslim and ʿAbd al-Karīm informed me that Mujāhid informed them that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā informed him that ʿAlī informed him: that the Prophet ﷺ commanded him to oversee his sacrificial camels, and commanded him to distribute all of his sacrificial camels – their meat, hides and covers – and not to give anything of them as the butcher's wage.
items.ma-1003: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from ʿAbd al-Karīm … and he mentioned the hadith, and said: “We ourselves give him his wage.”
items.ma-1004: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAjlān, Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥunayn narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade me the gold ring, reciting while I am in rukūʿ, qassī and safflower-dyed garments.
items.ma-1005: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to me, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Maysarah, from al-Nazzāl ibn Sabrah: that when ʿAlī had prayed Ẓuhr he called for a jug of water in al-Raḥabah and drank while standing. Then he said: Some men dislike this, and I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do as you saw me do. Then he wiped himself with the remainder and said: “This is the ablution of one who has not broken ablution.”
items.ma-1006: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAqīl, from Muḥammad Ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah, from his father, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The key to the ṣalāh is purification, its tahrīm is the takbīr, and its taḥlīl is the salām.”
items.ma-1007: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUqbah Abū Kibrān al-Murādī narrated to us, I heard ʿAbd Khayr say: ʿAlī said: Shall I not show you the ablution of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? Then he performed ablution three times each.
items.ma-1008: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Isḥāq ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Mushir ibn ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Salʿ narrated to us, my father ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Salʿ narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd Khayr used to lead us in Fajr, and he said: One day we prayed Fajr behind ʿAlī. When he gave the salām he stood and we stood with him; he walked until he reached al-Raḥabah, sat down and leaned his back against the wall, then raised his head and said: O Qanbar, bring me the leather vessel and the basin. Then he said to him: Pour. He poured over him, and he washed his palm three times, put his right palm in, rinsed his mouth and snuffed water into his nose three times, then put in both palms and washed his face three times, then put in his right palm and washed his right forearm three times, then washed his left forearm three times. Then he said: This is the ablution of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-1009: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Hishām ibn ʿUrwah narrated to us, from his father, he said: ʿAlī said: I was a man who emitted madhy often, and I felt shy to ask the Prophet ﷺ because of his daughter's position, so I commanded al-Miqdād and he asked him, and he said: “He washes his male organ and his testicles and performs ablution.”
items.ma-1010: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Mundhir Abū Yaʿlā, from Ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah: that ʿAlī commanded al-Miqdād, and he asked the Prophet ﷺ about madhy, and he said: “He performs ablution.”
items.ma-1011: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salimah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would relieve himself and then eat meat with us and recite the Qurʾān, and nothing prevented him – or kept him back – except janābah.
items.ma-1012: Wakīʿ and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray two rakʿahs after every obligatory ṣalāh, except Fajr and ʿAṣr. And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: at the end of every ṣalāh.
items.ma-1013: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Isḥāq ibn Ismāʿīl and Abū Khaythamah narrated to us, both said: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd Khayr, from ʿAlī, he said: I used to think the underside of the feet more deserving of wiping than their top, until I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wipe over their top.
items.ma-1014: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Isḥāq ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to me, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū al-Sawdāʾ, from the son of ʿAbd Khayr, from his father, he said: I saw ʿAlī perform ablution and wash the tops of his feet, and he said: Had I not seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wash the tops of his feet, I would have thought their undersides more deserving of washing.
items.ma-1015: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Isḥāq narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, another time, he said: I saw ʿAlī perform ablution and wipe over their tops.
items.ma-1016: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Isḥāq ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUqbah Abū Kibrān narrated to us, from ʿAbd Khayr, from ʿAlī, he said – meaning: This is the ablution of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then he performed ablution three times.
items.ma-1017: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād, from ʿAlī, he said: I never heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ offer anyone his parents as ransom except Saʿd ibn Mālik, for I heard him say to him on the day of Uḥud: “Shoot, O Saʿd, may my father and mother be your ransom.”
items.ma-1018: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Saʿd ibn ʿUbaydah, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿAlī, he said: The Prophet ﷺ sent a detachment and appointed over them a man of the Anṣār, and commanded them to listen to him and obey. He said: They angered him over something, and he said: Gather firewood for me. They gathered firewood. Then he said: Kindle a fire. They kindled a fire for him. He said: Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ not command you to listen to me and obey? They said: Yes. He said: Then enter it. He said: They looked at one another and said: We only fled to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from the fire. They remained so until his anger subsided and the fire went out. He said: When they came to the Prophet ﷺ they mentioned that to him, and he said: “Had they entered it they would not have come out of it. Obedience is only in what is right.”
items.ma-1019: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, and ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Sufyān informed us, from ʿĀṣim – meaning Ibn Kulayb – from Abū Burdah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade me to put the ring on this or on this. ʿAbd al-Razzāq said, of his two fingers: the index and the middle.
items.ma-1020:
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Abū Hāshim al-Qāsim ibn Kathīr, from Qays al-Khārifī, he said: I heard ʿAlī say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took the lead, Abū Bakr came second, and ʿUmar third; then a fitnah struck us – or befell us – so what Allah ﷻ willed.
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: My father said: His saying: “then a fitnah struck us” – he meant to be humble by that.
items.ma-1021: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, Shuʿbah and Ḥammād ibn Salamah, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Ḥujayyah ibn ʿAdī: that a man asked ʿAlī about the cow. He said: On behalf of seven. He said: The horn? He said: It does not harm you. He said: The lame one? He said: If it reaches the place of sacrifice. He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to examine the eye and the ear closely.
items.ma-1022: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, he said: I heard Ḥujayyah ibn ʿAdī say: I heard ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, when a man asked him … and he mentioned the hadith.
items.ma-1023: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from Abū Isḥāq, from Ḥārithah ibn Muḍarrib, from ʿAlī, he said: We had no horseman on the day of Badr other than al-Miqdād, and I saw us when there was none among us but a sleeper, except the Messenger of Allah ﷺ beneath a tree, praying and weeping until morning.
items.ma-1024: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Abū Ḥuṣayn, from ʿUmayr ibn Saʿīd, from ʿAlī, he said: There is no man on whom I carried out a ḥadd and who died whom I feel anything about in myself, except in the case of khamr, for if he had died I would have paid blood-money for him, because the Prophet ﷺ did not establish a Sunnah for it.
items.ma-1025: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū Ḥayyah, from ʿAlī: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to perform ablution three times each.
items.ma-1026: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Zāʾidah ibn Qudāmah, from Abū Ḥuṣayn al-Asadī; and Ibn Abī Bukayr, Zāʾidah narrated to us, Abū Ḥuṣayn al-Asadī informed us, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAlī, he said: I was a man who emitted madhy often, and the daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was my wife, so I commanded a man and he asked him, and he said: “Perform ablution and wash it.”
items.ma-1027: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Warkānī narrated to us, Sharīk informed us, from Khālid ibn ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Khayr, he said: We prayed the morning ṣalāh, then went to him and sat with him, and he called for water for ablution. A small leather vessel containing water and a basin were brought. He poured the vessel over his right hand and washed his hands three times, rinsed his mouth three times and snuffed water out of his nose three times, each with one palm. Then he washed his face three times and his forearms three times each. Then he put his hand into the vessel and wiped his head with both palms together, once. Then he washed his feet three times each. Then he said: This is the ablution of your Prophet ﷺ, so know it.
items.ma-1028: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Zāʾidah narrated to us, from al-Rukayn ibn al-Rabīʿ, from Ḥuṣayn ibn Qabīṣah, from ʿAlī, he said: I was a man who emitted madhy often, so I asked the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “When you see madhy, perform ablution and wash your male organ; and when you see the gushing of water, bathe.” I mentioned it to Sufyān and he said: I heard it from Rukayn.
items.ma-1029: Muʿāwiyah and Ibn Abī Bukayr narrated to us, both said: Zāʾidah narrated to us, al-Rukayn ibn al-Rabīʿ ibn ʿAmīlah al-Fazārī narrated to us, and he mentioned the like of it, and both said: “the gushing of water.” And Ibn Abī Bukayr narrated to us, Zāʾidah narrated to us, and he said: “gushing” likewise.
items.ma-1030: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Wahb ibn Baqiyyah narrated to me, Khālid informed us, from ʿAṭāʾ – meaning Ibn al-Sāʾib – from ʿAbd Khayr, from ʿAlī, he said: Shall I not inform you of the best of this Ummah after its Prophet ﷺ? Abū Bakr; then the best of it after Abū Bakr is ʿUmar; then Allah places the good wherever He Aḥabba.
items.ma-1031: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Baḥr ʿAbd al-Wāḥid al-Baṣrī narrated to me, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Khālid ibn ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Khayr, he said: When he had finished with the people of al-Baṣrah, ʿAlī said: The best of this Ummah after its Prophet ﷺ is Abū Bakr, and after Abū Bakr, ʿUmar. And we have introduced new matters, in which Allah does what He wills.
items.ma-1032: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Wahb ibn Baqiyyah al-Wāsiṭī narrated to me, Khālid ibn ʿAbd Allāh informed us, from Ḥuṣayn, from al-Musayyab ibn ʿAbd Khayr, from his father, he said: ʿAlī stood and said: The best of this Ummah after its Prophet ﷺ are Abū Bakr and ʿUmar. And we have since introduced new matters, in which Allah will decree what He wills.
items.ma-1033: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Hāniʾ ibn Hāniʾ, from ʿAlī, he said: ʿAmmār came asking permission to see the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “Let him in. Welcome to the good, the purified.”
items.ma-1034: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Abū Isḥāq, from Saʿīd ibn Dhī Ḥuddān, one who heard ʿAlī narrated to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called war deception.
items.ma-1035: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Hishām, my father informed me that ʿAlī said to al-Miqdād: Ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about a man who draws near to a woman and emits madhy, for I feel shy of him, because his daughter is with me. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “He washes his male organ and his testicles and performs ablution.”
items.ma-1036: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Shutayr ibn Shakal, from ʿAlī, he said: They kept us busy on the day of al-Aḥzāb from the ʿAṣr ṣalāh, until I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “They have kept us busy from the middle ṣalāh, the ʿAṣr ṣalāh. May Allah fill their graves, their houses and their bellies with fire.”
items.ma-1037: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, from his father, from ʿAlī, he said: We have nothing except the Book of Allah, Exalted, and this ṣaḥīfah from the Prophet ﷺ: “Al-Madīnah is ḥarām between ʿĀʾir and Thawr. Whoever introduces an innovation in it, or gives shelter to one who introduces an innovation, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels and all the people; no ʿadl or ṣarf will be accepted from him.” And he said: “The protection of the Muslims is one; whoever breaks the covenant of a Muslim, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels and all the people; no ṣarf or ʿadl will be accepted from him. And whoever attaches himself as a client to a people without the permission of his mawālī, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels and all the people; no ṣarf or ʿadl will be accepted from him.”
items.ma-1038: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from al-Aʿmash, from Saʿd ibn ʿUbaydah, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAlī, he said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, why do I see you choosing so carefully among Quraysh while leaving us, that you do not marry from us? He said: “Do you have someone?” I said: The daughter of Ḥamzah. He said: “She is the daughter of my brother by milk.”
items.ma-1039: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Abū al-Bakhtarī, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, he said: ʿAlī said: When I narrate to you a hadith from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, think of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what is most modest, most guided and most God-fearing.
items.ma-1040: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān and Shuʿbah, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from ʿAbd Khayr, from ʿAlī, that he said: Shall I not tell you of the best of this Ummah after its Prophet ﷺ? Abū Bakr, then ʿUmar.
items.ma-1041: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to me, Muṭṭalib ibn Ziyād narrated to us, from al-Suddī, from ʿAbd Khayr, from ʿAlī, regarding His saying: ﴿You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide﴾ [al-Raʿd: 7], he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ is the warner, and the guide is a man from Banū Hāshim.
items.ma-1042: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, from Ḥārithah ibn Muḍarrib, from ʿAlī, he said: When the fighting grew fierce on the day of Badr, we took shelter by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he was among the most fierce of the people; there was no one – or: there was not anyone – closer to the polytheists than he.
items.ma-1043: I recited to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān: from Mālik, from Nāfiʿ. And Isḥāq – meaning Ibn ʿĪsā – narrated to us, Mālik informed me, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥunayn – Isḥāq said: from his father – from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade wearing qassī and safflower-dyed garments, wearing a gold ring, and reciting the Qurʾān in rukūʿ.
items.ma-1044:
ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, my father and Abū Khaythamah narrated to me, both said: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ayyūb informed us, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibrāhīm ibn Fulān ibn Ḥunayn, from his grandfather Ḥunayn, he said: ʿAlī said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade me to wear safflower-dyed garments, qassī, a gold ring, and reciting in rukūʿ. Ayyūb said: or he said: that I recite while I am in rukūʿ.
Abū Khaythamah said in his narration: I was told that Ismāʿīl retracted “from his grandfather Ḥunayn.”
items.ma-1045: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb narrated to us, from Saʿīd, from a man, from al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtaybah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAlī, that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me to sell two slave boys who were brothers, and I sold them, separating them. I mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ and he said: “Catch up with them and take them back, and do not sell them except together, and do not separate them.”
items.ma-1046: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Khalaf ibn Hishām al-Bazzār narrated to us, Abū al-Aḥwaṣ narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū Ḥayyah, he said: I saw ʿAlī perform ablution. He washed his palms until he had cleaned them, then rinsed his mouth three times, then snuffed water into his nose three times, and washed his face three times and his forearms three times, wiped his head, and washed his feet to the ankles. Then he took the remainder of his ablution water and drank it while standing, and said: I wished to show you how the purification of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was.
items.ma-1047: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Khalaf ibn Hishām al-Bazzār narrated to us, Abū al-Aḥwaṣ narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, he said: ʿAbd Khayr mentioned from ʿAlī the like of the hadith of Abū Ḥayyah, except that ʿAbd Khayr said: When he had finished his purification he took in both palms some of the remainder of his ablution water and drank.
items.ma-1048: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb narrated to us, he said: Saʿīd was asked about the animal with a broken horn: may it be sacrificed? So he informed us from Qatādah, from Jurayy ibn Kulayb, a man of his people, that he heard ʿAlī say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade sacrificing an animal with a broken horn or a split ear. Qatādah said: I mentioned that to Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, and he said: ʿAḍab is half or more than that.
items.ma-1049: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, from Hubayrah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade me to wear a gold ring and to wear qassī and mayāthir.
items.ma-1051: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Ḥakam ibn Mūsā narrated to me, Shihāb ibn Khirāsh narrated to us, al-Ḥajjāj ibn Dīnār narrated to me, from Abū Maʿshar, from Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, he said: ʿAlqamah ibn Qays struck this minbar and said: ʿAlī ﵁ addressed us from this minbar. He praised Allah and extolled Him, mentioned what Allah willed that he mention, and said: The best of people after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was Abū Bakr, then ʿUmar; then we introduced after them new matters, in which Allah decrees.
items.ma-1052: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Ḥakam ibn Mūsā narrated to us, Shihāb ibn Khirāsh narrated to us, Yūnus ibn Khabbāb informed me, from al-Musayyab ibn ʿAbd Khayr, from ʿAbd Khayr, he said: I heard ʿAlī say: The best of this Ummah after its Prophet is Abū Bakr, then ʿUmar, ﵄.
items.ma-1053: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Mujammiʿ ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿImrān al-Anṣārī, from ʿAlī. And al-Masʿūdī, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hurmuz, from Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was neither short nor tall; large of head and beard, thick in the palms and feet, large in the joints, his face tinged with redness, with a long masrubah. When he walked he leaned forward as he walked, as though he were pulling himself from rock. I never saw anyone like him before him or after him ﷺ. And Abū al-Naḍr said: al-masrubah; and Abū Nuʿaym said: al-masrubah; and he said: as though descending a slope; and Abū Qaṭan said: al-masrubah; and Yazīd said: al-masrubah.
items.ma-1054: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Ḥakam ibn Mūsā narrated to us, Shihāb ibn Khirāsh narrated to us, al-Ḥajjāj ibn Dīnār narrated to us, from Ḥuṣayn ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū Juḥayfah, he said: I used to think that ʿAlī was the best of people after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ … and he mentioned the hadith. I said: No, by Allah, O Commander of the Believers, I did not think that any of the Muslims after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was better than you. He said: Shall I not tell you who was the best of people after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? I said: Yes. He said: Abū Bakr. Then he said: Shall I not inform you of the best of people after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abū Bakr? I said: Yes. He said: ʿUmar.
items.ma-1055: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Surayj ibn Yūnus narrated to me, Marwān al-Fazārī narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Salʿ informed us, from ʿAbd Khayr, he said: I heard him say: ʿAlī stood on the minbar and mentioned the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken, and Abū Bakr ﵁ was made successor; he acted as he had acted and followed his course, until Allah ﷿ took him in that state. Then ʿUmar was made successor and acted as the two of them had acted and followed their course, until Allah took him in that state.
items.ma-1056: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAlī ibn Rabīʿah, he said: I was riding behind ʿAlī ﵁. When he put his foot in the stirrup he said: In the name of Allah. When he was seated firmly he said: Praise be to Allah, glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have subdued it, and to our Rabb we shall return – and Abū Saʿīd, the mawlā of Banū Hāshim, said: Then he praised Allah three times, and said Allāhu akbar three times, then said: Glory be to Allah three times, then said: There is no god but You. Then he returned to the hadith of Wakīʿ – Glory be to You, I have wronged myself, so forgive me, for none forgives sins but You. Then he laughed. I said: What makes you laugh? He said: I was riding behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he did as you saw me do, then he laughed. I said: O Messenger of Allah, what makes you laugh? He said: “Allah ﵎ said: ʿAjab is for My servant: he knows that none forgives sins but Me.”
items.ma-1057: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salimah, from ʿAlī, he said: I fell ill, and the Prophet ﷺ came to me while I was saying: O Allah, if my appointed time has come, give me relief; and if it is delayed, heal me – or grant me well-being; and if it is a trial, grant me patience. The Prophet ﷺ said: “How did you say?” So I repeated it to him. He wiped with his hand and said: “O Allah, heal him – or grant him well-being.” He said: I did not complain of that pain again afterwards.
items.ma-1058: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Abū Isḥāq, from Hubayrah, from ʿAlī: that the Prophet ﷺ used to wake his family in the last ten nights.
items.ma-1059: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to us, Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Salʿ, from ʿAbd Khayr, he said: I heard ʿAlī say: Allah took His Prophet ﷺ in the best state in which any Prophet of the Prophets ﵈ has been taken. Then Abū Bakr was made successor and acted by the practice of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Sunnah of His Prophet, and ʿUmar likewise.
items.ma-1060:
ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Zakariyyā ibn Yaḥyā Zaḥmawayh narrated to us, ʿUmar ibn Mujāshiʿ narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd Khayr, he said: I heard ʿAlī say on the minbar: The best of this Ummah after its Prophet are Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, and had I wished to name the third I would have named him.
A man said to Abū Isḥāq: They say that you say: the best in evil. He said: A Ḥarūrī?!
items.ma-1061: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl and ʿAlī ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Abū Isḥāq, from Shurayḥ ibn al-Nuʿmān, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to examine the eye and the ear closely, and not to sacrifice an animal with a slit ear, a pierced ear, one cut at the front of the ear, or one cut at the back of the ear.
items.ma-1062: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from ʿAdī ibn Thābit, from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, from ʿAlī, he said: The Prophet ﷺ made a covenant with me: “None will love you except a believer, and none will hate you except a hypocrite.”
items.ma-1063: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from Ḥanash al-Kinānī: that some people in Yemen dug a pit for a lion, and it fell into it. The people crowded over it, and a man fell in and clung to another, and that one clung to another, until there were four in it. They disputed over that until some of them took up arms against others. ʿAlī said to them: Will you kill two hundred over four? But I shall judge between you with a judgment, if you accept it: the first receives a quarter of the blood-money, the second a third of the blood-money, the third half of the blood-money, and the fourth the full blood-money. They did not accept his judgment, so they came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “I shall judge between you with a judgment.” He said: Then he was informed of the judgment of ʿAlī ﵁, and he approved it.
items.ma-1064: Wakīʿ and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Ḥabīb, from Abū Wāʾil, from Abū al-Hayyāj, he said: ʿAlī said to me – ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: ʿAlī said to Abū al-Hayyāj –: I send you on what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me on: that you leave no raised grave without levelling it, and no image without effacing it.
items.ma-1065: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Zubayd, from Saʿd ibn ʿUbaydah, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “There is no obedience to any human being in disobedience to Allah.”
items.ma-1066: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Qatādah, he said: I heard Jurayy ibn Kulayb narrate from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade a broken ear and horn. He said: I asked Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab: What is ʿaḍab? He said: Half or more than that.
items.ma-1067: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Zāʾidah narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Saʿd ibn ʿUbaydah, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAlī, he said: We were with a funeral procession in Baqīʿ al-Gharqad, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us and sat, and we sat around him. He had a staff with which he was tapping the ground. Then he raised his gaze and said: “There is no soul that has been born among you but its seat in Paradise and in the Fire has been written, and it has been written wretched or fortunate.” The people said: O Messenger of Allah, shall we not stay with what is written for us and leave off deeds? For whoever is of the people of fortune will go to fortune, and whoever is of the people of wretchedness will go to wretchedness. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Rather, act, for each is made ready: as for the one of the people of wretchedness, he is made ready for the deeds of wretchedness; and as for the one of the people of fortune, he is made ready for the deeds of fortune.” Then he recited: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah and believes in the best reward, We shall ease him toward ease. But as for he who is stingy and considers himself free of need and denies the best reward, We shall ease him toward hardship﴾ [al-Layl: 5–10].
items.ma-1068: Ziyād ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Bakkāʾī narrated to us, Manṣūr narrated to us, from Saʿd ibn ʿUbaydah, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAlī, he said: We were with a funeral procession in Baqīʿ al-Gharqad … and he mentioned its meaning.
items.ma-1069: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Kurayb al-Hamdānī narrated to me, Muʿāwiyah ibn Hishām narrated to us, from Sufyān al-Thawrī, from Jābir, from Saʿd ibn ʿUbaydah, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAlī: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to fast on ʿĀshūrāʾ and command it.
items.ma-1070: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, he said: and Khalaf ibn Hishām al-Bazzār narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Whoever lies about his eyes will be charged on the Day of Resurrection with tying a knot between the two ends of a grain of barley.”
items.ma-1071: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Baḥr ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Ghiyāth al-Baṣrī narrated to me. And Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar and Sufyān ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us. And Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Ayyūb narrated to us, they said: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to us, from Abū Ḥuṣayn, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿAlī, that he said: I was a man who emitted madhy often, and I felt shy to ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, because his daughter was with me, so I commanded a man and he asked him, and he said: “Ablution is required because of it.”
items.ma-1072: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAqīl, from Muḥammad Ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The key to the ṣalāh is ablution, its tahrīm is the takbīr, and its taḥlīl is the salām.”
items.ma-1073: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, from Sufyān and Shuʿbah, from Manṣūr, from Hilāl, from Wahb ibn al-Ajdaʿ, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ: “Do not pray after ʿAṣr, unless you pray while the sun is still high.”
items.ma-1074: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Zakariyyā ibn Yaḥyā Zaḥmawayh narrated to me. And Muḥammad ibn Bakkār narrated to us. And Ismāʿīl Abū Maʿmar and Surayj ibn Yūnus narrated to us, they said: al-Ḥasan ibn Yazīd al-Aṣamm narrated to us – Abū Maʿmar said: the mawlā of Quraysh – he said: al-Suddī informed me – and Zaḥmawayh said in his narration: he said: I heard al-Suddī – from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿAlī, he said: When Abū Ṭālib died I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: Your old uncle has died. He said: “Go and bury him, and do nothing about his affair until you come to me.” I buried him and then came to him, and he said: “Go and bathe, and do nothing until you come to me.” I bathed and then came to him, and he made supplications for me with which I would not exchange the red camels and the black. And Ibn Bakkār said in his narration: al-Suddī said: ʿAlī ﵁ used to bathe whenever he washed a dead person.
items.ma-1075: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Aʿlā ibn Ḥammād al-Narsī narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever lies about me deliberately, let him take his seat in the Fire.”
items.ma-1076: Isḥāq ibn Yūsuf narrated it to us, Sufyān informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: “Do not pray after ʿAṣr, unless you pray while the sun is still high.” Sufyān said: I do not know whether he meant in Makkah or elsewhere.
