items.ma-1077: Wakīʿ narrated it to us, Misʿar narrated to us, from Abū ʿAwn, from Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Ḥanafī, from ʿAlī: that Ukaydir of Dūmah gave the Prophet ﷺ a ḥullah – or a garment of silk. He said: He gave it to me and said: “Cut it up into head-coverings for the women.”
items.ma-1078: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sabuʿ, he said: I heard ʿAlī say: This will surely be dyed from this. What is the most wretched one waiting for with me? They said: O Commander of the Believers, tell us who he is, and we shall destroy his kin. He said: Then, by Allah, you would be killing for me one who is not my killer. They said: Then appoint a successor over us. He said: No, but I shall leave you to what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left you to. They said: And what will you say to your Rabb when you come to Him? – and Wakīʿ said once: when you meet Him? – He said: I shall say: O Allah, You left me among them as long as it seemed good to You, then You took me to You while You were among them. If You will, You set them right, and if You will, You let them go to ruin.
items.ma-1079: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Hāniʾ ibn Hāniʾ, from ʿAlī, he said: We were sitting with the Prophet ﷺ when ʿAmmār came and asked permission, and he said: “Let him in. Welcome to the good, the purified.”
items.ma-1080: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Abū al-Bakhtarī, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: When a hadith is narrated to you from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, think of him that which is most modest, that which is most guided, and that which is most God-fearing.
items.ma-1081: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿUthmān narrated to me, Jarīr narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Abū al-Bakhtarī, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿAlī, the like of it.
items.ma-1082: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Ayyūb narrated to us, Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Saʿd ibn ʿUbaydah, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿAlī, that he said: When a hadith is narrated to you from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, think of him that which is most guided, that which is most God-fearing, and that which is most modest.
items.ma-1083:
ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah and Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr narrated to me, both said: Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, from Ḥuṣayn ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Saʿd ibn ʿUbaydah, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, he said: I heard ʿAlī say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me, Abū Marthad and al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām – and each of us was a horseman – and said: “Go until you reach Rawḍat Khākh.” Thus Ibn Abī Shaybah said: Khākh; and Ibn Numayr said in his narration: Rawḍat such-and-such.
And Ibn Numayr said: ʿAffān narrated it to us, Khālid narrated to us, from Ḥuṣayn, the like of it. He said: Rawḍat Khākh.
items.ma-1084: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Misʿar and Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Ḥuṣayn, from ʿUmayr ibn Saʿīd, he said: ʿAlī said: There is no man on whom I carried out a ḥadd and who died whom I feel anything about in myself, except the case of khamr, for if he had died I would have paid blood-money for him. And Sufyān added: that is because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not establish a Sunnah for it.
items.ma-1085: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān (ḥ) and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Khalīl, from ʿAlī, he said: I heard a man asking forgiveness for his parents, and they were both polytheists. I said: You ask forgiveness for your parents while they are polytheists? He said: Did Ibrāhīm not ask forgiveness for his father while he was a polytheist? He said: I mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and it was revealed: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists﴾ to the end of the two verses. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: And Allah revealed: ﴿And the asking of forgiveness by Ibrāhīm for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him﴾ [al-Tawbah: 114].
items.ma-1086: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us; and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Sufyān, from al-Aʿmash, from Khaythamah, from Suwayd ibn Ghafalah, he said: ʿAlī said: When I narrate to you a hadith from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, to fall from the sky is dearer to me than to lie about him; and when I speak to you of what is between me and you, then war is deception. I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “In the last of time a people will come forth, young in years, foolish – and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: most foolish – in their reasoning. They will speak of the best of what is said by creation. They will recite the Qurʾān, which will not pass beyond their throats – ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: their faith will not pass beyond their throats. They will pass out of the religion as the arrow passes out of the game. So when you meet them, kill them, for in killing them there is reward for whoever kills them, with Allah ﷿ on the Day of Resurrection.” ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: “So when you meet them, kill them, for killing them is a reward for whoever kills them on the Day of Resurrection.”
items.ma-1087: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Isḥāq ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Yaḥyā ibn Abī Bukayr narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ: “﴿And you make your provision﴾ – he said: your thanks – ﴿that you deny﴾ [al-Wāqiʿah: 82] – he said: You say: We were given rain by such-and-such a star.”
items.ma-1088: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Isḥāq ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Qabīṣah narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAlī – he said: I think he attributed it to the Prophet – he said: “Whoever lies about his dream will be charged on the Day of Resurrection with tying a knot in a grain of barley.”
items.ma-1089: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Ibrāhīm ibn al-Ḥasan al-Muqriʾ al-Bāhilī narrated to me, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Whoever lies about a dream deliberately, let him take his seat in the Fire.”
items.ma-1090: ʿAffān narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, Ḥuṣayn narrated to us, Saʿd ibn ʿUbaydah narrated to me, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me, al-Zubayr and Abū Marthad – and each of us was a horseman – and said: “Go until you reach Rawḍat Ḥājj – thus Abū ʿAwānah said – for in it is a woman with a letter from Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿah to the polytheists.” And he mentioned the hadith at length.
items.ma-1091: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, he said: The Prophet ﷺ ruled that debt is settled before the bequest, while you recite: ﴿after any bequest which is made or any debt﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 12]; and that the full brothers inherit from one another, not the banū al-ʿallāt.
items.ma-1092: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Khaythamah Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb narrated to me, Jarīr narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Abū al-Bakhtarī, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, he said: ʿAlī said: When a hadith is narrated to you from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, think of him that which is most modest, that which is most guided, and that which is most God-fearing.
items.ma-1093: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Nājiyah ibn Kaʿb, from ʿAlī, he said: When Abū Ṭālib died I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: Your old, astray uncle has died. He said: “Go and bury him, and do nothing until you come to me.” He said: So I went and buried him, and he commanded me and I bathed. Then he made supplications for me with which I would not wish to have the whole breadth of anything in exchange.
items.ma-1094: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Masʿūd ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood for a funeral and we stood; then he sat and we sat.
items.ma-1095: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar al-Qawārīrī narrated to us, Ibn Mahdī narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Zubayd, from Saʿd ibn ʿUbaydah, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “There is no obedience to any created being in disobedience to Allah ﷿.”
items.ma-1096: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, he said: ʿAlī said: I said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Shall I not direct you to the most beautiful girl in Quraysh? He said: “And who is she?” I said: The daughter of Ḥamzah. He said: “Do you not know that she is the daughter of my brother by milk? Allah has made unlawful by milk what He has made unlawful by lineage.”
items.ma-1097: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I have pardoned you from the ṣadaqah on horses and slaves, but bring a quarter of a tenth: one dirham out of every forty dirhams.”
items.ma-1098: Wakīʿ and ʿUthmān ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, both said: Usāmah ibn Zayd narrated to us; Wakīʿ said: he said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥunayn, and ʿUthmān said: from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥunayn, I heard ʿAlī say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade me – and I do not say: he forbade you – safflower-dyed garments and wearing a gold ring.
items.ma-1099: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr narrated to me, my father narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Saʿd ibn ʿUbaydah, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAlī, he said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, why do I see you choosing so carefully among Quraysh while leaving us? He said: “Do you have someone?” I said: The daughter of Ḥamzah. He said: “She is the daughter of my brother by milk.”
items.ma-1100: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sayf ibn Sulaymān al-Makkī narrated to us, from Mujāhid, from Ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAlī: that when the Prophet ﷺ slaughtered the budn, he commanded me to give in charity their meat, their hides and their covers.
items.ma-1101: Wakīʿ narrated to us, he said: Sufyān added; and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Sufyān, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from Mujāhid, from Ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me not to give the butcher anything of it as wage for his butchering.
items.ma-1102: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to me, Abū al-Aḥwaṣ narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Hubayrah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the gold ring, the mīthara, qassī, and jiʿah.
items.ma-1103: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to me, Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Hubayrah, from ʿAlī, he said: When the last ten nights began, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would wake his family and raise the miʾzar. Abū Bakr was asked: What is “raised the miʾzar”? He said: He withdrew from women.
items.ma-1104: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Khaythamah narrated to me, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, from Sufyān, Shuʿbah and Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, from Hubayrah, from ʿAlī: that the Prophet ﷺ used to wake his family in the last ten nights of Ramaḍān.
items.ma-1105: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Yūsuf al-Ṣaffār, the mawlā of Banū Umayyah, and Sufyān ibn Wakīʿ narrated to me, both said: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Hubayrah ibn Yarīm, from ʿAlī, he said: When the last ten nights began, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would tighten the miʾzar and wake his wives. Ibn Wakīʿ said: raised the miʾzar.
items.ma-1106: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Bakkār, the mawlā of Banū Hāshim, narrated to me, Abū Wakīʿ al-Jarrāḥ ibn Malīḥ narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq al-Hamdānī, from Hubayrah ibn Yarīm, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded that we examine the eye and the ear closely, and upward.
items.ma-1107: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Abū Hāshim ibn Kathīr, from Qays al-Khārifī, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took the lead, Abū Bakr came second, and ʿUmar third; then a fitnah struck us, so it is what Allah wills.
items.ma-1108: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿUthmān al-Thaqafī, from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd, from ʿAlī, he said: The Prophet ﷺ forbade us to put a donkey to a mare.
items.ma-1109: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Hishām ibn ʿUrwah narrated to us, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The best of its women is Khadījah, and the best of its women is Maryam bint ʿImrān.”
items.ma-1110: Wakīʿ narrated to us, al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Saʿd ibn ʿUbaydah, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿAlī, he said: We were sitting with the Prophet ﷺ at a funeral – I think he said: at Baqīʿ al-Gharqad – and he tapped the ground, then raised his head and said: “There is none of you but his seat in Paradise and his seat in the Fire has been written.” We said: O Messenger of Allah, shall we not rely on that? He said: “No. Act, for each is made ready.” Then he recited: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah and believes in the best reward, We shall ease him toward ease. But as for he who is stingy and considers himself free of need and denies the best reward, We shall ease him toward hardship﴾ [al-Layl: 5–10].
items.ma-1111: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Suwayd ibn Saʿīd narrated to me, ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd ibn al-Ḥasan al-Hilālī informed me, from Abū Isḥāq, from Hubayrah ibn Yarīm, from ʿAlī, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Seek Laylat al-Qadr in the last ten nights; and if you are overcome, do not be overcome in the remaining seven.”
items.ma-1112: Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Ribʿī ibn Ḥirāsh, from a man, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A servant will not truly believe until he believes in four: he believes in Allah; that Allah sent me with the truth; he believes in the resurrection after death; and he believes in the Qadar, its good and its evil.”
items.ma-1113: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Isḥāq ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbbād narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq informed me, from Hubayrah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the gold ring, wearing qassī, and the mīthara.
items.ma-1114: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Mūsā Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to me, Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq narrated to me, from Hubayrah ibn Yarīm, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to wake his family in the last ten nights and raise the miʾzar.
items.ma-1115: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Surayj ibn Yūnus narrated to me, Salm ibn Qutaybah narrated to us, from Shuʿbah and Isrāʾīl, from Abū Isḥāq, from Hubayrah ibn Yarīm, from ʿAlī: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to wake his family in the ten.
items.ma-1116: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿAlī ibn Ḥakīm al-Awdī narrated to me, Sharīk narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Hubayrah ibn Yarīm, he said: We were with ʿAlī, and he called a son of his, who was called ʿUthmān, who had a forelock.
items.ma-1118: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū al-Sarī Hannād ibn al-Sarī narrated to me, Sharīk narrated to us. And ʿAlī ibn Ḥakīm al-Awdī narrated to us, Sharīk informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Hubayrah, from ʿAlī; ʿAlī ibn Ḥakīm said in his narration: Do you not feel protective jealousy that your women go out? And Hannād said in his narration: Do you not feel shame or protective jealousy? For it has reached me that your women go out in the markets jostling the ʿulūj.
items.ma-1119:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, he said: I heard al-Qāsim ibn Mukhaymirah narrate from Shurayḥ ibn Hāniʾ: that he asked ʿĀʾishah about wiping over the leather socks, and she said: Ask ʿAlī about that, for he used to go on expeditions with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So he asked him, and he said: For the traveller three days and their nights, and for the resident a day and a night.
Muḥammad was asked: Did he attribute it to the Prophet? He said: He thought it was attributed to him, but he held back from saying so.
items.ma-1120: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿAdī narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAwn, from al-Shaʿbī, he said: Muḥammad ﷺ cursed the one who consumes ribā, the one who feeds it, the one who writes it, the one who witnesses it, the woman who tattoos and the woman who has herself tattooed – Ibn ʿAwn said: I said: Unless from an illness? He said: Yes – and the one who makes lawful and the one for whom it is made lawful, and the one who withholds the ṣadaqah. And he said: And he used to forbid wailing, and did not say: he cursed. I said: Who narrated to you? He said: al-Ḥārith al-Aʿwar al-Hamdānī.
items.ma-1121: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Ibrāhīm ibn al-Ḥajjāj al-Nājī and Muḥammad ibn Abān ibn ʿImrān al-Wāsiṭī narrated to us, both said: Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us – and this is the wording of Muḥammad ibn Abān – from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Zādhān, from ʿAlī, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever leaves the place of a single hair from janābah that water has not reached, such-and-such will be done to him from the Fire.” ʿAlī said: From then on I have been hostile to my hair, as you see.
items.ma-1122: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Ibn ʿUmayr. Sharīk said: I said to him: From whom, O Abū ʿUmayr? From whom did he narrate? He said: From Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr, from his father, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was large of head, his face tinged with redness, thick in the palms and feet, large of beard, with a long masrubah, large in the joints. He walked as though going down a slope, leaning forward as he walked, neither short nor tall. I never saw anyone like him before him or after him ﷺ.
items.ma-1123: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, Ibn Abī Laylā narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salimah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to have us recite the Qurʾān so long as he was not in janābah.
items.ma-1124:
ʿAlī ibn ʿĀṣim narrated to us, ʿĀṣim ibn Kulayb al-Jarmī informed us, from Abū Burdah ibn Abī Mūsā, he said: I was sitting with my father when ʿAlī came and stood over us and greeted us, then commanded Abū Mūsā in certain matters of the people's affairs. He said: Then ʿAlī said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: “Ask Allah for guidance, and by that intend the guidance of the road; and ask Allah for straightness, and by that intend your straightening of the arrow.”
And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade me to put my ring on this or on this: the index and the middle. He said: He was standing, so I do not know on which of them.
He said: And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade me the mīthara and the qassiyyah. We said to him: O Commander of the Believers, and what is the mīthara? He said: Something that women make for their husbands, on their saddles. He said: We said: And what is the qassiyyah? He said: Garments that come to us from the direction of al-Shām, ribbed, with patterns like citrons on them. Abū Burdah said: When I saw the sabanī I knew that it was that.
items.ma-1125: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Wahb ibn Baqiyyah al-Wāsiṭī narrated to me, Khālid ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Maysarah and Zādhān, both said: ʿAlī ﵁ drank while standing, then said: If I drink standing, I have seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ drink standing; and if I drink sitting, I have seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ drink sitting.
items.ma-1126: Isḥāq ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us. And ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Sufyān informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Qays, from al-Ḥakam, from al-Qāsim ibn Mukhaymirah, from Shurayḥ ibn Hāniʾ, from ʿAlī ﵁, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made it three days and their nights for the traveller, and a day and a night for the resident.
items.ma-1127: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī and Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, both said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAwn ibn Abī Juḥayfah, from his father, he said: ʿAlī said: When I narrate to you a hadith from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, to fall from the sky to the earth is dearer to me than to say about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what he did not say; but war is deception.
items.ma-1128: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Ibrāhīm ibn al-Ḥajjāj narrated to me, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Zādhān: that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib drank while standing, and the people looked and disapproved of that. ʿAlī said: What are you looking at? If I drink standing, I have seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ drink standing; and if I drink sitting, I have seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ drink sitting.
items.ma-1129: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Ḥafṣ ʿAmr ibn ʿAlī narrated to me, Abū Dāwūd narrated to us, Warqāʾ informed me, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Abū Jamīlah, from ʿAlī: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had himself cupped and gave the cupper his wage.
items.ma-1130: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Khaythamah narrated to me, Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim narrated to us. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: And ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Ziyād narrated to me, Abū Dāwūd narrated to us, both said: Warqāʾ narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Abū Jamīlah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had himself cupped, and commanded me, and I gave the cupper his wage.
items.ma-1131: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to me, Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUthmān, from Zādhān, from ʿAlī, he said: Khadījah asked the Prophet ﷺ about two children of hers who had died in the Jāhiliyyah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “They are in the Fire.” He said: When he saw the dislike in her face he said: “Had you seen their place, you would have hated them.” She said: O Messenger of Allah, and my child by you? He said: “In Paradise.” He said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The believers and their children are in Paradise, and the polytheists and their children are in the Fire.” Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: ﴿And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith, We shall join their descendants with them﴾ [al-Ṭūr: 21].
items.ma-1132: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from al-Ḥakam, from Yaḥyā ibn al-Jazzār, from ʿAlī: that the Prophet ﷺ was sitting on the day of al-Khandaq at one of the openings of the trench, and said: “They have kept us busy from the middle ṣalāh until the sun set. May Allah fill their bellies and their houses with fire.”
items.ma-1133: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Zāʾidah ibn Qudāmah narrated to us, from Khālid ibn ʿAlqamah, ʿAbd Khayr narrated to us, he said: ʿAlī sat in al-Raḥabah after he had prayed Fajr, then said to his servant: Bring me water for purification. The servant brought him a vessel containing water, and a basin – ʿAbd Khayr said: and we were sitting looking at him – and he took the vessel in his right hand and tipped it over his left hand, then washed his palms. Then he took the vessel in his right hand and poured over his left hand and washed his palms; he did that three times – ʿAbd Khayr said: each time without putting his hand into the vessel until he had washed it three times – then he put his right hand into the vessel, rinsed his mouth, snuffed water into his nose and blew it out with his left hand; he did that three times. Then he put his right hand into the vessel and washed his face three times. Then he washed his right hand three times up to the elbow, then washed his left hand three times up to the elbow. Then he put his right hand into the vessel until the water covered it, then raised it with the water it held and wiped it with his left hand. Then he wiped his head with both hands once. Then he poured with his right hand three times over his right foot, then washed it with his left hand; then poured with his right hand over his left foot, then washed it with his left hand three times. Then he put in his right hand, scooped up with his palm and drank. Then he said: This is the purification of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, so whoever would like to look at the purification of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, this is his purification.
items.ma-1134: ʿAbd al-Wahhāb narrated to us, from Saʿīd, from Qatādah, from Abū Ḥassān al-Aʿraj, from ʿAbīdah al-Salmānī, from ʿAlī, that the Prophet ﷺ said on the day of al-Aḥzāb: “O Allah, fill their houses and their graves with fire, as they kept us busy from the middle ṣalāh until the sun went down.”
items.ma-1135: Ismāʿīl ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, Ayyūb informed us, from Mujāhid, he said: ʿAlī said: Once in al-Madīnah I was extremely hungry, so I went out seeking work in the outskirts of al-Madīnah, and there was a woman who had gathered clods of earth. I thought she wanted to wet them, so I came to her and agreed with her on a date for every bucket. I drew sixteen buckets until my hands were blistered. Then I went to the water and drank from it, then came to her and held out my palms like this before her – and Ismāʿīl spread his hands and brought them together – and she counted out for me sixteen dates. Then I went to the Prophet ﷺ and told him, and he ate of them with me.
items.ma-1136: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to me, Wakīʿ narrated to us. And Sufyān ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Abū Janāb, from Abū Jamīlah al-Ṭuhawī, he said: I heard ʿAlī say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had himself cupped, then said to the cupper when he had finished: “How much is your daily charge?” He said: Two ṣāʿs. So he reduced it for him by one ṣāʿ, and commanded me, and I gave him one ṣāʿ.
items.ma-1137: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Isḥāq ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān (ḥ) and Abū Khaythamah narrated to me, Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā al-Thaʿlabī, from Abū Jamīlah, from ʿAlī: that a servant girl of the Prophet ﷺ had committed fornication, and he commanded me to carry out the ḥadd on her, but I found that her bleeding had not yet dried. So I came to him and mentioned it to him, and he said: “When her bleeding has dried, carry out the ḥadd on her. Carry out the ḥudūd on those whom your right hands possess.” And this is the wording of the hadith of Isḥāq ibn Ismāʿīl.
items.ma-1138: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah and al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Walīd al-Narsī narrated to me, both said: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Abū Jamīlah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Prophet ﷺ was informed of a slave woman of his who had committed fornication … and he mentioned the hadith.
items.ma-1139: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam, that he said: I was present with ʿAlī and ʿUthmān between Makkah and al-Madīnah, and ʿUthmān was forbidding the mutʿah and combining the two. When ʿAlī saw that, he pronounced the talbiyah for both, saying: Labbayka for ʿumrah and ḥajj together. ʿUthmān said: You see me forbid the people from it, and you do it? He said: I would not leave the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for the saying of anyone among the people.
items.ma-1140: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, my father and Isḥāq ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to me, both said: Ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib. And Sufyān ibn Wakīʿ narrated to me, ʿImrān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, both from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Maysarah: I saw ʿAlī drink while standing, and I said: You drink while standing?! He said: If I drink standing, I have seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ drink standing; and if I drink sitting, I have seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ drink sitting.
items.ma-1141: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, he said: I heard Ibn Abī Laylā: ʿAlī narrated to us: that Fāṭimah complained of what she suffered from the mark of the millstone on her hand, and captives had come to the Prophet ﷺ. She went but did not find him, and met ʿĀʾishah and told her. When the Prophet ﷺ came, ʿĀʾishah told him of Fāṭimah's coming to her. The Prophet ﷺ came to us when we had already taken to our beds, and we went to rise, but the Prophet ﷺ said: “Stay where you are.” He sat between us until I felt the coolness of his feet on my chest, and said: “Shall I not teach you something better than what you asked for? When you take to your beds, say Allāhu akbar thirty-four times, glorify Him thirty-three times, and praise Him thirty-three times. That is better for you than a servant.”
items.ma-1142:
ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Bakkār, the mawlā of Banū Hāshim, and Abū al-Rabīʿ al-Zahrānī narrated to me, both said: Abū Wakīʿ al-Jarrāḥ ibn Malīḥ narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā al-Thaʿlabī, from Abū Jamīlah, from ʿAlī – and Abū al-Rabīʿ said in his narration: from Maysarah Abū Jamīlah, from ʿAlī – that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me to a black slave woman of his who had committed zinā, to scourge her with the ḥadd. He said: I found her in her blood, so I came to the Prophet ﷺ and told him of that, and he said to me: “When she has recovered from her postpartum bleeding, scourge her fifty.”
And Abū al-Rabīʿ said in his narration: He said: I informed the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “When her bleeding has dried, carry out the ḥadd on her.” Then he said: “Carry out the ḥudūd.”
items.ma-1143: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to us, Abū Usāmah narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar ibn ʿAlī, from his father, from his grandfather: that ʿAlī would travel until, when the sun had set and it had grown dark, he would dismount and pray Maghrib, then pray ʿIshāʾ right after it, then say: This is how I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do.
items.ma-1144: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, al-Ḥakam informed us, he said: I heard Ibn Abī Laylā: that ʿAlī narrated to them: that Fāṭimah complained to her father of what she suffered in her hands from the millstone … and he mentioned the meaning of the hadith of Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar, from Shuʿbah.
items.ma-1145: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, he said: I heard Abū al-Bakhtarī al-Ṭāʾī say: One who heard ʿAlī informed me, saying: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me to Yemen, I said: You send me while I am a young man and have no knowledge of much of judging? He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck my chest and said: “Go, for Allah ﷿ will make your tongue firm and guide your heart.” He said: And I was never at a loss in judging between two parties.
items.ma-1146: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, he said: ʿAlī and ʿUthmān met at ʿUsfān, and ʿUthmān was forbidding the mutʿah or the ʿumrah. ʿAlī said: What do you intend by forbidding something the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did? ʿUthmān said: Leave us out of it.
items.ma-1147: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us. And Ḥajjāj, Shuʿbah informed us, from Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm, he said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād say: ʿAlī said: I never saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ join his parents together for anyone other than Saʿd ibn Mālik, for on the day of Uḥud he kept saying: “Shoot; may my father and mother be your ransom.”
items.ma-1148:
ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, my father, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar al-Qawārīrī, Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr al-Muqaddamī and Muḥammad ibn Bashshār Bundār narrated to me, they said: Muʿādh ibn Hishām narrated to us, he said: my father narrated to me. And Abū Khaythamah narrated to me, ʿAbd al-Ṣamad and Muʿādh ibn Hishām narrated to us, both said: Hishām narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Abū Ḥarb ibn Abī al-Aswad, from Abū al-Aswad – and Abū Khaythamah said in his narration: Ibn Abī al-Aswad, from his father – from ʿAlī, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The urine of the nursing boy is sprinkled over, and the urine of the girl is washed.”
Qatādah said: This is so long as they have not eaten food; when they have eaten food, both are washed.
ʿAbd Allāh said: Abū Khaythamah did not mention the saying of Qatādah in his narration.
items.ma-1149:
ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn ʿAbd al-Wārith narrated to us, Hishām narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Abū Ḥarb ibn Abī al-Aswad al-Dīlī, [from his father], from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said regarding the nursing infant: “The urine of the boy is sprinkled over, and the urine of the girl is washed.”
Qatādah said: This is so long as they have not eaten food; when they have eaten, both are washed.
items.ma-1150: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: I heard Qatādah, from Abū Ḥassān al-Aʿraj, from ʿAbīdah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of al-Aḥzāb: “They have kept us busy from the middle ṣalāh until the sun went down. May Allah fill their graves with fire, and their houses – or their bellies.” Shuʿbah was unsure between houses and bellies.
items.ma-1151: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to me, he said: I heard Qatādah say: I heard Abū Ḥassān narrate from ʿAbīdah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of al-Aḥzāb: “They have kept us busy from the middle ṣalāh until the sun went down. May Allah fill their graves, and their houses – or their bellies – with fire.” He was unsure between houses and bellies; as for the graves, there is no doubt about it.
items.ma-1152: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed witr at every part of the night: at its beginning, its middle and its end; and his witr ended at the last part of it.
items.ma-1153: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Hubayrah, from ʿAlī: that the Prophet ﷺ used to wake his family in the last ten nights of Ramaḍān.
items.ma-1154: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Hubayrah, from ʿAlī: that a silk ḥullah was given as a gift to the Prophet ﷺ and he clothed me with it. ʿAlī said: I went out in it, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “I am not pleased to give you what I dislike for myself.” He said: So he commanded me and I cut it up among my women as head-coverings: between Fāṭimah and his aunt.
items.ma-1155: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd ibn Ḥisāb narrated to me, Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, ʿUtaybah – the blind – narrated to us, from Burayd ibn Aṣram, he said: I heard ʿAlī say: A man of the people of al-Ṣuffah died, and it was said: O Messenger of Allah, he left a dīnār and a dirham. He said: “Two brandings. Pray over your companion.”
items.ma-1156: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, he said: Abū Khaythamah narrated to me, Ḥabbān ibn Hilāl narrated to us, Jaʿfar narrated to us … and he mentioned the like of it.
items.ma-1157:
Ḥajjāj narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to me, from Qatādah, he said: I heard Jurayy ibn Kulayb say: I heard ʿAlī say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade a broken horn and ear.
Qatādah said: I asked Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab. I said: What is a broken ear? He said: When it is half or more than that.
items.ma-1158:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah, from Jurayy ibn Kulayb: that he heard ʿAlī say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade sacrificing an animal with a broken horn and ear.
Qatādah said: I mentioned that to Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab and he said: Yes, ʿaḍab is half, or more than that.
items.ma-1159: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Hubayrah, from ʿAlī: that the Prophet ﷺ forbade – or forbade me – the mīthara, qassī and the gold ring.
items.ma-1160: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Hāniʾ ibn Hāniʾ, from ʿAlī: that ʿAmmār asked permission to see the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: “The good, the purified. Let him in.”
items.ma-1161: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, he said: I heard Ḥārithah ibn Muḍarrib narrate from ʿAlī, he said: I saw us on the night of Badr, and there was no one among us but asleep, except the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, for he was praying toward a tree and supplicating until morning. And we had no horseman on the day of Badr other than al-Miqdād ibn al-Aswad.
items.ma-1162: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl ibn Sumayʿ, Mālik ibn ʿUmayr narrated to me, he said: Zayd ibn Ṣūḥān came to ʿAlī and said: Tell me what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade you. He said: He forbade me the ḥantam, the gourd, the naqīr and the jiʿah; and the gold ring – or he said: the gold band – and silk, qassī and the red mīthara. He said: And a silk ḥullah was given as a gift to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he clothed me with it, and I went out in it. He took it and gave it to Fāṭimah, or to his aunt. Ismāʿīl says that.
items.ma-1163: Yūnus narrated it to us, ʿAbd al-Wāḥid narrated to us … and he mentioned it with its isnād and its meaning, except that he said: Ṣaʿṣaʿah ibn Ṣūḥān came to ʿAlī ﵁.
items.ma-1164: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Bakkār narrated to us, Ḥibbān ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, from Ḍirār ibn Murrah, from Ḥuṣayn al-Muzanī, he said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said on the minbar: O people, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Nothing cuts the ṣalāh except a ḥadath.” I am not shy before you of what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was not shy of. He said: “And the ḥadath is to break wind, silently or noisily.”
items.ma-1165: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Qaṭan ibn Nusayr Abū ʿAbbād al-Dhāriʿ narrated to me, Jaʿfar ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, ʿUtaybah the blind narrated to us, Burayd ibn Aṣram narrated to us, he said: I heard ʿAlī say: A man of the people of al-Ṣuffah died and left a dīnār and a dirham. It was said: O Messenger of Allah, he left a dīnār and a dirham. He said: “Two brandings. Pray over your companion.”
items.ma-1166: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr al-Muqaddamī narrated to me, Saʿīd ibn Salamah – meaning Ibn Abī al-Ḥusām – narrated to us, Muslim ibn Abī Maryam narrated to us, from a man of the Anṣār, from ʿAlī, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever visits a sick person walks in the khirāf of Paradise; and when he sits with him he is immersed in mercy; and when he leaves him, seventy thousand angels are assigned to him, asking forgiveness for him that day.”
items.ma-1167: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us. And Ḥajjāj, Shuʿbah informed us, he said: I heard Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir say: I heard Masʿūd ibn al-Ḥakam say: I heard ʿAlī – Ḥajjāj said: he said: ʿAlī ﵁ narrated to us – he said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stand for a funeral and we stood, and I saw him sit and we sat.
items.ma-1168: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Kulayb, he said: I heard Abū Burdah say: I heard ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Say: O Allah, I ask You for guidance and straightness; and by guidance remember your guiding of the road, and by straightness remember your straightening of the arrow.” He said: And he forbade – or forbade me – qassī and the mīthara, and the ring on the index finger or the middle finger.
items.ma-1169: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū ʿAwn, he said: I heard Abū Ṣāliḥ say: ʿAlī said: I mentioned the daughter of Ḥamzah to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: “She is the daughter of my brother by milk.”
items.ma-1170: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Dāwūd al-Mubārakī Sulaymān ibn Muḥammad narrated to me, Abū Shihāb narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from al-Ḥakam, from Abū al-Muwarriʿ, from ʿAlī, he said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at a funeral and he said: “Who will go to al-Madīnah and leave no grave without levelling it, no image without smearing it over, and no idol without breaking it?” A man stood up and said: I. Then he feared the people of al-Madīnah and sat down. ʿAlī said: So I went, then came back and said: O Messenger of Allah, I left in al-Madīnah no grave without levelling it, no image without smearing it over, and no idol without breaking it. He said: “Whoever returns and does any of that has disbelieved in what Allah revealed to Muḥammad. O ʿAlī, do not be a stirrer of fitnah – or he said: a conceited man – and do not be a trader, except a trader in good, for those are the ones who put off deeds.”
items.ma-1171: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū ʿAwn, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, he said: I heard ʿAlī say: A siyarāʾ ḥullah was given as a gift to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent it to me, so I went out in it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ became angry until I saw the anger in his face, and he said: “I did not give it to you to wear.” He said: So he commanded me and I distributed it among my women.
items.ma-1172: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Mudrik, from Abū Zurʿah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nujayy, from his father, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “The angels do not enter a house in which there is an image, a person in janābah, or a dog.”
items.ma-1173: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Maysarah, from al-Nazzāl ibn Sabrah: that he was present when ʿAlī prayed Ẓuhr, then sat in al-Raḥabah attending to the needs of the people. When ʿAṣr came, a basin was brought to him, and he took a handful of water and wiped his hands, forearms, face, head and feet, then drank its remainder while standing. Then he said: “Some people dislike to drink while standing, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did as I have done; and this is the ablution of one who has not broken ablution.”
items.ma-1174: ʿAffān narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Maysarah informed us, he said: I heard al-Nazzāl ibn Sabrah say: I heard ʿAlī … and he mentioned its meaning, except that he said: a jug was brought.
items.ma-1175: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: al-Ḥakam informed me, from Abū Muḥammad, from ʿAlī, he said: The Prophet ﷺ sent him to al-Madīnah and commanded him to level the graves.
items.ma-1176: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Shaybān Abū Muḥammad narrated to me, Ḥammād – meaning Ibn Salamah – narrated to us, Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāh informed us, from al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtaybah, from Abū Muḥammad al-Hudhalī, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a man of the Anṣār to level every grave and smear over every idol. He said: O Messenger of Allah, I dislike to enter the houses of my people. He said: So he sent me, and when I came he said: “O ʿAlī, do not be a stirrer of fitnah, nor conceited, nor a trader except a trader in good, for those are the ones who put off – or who are outstripped – in deeds.”
items.ma-1177: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from a man of the people of al-Baṣrah – he said: the people of al-Baṣrah gave him the kunyah Abū Muwarriʿ, and he said: the people of al-Kūfah gave him the kunyah Abū Muḥammad – he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was at a funeral … and he mentioned the like of the hadith of Abū Dāwūd, from Abū Shihāb.
items.ma-1178: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, he said. And Ḥajjāj said: Shuʿbah narrated to me, he said: I heard Mālik ibn ʿUrfuṭah say: I heard ʿAbd Khayr say: I saw ʿAlī, a chair was brought to him and he sat on it. Then a jug was brought – Ḥajjāj said: a basin of water – and he washed his hands three times, rinsed his mouth three times along with snuffing water into his nose, with one handful of water, washed his face three times, and washed his forearms three times – Ḥajjāj said: three times each – with one hand, and put his hands into the basin. Then he wiped his head – Ḥajjāj said: he gestured with his hands from the front of his head to the back of his head, and said: I do not know whether he brought them back to the front of his head or not – and washed his feet three times – Ḥajjāj said: three times each. Then he said: Whoever would like to look at the purification of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, this is the purification of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-1179: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar al-Qawārīrī narrated to me, Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us, Jamīl ibn Murrah narrated to us, from Abū al-Waḍīʾ, he said: I was present with ʿAlī when he killed the people of al-Nahrawān. He said: Look for the deformed one for me. They searched for him among the slain and said: We cannot find him. He said: Go back and search, for by Allah I have not lied and I have not been lied to. They went back and searched, and he repeated that several times, each time swearing by Allah: I have not lied and I have not been lied to. They went off and found him beneath the slain in mud, and brought him out and brought him. Abū al-Waḍīʾ said: It is as though I am looking at him: an Abyssinian, with a breast upon him that covered one of his arms, like the breast of a woman, with hairs on it like the hairs on the tail of a jerboa.
items.ma-1180: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Sulaymān, from Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, from al-Ḥārith ibn Suwayd, from ʿAlī: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the gourd and the pitch-coated vessel.
items.ma-1181:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Sulaymān, from Saʿd ibn ʿUbaydah, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ: that he was at a funeral and took a stick and tapped the ground, and said: “There is none of you but his seat in the Fire, or in Paradise, has been written.” They said: O Messenger of Allah, shall we not rely on that? He said: “Act, for each is made ready: ﴿As for he who gives and fears Allah and believes in the best reward, We shall ease him toward ease. But as for he who is stingy and considers himself free of need and denies the best reward, We shall ease him toward hardship﴾.”
Shuʿbah said: Manṣūr ibn al-Muʿtamir also narrated it to me, and I found nothing objectionable in it compared with the hadith of Sulaymān.
items.ma-1182: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: I heard Sulaymān narrate from al-Mundhir al-Thawrī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAlī, he said: I felt shy to ask the Prophet ﷺ about madhy because of Fāṭimah, so I commanded al-Miqdād ibn al-Aswad and he asked the Prophet ﷺ about it, and he said: “Ablution is required because of it.”
items.ma-1183: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah, from al-Ḥasan: that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb wanted to stone an insane woman, and ʿAlī said to him: You have no right to do that. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “The pen is lifted from three: from the sleeper until he wakes, from the child until he reaches puberty, and from the insane until he recovers – or regains his reason.” So ʿUmar averted it from her.
items.ma-1184: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Saʿīd narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh al-Dānāj, from Ḥuḍayn, he said: Testimony was given against al-Walīd ibn ʿUqbah before ʿUthmān that he had drunk khamr, and ʿAlī spoke to ʿUthmān about him. He said: Here is your cousin; scourge him. He said: Rise, O Ḥasan. He said: What have you to do with this? Give this to someone other than you. He said: Rather you have grown weak, frail and feeble. Rise, O ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar. So he scourged him, and ʿAlī counted. When he reached forty he said: Enough – or: hold – the Messenger of Allah ﷺ scourged forty, Abū Bakr forty, and ʿUmar completed it to eighty, and each is a Sunnah.
items.ma-1185: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah, from al-Shaʿbī: that Sharāḥah al-Hamdāniyyah came to ʿAlī and said: I have committed zinā. He said: Perhaps you are jealous, perhaps you saw it in your sleep, perhaps you were forced? To all that she said: No. So he scourged her on Thursday and stoned her on Friday, and said: I scourged her by the Book of Allah and stoned her by the Sunnah of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-1186: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Maʿmar narrated to us, al-Zuhrī narrated to me, from Abū ʿUbayd, the mawlā of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, he said: I was present with ʿAlī, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbid anyone to keep any of his sacrificial meat beyond three days.
items.ma-1187: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Khaythamah Zuhayr ibn Ḥarb and Sufyān ibn Wakīʿ ibn al-Jarrāḥ narrated to me, both said: Jarīr narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from al-Minhāl ibn ʿAmr, from Nuʿaym ibn Dijājah al-Asadī, he said: I was with ʿAlī when Abū Masʿūd came in to him and said to him: O Farrūkh, are you the one who says: A hundred years will not come upon the people while there is a blinking eye on the earth? Your backside has missed the hole! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only said: “A hundred years will not come upon the people while there is a blinking eye on the earth among those who are alive today.” And the ease and relief of this world is only after the hundred.
items.ma-1188: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr al-Muqaddamī narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us, Jamīl ibn Murrah narrated to us, from Abū al-Waḍīʾ, he said: I was present with ʿAlī when he killed the people of al-Nahrawān. He said: Search among the slain. They said: We have not found him. He said: Look for him, for by Allah I have not lied and I have not been lied to. Until they brought him out from beneath the slain. Abū al-Waḍīʾ said: It is as though I am looking at him: an Abyssinian, one of whose arms was like the breast of a woman, with hairs on it like the tail of a jerboa.
items.ma-1189:
ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Ḥajjāj ibn Yūsuf the poet narrated to me, ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn ʿAbd al-Wārith narrated to me, Yazīd ibn Abī Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, that Abū al-Waḍīʾ ʿAbbād narrated to him that he said: We were heading for al-Kūfah with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, and when we had come within a journey of two or three nights from Ḥarūrāʾ, many people broke away from us. We mentioned that to ʿAlī, and he said: Let their matter not alarm you, for they will return … and he mentioned the hadith at length.
He said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib praised Allah and said: My intimate friend informed me that the leader of these people is a man with a deformed arm, upon the nipple of whose breast are hairs like the tail of a jerboa. They searched for him and did not find him, so we came to him and said: We have not found him. He said: Search for him, for by Allah I have not lied and I have not been lied to – three times. We said: We have not found him. So ʿAlī came himself and began saying: Turn over this one, turn over this one. Until a man from al-Kūfah came and said: Here he is. ʿAlī said: Allāhu akbar. Will no one come to you to tell you who his father is? The people began saying: This is Mālik, this is Mālik. ʿAlī said: Whose son is he?
items.ma-1190: Bahz narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, Salamah ibn Kuhayl informed us, from al-Shaʿbī: that ʿAlī said to Sharāḥah: Perhaps you were forced, perhaps your husband came to you, perhaps, perhaps? She said: No. He said: When she had given birth to what was in her womb, he scourged her, then stoned her. It was said to him: You scourged her, then stoned her?! He said: I scourged her by the Book of Allah and stoned her by the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-1191: Yazīd narrated to us, Shuʿbah informed us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Habbah al-ʿUranī, he said: I heard ʿAlī say: I am the first man to have prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-1192: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us. And Ḥajjāj: from Shuʿbah, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, he said: I heard Habbah al-ʿUranī say: I heard ʿAlī say: I am the first to have prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
items.ma-1193: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from Abū ʿUbayd, the mawlā of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, he said: … Then I was present with ʿAlī, and he prayed before giving the khuṭbah, without adhān or iqāmah, then gave the khuṭbah and said: O people, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade you to eat your sacrificial meat after three nights, so do not eat it after that.
items.ma-1194: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Hilāl ibn Yasāf, from Wahb ibn al-Ajdaʿ, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: “Do not pray after ʿAṣr, unless you pray while the sun is still high.”
items.ma-1195: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAlī: that the Prophet ﷺ used to fast continuously from one suḥūr to the next.
items.ma-1196: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Ibn ʿUyaynah informed us, from Muḥammad ibn Sūqah, from Mundhir al-Thawrī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, he said: Some people came to ʿAlī and complained of ʿUthmān's collectors. He said: My father said to me: Take this letter to ʿUthmān and say to him: The people have complained of your collectors, and this is the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ regarding the ṣadaqah, so command them to follow it. He said: I came to ʿUthmān and mentioned that to him. He said: Had he been going to mention anything against ʿUthmān, he would have mentioned it that day – meaning anything bad.
items.ma-1197: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Ḥajjāj ibn al-Shāʿir narrated to me, ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn ʿAbd al-Wārith narrated to me, Yazīd ibn Abī Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, that Abū al-Waḍīʾ ʿAbbād narrated to him that he said: We were heading for al-Kūfah with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib … and he mentioned the hadith of the deformed one. ʿAlī said: By Allah, I have not lied and I have not been lied to – three times. ʿAlī said: Indeed, my intimate friend informed me of three brothers from the jinn; this one is the eldest of them, the second has a great following, and the third has weakness in him.
items.ma-1198: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Zakariyyā ibn Yaḥyā Zaḥmawayh narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from Khālid ibn ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Khayr, he said: We prayed the morning ṣalāh and sat with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, and he called for water for ablution. He washed his hands three times, rinsed his mouth twice from one palm, then washed his face three times, then washed his forearms, then washed his feet three times. Then he said: This is the ablution of your Prophet ﷺ, so know it.
items.ma-1199: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Baḥr narrated to us, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Khālid ibn ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Khayr, he said: We came to ʿAlī after he had prayed, and he called for a jug. Then he rinsed his mouth three times and snuffed water into his nose three times, rinsing his mouth from the palm with which he took the water. He washed his face three times, his right hand three times and his left hand three times each. Then he said: Whoever is pleased to know the ablution of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, this is it.
items.ma-1200: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from Layth, from Mujāhid, from Abū Maʿmar, he said: We were with ʿAlī when a funeral passed by him and some people stood for it. ʿAlī said: Who gave you this fatwā?! They said: Abū Mūsā. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did that only once, when he was imitating the People of the Book; then when he was forbidden, he stopped.
items.ma-1201:
ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, Ibn Shihāb narrated to me, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, from his father Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: ʿAlī said: I received an old she-camel with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from the spoils on the day of Badr, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave me another old she-camel. One day I made them kneel at the door of a man of the Anṣār, wishing to load them with idhkhir to sell it, and I had with me a goldsmith of Banū Qaynuqāʿ, so that I might use it to help with the wedding feast of Fāṭimah. Ḥamzah ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib was drinking in that house, and Ḥamzah sprang at the two camels with his sword, cut off their humps, split open their flanks, and then took some of their livers. I said to Ibn Shihāb: And from the hump? He said: He cut off their humps and took them away.
He said: I looked at a sight that appalled me, so I went to the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, with whom was Zayd ibn Ḥārithah, and told him what had happened. He came out with Zayd and went with him and entered upon Ḥamzah, and was angry with him. Ḥamzah raised his gaze and said: Are you anything but slaves of my father! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went back, retreating, until he left them. That was before the prohibition of khamr.
items.ma-1202: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to me, Abū al-Aḥwaṣ narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, he said: Some of the companions of ʿAlī said to ʿAlī ﵁: Will you not tell us about the ṣalāh of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by day, and the voluntary prayer? ʿAlī said: You cannot bear it. They said to him: Tell us of it, and we will take of it what we can bear … and he mentioned the hadith at length.
items.ma-1203: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Kāmil al-Jaḥdarī Fuḍayl ibn al-Ḥusayn dictated to me from his book, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, that he was asked about the ṣalāh of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by day, and he said: He used to pray sixteen rakʿahs. He said: When the sun was here as it is there, like the time of ʿAṣr, he would pray two rakʿahs; and when the sun was here as it is there, like the time of Ẓuhr, he would pray four rakʿahs. And he used to pray four rakʿahs before Ẓuhr and two after Ẓuhr, and four rakʿahs before ʿAṣr.
items.ma-1204: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from al-Ḥasan and ʿAbd Allāh, the two sons of Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from their father Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī: that he heard his father ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib say to Ibn ʿAbbās, when it reached him that he had permitted the mutʿah of women: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade it on the day of Khaybar, and the flesh of domestic donkeys.
items.ma-1205: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū Ḥayyah ibn Qays, from ʿAlī: that he performed ablution three times each, then wiped his head, then drank the remainder of his ablution water, then said: Whoever is pleased to look at the ablution of the Prophet ﷺ, let him look at this.
items.ma-1206: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from an old man of theirs called Sālim, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mulayl, he said: I heard ʿAlī say: Every Prophet was given seven nobles from his Ummah, and the Prophet ﷺ was given fourteen nobles from his Ummah, among them Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.
items.ma-1207: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from al-Ḥasan, from Qays ibn ʿUbād, he said: We were with ʿAlī, and whenever he was present at a scene, or looked out over a rise, or descended into a valley, he would say: Glory be to Allah; Allah and His Messenger have spoken the truth. I said to a man of Banū Yashkur: Come with us to the Commander of the Believers, so that we may ask him about his saying: Allah and His Messenger have spoken the truth. We went to him and said: O Commander of the Believers, we saw that when you were present at a scene, or descended into a valley, or looked out over a rise, you said: Allah and His Messenger have spoken the truth. Did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ make any covenant with you about that? He turned away from us and we pressed him, and when he saw that he said: By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made no covenant with me except what he made with the people. But the people fell upon ʿUthmān and killed him, and others than I were worse in state and deed in that than I. Then I saw that I was the most deserving of them for this matter, so I leapt upon it, and Allah knows best whether we were right or wrong.
items.ma-1208: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Isḥāq ibn Ismāʿīl and Abū Khaythamah narrated to us, both said: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Abū Isḥāq. And my father narrated to me, Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān and Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, he said: We asked ʿAlī about the voluntary prayer of the Prophet ﷺ by day. ʿAlī said: That is sixteen rakʿahs, the voluntary prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by day, and few are those who keep to it. ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Wakīʿ narrated to us, he said: And my father said: Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit said: O Abū Isḥāq, I would not want to have, in exchange for this hadith of yours, this mosque of yours filled with gold.
items.ma-1209: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, from Ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me to oversee his budn and to give in charity their hides and covers.
items.ma-1210: Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā ibn Abī Zāʾidah narrated to us, Mujālid informed us, from ʿĀmir, he said: Shurāḥah became pregnant while her husband was away, and her master took her to ʿAlī. ʿAlī said to her: Perhaps your husband came to you, or perhaps someone forced you against yourself? She said: No. And she confessed to zinā. ʿAlī scourged her on Thursday, I was witness to it, and stoned her on Friday, I was witness to it. He commanded concerning her and a pit was dug for her up to the navel. Then he said: Stoning is a Sunnah from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the verse of stoning was revealed, but those who used to recite it, and verses of the Qurʾān, perished at al-Yamāmah.
items.ma-1211: Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, from Zāʾidah, from Simāk, from Ḥanash, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When two men bring a dispute to you for judgment, do not judge for the first until you hear what the other says; then you will see how to judge.” He said: I have remained a judge ever since.
items.ma-1212: Muḥammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, Hishām ibn ʿUrwah narrated to us, from his father, that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar narrated to him that he heard ʿAlī say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “The best of its women is Maryam bint ʿImrān, and the best of its women is Khadījah.”
items.ma-1213: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn ʿAbbād narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muʿādh – meaning al-Ṣanʿānī – narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Whoever would be pleased to have his life extended, his provision made broad, and an evil death averted from him, let him fear Allah and maintain his ties of kinship.”
items.ma-1214: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Khaythamah narrated to me, Jarīr narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allah ﷿ is Witr, and Yuḥibbu the witr, so pray witr, O people of the Qurʾān.”
items.ma-1215: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar al-Qawārīrī narrated to me, Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ narrated to me, Shuʿbah narrated to me, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed witr at every part of the night: at its beginning, its middle and its end; and his witr ended at the last part of the night.
items.ma-1216: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, al-Ḥasan ibn al-Ḥurr narrated to us, al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtaybah narrated to us, from a man called Ḥanash, from ʿAlī, he said: The sun was eclipsed and ʿAlī led the people in ṣalāh. He recited ﴿Yā Sīn﴾ or the like, then went into rukūʿ for about the length of a sūrah, then raised his head and said: Samiʿa Allāhu liman ḥamidah. Then he stood for the length of a sūrah, supplicating and saying takbīr, then went into rukūʿ for the length of his recitation again, then said: Samiʿa Allāhu liman ḥamidah. Then he stood again for the length of a sūrah, then went into rukūʿ for the same again, until he had prayed four rukūʿs. Then he said: Samiʿa Allāhu liman ḥamidah, and prostrated. Then he rose for the second rakʿah and did as he had done in the first rakʿah. Then he sat supplicating and beseeching until the sun cleared. Then he told them that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had done likewise.
items.ma-1217: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Khaythamah narrated to me, Jarīr and Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, from Muṭarrif, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Prophet ﷺ never prayed a ṣalāh but prayed two rakʿahs after it.
items.ma-1218: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Khaythamah narrated to me, Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, from Muṭarrif, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray witr at the beginning of the night, in its middle and at its end; then his witr settled at the end of it.
items.ma-1219: Yaḥyā ibn Ādam narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, he said: I heard ʿAlī say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When a servant sits in his place of prayer after the ṣalāh, the angels send ṣalāh upon him, and their ṣalāh upon him is: O Allah, forgive him; O Allah, have mercy on him. And if he sits waiting for the ṣalāh, the angels send ṣalāh upon him, and their ṣalāh upon him is: O Allah, forgive him; O Allah, have mercy on him.”
items.ma-1220: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿAlī ibn Ḥakīm al-Awdī narrated to us, Sharīk informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, he said: Witr is not obligatory, but it is a Sunnah which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ established.
items.ma-1221: Yazīd narrated to us, Hishām informed us, from Muḥammad, from ʿAbīdah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of al-Khandaq: “What is the matter with them? May Allah fill their houses and their graves with fire, as they have held us back from the middle ṣalāh until the sun set.”
items.ma-1222: Yazīd narrated to us, Zakariyyā informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, he said: You recite: ﴿after any bequest which is made or any debt﴾, yet the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that debt is settled before the bequest; and that the full brothers inherit from one another, not the banū al-ʿallāt: a man inherits from his brother by his father and mother, not from his brother by his father alone.
items.ma-1223: Yazīd narrated to us, Misʿar informed us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Maysarah, from al-Nazzāl ibn Sabrah, he said: A vessel of water was brought to ʿAlī and he drank while standing. Then he said: It has reached me that some people dislike that one of them drink while standing, yet I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do as I have done. Then he took some of it and wiped himself, then said: This is the ablution of one who has not broken ablution.
items.ma-1224: Yazīd narrated to us, Hishām informed us, from Muḥammad, from ʿAbīdah, he said: ʿAlī said of the people of the river: Among them is a man with a stunted hand – or a small hand, or a deformed hand. Were it not that you would become arrogant, I would inform you of what Allah has decreed upon the tongue of His Prophet ﷺ for those who kill them. ʿAbīdah said: I said to ʿAlī: Did you hear it? He said: Yes, by the Rabb of the Kaʿbah. He swore to it three times.
items.ma-1225: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Isḥāq ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to me, Jarīr narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allah is Witr, and Yuḥibbu the witr, so pray witr, O people of the Qurʾān.”
items.ma-1226: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Isḥāq ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Wakīʿ narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah al-Salūlī, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray two rakʿahs after every obligatory ṣalāh, except Fajr and ʿAṣr.
items.ma-1227: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Isḥāq ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Jarīr and Muḥammad ibn Fuḍayl ibn Ghazwān narrated to us, from Muṭarrif, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never prayed a ṣalāh after which prayer is made but prayed two rakʿahs after it.
items.ma-1228: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to me, Jarīr narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allah is Witr, and Yuḥibbu the witr, so pray witr, O people of the Qurʾān.”
items.ma-1229: Yazīd narrated to us, al-ʿAwwām informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAlī, he said: The Prophet ﷺ came to us one night, until he put his foot between me and Fāṭimah, and taught us what to say when we take to our beds: thirty-three tasbīḥahs, thirty-three taḥmīdahs and thirty-four takbīrahs. ʿAlī said: I have not left it since. A man said to him: Not even the night of Ṣiffīn? He said: Not even the night of Ṣiffīn.
items.ma-1230: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us, Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūbah informed us, from ʿAbd Allāh al-Dānāj, from Ḥuḍayn ibn al-Mundhir ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Waʿlah: that al-Walīd ibn ʿUqbah led the people in the Ṣubḥ prayer with four rakʿahs, then turned to them and said: Shall I add to it for you?! That was reported to ʿUthmān, who commanded that he be scourged. ʿAlī said to al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī: Rise, O Ḥasan, and scourge him. He said: And what have you to do with that?! ʿAlī said: Rather you have grown weak and frail. Rise, O ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, and scourge him. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar rose and scourged him while ʿAlī counted. When he reached forty he said to him: Hold. Then he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck forty for khamr, and Abū Bakr struck forty, and ʿUmar in the early part of his caliphate; then ʿUmar completed it to eighty, and each is a Sunnah.
items.ma-1231: Yazīd narrated to us, Sufyān ibn Saʿīd informed us, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā al-Thaʿlabī, from Abū Jamīlah, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib: that a servant girl of the Prophet ﷺ had given birth following zinā, and the Prophet ﷺ sent me to carry out the ḥadd on her. I found her in her blood, which had not yet dried from her, so I returned to the Prophet ﷺ and told him, and he said to me: “When the blood has dried from her, scourge her with the ḥadd.” Then he said: “Carry out the ḥudūd on those whom your right hands possess.”
items.ma-1232: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn Muḥammad ibn Bukayr al-Nāqid narrated to me, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dāwūd al-Kharībī narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, he said: Witr is not obligatory, but it is a Sunnah which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ established, so pray witr, O people of the Qurʾān.
items.ma-1233: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Walīd al-Narsī narrated to me, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I have pardoned you from horses and slaves, so pay the ṣadaqah on silver: one dirham out of every forty dirhams. There is nothing on a hundred and ninety, and when it reaches two hundred, there are five dirhams on it.”
items.ma-1234: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Walīd narrated to me, Abū ʿAwānah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, he said: ʿAlī was asked about the ṣalāh of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: He used to pray sixteen rakʿahs by night.
items.ma-1235: Yazīd narrated to us, Isrāʾīl ibn Yūnus informed us, from Thuwayr ibn Abī Fākhitah, from his father, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: Kisrā gave a gift to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he accepted it from him; Qayṣar gave a gift to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he accepted it from him; and the kings gave gifts and he accepted from them.
items.ma-1236: Yazīd narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah informed us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Rabīʿah ibn al-Nābighah, from his father, from ʿAlī: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade visiting graves, and the vessels, and keeping the meat of sacrifices beyond three days. Then he said: “I had forbidden you to visit graves; now visit them, for they remind you of the Hereafter. And I forbade you the vessels; now drink in them, but avoid everything that intoxicates. And I forbade you to keep the meat of sacrifices beyond three days; now keep what you wish.”
items.ma-1237: ʿAffān narrated it to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, ʿAlī ibn Zayd informed us, from Rabīʿah ibn al-Nābighah, from his father, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade visiting graves … and he mentioned its meaning, except that he said: “And beware every intoxicant.”
items.ma-1238: Yazīd narrated to us, Sharīk informed us, from al-Rukayn ibn al-Rabīʿ, from Ḥuṣayn ibn Qabīṣah, from ʿAlī, he said: I was a man who emitted madhy often, and I felt shy to ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ because of his daughter, so I commanded al-Miqdād and he asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about a man who finds madhy. He said: “That is the fluid of the male, and every male has fluid. Let him wash his male organ and his testicles and perform ablution as he does for the ṣalāh.”
items.ma-1239: Yazīd narrated to us, Ashʿath ibn Sawwār informed us, from Ibn Ashwaʿ, from Ḥanash ibn Abī al-Muʿtamir: that ʿAlī sent the head of his police and said: I send you on what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me on: leave no grave without levelling it, and no image without putting it down.
items.ma-1240:
ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to me, Jarīr narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Sālim, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “On what the sky waters there is a tenth, and on what is watered by the bucket and the water-wheel there is half of a tenth.”
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: I narrated to my father the hadith of ʿUthmān, from Jarīr, and he rejected it strongly. My father used not to narrate to us from Muḥammad ibn Sālim because of his weakness in his view, and his rejection of his hadith.
items.ma-1241: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿUmar narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Raḥīm – meaning al-Rāzī – narrated to us, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Musayyab, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray sixteen rakʿahs by night apart from the obligatory prayer.
items.ma-1242: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar narrated to me, ʿAbd al-Raḥīm al-Rāzī informed us, from Zakariyyā ibn Abī Zāʾidah and al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Musayyab, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, he said: We came to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and said: O Commander of the Believers, will you not tell us about the ṣalāh of the Prophet ﷺ, his voluntary prayer? He said: And which of you can bear it? They said: We will take from it what we can bear. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray sixteen rakʿahs by day apart from the obligatory prayer.
items.ma-1243: Yazīd narrated to us, Sufyān and Sharīk informed us, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “I have pardoned you from the ṣadaqah on horses and slaves, so pay a quarter of a tenth.”
items.ma-1244: Yazīd narrated to us, Isrāʾīl ibn Yūnus informed us, Abū Isḥāq narrated to us, from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: “O ʿAlī, I love for you what I love for myself, and dislike for you what I dislike for myself. Do not recite while you are in rukūʿ, nor while you are in sujūd; do not pray with your hair tied in a knot, for that is the seat of Shayṭān; do not sit on your heels between the two prostrations; do not play with pebbles; do not spread your forearms; do not prompt the imām; do not wear a gold ring; do not wear qassī; and do not ride on mayāthir.”
items.ma-1245: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Qays, from al-Ḥakam, from al-Qāsim ibn Mukhaymirah, from Shurayḥ ibn Hāniʾ, he said: I came to ʿĀʾishah to ask her about the leather socks, and she said: Go to the son of Abū Ṭālib and ask him, for he used to travel with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I went to him and asked him, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set three days and their nights for the traveller, and a day and a night for the resident.
items.ma-1246: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Sufyān informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Shutayr ibn Shakal al-ʿAbsī, he said: I heard ʿAlī say: On the day of al-Aḥzāb we prayed ʿAṣr between Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “They have kept us busy from the middle ṣalāh, the ʿAṣr ṣalāh. May Allah fill their graves and their bellies with fire.”
items.ma-1247: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Shaybān Abū Muḥammad narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Wārith ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, al-Ḥasan ibn Dhakwān narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Khālid, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Jibrīl ﵇ came to me but did not enter.” The Prophet ﷺ said to him: “What kept you from entering?” He said: We do not enter a house in which there is an image or urine.
items.ma-1248:
ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, he said: and Shaybān narrated it to us another time, ʿAbd al-Wārith narrated to us, from Ḥusayn ibn Dhakwān, from ʿAmr ibn Khālid, from Habbah ibn Abī Habbah, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: “Jibrīl came to me to give greetings of peace to me …” and he mentioned the hadith, the like of it.
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: My father used not to narrate from ʿAmr ibn Khālid; meaning, his hadith was worth nothing in his view.
items.ma-1249: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar al-Qawārīrī narrated to me, Yazīd Abū Khālid al-Baysarī al-Qurashī narrated to me, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit informed me, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: “Do not expose your thigh, and do not look at the thigh of a living or a dead person.”
items.ma-1250: Aswad ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥusayn and Abū Aḥmad al-Zubayrī narrated to us, they said: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Hubayrah ibn Yarīm, from ʿAlī, he said: I said to Fāṭimah: If only you went to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him for a servant, for grinding and work have worn you out – Ḥusayn said: grinding and work have exhausted you, and Abū Aḥmad said likewise – she said: Then come with me. He said: I went with her and we asked him, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “Shall I not direct you to what is better for you than that? When you retire to your bed, glorify Allah thirty-three times, praise Him thirty-three times, and say takbīr thirty-four times. That is a hundred on the tongue and a thousand in the Scale.” ʿAlī ﵁ said: I have not left it since I heard it from the Prophet ﷺ. A man said: Not even the night of Ṣiffīn? He said: Not even the night of Ṣiffīn.
items.ma-1251: Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, he said: I went in to Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī after he had prayed Fajr and he was sitting in the mosque. I said: Would it not be more comfortable for you if you went to your bed? He said: I heard ʿAlī say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever prays Fajr and then sits in his place of prayer, the angels send ṣalāh upon him, and their ṣalāh upon him is: O Allah, forgive him; O Allah, have mercy on him. And whoever waits for the ṣalāh, the angels send ṣalāh upon him, and their ṣalāh upon him is: O Allah, forgive him; O Allah, have mercy on him.”
items.ma-1252: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar narrated to me, al-Muḥāribī narrated to us, from Fuḍayl ibn Marzūq, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed Ḍuḥā when the sun in the east was where it is in the west at the time of the ʿAṣr ṣalāh.
