items.ma-1253: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Abī Samīnah narrated to me, ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Ḥasan ibn Dhakwān narrated to us, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever begs while having no need, is thereby multiplying for himself the heated stones of Jahannam.” They said: What is ‘having no need’? He said: “The evening meal of a night.”
items.ma-1254: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā narrated to me, ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Ḥasan ibn Dhakwān narrated to us, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī: that the Prophet ﷺ forbade every beast of prey with a fang, every bird with a talon, the price of carrion, the flesh of domestic donkeys, the earnings of a prostitute, the stud-fee of the male, and crimson mayāthir.
items.ma-1255: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Ṭāriq ibn Ziyād, he said: ʿAlī marched to al-Nahrawān and killed the Khawārij. He said: Search, for the Prophet ﷺ said: “A people will come who speak the word of truth which does not pass beyond their throats. They pass out of Islam as the arrow passes out of the game. Their mark – or: among them – is a black man with a deformed arm, on whose arm are black hairs.” If he is among them, you have killed the worst of people; and if he is not among them, you have killed the best of people. He said: Then we found the deformed one. He said: We fell down in prostration, and ʿAlī fell down in prostration with us.
items.ma-1256: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, Sharīk narrated to us, from al-Aswad ibn Qays, from ʿAmr ibn Sufyān, he said: A man gave a khuṭbah on the day of al-Baṣrah when ʿAlī had prevailed, and ʿAlī said: This is the eloquent orator. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took the lead, Abū Bakr prayed, and ʿUmar was third; then a fitnah struck us after them, in which Allah does what He wills.
items.ma-1257: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, Misʿar narrated to us, from Abū ʿAwn, from Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Ḥanafī, from ʿAlī, he said: It was said to ʿAlī and to Abū Bakr on the day of Badr: With one of you is Jibrīl, and with the other Mīkāʾīl, and Isrāfīl is a great angel who attends the fighting – or he said: attends the rank.
items.ma-1258: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, Misʿar narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim, from ʿAlī: that the Prophet ﷺ prayed four rakʿahs before Ẓuhr.
items.ma-1259: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Qāsim ibn Kathīr Abū Hāshim, the seller of fine cloth, from Qays al-Khārifī, he said: I heard ʿAlī say on this minbar: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took the lead, Abū Bakr prayed, and ʿUmar was third; then a fitnah struck us – or befell us – and it was what Allah willed.
items.ma-1260: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbdawayh Abū Muḥammad, the mawlā of Banū Hāshim, narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed witr at every part of the night: at its beginning, its middle and its end; and his witr ended at the last part of the night.
items.ma-1261: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to me, Saʿīd ibn Khuthaym Abū Maʿmar al-Hilālī narrated to us, Fuḍayl ibn Marzūq narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Prophet ﷺ used to pray eight rakʿahs of voluntary prayer, and by day twelve rakʿahs.
items.ma-1262: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sandal and Suwayd ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, together in the year two hundred and twenty-six, both said: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah al-Salūlī, he said: ʿAlī said: Witr is not obligatory like your obligatory ṣalāh, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed witr, then said: “Pray witr, O people of the Qurʾān; pray witr, for Allah is Witr, and Yuḥibbu the witr.” And this is the wording of the hadith of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sandal, and their meaning is one.
items.ma-1263: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, Fiṭr narrated to us, from Kathīr ibn Nāfiʿ al-Nawwāʾ, he said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mulayl say: I heard ʿAlī say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There was no Prophet before me but was given seven noble companions, ministers; and I have been given fourteen: Ḥamzah, Jaʿfar, ʿAlī, Ḥasan, Ḥusayn, Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, al-Miqdād, Ḥudhayfah, Salmān, ʿAmmār and Bilāl.”
items.ma-1264: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, Yūnus narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd Khayr, he said: I saw ʿAlī perform ablution and wipe over his sandals. Then he said: Had I not seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do as you saw me do, I would have thought the underside of the feet more deserving of wiping than their top.
items.ma-1265: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to me, Sharīk narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, he said: There is no zakāh on wealth until a year has passed over it.
items.ma-1266: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to me, Sharīk narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, he said: I said to al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī: The Shīʿah claim that ʿAlī will return! He said: Those liars have lied. Had we known that, his wives would not have married, nor would we have divided his inheritance.
items.ma-1267: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Ayyūb narrated to us, Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I have pardoned you from horses and slaves; there is no ṣadaqah on them.”
items.ma-1268: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn Muḥammad al-Nāqid narrated to me, ʿAmr ibn ʿUthmān al-Raqqī narrated to us, Ḥafṣ Abū ʿUmar narrated to us, from Kathīr ibn Zādhān, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever recites the Qurʾān and learns it by heart will be granted intercession for ten of his household on whom the Fire had become due.”
items.ma-1269: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Ishkāb narrated to me, Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUbaydah narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I have pardoned horses and slaves in the matter of ṣadaqah.”
items.ma-1270: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Salm Khalīl ibn Salm narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Wārith narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan ibn Dhakwān, from ʿAmr ibn Khālid, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī: that Jibrīl came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “We do not enter a house in which there is an image or a dog.” And there was a dog belonging to al-Ḥasan in the house.
items.ma-1271: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Ismāʿīl Abū Maʿmar narrated to me, Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, from Yūnus, from al-Ḥasan, from Qays ibn ʿUbād, he said: I said to ʿAlī: Tell me about this march of yours: is it a covenant the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made with you, or an opinion you formed? He said: What do you want with this? I said: Our religion, our religion. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made no covenant with me concerning it; rather it is an opinion I formed.
items.ma-1272: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Khalīl, from ʿAlī, he said: Al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah had a spear, and whenever we went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on an expedition he took it out with him, and would plant it in the ground, and people passing by would pick it up. I said: If I go to the Prophet ﷺ I shall tell him. He said: “If you do, you will not take up a stray.”
items.ma-1273: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū Ḥayyah ibn Qays, he said: ʿAlī performed ablution three times each, then drank the remainder of his ablution water, then said: This is how I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform ablution.
items.ma-1274: Muʿāwiyah ibn Hishām narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from Sālim ibn Abī Ḥafṣah, he said: A narration from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mulayl reached me, so I went early to him and found them at a funeral. A man narrated to me from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mulayl, he said: I heard ʿAlī say: Every Prophet was given seven nobles, and your Prophet was given fourteen nobles, among them Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd and ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir.
items.ma-1275: Yaḥyā ibn Abī Bukayr narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, Abū Isḥāq informed us, from Shurayḥ ibn al-Nuʿmān – he said: and he was a truthful man – from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded us to examine the eye and the ear closely, and not to sacrifice an animal that is one-eyed, nor one cut at the front of the ear, nor one cut at the back, nor one with a slit ear, nor one with a pierced ear. Zuhayr said: I said to Abū Isḥāq: Did he mention the broken-horned? He said: No. I said: What is muqābalah? He said: It is the one whose ear-tip is cut off. I said: And mudābarah? He said: The one whose back of the ear is cut. I said: What is sharqāʾ? He said: The one whose ear is slit. I said: And what is kharqāʾ? He said: The one whose ear is pierced by the brand.
items.ma-1276: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us, Sufyān ibn Ḥusayn informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from Abū ʿUbayd, the mawlā of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, he said: I heard ʿAlī say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade you to keep the meat of sacrifices beyond three days.
items.ma-1277: Yazīd narrated to us, al-Ḥajjāj ibn Arṭāh informed us, from al-Ḥakam, from al-Qāsim ibn Mukhaymirah, from Shurayḥ ibn Hāniʾ, he said: I asked ʿĀʾishah about wiping over the leather socks, and she said: Ask ʿAlī, for he knows this better than I; he used to travel with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. I asked ʿAlī and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “For the resident a day and a night, and for the traveller three days and their nights.”
items.ma-1278: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Bakkār narrated to me, Ḥafṣ ibn Sulaymān – meaning Abū ʿUmar al-Qāriʾ – narrated to us, from Kathīr ibn Zādhān, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamrah, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever learns the Qurʾān, masters it and memorizes it, Allah will admit him to Paradise and grant him intercession for ten of his household, every one of whom the Fire had become due.”
items.ma-1279: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah and Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd al-Muḥāribī narrated to me, both said: Sharīk narrated to us, from Abū al-Ḥasnāʾ, from al-Ḥakam, from Ḥanash, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me to sacrifice two rams on his behalf, so I love to do it. And Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd al-Muḥāribī said in his narration: He sacrificed two rams on his behalf: one for the Prophet ﷺ and the other for himself. It was said to him about it, and he said: He commanded me, so I shall never leave it.
items.ma-1280: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥriz ibn ʿAwn ibn Abī ʿAwn narrated to me, Sharīk narrated to us, from Simāk, from Ḥanash, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me as a judge and said: “When the two disputants come to you, do not judge against either of them until you hear from the other, for then the judgment will become clear to you.”
items.ma-1281:
ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū al-Rabīʿ al-Zahrānī narrated to me. And ʿAlī ibn Ḥakīm al-Awdī narrated to us. And Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Warkānī narrated to us. And Zakariyyā ibn Yaḥyā Zaḥmawayh narrated to us. And ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir ibn Zurārah al-Ḥaḍramī narrated to us. And Dāwūd ibn ʿAmr al-Ḍabbī narrated to us, they said: Sharīk narrated to us, from Simāk, from Ḥanash, from ʿAlī, he said: The Prophet ﷺ sent me to Yemen as a judge, and I said: You send me to a people while I am young in years and have no knowledge of judging? He put his hand on my chest and said: “May Allah make you firm and keep you straight. When the two disputants come to you, do not judge for the first until you hear from the other, for it is more likely that the judgment will become clear to you.” He said: I have remained a judge ever since.
And this is the wording of the hadith of Dāwūd ibn ʿAmr al-Ḍabbī, and some of them are more complete in wording than others.
items.ma-1282: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān Luwayn narrated to me, Muḥammad ibn Jābir narrated to us, from Simāk, from Ḥanash, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, he said: The Prophet ﷺ sent me as a judge to Yemen … and he mentioned the hadith. He said: “Allah is making your heart firm and guiding your heart.” And he mentioned the hadith.
items.ma-1283: Luwayn said: And Sharīk narrated to us, from Simāk, from Ḥanash, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ, with the like of its meaning.
items.ma-1284: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar al-Qawārīrī narrated to me, al-Sakan ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to us, al-Ashʿath ibn Sawwār narrated to us, from Ibn Ashwaʿ, from Ḥanash al-Kinānī, from ʿAlī: that he sent the head of his police and said to him: Do you know what I am sending you on? On what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me on: to chisel away every – meaning – image, and to level every grave.
items.ma-1285: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, my father narrated to me. And Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to me, both said: Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, from Zāʾidah, from Simāk, from Ḥanash, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: “When two men bring a dispute to you for judgment, do not judge for the first until you hear what the other says, for then you will see how to judge.”
items.ma-1286: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shaybah narrated to me, Sharīk narrated to us, from Abū al-Ḥasnāʾ, from al-Ḥakam, from Ḥanash, he said: I saw ʿAlī ﵁ sacrificing two rams, and I said to him: What is this? He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ charged me to sacrifice on his behalf.
items.ma-1287: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Bakr narrated to me, ʿAmr ibn Ḥammād narrated to us, from Asbāṭ ibn Naṣr, from Simāk, from Ḥanash, from ʿAlī: that when the Prophet ﷺ sent him with Barāʾah, he said: O Prophet of Allah, I am not fluent, nor an orator. He said: “It must be that either I go with it, or you go with it.” He said: If it must be, then I shall go. He said: “Then go, for Allah makes your tongue firm and guides your heart.” He said: Then he placed his hand on his mouth.
items.ma-1288: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Jābir, that ʿĀṣim ibn Bahdalah said: I heard Zirr narrate from ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said on the day of Uḥud: “They have kept us busy from the middle ṣalāh until the sun set. May Allah fill their graves, their houses and their bellies with fire.”
items.ma-1289: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Jābir, he said: I heard al-Shaʿbī narrate from al-Ḥārith, from ʿAlī, that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the one who consumes ribā, the one who feeds it, its two witnesses, the one who writes it, the woman who tattoos and the woman who has herself tattooed, the one who makes lawful and the one for whom it is made lawful, and the one who withholds the ṣadaqah; and he forbade wailing.
items.ma-1290: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Jābir, he said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nujayy narrate from ʿAlī, he said: I had an hour with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the night, in which Allah ﷿ benefits me with what He wills. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The angels do not enter a house in which there is an image, a dog or a person in janābah.” He said: “I looked, and there was a puppy of al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī beneath the bed, so I took it out.”
items.ma-1291: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Jābir, he said: I heard Abū Burdah narrate from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade me to put the ring on the middle finger.
items.ma-1292: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Ribʿī ibn Ḥirāsh, that he heard ʿAlī giving a khuṭbah, saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do not lie about me, for whoever lies about me will enter the Fire.”
items.ma-1293: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar al-Qawārīrī narrated to me, Khālid ibn al-Ḥārith narrated to us, Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah that he heard Jurayy ibn Kulayb narrate: that he heard ʿAlī say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade an animal with a broken horn and ear.
items.ma-1294: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Khaythamah narrated to me, ʿAbdah ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, from Saʿīd, from Qatādah, from Jurayy ibn Kulayb al-Nahdī, from ʿAlī, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade sacrificing an animal with a broken horn and ear.
items.ma-1295: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Ibrāhīm ibn al-Ḥajjāj al-Nājī narrated to me, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Hishām ibn ʿAmr al-Fazārī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say at the end of his witr: “O Allah, I seek refuge in Your Riḍā from Your Sakhaṭ, and in Your pardon from Your punishment, and I seek refuge in You from You. I cannot count the praise of You; You are as You have praised Yourself.”
items.ma-1296: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Naṣr ibn ʿAlī al-Azdī narrated to me, my father informed me, from Abū Salām ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Muslim ibn Salām, from ʿImrān ibn Ẓabyān, from Ḥukaym ibn Saʿd, from ʿAlī: that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ intended a journey he would say: “O Allah, by You I attack, by You I move, and by You I travel.”
items.ma-1297: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān Luwayn narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Jābir narrated to us, from Simāk, from Ḥanash, from ʿAlī, he said: When ten verses of Barāʾah were revealed to the Prophet ﷺ, the Prophet ﷺ called Abū Bakr and sent him with them to recite them to the people of Makkah. Then the Prophet ﷺ called me and said to me: “Catch up with Abū Bakr, and wherever you overtake him take the document from him, go with it to the people of Makkah and recite it to them.” I overtook him at al-Juḥfah and took the document from him, and Abū Bakr returned to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, has something been revealed about me? He said: “No, but Jibrīl came to me and said: None will convey it on your behalf except you, or a man from you.”
items.ma-1298: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Sulaymān, from Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, from al-Ḥārith ibn Suwayd, he said: It was said to ʿAlī: Your Messenger used to single you out for something apart from the people in general? He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not single us out for anything he did not single the people out for, except for something in the scabbard of this sword of mine. He took out a writing in which were some of the ages of camels, and in it was: “Al-Madīnah is a ḥaram from between Thawr to ʿĀʾir. Whoever introduces an innovation in it, or gives shelter to one who introduces an innovation, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels and all the people; on the Day of Resurrection no ṣarf or ʿadl will be accepted from him. The protection of the Muslims is one; whoever breaks the covenant of a Muslim, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels and all the people; on the Day of Resurrection no ṣarf or ʿadl will be accepted from him. And whoever attaches himself as a client to a mawlā without their permission, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels and all the people; on the Day of Resurrection no ṣarf or ʿadl will be accepted from him.”
items.ma-1299:
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Sulaymān, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Shutayr ibn Shakal, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said on the day of al-Aḥzāb: “They have held us back from the middle ṣalāh, the ʿAṣr ṣalāh, until the sun set. May Allah fill their graves and their houses – or their graves and their bellies – with fire.”
Shuʿbah said: “May Allah fill their graves and their houses, or their graves and their bellies, with fire” – I do not know whether it is in the hadith or not; I am unsure about it.
items.ma-1300: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Naṣr ibn ʿAlī narrated to me, Nūḥ ibn Qays narrated to us, Khālid ibn Khālid narrated to us, from Yūsuf ibn Māzin: that a man asked ʿAlī, saying: O Commander of the Believers, describe the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to us, give us his description. He said: He was not excessively tall, and was above medium height; when he came among a group he surpassed them. He was white, intensely radiant, large of head, with a bright forehead and brows set apart, long of eyelashes, thick in the palms and feet. When he walked he lifted his feet as though descending a slope. It was as though the sweat on his face were pearls. I never saw anyone like him before him or after him, may my father and mother be his ransom ﷺ.
items.ma-1301: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr al-Muqaddamī narrated to me, Nūḥ ibn Qays narrated to us, Khālid ibn Khālid narrated to us, from Yūsuf ibn Māzin, from a man, from ʿAlī, that it was said to him: Describe the Prophet ﷺ to us. He said: He was not excessively tall … and he mentioned exactly the like of it.
items.ma-1302: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Naṣr ibn ʿAlī narrated to me, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, from Nuʿaym ibn Ḥakīm, from Abū Maryam, from ʿAlī, he said: There were idols on the Kaʿbah, and I went to lift the Prophet ﷺ up to them but could not, so he lifted me, and I began cutting them down. Had I wished, I could have reached the sky.
items.ma-1303: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Khaythamah narrated to me, Shabābah ibn Sawwār narrated to us, Nuʿaym ibn Ḥakīm narrated to me, Abū Maryam narrated to me, ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib narrated to us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A people will pass out of Islam as the arrow passes out of the game. They recite the Qurʾān, which does not pass beyond their collarbones. Ṭūbā for whoever kills them and whom they kill. Their sign is a man with a deformed arm.”
items.ma-1304:
ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Naṣr ibn ʿAlī and ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar narrated to me, both said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dāwūd narrated to us, from Nuʿaym ibn Ḥakīm, from Abū Maryam, from ʿAlī: that the wife of al-Walīd ibn ʿUqbah came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, al-Walīd beats her – and Naṣr ibn ʿAlī said in his narration: complaining of him – He said: “Say to him: He has granted me protection.” ʿAlī said: She stayed but a short while before she returned and said: It did not increase him except in beating me. So he took a fringe of his garment and handed it to her and said: “Say to him: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has granted me protection.” She stayed but a short while before she returned and said: It did not increase him except in beating me. So he raised his hands and said: “O Allah, upon You is al-Walīd; he has sinned against me twice.”
This is the wording of the hadith of al-Qawārīrī, and their meaning is one.
items.ma-1305: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah and Abū Khaythamah narrated to me, both said: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Mūsā narrated to us, Nuʿaym ibn Ḥakīm informed us, from Abū Maryam, from ʿAlī: that the wife of al-Walīd ibn ʿUqbah came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ complaining of al-Walīd, that he beat her … and he mentioned the hadith.
items.ma-1306: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Yaḥyā ibn al-Jazzār, from ʿAlī, from the Prophet ﷺ: that on the day of al-Aḥzāb he was at one of the openings of the trench, and said: “They have kept us busy from the middle ṣalāh until the sun set. May Allah fill their graves and their houses – or their bellies and their houses – with fire.”
items.ma-391:
Isḥāq ibn ʿĪsā al-Ṭabbāʿ narrated to us, Mālik ibn Anas narrated to us, Ibn Shihāb narrated to me, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUtbah ibn Masʿūd, that Ibn ʿAbbās informed him: that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf returned to his lodging – Ibn ʿAbbās said: and I used to teach ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf to recite, and he found me while I was waiting for him, and that was at Minā in the last Ḥajj that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb performed – ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf said: A man came to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and said: So-and-so says: If ʿUmar were to die, I would pledge allegiance to so-and-so. ʿUmar said: I am standing this evening among the people, and I will warn them about these men who want to seize their affair from them. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: I said: O Commander of the Believers, do not do so, for the season gathers the riffraff and rabble of the people, and they are the ones who will overcome your assembly when you stand among the people, and I fear that you will say a statement which those will carry off in flight, not preserving it, nor placing it in its proper places. Rather wait until you come to al-Madīnah, for it is the abode of the hijrah and the sunnah, and you will be alone with the scholars of the people and their nobles, and you will say what you say with composure, and they will preserve your statement and place it in its proper places. ʿUmar said: If I reach al-Madīnah safe, I will speak to the people there at the first occasion I stand.
When we came to al-Madīnah at the close of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, and it was the day of Jumuʿah, I hastened in the afternoon like the striking of the blind – I said to Mālik: What is the striking of the blind? He said: He does not care at what hour he goes out; he does not know heat and cold and the like of this – and I found Saʿīd ibn Zayd at the right corner of the minbar, having preceded me, so I sat opposite him, my knee rubbing his knee, and it was not long before ʿUmar came out. When I saw him I said: He will surely say this evening on this minbar a statement that no one before him has said on it. Saʿīd ibn Zayd denied that and said: What could you expect him to say that no one has said?
ʿUmar sat on the minbar, and when the muʾadhdhin fell silent, he stood and extolled Allah as He deserves, then said: To proceed, O people, I am about to say a statement which it has been decreed for me to say; I do not know, perhaps it is just before my appointed time. So whoever preserves it and understands it, let him narrate it wherever his mount takes him, and whoever does not preserve it, I do not make it lawful for him to lie about me: Indeed Allah ﵎ sent Muḥammad ﷺ with the truth and sent down the Book upon him, and among what He sent down upon him was the verse of the rajm. We recited it and preserved it, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stoned and we stoned after him. I fear that if a long time passes over the people, someone will say: We do not find the verse of the rajm in the Book of Allah ﷿, so they will go astray by abandoning an obligation that Allah ﷿ sent down. So the rajm in the Book of Allah is a right upon whoever commits zinā when he is muḥṣan, among men and women, when the proof is established, or there is pregnancy, or confession. Beware! We used to recite: Do not turn away from your fathers, for it is kufr in you to turn away from your fathers. Beware! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Do not praise me excessively as ʿĪsā ibn Maryam ﵇ was praised excessively; I am only the servant of Allah, so say: The servant of Allah and His Messenger.” It has reached me that someone among you says: If ʿUmar were to die, I would pledge allegiance to so-and-so. Let no man be deluded into saying: The pledge of allegiance to Abū Bakr ﵁ was a faltah. Beware! It was indeed like that, except that Allah ﷿ guarded against its evil, and there is not among you today one toward whom necks are cut like Abū Bakr. Beware! Of our affair when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ died: that ʿAlī and al-Zubayr, and those with them, stayed behind in the house of Fāṭimah ﵂, daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Anṣār stayed behind from us altogether in the Saqīfah of Banū Sāʿidah, and the Muhājirūn gathered to Abū Bakr. I said to him: O Abū Bakr, let us go to our brothers of the Anṣār. So we set off, heading for them, until two righteous men met us, and mentioned to us what the people had done, and said: Where are you going, O company of the Muhājirūn? I said: We want these brothers of ours of the Anṣār. They said: There is no blame upon you for not approaching them; settle your matter, O company of the Muhājirūn. I said: By Allah, we will go to them.
So we set off until we came to them in the Saqīfah of Banū Sāʿidah, and they were gathered, and in their midst was a man wrapped up. I said: Who is this? They said: Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah. I said: What is the matter with him? They said: He is ill. When we sat, their speaker stood and extolled Allah ﷿ as He deserves, and said:
To proceed: we are the helpers of Allah ﷿ and the battalion of Islam, and you, O company of the Muhājirūn, are a group of ours, and a group from among you has come hurrying, wanting to cut us off from our origin and to deprive us of the matter. When he fell silent I wanted to speak, and I had prepared a statement that pleased me; I wanted to say it before Abū Bakr, and I had been handling with care some sharpness of his; and he was more forbearing than I and more dignified. Abū Bakr said: Gently. I disliked to anger him, and he knew more than I and was more dignified. By Allah, he left no word that had pleased me in my preparation but that he said it in his impromptu speech, and better, until he fell silent. He said: To proceed: whatever of good you have mentioned, you are deserving of it; but the Arabs did not recognise this matter except for this clan of Quraysh; they are the best of the Arabs in lineage and abode, and I have approved for you one of these two men, whichever you wish. And he took my hand and the hand of Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ. I disliked nothing of what he said except that; and by Allah, that I be brought forward and my neck struck, without that drawing me nearer to any sin, was dearer to me than that I should be made commander over a people among whom is Abū Bakr, unless my self changes at death. Then a speaker of the Anṣār said: I am its little rubbing-post that is rubbed against, and its little date-palm that is propped up; from us a commander and from you a commander, O company of Quraysh – I said to Mālik: What is the meaning of “I am its little rubbing-post that is rubbed against, and its little date-palm that is propped up”? He said: As though he is saying: I am its shrewd one –. He said: The clamour grew, and voices were raised, until I feared disagreement, and I said: Stretch out your hand, O Abū Bakr. He stretched out his hand and I pledged allegiance to him, and the Muhājirūn pledged allegiance to him, then the Anṣār pledged allegiance to him, and we leapt upon Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah. One of them said: You have killed Saʿd. I said: May Allah kill Saʿd.
And ʿUmar ﵁ said: By Allah, in what we witnessed we found no matter stronger than the pledge of allegiance to Abū Bakr ﵁. We feared that if we left the people, and there was no pledge, they would make a pledge after us, so either we would follow them in what we did not approve, or we would oppose them and there would be corruption in it. So whoever pledges allegiance to a commander without consultation of the Muslims has no pledge, nor has the one who pledged allegiance to him, at the risk that the two of them be killed.
Mālik said: And Ibn Shihāb informed me, from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr: that the two men who met them were ʿUwaym ibn Sāʿidah and Maʿn ibn ʿAdī. Ibn Shihāb said: And Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab informed me: that the one who said: “I am its little rubbing-post that is rubbed against, and its little date-palm that is propped up” was al-Ḥubāb ibn al-Mundhir.
